title: Paramedic Capstone
description: Framework for the management of quality and safety in pre-hospital care in an Australian context. Clinical governance, clinical indicators, leadership, inter-professional collaboration and communication, working safely and ethical behaviour. Includes concepts of consumer value, audit, clinical risk, professional development and how policy and procedure integrate with structure and governance.

title: Fundamentals of Reservoir Engineering
description: This unit covers the fundamental knowledge a petroleum reservoir engineer needs to know in providing a qualitative and quantitative description of a hydrocarbon reservoir and how to manage its performance. The early part of the unit, apart from covering basic rock and fluid properties (e.g. porosity, saturation, gas-oil ratio (GoR), gas solubility (Rs), formation volume factor (FVF), etc.), it also defines and discusses concepts such the volumetrics, reserves, reservoir drive mechanisms, recovery factor and static fluid distribution in real hydrocarbon reservoirs. The unit further covers the fundamentals of reservoir dynamics. Initially, the Darcy’s Law and its applications are discussed in details. Then, the Radial Diffusivity Equation (RDE) is derived and used to model fluid flow in porous rocks under various flowing phases. The unit also covers the basics of transient well testing of oil wells where the transient solution to RDE is used to analyse the results of drawdown and build-up tests in the context of some basic reservoir heterogeneities such the presence of a single sealing fault. The last part of the unit covers the derivation of a new version of RDE using the gas pseudo pressure suitable for handling gas flow in porous media. It also covers the derivation of various forms of deliverability equation for gas wells and how they can be used to interpret the results of different types of deliverability tests.

title: Hydrocarbon Phase Behaviour
description: The fundamental purpose of subsea systems is to effectively transport well fluids from wellhead to production facilities. To achieve this requires an understanding of fluid properties and how they flow. The topics covered in this unit include petroleum chemistry, hydrocarbon phase behaviour and its prediction using equations of state, single and multiphase fluids flow, gas hydrates, flow measurements and metering techniques, oil and gas flow threats and remediation techniques.

title: Numerical Reservoir Simulation
description: Fundamentals for numerical simulation, and types of petroleum reservoir simulation models; Numerical methods for solving the basic governing equation of fluid flow through porous media using finite difference techniques; Reservoir modelling, data preparartion; Concepts related to model building; grid design and model initialisation; Concepts related to history matching and forecasting of a reservoirs future performance; Familiarity with the application of commercial simulation software.

title: Petroleum Geology and Geophysics
description: Geological principles, Minerals and rocks, digenetic processes, Geological time and stratigraphy, Structural framework, Depositional patterns and Reservoir rocks, Petroleum system, Subsurface mapping, Volumetric calculation, Reservoir Heterogeneity, Reservoir Modelling Review, Hydrocarbon exploration methods.

title: Study Tour
description: In this unit, students will engage in immersive learning in an off-campus environment. Students will travel away from Perth to engage with people of different backgrounds to gain an appreciation of how stories, art and/or media or cultural analysis are conducted in different cultural environments. They will focus on a cultural learning experience, through on-ground research, creative productions, and critical reflection. This Unit will provide an intensive learning experience, alongside significant cross-cultural awareness, personal growth, and leadership skills.

title: Applied Bioscience for Health Instability 2
description: The unit covers pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnosis and clinical decision making for individuals with adverse health events: respiratory, cardiovascular, neoplasia, hepatobiliary, gastrointestinal and urological dysfunction, and fluid and electrolyte disturbances. Students learn about immune dysfunction, infection, anaphylaxis, changes to normal brain functioning; impacting upon cognition: dementia, delirium. The unit focuses applicable pharmacology and quality use of medicines.

title: Energy Production
description: The unit provides an overview of various energy sources used to meet energy demand, their extraction and production processes, including associated technologies, the policies and regulations governing the energy sector, the challenges facing the industry, and opportunities for advancement through innovation. Additionally, students will need to address the synergy between energy production and consumption with an emphasis on the analysis and evaluation of risks and challenges from the perspective of techno-economic and social impacts.

title: Nursing Practice for Health Instability 2
description: This unit uses a systems approach to assess, diagnose, plan, manage, document and evaluate care related to unstable conditions across the lifespan. Students apply therapeutic communication and critical reasoning to meet nursing competency standards in selected clinical contexts. The unit expands on medication (parenteral, paediatric) preparation, administration and recording, dosage calculations and medication infusion devices including the PICC line. The unit covers Intravenous fluid replacement therapy including introduction to blood product 	replacement; advanced pain management and applied pharmacology relating to pain management, antimicrobials, diabetic therapy and anticoagulant treatment. Other content covered includes cardiac and neurovascular assessment and monitoring; assessing the mental health needs of people in a range of settings, particularly anxiety and depression; recognising and responding to the deteriorating patient (adults and paediatrics) advanced wound care and staging of pressure injuries; surgical wounds and stoma care; nutritional support; pre/post operative care, inter professional care planning, principles of isolation, ANTT, and barrier nursing; Primary Health Care for discharge planning and home care support.

title: Human Computer Interface
description: An introduction to human computer interfaces, including the motivation and contexts for using these. The class teaches a process for user centred development as well as different measures for evaluation and models that inform human computer interface design. Social issues influencing human computer interface design and use are considered, as well as multi-cultural interaction and communication in order to accommodate human diversity. The different user interface standards and principles of graphical user interfaces are covered in addition to designing and programming GUIs both in native and web formats and widgets. Geometry management, event management and user interaction are introduced. Finally, user interface programming environments and future developments are discussed.

title: Process Plant Engineering
description: Interpretation and creation of PFDs, P&IDs, mechanical drawings, plot plans and equipment specification sheets; Materials Selection & Specification. Fluid Flow, Pipe Friction for Single and Multi-phase Flow Friction. Pipeline & Pumping Design. Valves, Pumps, Seals. Piping System Design. Pressure Vessel Design. Pressurised Systems. Foundation Design. Plant Energy Systems and Utilities etc.

title: Built Environment Special Topic
description: Individual or group work on a topic approved by your Course Coordinator. The topic should further develop an area of study related to the practice of your discipline.

title: Clinical Radiation Therapy Practice 3
description: This unit provides authentic radiation therapy professional practice experience in the clinical setting, at the level appropriate for the intermediate/advanced beginning reflective professional. Students will have the opportunity to advance their capacity for mentoring.

title: Democracy and Dictatorship
description: This unit explores the historical forces that have shaped the governing of nation-states around the world. Examining concepts such as democracy, authoritarianism, citizenship, and social movements, this unit analyses how and why different kinds of government have arisen over the course of history. What is democracy, and why is it still a cherished ideal in many parts of the world? What factors have historically supported the rise, and fall, of democracies, as well as authoritarian rule? Students will explore such questions by looking at the different political paths taken in various countries and the struggles to express political aspirations from the 19th- to the 21st century.

title: Legacies of Empire
description: This unit examines the major world empires of the fifteenth to twentieth centuries to analyse the role of imperialism in shaping the modern world. Using case studies drawn from various regions of the world, students evaluate the social, political, economic, and environmental effects of empires and imperialism today. This unit provides a strong grounding for students to explain the major historical factors that underpin international politics and society.

title: Geoscience Analytical Techniques
description: This unit provides an introduction to a range of specific analytical techniques and/or methodologies used to solve scientific problems and Earth and Planetary Sciences. Each analytical technique will be covered in a work integrated learning environment, encompassing main applications, the theoretical background, instrument technical specifications, approaches to data acquisition and processing, and evaluation of the quality and scientific reliability of data. Where appropriate, opportunities will be provided to experience geoscientific analysis first hand. This unit involves a fieldwork component in which various pre-existing geoscience analytical datasets are evaluated and incorporated with newly collected data to interpret the geology of a region.

title: Competition Law and Policy
description: In this unit students will examine Australian competition law and policy, particularly under the Commonwealth Competition & Consumer Act 2010. Students will consider the economic policy rationale for competition law, its historical development, and the key legislative provisions. Anti-competitive practices covered include cartel conduct, misuse of market power, exclusive dealing, resale price maintenance and anti-competitive mergers and acquisitions. The regulatory role of the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) as well as the role of National Competition Policy is discussed.

title: Design for Indoor Comfort
description: Comprehensive overview of various issues of human inhabitation and personal sensation in order to understand indoor comfort and its multifaceted aspects - thermal, visual, acoustic, and air quality. Provides an in depth summary of good design practices and how specific factors of the built environment affect human well-being.

title: Cross Institutional Study (within Australia)
description: Please refer to syllabus for the equivalent course

title: Go Practice - Internship 4
description: This unit provides students with fieldwork opportunities through internships or industry and community engagement opportunities in simulated work-based environments. Independent student learning will be supported by academics and industry advisors, and students in courses without professional work experience are encouraged to apply.

title: International Commercial Law
description: This unit discusses the international sale of goods under both domestic law and international instruments including the Incoterms Rules and the Convention on Contracts for the International Sales of Goods (CISG), the international carriage of goods by sea, air and land, payment in international trade, the use of letters of credit under UCP 600, and marine and aviation Insurance. The unit also examines the history and structures of the World Trade Organization (WTO), including GATT, GATS and TRIPS, and WTO Trade Law Fundamentals, including Tariffs, Quotas and Non-discrimination, Subsidies, Countervailing Duties, Dumping & Dispute Settlement. Finally, the role of the WTO in matters such as development, human rights, the environment and food security is discussed.

title: Clinical Radiation Therapy Practice 2
description: This unit provides authentic radiation therapy professional practice experience in the clinical setting, at the level appropriate for the intermediate beginning reflective professional. Students will have the opportunity to develop their capacity for mentoring.

title: Business Applications
description: Review of modern business technology trends and issues. This may include overviews of modern business applications including enterprise resource planning (ERP), e-commerce, m-commerce, knowledge management and groupware, customer relationship management, supply chain management, data warehousing, data mining, business intelligence, competitive intelligence. Their impact on the organisation is reviewed.

title: Physiotherapy Clinics 3
description: This fieldwork unit will cover physiotherapy clinical practice, to entry level standard according to the Physiotherapy practice thresholds in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand for Physiotherapy, managing clients in a community setting with a range of caseloads and model/s of intervention and service delivery.

title: Calculus 1
description: This unit builds on students’ knowledge of calculus, further extending to a range of techniques used in solving problems arising from science, engineering and business related fields. Students will extend their differentiation skills to implicit, logarithmic and partial differentiation, and will apply their differentiation techniques to optimisation problems and the approximation of functions. This unit will cover a range of integration techniques, and students will apply these to find volume, length and surface area. Students will also learn to solve a variety of first and second order differential equations, and be introduced to several techniques for testing the convergence of a series. This unit is designed for those students who have passed WACE Mathematics Methods ATAR or equivalent.

title: Introduction to Indigenous Australian Community Governance and Organisational Practices
description: Introduction to Indigenous governance including internal and external organisational processes and structures and policy development which impact on own work and or community setting.

title: Interior Architecture Practice 2
description: This unit is designed to prepare students for the challenges and opportunities of a career in design practice that extends to the transdisciplinary nature of interior design professional practice. Students investigate the role of the interior designer within the complexities of a project and what it means to collaborate professionally with consultants, suppliers and clients. A range of practice-related topics will be introduced, including practice management, law, contracts and specifications, with various insights into the workplace culture.

title: Foundations of Counselling and Group Work
description: Individual and group counselling competencies that can be applied with a diverse range of people and contexts will be developed in this unit. Person-centred counselling will be utilised to understand and develop skills that underpin therapeutic engagement for individual and group approaches to occupational therapy interventions. Contemporary, evidence-based approaches will be used to develop individual and group practice. The principles and application of self-management and reflective practice will be utilised to foster ongoing professional development in this unit, including developing and maintaining ethical practice.

title: Foundations of Clinical Biochemistry
description: Anabolic pathways. Integration and organisation of metabolism and discussion of metabolic disease. Peptide, thyroid and steroid hormones, their receptors and mechanisms of action. Diagnostic enzymology and the role of clinical biochemistry in evaluating hepatic, renal, respiratory and thyroid function.

title: Property Finance and Capital Markets
description: This unit examines the theory of property finance and its application with local and international property markets. Students gain practical exposure to residential lending and a general understanding of finance for commercial property investment and development. The unit is structured around the development of practical computer-based analysis techniques through a case study approach.

title: Introduction to Pathophysiology
description: This unit will introduce students to the cellular physiological and pathophysiological basis of common chronic diseases involving the blood, cardiovascular, respiratory, nervous, endocrine, urinary and gastrointestinal systems using a case based learning approach. Students will evaluate responses to trauma, minor infections and disease. ANS regulation and inflammation will be present as the themes bringing pathophysiology of the organs systems together.

title: Cinematic Storytelling and Production
description: Introduction to classical and contemporary screen genres and methods of screen appreciation, including fiction and non-fiction modes of film making. This unit combines critical studies and creative practice through action/reflection and production/analysis tasks.

title: Stochastic Processes
description: This unit will cover the probabilistic framework for developing stochastic models for real world processes with an emphasis on models used in actuarial practice. Students will acquire practical skills in developing mathematical models for stochastic processes, compute various probabilities of interest and estimate parameters of the underlying models. Topics covered include Markov chains and their application to experience rating; Markov process models with application to survival; sickness and marriage models; and simple stimulation models.

title: Speech Pathology Fieldwork 3
description: In this unit, students will undertake speech pathology clinical practice to develop competency according to Speech Pathology Australia Competency-Based Occupational Standards (CBOS). This unit will facilitate the development of skills in the management of paediatric or adult clients across a range of practice areas. Students will be expected to demonstrate competency relative to their stage of their fieldwork progression; They will demonstrate approaching entry-level competency at the end of their penultimate placement placement and entry level competency at the end of their final placement.

title: Occupational Hygiene
description: The recognition, evaluation and control of occupational hygiene hazards, with emphasis on physical agents such as noise, vibration, heat and pressure, together with chemical agents such as dusts, fibres, gases, vapours, fumes and mists. Toxicological evaluation of hazardous chemicals, qualitative and quantitative risk assessment techniques, and the accessing of relevant sources of occupational hygiene information. The use of workplace exposure standards and the selection, application and evaluation of control measures for dealing with occupational hygiene hazards in the workplace.

title: ELICOS Unit
description: Created for administrative enrolling purposes only.

title: Nutrition and Chronic Disease
description: This unit builds upon your knowledge of human physiology, biochemistry and nutrition principles to develop your understanding of health and chronic disease. You will also be applying your statistical analysis knowledge to answer research questions based on the data that you collect during your labs. Throughout this unit you will integrate these fields of learning to develop an understanding of how nutrition may prevent or accelerate the progression of chronic disease.

title: UX Accessibility and Analytics
description: User experience (UX) is one of the most important aspects of business and contemporary marketing. As poor UX with products and platforms can lead to frustrated customers, lost leads, and lower conversion rates, it is essential to ensure that users have intuitive, enjoyable and accessible experiences. This unit addresses important gaps in business education relating to analysing and evaluating user experiences for a diverse range of users. It addresses the crucial considerations of accessible design for users with a range of accessibility challenges (i.e. motor, visual, auditory, cognitive, and cultural), gives students hands-on experience with user testing, and builds professional analytical competencies that shape user experience’s impact on business outcomes. In doing so, students learn to foster important ‘Principles of Responsible Management Education’ (PRME) in accordance with the UN’s ‘Sustainable Development Goals’ (SDGs).

title: Antimicrobial Chemotherapy
description: In this unit, students explore principles of treatment - clinical diagnosis; bacteriological diagnosis; place of antimicrobial chemotherapy in medicine; considerations relevant to effective antibiotic use; reasons for treatment failure; mechanisms for the development of antimicrobial resistance. The unit introduces students to the scope of antimicrobial chemotherapy and considers antibiotic treatment of specific conditions including skin infections, respiratory infections, tuberculosis and travel health. Core unit concepts include: principles of selective toxicity; classification of antibiotics, antimicrobial combination therapy and antibiotic policies. Students investigate mechanism of action, spectrum, pharmacokinetics and adverse events of the major classes of antimicrobial agents.

title: Planning for Economic Development
description: Examine the theories and principles aligned with economic development as part of a more integrated approach to urban and regional planning.

title: Corporate Stewardship
description: Corporate stewardship engages with diverse issues, including the question of legal personality, human rights, employee rights, environmental protection, supplier relationships, monitoring and stakeholder rights and responsibilities. The recent evolution of the corporate stewardship agenda will be reviewed, in relation to changing perceptions on values, compliance and respect for people, communities and the environment. While it is proposed that corporate stewardship is a worthwhile investment in the future prosperity of the organisation, wider community and the environment, we investigate the limitations of arguing the profit case alone. We explore and critique evolving best practice approaches for organisations to develop and implement effective corporate stewardship programs that bring value to the organisation and its stakeholders, while ensuring that perceptions of ‘greenwash’ are not justified.

title: Planning Report
description: Design and carry out an individual research project on a specific planning problem and present it as a professional report.

title: Military Technology and the Arms Race
description: In this unit students will learn about the key drivers behind military technological innovation, contemporary technological warfare and the so-called arms race. Technological warfare, which brings together strategies, operational art, tactics, and applied science, continues to alter military balances, and by that affect the international security environment. Students will be introduced to the history of technical warfare, become familiar with pathways to military superiority; the difference between incremental processes and quantum leaps; and learn about the challenges and benefits of self-reliance as well as risks of overdependence.

title: Ethics and Sustainability in Engineering
description: This unit focuses on how the Profession of Engineering can support people and the planet by providing future Engineers with appropriate tools, ways of thinking, and a sense of responsibility and agency to lead for change. The unit includes the importance of the context in which Engineering is practised, which incorporates an appreciation of diverse perspectives and societal values in considering sustainability, including reflecting on the values of traditional First Nations Peoples. The unit content is broadly organised into three clusters: (1) Engineering Ethics and Sustainable Development: an introduction to the sustainable development agenda and debate and ethical responsibilities of the Profession of Engineering. (2) Resource Management Tools and Practices: the 'nuts and bolts' of efficient resource utilisation in 'industrial' operations, including life cycle assessment, ecoefficiency analysis, triple bottom line analysis, and environmental management system. (3) Sustainable Technology: an exploration of technology's role (engineering) in achieving sustainable development.

title: Introduction to Indigenous Australian Community Development and Management
description: Development of key concepts, principles and ethics of Indigenous Community Development and Management including conflict management, inter and intra communication and promotion of Indigenous self-determination.

title: Korean Society and Politics
description: This unit is suitable for students with no prior knowledge of Korean language or culture. It introduces students to the main events in the modern history of the Korean peninsula, Korean social and political structures, as well as the fractious relations between the two Koreas. The unit is designed is designed for learners who will require an in-depth understanding of Korea in their future careers, and covers topics such as family structures and values, gender relations, migration and the significance of the corporate sector to Korean society and politics. The unit also covers aspects of North Korean society and relations between the two Koreas. Assessments for this unit focus on developing skills in providing research and evidence-based recommendations to employers in workplace contexts and conducting a simulated symposium.

title: Illustration 2
description: This unit focuses on the use of illustration in narrative communication. Students are free to explore different illustration genres including; storyboarding, concept art, environmental and character development, graphic novels, comics and editorial.

title: Photogrammetry
description: This unit is an introduction into Photogrammetry and will cover not only the fundamentals of photogrammetry, the photogrammetric workflow and its products but also will provide information about sensor technology and the current trends in the Spatial Science profession. The unit will focus on different application areas such as close range photogrammetry, drone photogrammetry and satellite photogrammetry. The learned theory in the lectures is reinforced during tutorials and practical laboratories. Students will plan a photogrammetric project, capture and process images and deliver basic products.

title: Valuation Methodology
description: This unit introduces students to foundations of real estate valuation. It provides students with an understanding of the methods used in the industry to value both residential and commercial property. Students will undertake a comprehensive written residential valuation report, replicating the type of work undertaken by valuers in the property industry.

title: Pharmacy Practice 1
description: This unit introduces students to communication skills for: establishing a professional relationship with patients; and patient counselling for a range of dosage forms. Students are introduced to the primary care (history/examination/diagnosis/management/monitoring) of wounds, minor oral health conditions, foot ailments and eye disorders, contact lens care and ear disorders. Students are provided with an overview of the pharmaceutical regulatory framework for the purpose of understanding the legal and ethical responsibilities related to pharmacy practice. The unit further explores principles of medication safety, and contemporary roles and responsibilities of pharmacists.

title: Interpersonal Communication Skills in Health
description: Interpersonal communication theories for health professionals; Intrapersonal communication: perception, self-concept and self-awareness; Interpersonal communication skills for ethical, professional practice; Intercultural communication and working with interpreters; Communication in an Aboriginal context; Interviewing skills.

title: Sustainability Challenge
description: This challenge-based unit provides students with the opportunity to engage in an interdisciplinary, team-based approach with undergraduate and postgraduate students to learn about industry-related and vital sustainability questions and problems. Students will then apply those learnings as they propose solutions to sustainability-related projects initiated by those industry partners and academics after careful consultation, education about the organisations/related parties, and further research on the sustainability issues in question. Students who are interested in applying interdisciplinary knowledge and skills to innovate and contribute to a more sustainable future are encouraged to apply to enrol in this unit.

title: Illustration 4
description: This unit will be split into two separate teaching modules. The first will focus on the concept behind the images that we create. The second module will be a technical unit focussing on digital enhancement of images. These modules combine to lead toward the creation of a graduate portfolio.

title: Solid State Physics
description: This unit begins with a discussion of crystal structures and principles of bonding in the four main types of solids. Finite temperature effects are introduced via the Heat Capacity of the Free Electron Gas. Using the reciprocal lattice, the principle of Bragg scattering is generalised. Substantial effort is devoted to solving the periodic Schroedinger Equation within the Kronig-Penney model. From this, band theory is applied to optical and electrical properties, including the phenomenon of holes. The unit concludes with a study of the lattice vibration theory of phonons.

title: Digital Narrative Experience Studio
description: This unit examines the crucial role of storytelling in crafting compelling creative digital experiences. In this unit, students will focus on how narrative structures combined with the appropriate creative principles and an understanding of relevant trends in the industry inform the creative process and user experience. Students will engage with industry practices and working in teams, in a studio centric approach to develop a digital creative experience. Through studio-based projects, reflective practice, and critical analysis, students will develop skills to craft compelling narratives that drive innovative digital experiences.

title: Allied Health Honours Professional Project
description: This unit introduces you to the knowledge and skills of project management, a capability that future employers are seeking in their employees. Working in collaboration with your learning team and project partner(s), you will draw from relevant project management approaches, your disciplinary knowledge and practice expertise to design, implement and disseminate the results of a small-scale project to address the partner(s) identified need. The focus will be that of a quality enhancement project broadly oriented towards supporting better health, social, or educational outcomes.

title: Applied Exercise and Sports Physiology
description: This unit examines areas with specific relevance to the physiology of elite sports performance. This will include, but not be limited to, mechanisms of adaptation, environmental stress, ergogenic aids, novel training approaches, limitations to exercise in healthy normal individuals, facilitating recovery, overtraining, and shortfalls in the exercise physiology knowledge base.

title: Publication Design
description: This unit introduces the role of the image in publication design. Through exploration of design fundamentals in print media students will examine how visual imagery can be utilised in the communication of information.

title: Complex Analysis
description: This unit broadly covers topics in Complex Analysis, which is the theory of functions of a complex variable. It has applications in a plethora of areas of science and engineering. Examples include theoretical and applied mathematics (and in particular number theory, statistics and combinatorics), physics (for example quantum mechanics, but also thermodynamics), and mechanical and electrical engineering (signal processing and control theory just to mention two). First, we discover that the set of complex numbers is a natural completion of the set of real numbers. Then, we proceed with the introduction of the fundamental complex elementary functions which generalise well-known functions over subsets of the real line: the complex exponential function, the complex sine/cosine and hyperbolic sine/cosine functions, the principal logarithm, power and exponent functions to name a few. We then introduce the notion of complex analytic function, which plays a central role in Complex Analysis: we will discover new regularity properties of complex analytic functions that have no counterpart in the real case.This unit culminates with the so-called Residue Theory, which gives us exciting new methods of integration which enable us to tackle the calculation of integrals that cannot be handled using the standard techniques developed in other units. A further mathematical tool developed in this unit is the Laplace transform, which has countless applications in all areas involving the solution of linear differential equations. Its role is to reduce a linear differential equation, or a system of linear differential equations, to an algebraic problem.

title: Sustainable Energy Systems Engineering
description: The Sustainable Energy Systems Engineering unit provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the principles and practices involved in designing, implementing, and managing sustainable energy systems. The unit covers a range of technical, economic, environmental, and social topics related to sustainable energy systems. Students learn about renewable and non-renewable energy sources, energy conversion technologies, energy storage, and energy management systems. They also learn about the design and analysis of sustainable energy systems, including energy efficiency and energy management strategies. The course covers energy system modelling and optimisation techniques, life cycle assessment, techno-economic analysis, and system integration. Additionally, the unit explores the challenges associated with integrating renewable energy sources into existing energy grids, such as intermittency, variability, and grid stability. Students learn about policy and regulatory frameworks that impact the deployment of sustainable energy systems, such as renewable energy targets, carbon pricing, and feed-in tariffs. The unit also covers the environmental impacts of energy systems, such as greenhouse gas emissions, air and water pollution, and land use impacts, and strategies to mitigate these impacts.

title: Introduction to Sexology Attitudes and Values
description: This unit is an introduction to sexology; the scholarly study of human sexuality. Students are encouraged to reflect upon and reassess their own beliefs, attitudes and values through the investigation and examination of a diverse range of key sexological concepts and topics. All reflections will be structured through a biopsychosocial approach. Broader societal and cultural issues are discussed. There is an emphasis on sex positivity, optimising sexual health, human rights, equality, and equitable service provision.

title: Astrobiology: Life in the Universe
description: Astrobiology is a multidisciplinary study of the origin, evolution, and distribution of life in the universe. This unit explores: a) the ingredients and conditions for life to emerge on the early Earth through investigations of ancient rock samples, geochemistry and habitats of microbial life and b) the search for life elsewhere in the solar system, and on exoplanets, through astronomical observations and solar system space missions. Laboratory activities include, but are not limited to, hands-on investigation of ancient rock samples and a virtual field trip to search for traces of ancient life and its habitats. The final activity will be group planning for a space mission to search for signs of life on Mars. This is a multidisciplinary STEM unit with opportunities to study individually and in a group through laboratory activities, presentations, and reports.

title: Advanced Wound Care
description: This unit develops advanced understanding of acute and chronic wound healing. Students engage in assessment of the person, their wound and wound healing environment. Application of evidence based goals of care and treatment interventions including pharmacology; use of clinical risk management tools and strategies for wound prevention are covered in this unit. Enhanced clinical decision making skills in the management of surgical and traumatic wound complications, lower leg ulcers, neuro ischaemic foot ulcers, pressure ulcers, non healing wounds, drains and tubes and wound pain Insertion and removal of sutures and staples Debridement methods and rationale for selection Appraisal of cultural diversity and health literacy impacts Optimisation of quality of life and multi disciplinary collaboration outcomes.

title: Digital Illustration Production
description: This unit focuses on the learning of contemporary digital techniques used to execute commercial illustrations. Students are instructed in and study the advanced technical processes used by industry professionals across the illustration industry.

title: Nutrition Professional Practice
description: Nutrition Professional Practice is a capstone unit to prepare final year students to enter the workforce. This unit provides students with fieldwork opportunities through practicum placement or industry and community engagement opportunities in work-based environments. During this fieldwork students will apply nutrition science knowledge and skills to improve food supply and/or human health and wellbeing, in addition to other competencies such as professionalism, teamwork and communication. The unit will focus on cultural competency development including Indigenous Australian culture and/or developing countries. Students will be able to work in a team with an experienced educator in nutrition to gain experience for employment. A major component will be the completion of work-based tasks including a project which will enable students to assess their competency development and achievements.

title: Structural Dynamics
description: This unit explores the dynamic behaviour of single and multi-degree of freedom structures under free and forced vibration modes, and application of the building Codes and Standards for dynamic loads such as earthquake and wind loads. Different types of lateral load resisting structural systems, design considerations for tall structures and approximate analysis for preliminary design are also included.

title: Secondary Professional Experience 3
description: This unit is the third in a sequence of four professional experience units. The unit will support your understanding and application of key education theories, concepts, and skills to develop your professional teaching practice. The professional expereince practical assessment is a 15 day full-time block placement intendend to enable practical application of the knowledge and skills gained, particularly in the PTP3 unit. This unit requires you to demonstrate a higher level of competence and developing mastery of core teaching skills than previous placement assessments. The unit's assessment tasks support your progression towards the requirements for the AfGT.All required clearances to work with children must be obtained and valid, and all other preparation requirements met prior to commencement of Professional Experience placement.

title: Drama Narratives
description: Students will study a variety of drama film styles and narrative screen forms in order to understand and critique a range of creative and filmic approaches to drama production. These investigations will inform the development and production of their own drama screen projects. Students will engage with a variety of technical, operational and aesthetic conventions and practices used in the concept development and production of screen drama.

title: English: The Early Years
description: This is an introductory unit examining the acquisition of language knowledge and skills of young children. The unit addresses the teaching of English across the early years of life and schooling. A specific focus will be placed on understanding the acquisition and interrelationships of language modes – reading, writing, speaking, listening, viewing and creating- and applying metalinguistic terms associated with these modes. Students will learn to design and justify instructional strategies and assessments aligned with curriculum standards (ACARA and ACECQA) for young learners and critically examine and compare theoretical perspectives to inform practical teaching applications. Throughout the unit, emphasis will be placed on assessing young children’s learning using diverse data sources to make valid instructional decisions. This unit aims to prepare educators with a grounding in the knowledge and skills needed to foster contextually and culturally respective inclusive learning environments that honour young children as active, agential learners.

title: Enterprise Architecture
description: This unit examines enterprise technologies in an evolving digital environment to facilitate business transformation. This includes the in-depth analysis of organizational problems and the evaluation of appropriate technologies to address these problems and implement a solution. The subsequent design and embedding of technologies to address appropriate business processes is examined. A particular focus is placed on ensuring enterprise knowledge generation through collaborative participation and sustainable business models enabled by digital technologies. Project planning and professional development to facilitate the implementation of technological solutions to business problems based on new and emerging technologies is considered.

title: Major Project Pre-production
description: This unit builds on previously acquired skills in production and screen studies, deepening application, evaluative and creative practices to select and develop a major screen project ready for production in semester two. Students will demonstrate that they are ready for the major drama, documentary or broadcast project in line with funding applications in industry, developing script, pre-production planning and budget, individual crew portfolio support and a finished pilot scene.

title: Business and Law International Study Abroad 1
description: International mobility experience for undergraduate students.

title: Writing and Communication Skills for Indigenous Australians
description: In this unit, students will develop and apply academic integrity and academic writing and research proficiency to effectively communicate ideas and to avoid plagiarism and academic misconduct. This unit also provides an introduction to, and development of, core skills in communication, critical analysis and reflective practice that are required at a tertiary level.

title: Indigenous Australian Arts
description: Explores Indigenous Visual Arts, Performing Arts, Storytelling and Literature and considers how Indigenous culture is portrayed and represented in both traditional and contemporary settings. Examination of the importance of maintaining traditional knowledge and practices.

title: Introduction to Paramedic Professional Practice
description: This unit will introduce the core principles of law, ethics and professional responsibilities that underpin contemporary patient-centred paramedic practice. Concepts explored will include confidentiality, capacity, consent, medication administration and the role of law in healthcare delivery and regulation. We will also explore professionalisation in paramedicine, as well as the associated concepts of professional culture and professional responsibilities outlined by the Paramedicine Board of Australia. We will examine the role of the paramedic as an allied health professional to contribute to an effective, safe and patient-centred health system.

title: Advanced Medical Microbiology
description: This unit involves the study and discussion of: infectious diseases affecting various body sites and their differential laboratory diagnosis; the pathogenesis and laboratory features of medically significant micro-organisms not discussed in previous units (viruses, fungi, parasites, selected bacteria) and their treatment; re-emerging and newly emerging microbial diseases.

title: Computational Mathematics
description: This unit covers various numerical methods for solving systems of linear equations, systems of nonlinear equations, ordinary differential equations, and partial differential equations.

title: Applied Genetics
description: Applied Genetics is a unit that introduces the field of molecular biology. It is designed to assist in the scientific development of students by transmitting recent innovations of genetic techniques, and how they are applied in agriculture, terrestrial and marine environments. The unit is delivered in three sections. Section 1 covers foundations in the structure and function of DNA/RNA, how it is isolated and sequenced. In Section 2, students will focus on a set of practical and bioinformatics exercises, inclusive of a group assignment and scientific writing, which are relevant to their academic discipline. Section 3 focuses on a 'capstone' essay that requires students to review scientific literature and apply the knowledge and research skills that are delivered throughout the semester. The unit focuses on problem solving and critical thinking - it conveys practical skills in molecular biology and bioinformatics. The aim of this course is to provide students with knowledge of how genetic technologies can be applied in a variety of scientific fields.

title: Social Change in Australian History
description: This unit examines movements for social change in Australia from the 19th century to the present. Students will learn how major phenomena such as war, migration, industrialisation, and political and economic struggles changed Australian society. Students will also gain an understanding of how global developments influenced Australia, as well as Australia’s contribution to social change internationally. From environmental protection to movements for peace, racial equality, women’s suffrage, and LGBTIQ+ rights, this unit looks at processes of change, including the role of contentious politics and responses of the state to a changing Australia. By examining primary sources as well as scholarly analysis of movements for social change, students will learn skills in source analysis and historical interpretation.

title: Advanced Photogrammetry
description: Review of photogrammetric concepts. Close range, airborne and space borne photogrammetric systems. Three dimensional rotations and coordinate transformations. Error sources and correction models. Interior, relative and absolute orientation as well as automatic aero-triangulation. Block adjustment models and the bundle method. Incorporation of geodetic observations and weighted parameters. GPS-assister aero triangulation. Self-calibration. Introduction to image processing and analysis.

title: Advanced Biomedical Science Research Project 2
description: Students will apply foundational research skills to solve a biomedical sciences research question. They will develop competence in undertaking guided independent research, and the evaluation of data in relation to the existing literature. Students will demonstrate and further develop their scientific written and verbal communication skills in both individual and group work. This unit will prepare students for entry into an individual research project.

title: Directing Theatre
description: Students analyse and present the work of major theatre directors and acquire and apply directing skills in a season of public performances.

title: Animation for Virtual Production
description: This unit focuses on developing students' skills and expanding their conceptual approaches in animation via the use of virtual production methods. Virtual production utilises game-engine enabled technologies which allows for a dynamic approach to animation production. In this unit students will learn industry standard workflows for virtual production and relevant techniques to create a compelling animated sequence. Students will utilise best industry practices to refine and develop their conceptual approaches and explore the technical possibilities of virtual production through experimentation.

title: Introduction to 3D Modelling
description: This unit introduces students to the foundations of 3D modelling, texturing and rendering in a digital environment. It enables students to work on a defined multi-phase project that encompasses the conceptual and technical elements that are fundamental to 3D design.

title: Industry Capstone Computing Project
description: This unit augments the project units Capstone Computing Project 1 and 2 when a student or group is working with an industry partner or appropriate external body with a member of staff assigned as their supervisor. This unit is usually taken in the same semester as Capstone Computing Project 2 but in some cases may be taken between Capstone Computing Project 1 and 2. The student works with the partner and is assessed in part by them, with moderation from their supervisor and unit co-ordinator. This unit allows industry projects to take on a scope larger than regular capstone projects, at the request of industry partners.

title: Space Environments and Operations
description: The environment of space, both in orbit and on planetary surfaces imposes challenges for the design and operation of spacecraft. This unit explores and describes the space and planetary environments of the Solar System, and then uses these environments to look at the factors and challenges of operating in space, and some of the practical methods used to successfully explore. This will cover a detailed overview of planetary environmental factors and the conditions in the space environment, such as factors like temperature, radiation etc. This will include the space weather phenomena, describe the origin in the context of the Sun and consider the array of destructive environmental effects the space environment causes on spacecraft, instrumentation and/or planetary bodies. This leads to discussion of practical spacecraft considerations, such as testing, design for redundancy and an analysis of some notable past failures. By looking at example spacecraft that must deal with a wide range of conditions, the learning outcomes will involve a fuller understanding of planetary and space conditions. This subject will extend into human environmental factors and needs for exploration and operations, and the technologies used to allow humans to live in space, and conclude by looking at future programs to return humans to the Moon and possible resource exploitation strategies that might be used.

title: Allied Health Honours Research Project
description: The unit develops students’ advanced technical and cognitive skills to create, plan, execute and evaluate project work and/or piece of research with some independence. Students engage in research, authorship and dissemination through oral and written presentations, evidencing effective clinical and ethical reasoning. The unit facilitates the development of collaborative relationships with industry partners and community stakeholders.

title: Language of Dress
description: The unit involves the examination of garment design and structure within an environmental and cultural context. It investigates the semiotics and language of garment and textiles as a vehicle for the expression of cultural identity. There is specific focus on the development of research and development skills.

title: Clinical Medical Imaging Practice 6
description: This unit provides authentic medical imaging professional practice experience in the clinical setting, at the level appropriate for the competent reflective professional. Students will have the opportunity to reflectively plan for their transition to professional practice.

title: Midwifery Capstone
description: This unit consolidates prior learning within the course as students transition to the role of midwife. It strengthens the conceptual and theoretical knowledge required to provide high quality, comprehensive and safe care underpinned by evidence-based practice. Self care is explored and future aims are based on sustainability and development goals. The unit prepares students for professional registration and students investigate clinical governance, factors influencing patient safety including communication, partnering with consumers, clinical risk management and the quality improvement process.

title: Diverse Abilities and Curriculum Differentiation
description: This unit provides an in-depth examination of the learning characteristics and curriculum differentiation for children with diverse abilities including learning disabilities, emotional and behaviour disorders, intellectual disabilities, attention disorders, sensory impairments, chronic health concerns, speech and language disorders and high ability. Skill is developed in individualizing, modifying and adapting the curriculum according to the different ability levels of children. Differentiating the curriculum occurs by changing: 1) the content of learning, 2) the processes of teaching and learning and 3) the methods of assessing the products of learning. With respect to the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers, this unit focuses most specifically on Standard 1 (know your students and how they learn) and Standard 3 (Plan for and implement effective teaching and learning)

title: Indigenous Australian Research
description: Focuses on the positioning of researchers past and present. Students are required to negotiate and articulate their own position and viewpoint. Examines the historical patterns of research undertaken in Indigenous contexts, and considers the politics and power relations of research.

title: Evidence Informed Medicine Use
description: This unit will focus on preparing students for their pharmacy careers by exploring in-depth the evidence that underpins all facets of medicine use. Learning activities will advance students’ theoretical knowledge of research methodology in medicines development, evaluation and use, and the translation of evidence into practice to address contemporary medicine-related problems. Students will apply skills in searching for evidence, critical evaluation of the literature, data analysis and interpretation and synthesis of information to inform patient-centred clinical decision-making. Applying an evidence-informed approach in situations where quality evidence or consensus are lacking, such as the use of complementary and alternative medicines, will also be addressed. Students will demonstrate effective written and oral communication with academic, clinical and lay audiences and practise working collaboratively in a group setting.

title: Psychology Undergraduate Dissertation Preparation
description: The preparation of a joint group research project. Theoretical input on specific areas of research methodology.

title: Software Engineering Project B
description: Software engineering projects are selected and undertaken in consultation with a member of the academic staff, usually working in a small group in conjunction with an industry partner or client. Projects are related to the design, implementation and testing of computing systems with associated literature reviews. Team-oriented software engineering processes are applied during all phases of the project. Management activities are undertaken and a range of software engineering tools are applied to resolve problems arising during the execution of the software development process.

title: Creative Advertising Studio
description: Introduction to digital audio production for radio advertising concept presentation. Introduction to basic video capture and digital editing for TV advertising concept presentation.

title: European Union Law
description: This unit will provide a perspective on the European Union legal order, the role of European institutions, the sources of law and their impact on national legal orders. In addition, the unit deals with judicial review as practised by the European Court of Justice (ECJ), the economic and historical origins of the European Union and the developing case law on social, economic and constitutional matters. Furthermore, insights to substantial EU law will be given, having Competition Law and State Aid Law in the focus.

title: Nutritional Epidemiology
description: Exploration of nutritional epidemiological principles relating to dietary assessment, study design and data analysis associated with disease incidence, prevalence and risk. Assessment of the nutritional epidemiological data for disease patterns and its relationship with public health recommendations for chronic disease prevention.

title: Population Genetics and Molecular Evolution
description: This unit focuses on the following topics: analysis of evolutionary processes, selection, mutation, migration and molecular aspects of evolution. Gene flow in populations and introductory population genetics. Applications of population and molecular genetics to human identification by DNA profiling and diagnosis of some inherited disorders.

title: The Science of Climate Change
description: Climate change is the biggest global challenge facing the world today, affecting both natural processes and the sustainability of human communities. From the weather experienced, through to food and water security, health, settlement viability, and the sustainability of our surrounding ecosystems, Earth’s climate system influences every aspect of our existence and environment. This unit will equip students from any academic area with a robust understanding of the science underpinning climate change. Students will start by learning the basic principles of how different parts of earth’s climate system work, and then go on to explore more specialised topics. These include how we understand past climates and use these to predict future changes and how we measure climate change in different systems. The unit supports students in understanding how science exists in a social and ethical context, including the disproportionate impact of climate change on Indigenous communities, and the importance of Indigenous perspectives and knowledge in monitoring and mitigation. Students will also explore issues around the use of data, science communication, and misinformation, growing their skills as ethical and critical thinkers.

title: Photography Professional Practices 2
description: This unit enables students to identify and investigate the particular mode of photographic practice that they may wish to pursue professionally.  Students are required create a body of work that demonstrates their technical and conceptual skills within that mode thereby enabling transfer of that practice to professional industry environments.  Students will produce work that conceptually and technically satisfies existing professional photographic practices or moves beyond them by creating original work through applied investigation and research. The methodology underpinning this research is designed to introduce students to the conventions of post-graduate study. Throughout the semester this broad goal is supported through dedicated seminars and workshops whilst still allowing for individual conceptual and technical investigations to be undertaken.

title: Behaviour Change for Exercise and Health
description: In this unit, students will learn about key principles, strategies, and frameworks of behaviour change and examine their application within exercise and health contexts. The knowledge and experience gained through this unit will enable students to develop, implement, and evaluate theory-informed and evidenced-based behaviour change interventions for exercise and health.

title: Foundational Geophysics
description: Industrial applications of Geophysical methods span the search and development of energy sources, exploration for strategic minerals, delineation of groundwater resources, and subsurface characterization for environmental and engineering projects. Pure research in geophysics helps use to image and understanding the deep interior structure of our earth and our nearest celestial neighbours. This unit systematically provides the foundational understanding of all core methods used in geophysics including seismic, gravity, magnetics, electromagnetics and radiometric. Students will work through practical application of each of the methods in a range of settings.

title: Foundations of Medical Science
description: In this unit students will be introduced to and begin to develop competencies in core aspects of Medical Science. The unit will encompass three modules: Professional Development, Molecular Pathology and Analytical Techniques.

title: Finance for Positive Futures
description: This unit provides opportunities to recognise this unique time's financial challenges and to take advantage of the opportunities that knowledge of financial systems offers Australian individuals, families and communities. This knowledge can foster the development of skills that can enable participants to flourish financially.

title: Teaching in Regional and Remote Schools
description: Investigation of cultural, professional and social complexities of teaching in regional and remote school environments. Impact of school demographics on teaching and learning. Resource and professional support in regional and remote schools.

title: Media and Indigenous Australian Issues
description: Examines the role of the mass media in producing public ideas about Indigenous Australians, and the important role of Indigenous media services in providing a 'voice' for Indigenous Australians. This unit also critiques journalistic practice and enables students to determine strategies for their own best practice in working with Indigenous people, and representing Indigenous issues and culture.

title: Professional Writing Placement and Project
description: This unit provides students with the opportunity to refine their professional writing skills on real-world projects. Students will either undertake a work placement in an approved public or private sector workplace, or they will work independently on a real-world project sourced by the Unit Coordinator. The unit requires students to communicate with their peers regarding their progress and lessons learned. Assessment and supervision will be provided by academic and workplace supervisors. Students will also develop professional documents to establish their professional persona or brand, such as a LinkedIn profile or an online portfolio of their own writing.

title: Critical Approaches to Research Literature
description: Aims to equip students with the knowledge, skills and understanding to review and critique literature and to locate their research within appropriate academic discourses. Equips students to be aware of, and knowledgeable about, current theoretical approaches applicable to their proposed research. Students are especially encouraged to seek out and give primacy to Indigenous literature relevant to their topic.

title: Drawing
description: In this unit you will explore drawing through investigation of the elements and principles of the visual language of drawing. You are encouraged to develop the formal, conceptual, experimental and expressive use of this language. Through set projects you will examine the effectiveness of various visual solutions by testing possibilities and experimenting with a range of appropriate media.

title: Preventing Non-Communicable Diseases
description: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are a major challenge for global health (e.g. cancer, cardiovascular disease, diabetes). The unit provides an examination of the rationale for a public health approach to the prevention of NCDs. Epidemiology, determinants, global trends, costs, politics, partnerships and interventions will be explored. Contemporary health promotion frameworks and strategies for examining NCDs will be presented. Priority-populations with specific needs and specific settings for interventions will be examined.

title: Scientific Data Analysis
description: Introduction to data analysis. Smoothing, frequency response. Convolution and correlation. Fourier analysis. Discrete Fourier Transforms (DFT). Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). Digital filters.

title: Curriculum and Instruction Senior Secondary: The Arts
description: This unit is designed to prepare pre-service teachers to teach the Senior Secondary Arts curriculum. The focus of the unit is on curriculum planning, teaching strategies, assessment, reporting, the demonstration of positive impact on student learning and research relating to Senior Secondary Arts. The unit examines moderation, the provision of feedback and responding to individual student needs.

title: Advertising Design 2
description: An introductory exploration into the design of brand and marketing communication (advertising design). The unit addresses basic marketing principles, media strategies and the development of advertising concepts and communication design.

title: Electromagnetism
description: This is a second year level unit for students who have previously undertaken the introductory electricity and magnetism unit (PHYS2003: Classical Mechanics and Electromagnetism, or any previous version) and have a satisfactory background in mathematics (MATH2009 Advanced Calculus, or any previous version). The unit begins with a review of the mathematical methods germane to classical electrodynamics: vector analysis, and differential and integral calculus in curvilinear co-ordinates. This is followed by the study of static electric fields (including the laws of Coulomb and Gauss), calculation of the electric potential, and capacitance. Laplace’s equation, and the method of images are introduced as a means to solve problems in electrostatics. The course then covers static magnetic fields, including the Biot-Savart and Ampère’s law, the magnetic vector potential, and multipole expansions of the electric and magnetic field. The course treats the electric and magnetic fields in matter. The final component of the course covers electrodynamics and relativity, Faraday’s law and inductance, Maxwell's equations, electrodynamic conservation laws, and electromagnetic waves. The laboratory sessions provide students with an advanced laboratory experience, and further enhance analytical, and report writing skills.

title: Garment and The Body
description: This unit provides an introduction to the relationships between cloth, garment and the body. This study is supported through the development of skills in garment construction and pattern making that are applied in conjunction with the principles of design examined in design foundation studies.

title: Public Health Nutrition
description: In this unit, students examine the dietary requirements for target groups across the lifecycle and identify population recommendations for public health nutrition. They analyse barriers and enablers to nutrition compliance and explore public health nutrition program applications across a socio-ecological perspective.

title: Fine Art Studio Materials
description: This unit will introduce you to visual art specialisations through a number of thematically-based projects. In this unit you will be encouraged to explore ideas through material exploration and inquiry. You will be exposed to a variety of disciplines to develop your understanding of contemporary art practice.

title: Health Assessment for the Clinician
description: This unit will provide culturally safe and contextually appropriate physical and psychosocial health assessment across the adult lifespan.  It will include interview techniques, health history and physical assessment using a systematic and holistic approach.  Students will develop clinical reasoning, and the ability to understand and interpret the health assessment in order to lead, manage care, document, communicate and collaborate with the interprofessional health care team.

title: Foundations of Strategic Studies
description: This unit introduces students to the key concepts and debates regarding the importance of the military factor in contemporary International Relations; the fundamentals of strategic behaviour of states as international actors; and foundations of contemporary strategy. Students will also familiarise themselves with basic principles of geographical dimensions of strategy, and current and emerging challenges of contemporary strategy.

title: Introduction to Creative Arts
description: This unit introduces students to the ways creative practitioners engage with and contribute to the world. In this unit, students will research and apply skills required to develop a creative practice. Students will expand on a personal perspective and develop methods of communication appropriate to Creative Arts. Students will research trends and opportunities in creative industries and determine which skills can be developed to be a successful creative practitioner.

title: Industrial and Systems Engineering Research Project 2
description: Students undertake a significant research project that either develops new knowledge or addresses an industrial and systems engineering problem of interest. Students are free to choose from a range of projects offered by the faculty members as well as by external partners. The theory units that they learn in the classroom provide them with existing knowledge in the field whereas the undergraduate project provides them with an opportunity to demonstrate their inventiveness, degree of effort and self-management skills. In this unit students will: carry out and complete the research project planned and commenced in Industrial and Systems Engineering Research Project 1. Projects involve the application of engineering research methodologies, including analytical, numerical or experimental investigation or design, which is carried out over a period of one year. The students submit their project work in the form of an undergraduate thesis at the end of 2 consecutive semesters, and deliver their research findings in an oral form to their peers and staff in a project research seminar.

title: Introduction to Public Relations and Strategic Communication
description: This unit explores the foundations of public relations and strategic communication across multiple settings and industries.Learners will gain a hands-on understanding of what PR is and what it’s not, enabling them to apply knowledge contextually through industry focussed case studies and a mock press conference.

title: Habitat and Landform Mapping
description: ERTH3000 Habitat and Landform Mapping is a practical, skills based class in which students use geospatial technology along side terrestrial and marine survey techniques to interprete and reconstruct land and seascapes, as well as map terrestrial and marine environments to detect environmental change. Students will examine ways in which spatial patterns can be visualised using cartographic and GIS tools, to then explain the relationships between geology, geomprphology, habitats and communities, on both temporal and spatial scales. The practical component will include GPS field mapping, air photo analysis of marine and terrestrial landforms and associated habitats. Students will become proficient cartographic and spatial data analysis though the use of ArcMap Software.

title: Pharmacology of Antimicrobial Agents
description: This unit communicates the principles of antimicrobial action and treatment, its place in medicine, with considerations relevant to effective antimicrobial agent use and mechanisms of antimicrobial resistance. Students investigate mechanisms of action, spectrum, pharmacokinetics, adverse reactions and drug interactions of antimicrobial agents. The unit introduces students to the scope of antimicrobial chemotherapy and considers antimicrobial treatment to a range of local and globally relevant infections. Core unit concepts include classification of antibiotics, their drug action and principles of selective toxicity.

title: Law and Technology
description: Technology is increasingly impacting the work of lawyers and judges, amongst other professional industries. This unit introduces students to the interaction between law and technology. Topic coverage in the unit will vary from year-to-year, as will the specific technologies that students will have the opportunity to work with. Possible topics include, for example, artificial intelligence, eCommerce and blockchain, cybercrime, information governance and cybersecurity, human rights and ethics, and technology in legal practice. Students will have the opportunity to engage with one or more forms of legal technology in a hands-on environment and to think critically and reflect upon the way in which technology is likely to impact upon their personal and professional lives.

title: Art Direction in Design and Advertising
description: Through a series of practical design projects, students will develop the skills necessary to craft meaningful and persuasive visual narratives within a Communication Design context.

title: Data Science in Practice
description: This unit will provide a broad introduction to four key aspects of data science: data retrieval and manipulation, data visualisation, statistical computation and machine learning, and presentation and communication. Students will use data from a variety of sources, be introduced to contemporary computing and database environments such as R and SQL, and be exposed to case studies from outside the classroom. Through this unit students will become acquainted with the challenges of contemporary data science and gain an appreciation of the foundational skills necessary to turn data into information.

title: Photography Contexts and Practice
description: An introduction to theory and practice of contemporary photography which will equip students with an understanding of applied photographic production, the function of photography in the cultural realm and associated critical theory. Students will be required to develop photographic works that demonstrate a clear and disciplined engagement with the practical, aesthetical and theoretical imperatives of the photographic medium.

title: Human Reproductive Science
description: This unit will explore human reproductive anatomy, physiology and histology. Students will be introduced to modern contraceptive methods, pregnancy and early human development, birth and lactation, and reproductive pathologies. Assisted reproductive technology (ART) and its associated ethics, will be explored in detail, with an industry site visit. Students will be required to research and communicate their findings on a contemporary topic in human reproductive health.

title: Mine Economics
description: In this unit students will be introduced to the fundamentals of mining economics, including project evaluation and economic decision- making techniques used in the mining industry. Students will study mineral and energy markets and the concept of supply and demand. They will also learn about approaches to quantifying economic risk components associated with mining, such as financial and technical uncertainty and environmental and social risks. Students will develop their knowledge and skills in estimating the full cost of capital and operating expenditure associated with developing, operating and closing a mine. They will learn how to use discounted cash flow and real option analysis methods as tools to adapt and revise economic valuations of mining projects under uncertain and fluctuating conditions.

title: Introduction to Business Law
description: In this unit, students will be introduced to the nature and sources of law and regulation in Australia connected to business. Key aspects of Australian business law and their engagement with and influences on business operations are explored. Students will solve introductory legal concepts centred on business operations and their interrelationship and influences on society including in the finance and insurance domains.

title: Space Systems Design
description: This unit provides students with a comprehensive high-level understanding of the aspects of a successful space mission and the skills required to design practical space systems. The unit covers mission design and mission architecture, basic spacecraft dynamics and orbital mechanics, the space environment, design of spacecraft systems, communications, sensors and payloads, verification and testing, industry requirements, launch, ground segment and mission operations. Students will develop their practical skills by designing, modelling and evaluating realistic space missions and systems.

title: Tort Liability for Business
description: Business organisations are faced with exposure to liability in tort in a number of ways. A small accountancy may be exposed to liability for professional negligence or negligent misstatement. A public relations consultancy or company with an active Facebook presence may be exposed to liability for defamation. Organisations of all sizes may face risks such as those relating to occupiers’ liability, the general law of negligence and a range of other torts. Tort Liability for Business equips business students with a practical understanding tort liability generally, as well as an examination of several torts with relevance to business organisations. The unit considers how potential exposure to liability can inform strategies designed to reduce, mitigate and indemnifying against such risk exposure. This practical and focused approach to select legal doctrines seeks to enhance students’ entrepreneurial mindset and further equip their career-capable toolkit. In addition, the unit develops students’ capacity as effective communicators.

title: Building Dissertation 1
description: In this unit, students will explore the research process applying critical thinking in research. Students will develop a research proposal and, literature review, demonstrating reasoning in research. Students will apply relevant research methods in the management and analysis of research data.

title: Health, Safety and Quality in the Built Environment
