description: This unit examines the importance of Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) and quality practices in the Australian construction industry and internationally, with a focus on quality assurance throughout all project phases, from conceptualisation to handover to the clients. Principles of implementing and applying best practice will be discussed in relation to global quality management theories in conjunction with real-world corporate and project case studies. The complex relationships between quality and the various aspects of design and construction activities will also be discussed. The risks associated with various construction methodologies will be reviewed to identify key considerations for the selection and implementation of appropriate environmental health and safety practices on construction sites.

title: Social Impact of Economic Changes in China and Japan
description: A comparative perspective on economic growth and social transformation is offered in this unit, with special emphasis on China and Japan. The unit explains the diverse paths of Asian countries to modernity, and topics include: Asian perspectives of economic development, state-led market economies, state power and political cultures, civil society and government policies, sustainable development and social movements, public opinion in environmental debates, historical issues and regional tension in Asia; the impact of nationalism, regionalism and globalisation on inter-state conflict; and regional integration in the Asian 21st century.

title: Environmental and Building Systems in Architecture
description: This unit explores the complexities of effective system integration within the built environment. Acoustic, lighting, electrical, hydraulic and mechanical systems are given particular focus and these are investigated through researching and analysing case studies, and observations of construction and detailing in a local context. Students will begin to interrogate the role of a designer as part of a network of professional consultants. Net zero considerations form part of this unit. Work integrated learning is incorporated through understanding the role of consultants.

title: Introduction to Astronomy
description: Introduction to Astronomy offers an introduction to the study of the Universe. We explain scientific method and how it has been applied to determine the structure and composition of celestial objects. The tools of modern astronomy are introduced (with an emphasis on optical telescopes). The unit also looks at star clusters and galaxies, leading into discussion of the evolution of stars and the Universe as a whole.

title: Sustainable Construction Practices in Building and Infrastructure
description: This unit discusses the impact of construction activities on the environment, society and the economy and how sustainable development affects the way the construction industry operates. Students will investigate construction practices in building and infrastructure projects, and develop strategies to address key sustainability issues.

title: Cost Management
description: In this unit, students will apply advanced processes and techniques for cost management including the techniques of cost modelling, composite rate, life cycle costing, value engineering and value management. The unit extends from the principles of estimating and cost planning for developing a more accurate or reliable cost plan.

title: Synthetic Methods in Chemistry
description: Advance organic synthesis: Retrosynthetic analysis, oxidation and reduction reactions, protecting groups, pericyclic reactions, carbanion chemistry, transition-metal catalysed reactions (including cross-coupling and olefin metathesis), advanced NMR techniques. Polymer chemistry: Synthesis and characterisation techniques as applied to polymer science.

title: Advanced Biological Chemistry
description: Enzymatic and receptor assays are an essential part of medical diagnosis, drug discovery and the biological sciences more broadly. This is a laboratory-focused unit, in which students will design an enzymatic assay and develop appropriate inhibitors. The key topics covered in this unit are: Advanced peptide chemistry; The use of absorbance and fluorescence in assays; Practical enzyme kinetics; Inhibitor modes of action and kinetics; Visualisation ligand-protein binding; and Inhibition assays. The laboratory will consist of both individual work and team experiments.

title: Bioanalytical and Biophysical Chemistry
description: This unit will consider experimental and computational approaches in the study of biomolecular systems. Computational biochemistry will introduce computational approaches to understanding of biomolecular structure and function, whilst bioelectrochemistry will discuss the experimental approaches used to study and harness biological electron transfer reactions for disease management and bio-energy conversion. Finally, biospectroscopy will consider the applications of spectroscopic techniques to determine the biological chemistry of disease, as a route to more effective disease therapies or diagnostic methods

title: Advanced Topics in Chemistry
description: Advanced topics in chemistry will be studied to illustrate how fundamental aspects of chemistry underpin the cutting edge of knowledge and research in a wide range of scientific disciplines and applications. Methods that can be used to communicate advanced chemical concepts will be discussed and implemented.

title: Analytical Chemistry and Spectroscopy
description: Theory and application of analytical techniques for structural characterisation. These could include, mass spectrometry (GC-MS, LC-MS, ICP-MS, MS-MS), electroanalytical techniques, molecular spectroscopy. The techniques will be chosen to reflect the cutting edge developments and current industry demand.

title: Chemistry Research Project
description: This unit provides a comprehensive understanding of best laboratory practices, including occupational health and safety (OH&S), risk assessments, chemical storage and disposal, NATA and ISO standards compliance, and ethics in science. Students will learn research methodology, review the research process, construct literature reviews using computer-based tools, and critically analyse research papers. Students will also conduct systematic independent investigations, interpret results in the context of previous studies, and effectively communicate research findings through a scientific report and presentation.

title: Predictive Analytics Principles
description: Predictive modelling and analytics uses historical data to capture relationships between predictors and explanatory variables and exploits them to predict future outcomes. It is widely used by actuaries in insurance and many other risk management applications. This unit will introduce students to the theory and practice of contemporary statistical and machine learning methods with a focus on actuarial applications. In addition to modelling students will learn about the importance of the business context, data cleaning and wrangling, model checking and evaluation, and effective and appropriate verbal and written communication of results.  Students will carry out analyses using open source software such as the R language environment for statistical computing.

title: Foundations of Digital Design
description: This unit focuses on digital design and computer architecture. It provides grounding on the foundations of digital logic design from the perspective of a Microprocessor without Interlocked Pipeline Storage (MIPS) processor architecture. Basic techniques on Boolean algebra and minimisation are covered to design combinational circuits and sequential systems which are building blocks to a MIPS. Using Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools and Very High Speed Integrated Circuit Hardware Description Language (VHDL) and examining assembly programs, students will be able to gain further understanding in the complex world of computer architecture design.

title: Cognition
description: Examination of human cognitive processes from neuropsychological and behavioural perspectives with a particular emphasis on memory and language. Other topics include imagery, capacity limitations in mental functioning, and the cognitive neuroscience of higher mental functions.

title: Advanced Topics in Chemical Analysis and Spectroscopy
description: This unit will impart skills in independent manipulation of techniques in chemical synthesis, analysis, and computation.  Students will solve a problem, first using practical techniques of relevance to the task, and then interpreting the outcome using computational techniques.  To achieve these goals, students will be inducted into research laboratory practices by applying electronic notekeeping and appropriate occupational health and safety procedures.

title: Architecture Design Studio 2B - Regional Studio
description: This unit investigates the impact of the physical, cultural and social context of a regional community on the design of a building and building groups. The design proposition is a medium scale public building in established regional settlements which provides students with an opportunity to understand local regions, their histories and to explore their potential futures. Work integrated learning is incorporated through exploring a range of complex social, regional and environmental factors in the production of architecture.

title: Hardware Fundamentals
description: This unit focuses on computer hardware and architecture. It provides grounding on the hardware fundamentals of digital logic design from the perspective of a Microprocessor without Interlocked Pipeline Storage (MIPS) processor architecture. Basic techniques on Boolean algebra and minimisation are covered to design combinational circuits and sequential systems which are building blocks to a MIPS. Using Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools and examining assembly language, students will be able to gain further understanding of complex computer architectures.

title: Architecture and Interior Architecture Methods 1B - Digital Literacy
description: This unit develops an understanding of architectural design processes through an introduction to 2D CAD and architectural drawing conventions and visual literacy. Modelling, diagramming, digital collage and photography will be used for 2D and 3D architectural representation and visual communication of space, form, structure and material.

title: Pharmaceutical Chemistry
description: This unit provides an introduction to core concepts within pharmaceutical chemistry. Students will be introduced to various laboratory techniques used for drug formulation analysis and learn about a range of physio-chemical properties of drugs which influence their pharmaceutical formulation, pharmacology and clinical use. This unit is divided into two learning modules. Module 1: Analysis of drug formulations via titrimetric, spectrophotometric and chromatographic methods. Module 2: Key functional groups in drugs, drug ionisation, drug solubility, drug stereochemistry, drug stability.

title: Psychological Science Experimental Methods
description: Experimental and quasi-experimental design and data analysis in psychology and human communication science.

title: Computer Project 1
description: The supervisor acts in the role of client. The student must gather requirements for the software project, decide upon appropriate software engineering processes, describe these in a project proposal and then follow the processes in designing, implementing and testing the software under design. Finally the student must describe the results of their efforts in a final project report.

title: Theoretical Foundations of Computer Science
description: Automata theory: deterministic and non-deterministic automata and conversions. Grammars: context free grammars, languages for grammars and Parse trees. Turing machines and abstractions of RAM. Decidability, reducibility P and PN classes. Time and spare complexity. NP completeness.

title: Intelligent Agents
description: This unit introduces intelligent agents and the artificial intelligence problems and approaches relating to them. Learners will become familiar with the modelling of autonomous agents, methods for programming agent behaviour as well as the basics of planning. This involves introducing a range of algorithms and logical processes which underlie agent behaviour. This unit introduces the need for machine learning in certain types of agents and introduces the logic involved but does not discuss details of machine learning techniques.

title: Programming Languages
description: Programming languages and focuses on the key design issues of various language constructs by analysing the design choices for these constructs in the context of several commonly used programming languages, and by comparing the design alternatives. The course has four major components. It starts by covering the procedural paradigm and basic compiler design while introducing a fundamental set of programming language design principles. The next two components cover scripting languages as well as the functional, logic paradigms. The final component of the course covers the object oriented paradigm which is currently the most popular programming paradigm.

title: App Development for the Apple Ecosystem
description: In this unit, you will evaluate and understand the tools, techniques and concepts needed to design, develop, build and test applications for the Apple Ecosystem (iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS and tvOS). You will be introduced to app development principles and practices applied to the design, implementation and evaluation of apps. This will entail learning the basics of the Swift programming language and learning how to utilise the Apple developer tools. This will be leveraged to build AR apps and to integrate web content into your apps in various ways.

title: Building Surveying
description: This unit is an introduction to Australia’s Building Control System including: the functions of the WA Building Commission; the role of Permit Authorities; planning legislation interaction with Building Construction; final commissioning of major projects from a regulatory perspective; sustainability and modern Building Control legislation and access for people with disabilities in current Codes.

title: Computer Technology Project 2
description: Writing of a thesis communicating the work done in CMPE3002 Computer Technology Project 1.

title: Plant Diversity and Adaptation
description: This unit explores the taxonomic and functional biodiversity of Australian vascular and non-vascular plants. It emphasises the interpretation of plant traits within ecological and evolutionary contexts, including adaptations related to fire, pollination, seed dispersal, and nutrient acquisition. Students will examine plant evolution and major lineages, with a focus on structural and functional changes across key groups. Skill development includes field-based botanical survey techniques and laboratory-based identification of plant taxa using morphological traits and taxonomic keys.

title: Principles and Processes in Chemistry
description: This unit is designed for students who have passed WACE Chemistry 3A/3B or equivalent. Students who have not previously studied chemistry should take CHEM1003 Introduction to Chemistry. An exploration of the historical pattern of thought will illustrate that chemistry is both testable and contestable and that theories may be limited by or to certain conditions. Physical and chemical properties of molecules will illustrate how a fundamental understanding of atomic and bonding theory can explain macroscopic observations. Energy is the interconvertible capacity to do work, however not all energy can be converted into work and is usually transferred in the form of heat. Heat transfer can be measured in some reactions to predict the heat transfer in other reactions. The principles of thermodynamics can assist in predicting outcome of reversible and irreversible chemical reactions. Electrochemical processes can be utilised to provide energy in the form of electricity without many of the limitations of other energy production systems. The principles of stoichiometry along with the purpose and limitations of chemical measurement will be explored by highlighting their role in everyday life and the breadth of techniques, methodologies and instruments available to perform analyses of relevant species.

title: Introduction to Actuarial Science
description: This unit provides an overview of the work of actuaries in the financial services sector. Students will gain a broad understanding of the context in which the key industries of insurance, superannuation and banking operate (e.g. the regulatory, taxation and public policy environment) and the types of products sold. The fundamental concepts of pricing uncertain events and risk management will be introduced and the role which actuaries play discussed using relevant industry and government examples.  Guest speakers will discuss their experiences and provide insight to industry practice.

title: Writing for Children
description: An advanced, special topic in writing for children leading to the production of marketable concepts for works of children's literature.

title: Writing Genre Fiction
description: An intermediate unit in theory and practice of writing short prose fiction. The particular genres studied depend on availability of staff. Emphasis on critical workshop discussion leading to completed examples of the student's own work

title: Experimental Writing
description: An intermediate unit in the theory and practice of creative writing with a particular emphasis on contemporary avant-garde poetics and other experimental forms.

title: Travel Writing
description: This unit concentrates on contemporary travel writing in the short story/feature/essay form and has instructional value for both creative and professional writing students.

title: Creative Writing
description: An introductory creative writing unit leading to completed examples of the student's own prose, poetry and writing for performance.

title: Writing Poetry
description: An intermediate unit on the theory and practice of writing poetry. An appreciation of language through textual consideration and the practice of creative writing, including drafting and editing.

title: Programming Design and Implementation
description: Students will be introduced to the Linux operating system and programming environment. They will then learn how to design software in pseudocode, and implement their designs in the Java programming language. Topics covered include: compiling and executing a Java program; primitive and reference data types; numeric expressions; the principles behind programming control structures and their implementation in Java; the design and implementation of sub-modules; file input and output; and searching and sorting. The unit also includes applications to real-world problems and number systems.

title: Writing Short Fiction
description: An intermediate unit in the theory and practice of writing short prose fiction. Emphasis on critical workshop discussion leading to completed examples of the students own work. The curriculum further encourages an appreciation of language through textual consideration and the practice of creative writing, including drafting and editing.

title: Hydraulic Engineering and Flood Control
description: Advanced levels of civil engineering hydraulics and hydrology will be presented in this unit. The hydraulic principles related to hydraulic structures (dams, weirs, spillways, culverts, stilling basins), sediment transport, groundwater and hydraulic equipment will be presented. The techniques, methods and policies behind planning, design, operation and maintenance of water distribution and wastewater collection networks will be applied and evaluated. Computational fluid dynamics, river and reservoir routing and flood routing will be covered.

title: Civil and Construction Engineering Research Project 2
description: This unit allows students to synthesise their learning across the engineering program by undertaking a major and authentic engineering project activity. The activity requires students to plan, execute, complete and present project work- a piece of research and scholarship with some independence, guided by a supervisor. Students will draw on technical knowledge and skills, problem solving capabilities, design skills, research skills and generic skills developed during the course of their engineering studies.

title: Civil and Construction Engineering Research Project 1
description: This unit allows students to synthesise their learning across the engineering program by undertaking a major and authentic engineering project activity. The project requires students to plan and execute project work - a piece of research and scholarship with some independence, guided by a supervisor. Students will draw on technical knowledge and skills, problem solving capabilities, design skills, research skills, and generic skills developed during the course of their engineering studies.

title: Advanced Molecular Biology
description: This unit builds on the foundations of biochemistry and molecular biology taught in second year and reflects a rapidly developing area of science which is at the crossroads of the biological, computational and chemical sciences. It has a strong focus on developing students' practical and analytical skills and for them to experience applications of selected bioinformatics tools

title: Creative Writing Supervised Project
description: Extended, advanced study in a selected genre or individual project under the supervision of a lecturer. Applications to enrol in this unit, when pre-requisites have not been met, will be considered by the Unit Coordinator.

title: Water and Environmental Resources
description: This unit introduces the key concepts and methods that are needed by Civil Engineers to understand, evaluate and analyse engineering activity in water and environmental development. Students will learn the key concepts and measures of water quality; as well as treatment methods for both water and wastewater. Basic design and evaluation of the principles of conventional water and wastewater treatment recycling and re-use will be addressed, as well as emerging trends. Current legislation and best management practices regarding water, air quality, biodiversity and other aspects of the local environment will be discussed. Students will learn to identify, select and evaluate key environmental methods and best practices that lead towards more sustainable engineering actions.

title: Civil Engineering Construction Materials
description: Properties, production, durability and sustainability of conventional and emerging Civil Engineering materials will be examined. Construction materials such as conventional concrete, special concrete (e.g.: low carbon concrete which utilise industrial by-products and recycled materials, fibre reinforced concrete, self-compacting concrete and 3D printed concrete), steel, timber, masonry, asphalt, geotextiles and bio-based materials will be investigated.

title: Teaching About Sacraments in Catholic Schools
description: This unit explores the signs, symbols and rituals of key sacred liturgies within the Catholic tradition and their scriptural and historical origins. Participants are to understand the significance of the sacraments and liturgies to Christian life, especially the celebration of the Mass and how this is applied through the Perth Archdiocesan Religious Education Units of Work to the life experience of students within Catholic school settings. The unit provides opportunities for participants to reflect critically on the personal and professional readiness of staff to be supportive of or teach sacraments and liturgies in Catholic schools.

title: Reinforced Concrete Design
description: The principles underpinning the Australian concrete structures design code are examined and utilised in the design of reinforced concrete beams, slabs and columns. Flexural Theory is introduced for the design of singly reinforced concrete beams, doubly reinforced concrete beams, T beams, continuous beams and slabs. Further, shear and torsion, bond and anchorage, serviceability including deflection and detailing for reinforced concrete beams, slabs and columns are considered.

title: Structural Actions and Steel Design
description: Students are introduced to structural design by considering broad design concepts and the utilisation of a limits states approach in design codes of practice. Structural design actions and limit state load combinations are determined using the Australian structural design actions codes of practice, and applied to design scenarios. The principles underpinning the Australian steel structures design code are examined and utilised in the design of structural steel elements subject to tension, compression, bending and combined actions, connection of steel elements, member restraints, structural bracing and steel member fatigue. Steel Design Capacity Tables are introduced.

title: Civil Engineering Practices, Quality and Legislation
description: This unit provides an introduction to contractual procedures as well as laying out the fundamentals of contract law and standard construction contracts. General conditions of contract for civil engineering and construction works (particularly AS21241 AS4000) are examined, highlighting variation and claims procedures in construction projects, alongside an exploration of environmental legislation and indigenous/heritage-aware applications, to build-in professional responsibility and negligence. Recognition that standard-methods of mensuration and specifying civil engineering components must compliment quality management systems (namely IS09000 and ISO9001 and associated requirements) for civil engineering organisations, in conjunction with the tools and techniques of continuous improvement, alongside EPEP finalisation if/as necessary.

title: Internet of Things Design and Communications
description: There are two main sections in this unit. In the first section, infrastructure and Ad Hoc wireless network is explained including Wireless Local Area Network (LAN) setup & troubleshooting, IEEE 802.11 technologies, Radio Technologies, Wireless LAN applications and resilient products. Also by completing the first section student will learn how to design, install, configure and troubleshoot Wireless LAN using the current technologies as part of laboratory activity.The second section focuses on the rapidly developing “Internet of Things” (IoT). This covers the protocol and technologies used in IoT system design and explains the Wireless Sensor Network (WSN).

title: Teaching About the Gospels in Catholic Schools
description: This unit explores the key structures and literary genres of the four Gospels as understood within the Catholic Church tradition. Participants are to understand how the Gospel writers wanted to convey Jesus’ message of the Christian ‘Way, Truth and Life’ and how this message is applied through the Perth Archdiocesan Religious Education Units of Work to the life experience of students within Catholic school settings. The course provides opportunities for participants to reflect critically on the personal and professional readiness of staff to be supportive of or about how to promote Gospel values in Catholic schools.

title: Hydraulics and Hydrology
description: This unit covers two main sections in Water Engineering; hydraulics and hydrology. Hydraulics part provides principles of hydraulic pumps and open channel flow and their applications in civil engineering. Hydraulic pumps introduces civil engineering applications of hydraulic pumps including efficiency of hydraulic pumps, pumps and pipeline systems, operation of multiple pumps, pump characteristics and pump laws. Open channel flow introduces basic concepts of open channels flow, such as energy and critical flow, flow transition, uniform and non-uniform flow, and hydraulic jump. Hydrology part covers the basic theories and applications of surface water hydrology and ground water hydrology. Analysis of main components of hydrological cycle (precipitation, evapotranspiration, infiltration, runoff, and groundwater) and techniques for hydrological assessments such as hydrographs, frequency analysis and urban hydrology will be introduced.

title: Teaching About Jesus in Catholic Schools
description: This unit explores the nature of the person of Jesus and his core gospel teachings as understood within the Catholic Church tradition. Participants are to understand Jesus’ mission to proclaim the ‘good news’ of the kingdom of God and how this news is applied through the Perth Archdiocesan Religious Education Units of Work to the life experience of students within Catholic school settings. The course provides opportunities for participants to reflect critically on the personal and professional readiness of staff to be supportive of or teach Jesus’ gospel message in Catholic schools.

title: Integrated Pest Management
description: Integrated Pest Management will introduce students to key pest management concepts in different scenarios. Topics to be covered include the concept of plant pathology and the importance of integrated management of diseases, factors influencing disease development, economic constraints in disease management, traditional and molecular diagnosis methods, disease development in complex pathogen populations, principles of plant disease control and pesticide-resistance management strategies.

title: Advanced Chinese: Engagement with the Chinese Community
description: This unit aims to develop a high level of competence that enables advanced students to communicate with explicit knowledge of Chinese society and culture. The unit further develops students' language skills through close reading of non-authentic and authentic texts in Chinese language. These skills will be demonstrated by the application of complex vocabulary and grammatical techniques. A systematic examination of cultural practices and social etiquette will enable effective communication with Chinese speakers.

title: Process Synthesis and Design
description: Process Synthesis and Design integrates knowledge and skills from some previous chemical engineering units for the purpose of synthesising chemical processes. The skill of simulating those processes through the use of chemical process simulators is taught in parallel. Applications and case studies are drawn from the general chemical, hydrocarbon and mineral processing industries. The main process synthesis topics covered include the systematic consideration of process alternatives; reactor simulation and reactor network synthesis; separator simulation and separator network synthesis; reactor-separator-recycle network synthesis; heat exchanger network design; and process economics. Students will also learn about conducting sensitivity analysis and optimisation on the simulated chemical processes. A variety of supporting topics are addressed through the semester including the selection of thermodynamic property packages, utility systems, dynamic simulation, batch process scheduling, solids simulation and process intensification.

title: VLSI Design
description: This unit prepares students to meet industrial demand for jobs related to digital IC design. In this unit, students learn Register Transfer Level (RTL) programming as well as various IC verification methods. The students will be able to use industry-standard electronic design automation (EDA) tools to design ICs based on given requirements.

title: Applied Contract Law
description: Students discover how the rules of contract formation and operation apply in the business world. Students learn how to understand common business contractual terms and implications to develop an appreciation of how contracts are used to allocate risk. Global, technological, social and ethical issues in relation to contracts are explored and finally, students learn about common law rules dealing with disputes and damages and how businesses resolve contractual disputes in the real world.

title: Sustainable Aquaculture
description: With the increasing human population and worldwide depletion of wild fish stocks, the demand for a continual supply of seafood will only put more pressure on aquaculture. Sustainable Aquaculture will introduce students to the interactions between sustainability issues that can contribute to the global food security through sustainable development of aquaculture. Global sustainability challenges and opportunities at each stage of the process will be addressed through topics and activities on farming practices, diversification in system design, recirculating aquaculture systems, live feed production technology, international trade and value addition through quality improvement of aquatic products.

title: Nursing Practice for Health Complexity 1
description: This unit uses a systems approach to assess, diagnose, plan, manage, document and evaluate care related to complex health needs of people. Students apply therapeutic communication and critical thinking / clinical reasoning to meet nursing competency standards in selected clinical contexts. This unit has a focus on acute mental health nursing care, contemporary mental health nursing issues and models of mental health care. Assessment and planning strategies, particularly with people in crisis (self harm). The unit also provides an introduction to critical care nursing 	including: integrated comprehensive physical and mental health assessment and management. Neurological assessment; advanced pain management of people in cardiac and respiratory crisis. Students continue advanced wound care; advanced medication administration: medications via central lines (CVCs/PICCs), TPN, and PCAs, including dosage calculations and applied pharmacology for Step 3 pain 	management, cardiac, respiratory and mental disorders.

title: Markets and Legal Frameworks
description: This unit explores how key business disciplines are connected. Students will develop an understanding of market types, and how business and marketing strategies can create value and impact upon society and the environment. Students will also develop an understanding of the relationship between a business enterprise and various stakeholders, including government, customers and the broader community. The unit also explains basic concepts of law and regulation, and identifies the legal structures of business.

title: Foundations for Professional Health Practice
description: Introduction to ethical decision making in the context of professional health practice. Application of academic standards and development of skills required for studying at university. Introduction to professional requirements which impact on the safety and quality of client centred service/care when working in a health setting. Examination of differences in Australian and international health systems. Students will learn the value of diversity in inter-professional practice through working in teams. Students will reflect on their learning and begin to develop lifelong learning skills.

title: Self, Culture and Society
description: This unit offers an introduction to anthropology and sociology, covering classical and recent developments in both practice and theory, to help students understand the social world. Topics include: social change and stability, politics and power, structural divisions (race, class, gender, sexualities), changing patterns of human relationships, religion, social aspects of health, culture and the sociology of knowledge. A core theme uniting the different topics is analysis of what the 'self' is and how it comes to be, how it may be known, and how comparative studies can shed light on its formation.

title: Petroleum Field and Refinery Processing
description: This unit covers the processing steps in the conversion of crude oil into refinery products: the overall process and details of the individual operations; alternate process technologies and considerations involved in design work; and the key issues and phenomena encountered. There are two sections—Field Processing and Refinery Processing. In Field Processing, students learn about crude oil formation, drilling and production; two-phase and three-phase separation, dehydration, desalting, stabilization and sweetening; and crude oil storage and transportation. Refinery Processing deals with the importance of crude oil, its types, composition, refinery products and product test methods; crude oil evaluation; refinery configurations: different refinery flowsheets, the function of each operation and their integration; distillation: atmospheric and vacuum; refinery gas processing; reforming and cracking; heavy end processing: thermal cracking, hydrocracking, visbreaking and coking; lube oil refining; instrumentation and control; safety and environmental systems; and refinery logistics and economics.

title: Advanced Bioinformatics
description: In this unit, students will use the command line to undertake the analysis of sequence data and then derive biological inference and interpretation from those data, using diverse programs and scripting. Topics include sequence quality control, mapping, variant calling, differential expression and visualisation; as applied to the whole genome, the epigenome and the transcriptome. The rapid and large-scale acquisition of data renders bioinformatics an essential skill for modern Biologists.

title: Machine Perception
description: This unit provides an introduction to the general machine perception problem. It covers image data capture and processing (including data compression and biometrics) as well as video processing. Applications covered include speech recognition, 3D object recognition and object tracking. Tools used in machine perceptions are also addressed, including syntactic pattern recognition, string/graph matching, statistical pattern recognition, decision trees (especially the C4.5 algorithm) and neural networks.

title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
description: Algorithms are an essential part of any efficient solutions for computer applications that evolve with the development in computing technologies. Therefore it is imperative for any computing student to have sufficient knowledge of standard algorithm design techniques and analysis. In this unit the students will learn these standard techniques: divide and conquer, greedy, and dynamic programming. The unit shows how the techniques, among others, are used in sorting algorithms, graph algorithms, data compression, 0/1 knapsack, string searching, matrix-chain multiplication, longest common subsequence, and parallel and distributed algorithms. The students will also learn how to use the growth of functions concept to analyse algorithm resource requirement.

title: Computerised Accounting Systems
description: Provides practical hands-on knowledge and skills needed to implement and use a fully integrated accounting software package. Topics include: introduction to Mind Your Own Business (MYOB) software, system development life cycle, analysis and design of accounting information systems, and principles of accounting software selection.

title: Fundamentals of Programming
description: This unit aims at equipping students with the ability to write simple programs as part of managing large volumes of data. Topics include data representation in a computer, algorithm design, submodules, Boolean expressions, selection and repetition control structures, basic Object Oriented programming design and File I/O. These will be discussed in the context of implementation in the Python programming language.

title: Engaging Media
description: Contemporary media is a vital and pervasive presence in many aspects of our lives, both personal and professional. This unit explores the ways in which 21st century media 'engages' our attention through a variety of texts and communicative modes. It also focuses on the ways in which we, as users, consumers and producers, engage with the media. We will explore how our relation to media is impacted by the institutions and processes involved in its production.

title: Natural Gas Processing
description: This unit is a comprehensive overview of the processing of natural gas from its extraction to the production of its major products: liquefied natural gas (LNG), liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), sales gas and a feedstock for the petrochemical industry. Students begin by learning about wellhead conditions, gas separation, transport and flow assurance, hydrates and their control, dehydration and the removal of contaminants, including CO2, H2S and Hg. LNG production covers precooling, cold section distillation, liquefaction, storage, transport and regasification. Emphasis is given to LNG refrigeration: basic thermodynamics, practical configurations and their optimisation. LPG production includes product specifications, C3 and C4 separation, condensate treatment and storage. Optimised configurations for sales gas production and gas distribution are covered. In addition, students learn about safety, risk management, material selection, control and economics related to natural gas processing.

title: Brain and Behaviour
description: Examination of the structural and functional organisation of the central nervous system. Maturational and evolutionary brain development. Introduction to the basic methods used to study brain structure and function. Interrelationships between physiological functioning and behaviour, with special reference to sensory processes and perception, learning and memory, motivation and emotion, sleep and arousal, and language.

title: Oral Health Sciences
description: In this unit you will gain an understanding of head/neck anatomy and the histological characteristics of tissues. You explore the differences between the deciduous and permanent dentition. The process of development, eruption and exfoliation of teeth is presented, including the microscopic structures and characteristics. You will gain an understanding how the developmental differences affect your care planning and treatment decisions. Pain perception is discussed to allow you to understand the principles of local anaesthesia. You will be introduced to characteristics of the dental biofilm and the impact on oral health. You will investigate the process of infection, inflammation, and healing. You will review the important role of saliva to oral health and risk management.

title: Dental Materials, Prosthodontics and Orthodontics
description: In this unit you will get an introduction to dental material sciences and analyse the different characteristics of dental materials. You will apply an evidence-based approach to select the most appropriate material for specific treatments. Prosthodontics will provide you with different treatment options to repair damaged or missing teeth and how the visual appearance of teeth can be improved. You will gain broad knowledge of prosthodontic and restorative treatments and learn which techniques are within the scope of practice from an oral health therapist. You will be familiarised with fixed and removable prosthodontic solutions, orthodontics and the importance of maintenance strategies (including dental implants).

title: Terrestrial Ecology
description: Two areas of emphasis are identified: a general outline of the science of ecology and developing the skills to do ecological research. Areas covered include factors affecting the distribution and abundance of species (abiotic limitations, interspecific interactions, dispersal, habitat selection and anthropogenic influences) and the functioning of communities and ecosystems. Concepts and theory will be introduced and supported by contemporary examples. Skills to conduct ecological research will be developed by conducting small research projects, following the scientific method of hypothesis testing; reviewing and interpreting scientific literature and presenting information in reports and posters.

title: Data Structures and Algorithms
description: This unit explores the use of fundamental data structures and algorithmic techniques in computing, in order to prepare students to design efficient software applications to implement moderately-complex requirements. The unit demonstrates how various recursive and iterative algorithms work in order to solve specific problems, such as sorting and implementing operations on stacks, queues, linked lists, trees, hash tables and heaps. Students are also shown how to analyse and compare the computational complexity of these algorithms.

title: Professional Foundations for Oral Health Therapy
description: In this subject you will be introduced to the theory and practical foundation for oral health therapy. You are introduced to the roles and responsibilities of the members of the dental team and their individual scope of practice. You will learn how to distinguish oral health from oral disease, and how to support people to achieve (and maintain) good oral health. You gain insight in preventive oral health care strategies, the importance of behavioural change management and minimally invasive dentistry procedures. You learn the theory underpinning the clinical decision-making process. An introduction to oral health promotion and the social determinants of health enables you to understand the factors that affect (oral) health behaviour, the importance for equal access to preventive oral health care and your role in improving oral health literacy. You will be trained in performing non-surgical periodontal instrumentation and restorative dentistry on a manikin. You will be introduced to infection control and how to take dental radiographs. An important part of this unit is applying the different skills in a variety of simulated settings, through case studies, peer-discussions, and student-on-student practical sessions, under the supervision of experienced educational facilitators.

title: Risk Assessment and Care Planning
description: In this unit topics are presented to provide you with the tools to assess the risk for oral disease in a variety of patients. You will compare different risk assessment tools and determine the consequences of factors that affect oral health. You will gain a theoretical foundation to enable you to interpret different oral health processes. You will identify which assessments are needed to make evidence based clinical decisions. You will learn when to perform additional investigations, and why these additional investigations are necessary. You will study the different orthodontic assessments, advanced diagnosis of specific diseases of the soft and hard tissues and identify how to manage and diagnose different types of dental trauma.

title: Behavioural Ecophysiology
description: This unit examines the evolutionary and adaptive response of organisms to common environmental challenges that act as major selective pressures. Comparative behavioural and physiological responses to these challenges will be studied for a range of taxa in differing ecosystems. The unit will examine the interrelationship between structure and function to explore a range of biological mechanisms, processes and responses.

title: The Independent Oral Health Therapist
description: In this subject you continue to treat patients in a variety of clinical settings. You will work with people who experience different complexities of oral disease. You will manage patients with special care needs and complex medical histories. The placements in this unit will prepare you for independent practice as a newly qualified oral health therapist. You will explore your potential role as oral health therapist and apply your full scope of practice within the current regulation. An important part of your responsibility when providing independent oral health therapy care is knowing how to prepare referrals to other dental/health practitioners. You will familiarise yourself with how to treat patients from a holistic point of view and to consider the systemic-oral health link. In clinical discussions you prepare yourself for independent care planning. You continue to reflect on your behaviour and explore cultural bias, to make sure you offer the best care to all your patients. You improve your time management in clinic, offering quality care whilst being efficient. You will constantly analyse your skills and knowledge and display a life-long learning attitude. You will collect further evidence that you have met all the Australian Dental Council descriptors for the newly qualified oral health therapist.

title: Environmental Research Project
description: Environmental Research Project is a unit that tasks students with developing and carrying out a laboratory or field-based research project relevant to their major and stream. This is a capstone-type unit, preparing students for employment in a range of workplaces including Federal, State and Local Government, environment and conservation agencies, environmental consulting firms and nongovernment organisations. It will be particularly useful for students wishing to pursue postgraduate study in terrestrial, coastal or marine research. Students will review and put into practice, skills gained through their major (e.g. experimental design, field sampling and data analysis skills). They then develop a research question, design a study and collect samples and/or observational data to address their hypothesis. The on-campus practical sessions are set aside for processing of samples and data analysis. Student will produce a research paper on their particular study, demonstrating the application of their scientific research skills, to the specifications of one of a range of relevant journals. They will get feedback to allow final submission of their article. High achieving students will have the opportunity to conduct individual research projects.

title: Evidence-based Oral Health Practice
description: In this unit you will learn how apply research methods and skills in evidence informed practice. In this unit you will prepare a comprehensive literature review based on research evidence addressing a clinical or non-clinical problem. You are invited to select a topic based on your experiences in clinical practice or, from other placement settings. You will learn the importance of evidence-based practice to ensure your interventions are based on the most recent scientific research evidence. During this unit you will prepare a report and will be required to include efficacy, safety, cost effectiveness and patient preference in your review. The report will be developed in several stages including; defining a question related to a clinical (or non-clinical/policy) problem, performing a literature search, appraising and critiquing the evidence, discussing your findings and finally, providing recommendations for solutions that may be applied in (clinical) practice. The report will be presented in the format of a journal review article. This unit is based on self-directed learning, a scaffolded assessment submission and you can participate in regular consultation or support sessions and ‘sit down and write sessions’. At the end of this unit, you will present the information in a format that is useful for clinicians, patients or other key stakeholders.

title: Introduction to Clinical Oral Health Therapy
description: In this unit you will treat patients in a variety of clinical settings. You are introduced to how to offer clinical oral health care to people from different age groups and apply your acquired oral health therapy skills in children and adults. Under the supervision of experienced clinicians, you will perform oral health risk assessments, oral examinations, care and treatment planning and you will evaluate the outcomes of your care. You learn to formulate clinical diagnoses for different oral health diseases and manage care within your scope of practice. An important part of your training will be the practical application of pain management strategies (i.e., local anaesthesia). In the simulation lab you will further develop your technical skills in advanced oral health therapy procedures and treatments. You will refine your dental radiography skills (including OPG). You apply oral health promotion theory and strategies in different situations, with different target groups and you learn different theories to manage behavioural changes. You reflect on your learning process, your ethical and professional practice, and constantly develop strategies to improve your skills or consolidate your level of competence in oral health therapy.

title: Cultures of Oral Health
description: In this unit you will explore cultural dimensions and you will investigate the concept of cultural bias. You explore the role of an oral health therapist in a global context. You will further develop your own cultural competence through an elective regional, interstate, or overseas placement. You might participate in a virtual cross cultural learning activity and acquire a transcultural perspective. You develop your own social responsibility project to improve access to preventive oral care.

title: International Agricultural Trade
description: This unit provides an introduction to international agricultural marketing and trade including the planning, implementation and control of international agribusiness activities. There is a focus on international trade environments and trade policy, support agencies and trade enhancement programs, modes of market entry, product modification and adaptation, cross cultural issues, supply chain management, distribution, promotion and payment options. Examples will be provided in trading commodities and differentiated food products. An international market of the student's choice will be studied in greater depth.

title: Soil Systems
description: This unit will evaluate the key aspects of soil biology, chemistry and physics that influence productive soil systems. Natural and induced processes that modify soil conditions in agricultural, horticultural and mine site environments will be explored. Methodologies used to improve soil conditions to restore or sustainably manage soils will be evaluated. Techniques to sample, analyse and interpret soil conditions will be investigated.

title: Sustainable Agricultural Systems and Food Security
description: Exploration of agricultural systems in terms of social, economic and environmental sustainability - the triple bottom line. Sustainable agricultural systems appropriate for land management units including intensive, rangeland and broad-acre examples, in both Australia and other environments. The balance of production between food security, resource and energy commodities from agricultural systems. The impacts on Western Australian agriculture caused by national and global changes. Sustainable practice adoption and social capacity for change. Students will undertake field trips in this unit.

title: Agribusiness Professional Practice
description: Agribusiness Professional Practice is a work placement unit for credit, designed for students who have completed first year of the Associate Degree Agribusiness. Students will research, contact and find a work placement within an Agribusiness-related enterprise, community group, or government agency. The work placement will be full or part-time for a minimum of 75 hours (10 days FTE) but may be longer by agreement between the host organisation, the student and the Unit Coordinator. In addition to the hands-on development of industry-specific skills, knowledge and networks, students are required to participate in a series of career development workshops. The workshops are primarily designed to increase students' ability to apply for and be selected for advertised positions by improving job searching skills, resumes, cover letters, statements addressing selection criteria using STAR/SAO techniques, interview preparation, assessment of personal goals, self-reflection, and professional communication. A post-placement report and presentation enables students to assess supervisors’ feedback, reflect on their overall Work Integrated Learning (WIL) experience, share their experiences and identify how they have enhanced their employment and employability skills.

title: Palliative Care
description: This unit will focus on socio-cultural perspectives of death and dying in Australia; social-cultural, psychological and spiritual dimensions of palliative care across diverse people; principles of a palliative approach to care; ethical issues surrounding end-of-life-care; coping with dying and bereavement; the inter-professional team approach to health assessment and support; clinical assessment and application of evidence-informed pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions for common end of life symptoms;and personal responses to end of life conditions.

title: Architectural Documentation and Detailing
description: This unit explores the notion of architecture and making by focusing on the relationship of methods of construction, integration of structural principles and selection of materials in the design, documentation and detailing process of small scale architecture. Work integrated learning is incorporated through integration and application of construction knowledge and design documentation.

title: Architecture Design Studio 3A - Multi Residential
description: This Design unit explores medium density multi residential and mixed use typologies to generate architectural outcomes for a selected site. Students are asked to take a theoretical position and develop a strong narrative to their design approach. Work integrated learning is incorporated through exploration and expression of theoretical positions through design simulating the real world conditions.

title: Architecture Methods 2A - Digital Fabrication
description: This unit informs the architectural design processes and investigates the relationships and translations between digital and physical modelling, drawings and their application in design. 3D Software for modelling and fabrication are employed for prototyping and representation of architectural materials and space.

title: Architecture History and Identity
description: This unit explores socio-cultural, historical and heritage themes in Architecture. Through research and site visits this unit examines the role of Architecture in the development of national and local identity. Global, national and local heritage issues impacting on architecture are also investigated in this unit.

title: Ethnographies of the City
description: This unit explores the anthropology and sociology of cities and cultural life within them. It deals with such topics as the origins and growth of cities, kinship, family and neighbourhood in urban contexts, work and recreation in cities, class, ethnicity and gender in urban life, the role of different senses in the experience of city life and ethnographic studies in and of urban settings. The guiding theoretical notions for this unit are governance, community, senses and resistance.

title: Society and Culture in a Globalising World
description: The global movement of peoples resulting in cultural and economic exchange, and also domination, has an extremely long history; however, contemporary understandings about globalisation often focus on the gradual increase in international political and economic organisation since 1970s, alongside developments in communications technology, and the impact of changes brought about by the end of the Cold War in the late 1980s. This unit introduces a sociology of globalisation, exploring some of the cultural, political and economic elements of social organisation in the globalising world, and critically examining the ways that experiences and understandings of globalisation may differ according to social and cultural context. Key topics include: theories about globalisation; political and economic organisation in a globalising world; cultural and migration flows; diversity and social inequality; and the impact of globalisation on work, community and the environment.

title: Advanced Statistics for Environment and Agriculture
description: Application of statistical methods for solving problems in agribusiness. Review of principles and applications of various statistical techniques. Review of statistical concepts and methods, including presentation of data calculating numerical measures of location and variability, sampling methods, design sample frame, and data transformation. Exploration of the relationship between experimental design and analysis, including variance (ANOVA), multivariable analysis of variance, non-parametric techniques, time series analysis, comparison of means (t-test), correlation analysis, multiple regression analysis, factor analysis, discriminant analysis, and cluster analysis. Study of various techniques for analysing and presenting qualitative and quantitative data, as well as other numerical measures of univariate and multivariate statistics.

title: Pasture and Rangeland Management
description: The role and types of pasture systems in cropping and animal production enterprises will be explored. Preparation and establishment of pastures as a component of the production cycle, management of pastures and rangelands with emphasis on nutritive values and grazing strategies and exploration of research areas to enhance productivity and sustainability.

title: Advanced Livestock Production Systems
description: Application of the principles of animal production to develop sustainable and efficient production systems to meet the challenges of domestic and global needs. Through simulation programs students will explore production case studies and develop advisory plans. Focal areas will include animal health and management, whole farm production systems and the challenges to animal production from changing climate, food safety and quality, consumer requirements and animal welfare. Students will undertake a field trip in this unit.

title: Doing Social Research A
description: We explore the ways social sciences engage in research across a range of methods and sites, providing practical skills to understand society and culture. This unit positions students to develop and apply their knowledge so they can 'do' - rather than just 'read' – social science. Students deploy observation and interviewing methods to examine the cultures of everyday life, while also learning about a range of other social research methods that can be applied in a range of work and community settings.

title: Crop and Pasture Science
description: Scientific physiological and ecological principles that underpin crop and pasture production, including drivers of plant growth and development, reproduction, nutrition, genetics, crop and pasture health and associated pests. The unit will incorporate a field experiment with associated written scientific report and visits to crop and pasture field days.

title: Architecture Methods 3A - Digital Futures
description: This unit explores the importance of visualisation in ideation, conceptual design and developed design. It consolidates previously learnt methods of site analysis and precedent studies. It focuses on investigation and application of three dimensional visualisation methods to represent complex spatial, programmatic and functional relationships using new technologies that are at the forefront of architectural design and practice. Work Integrated Learning is incorporated through exploring the use of three-dimensional methods in architectural practice.

title: Atmospheric and Oceanographic Sciences
description: This unit will cover the fundamentals of atmosphere and ocean dynamics, meteorology, ocean tides and waves, and aims to put these in the context of climate change in the 21st century. Lectures will focus on (1) the physical mechanisms responsible for large-scale atmospheric and oceanic circulation, (2) the global energy balance and hydrological cycle, (3) mesoscale weather systems, (4) ocean waves and tides, and (5) how these processes impact the coast at the local scale. Students will be introduced to the key concept of a coupled atmosphere and ocean, and how these combined systems influence marine biogeography and coastal landforms.

title: Discovering Asia
description: This unit is area-focused and interdisciplinary, designed to enhance Asia literacy by discovering Asia's diversity from historical developments to current global engagements. It covers traditional topics such as history and geography, as well as more contemporary issues facing Asia today, such as the issues of gender equality, environmental sustainability and globalisation. This unit employs a topical approach and provides an introduction to three of the largest Asian countries: China, India and Indonesia.

title: Asian Century Issues and Perspectives
description: This unit examines the ways in which specialists in area studies have conducted research, through engagements with ideas and bodies of evidence. It also explores the ways in which area specialists' knowledge is applied in the workplace and business environments of Asia. The unit develops reflective understandings of doing research on Asia-focused issues and perspectives.

title: Biochemistry of Nutrition
description: In this unit, students learn about the structure of proteins, carbohydrates, and lipids, and how this affects their digestion absorption, and function within the body. The metabolic pathways involved in the cellular metabolism of carbohydrates for energy is also studied. In the laboratory component, students gain experience in using a range of analytical techniques and laboratory equipment central to biochemistry.

title: Bank Lending
description: This unit addresses the sphere of aspects that are related to the proficient credit risk assessment of consumers and businesses from a banking perspective. The content includes the role, main activities and organisational structures of banks; essential components of credit risk management; and the principles and process of dealing with credit risk assessment. Students are also familiarised with Islamic bank lending conducted by Sharia banks.

title: Professional Practice in Construction
description: Students will work on practical problems within the construction industry and develop dedicated technical solutions. Students will practise skills through case studies with industry partners.

title: Data Analytics in Accounting
description: In this unit, students will develop skills in data analytics which will equip them to add value to organisations in data-driven business environments. Students will learn to identify situations where data analytics can support problem solving and decision making. They will also apply statistical and decision analysis techniques and statistical packages (for example, Excel) in the accounting context.

title: Embedded Systems Engineering
description: Microcontrollers are ubiquitous devices found in many facets of our daily lives, from simple toys, household appliances, smart cities to sophisticated space exploration projects. This unit provides an introduction to the basics elements of embedded systems, which allows one to harness and exploit their capabilities. Key topics in embedded systems, covering architectural issues, programming fundamentals, scheduling, and the basics of interfacing are presented. Students will be able to gain knowledge to work with a modern day embedded system.

title: Advanced Modelling and Control
description: Cascade, Ratio and Feedforward control. PID Enhancements: inferential, over-ride and selective control; scheduling controller tuning; implementation Other Advanced Control Techniques: deadtime compensation; adaptive control (programmed adaptation; self-tuning control; online parameter estimation). Multi-input Multi-output Systems: process and control loop interactions; control loop pairings; decoupling control systems; multivariable control. Digital Control Systems: Z transforms; discrete time models; dynamic response; discrete time control algorithms; closed loop analysis; digital control system implementation. Review of process modelling and simulation techniques. Modelling for Fault Diagnosis: prediction-based and identification-based diagnosis. Empirical Modelling: linear and non-linear models; artificial neural networks; ARMAX models. Modelling Hybrid (Discrete-Continuous) Systems: representation and solution. Case Studies and Applications in Process Engineering.

title: Process Heat Transfer
description: Modes of heat transfer, energy balances; Conduction (1-D & 2-D steady, lumped & 1-D transient); Heat exchangers (types, OHTC, fouling, LMTD and ε-NTU analyses, detailed design of shell and tube heat exchangers); Convection ( forced convection correlations for internal & external flow, free convection correlations, boiling and condensation equations); Radiation (the blackbody, radiative surface properties, Kirchhoff’s law, view factors, radiation network diagrams, radiation exchange between surfaces, radiation shields)

title: Social Work Lifespan, Resilience and Risk
description: This unit introduces psychological, biological, neurological, sociological, psychodynamic and cultural approaches to lifespan development. Students will explore how resilience, risks and opportunities shape social work practice. In this unit students will undertake a critique of dominant understandings and approaches in life span development.

title: Fluid and Particle Processes
description: In this unit we cover different aspects of fluid and particle processing. We start with single phase compressible and incompressible flow in nozzles and pipes. Then we continue the unit with two phase flow of gas and liquid in horizontal and vertical pipes. Particle properties in terms of shape and size are discussed followed by study of particle in liquid: single particle, multiple particles, and wall effect. Then we discuss about flow in porous flow, which is followed by filtration and sedimentation theory: batch and continuous. We will discuss about fluidisation in the following chapter, and solid separation using cyclone and centrifuge in the next chapter. The last chapter is dedicated to discussing about slurry transport and pneumatic transport.

title: Process Mass Transfer
description: In Process Mass Transfer, students will learn the fundamental theory and introductory practical applications of separation processes. The fundamental theory they will study includes molecular diffusion, convective mass transfer, interphase mass transfer, the two-film model, film and overall mass transfer coefficients and vapour-liquid equilibrium. Mass transfer theory is used to design and analyse unit operations for separation processes. These include flash and continuous distillation, gas absorption and stripping, solvent extraction, solid leaching and humidification. The methods used to study the unit operations are material balances for stage and continuous contact processes, McCabe-Thiele design methods, and packed tower design.

title: Chemical Sensing and Measurement
description: This unit will be delivered in three modules covering topics on electroanalytical methods, scanned microscopy techniques, advanced electrochemical and electrical characterisation, respectively. Students will be introduced to electroanalytical methods such as pulsed and stripping voltammetry, ion-selective electrodes and explores micro- and nano-electrodes. Advanced electrochemical and electrical characterisation techniques such as electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, molecular electrochemistry and single-molecule sensing will be discussed. Students will learn microscopy techniques to characterise samples with regards to their physical and chemical properties.

title: Building Dissertation 2
description: Students will be engaged in an independent research process under a supervision. They will think critically as they handle a research problem, and as they further develop the research proposal they have presented prior. Students will explore scholarly materials and develop conceptual solutions through intellectual reasoning and critiquing. They will develop and use clear methodologies to collect and analyse data quantitatively and qualitatively. Students will construct new knowledge and discuss the place of their new constructs in existing knowledge. Students will write a dissertation and present their research findings orally.

title: Software Engineering Testing
description: An in depth examination of unit, integration and system testing and the maintenance of large software based systems. Topics include automated and manual techniques for generating and validating test data, the testing process, static vs. dynamic analysis, functional testing, inspections, and reliability assessments. Testing approaches based on graph theory, finite state machines, formal specifications, logic and syntax based testing. Testing of graphical user interfaces, Stress testing. Development of a software configuration management plan encompassing tool selection, identification of artefacts, baseline and change control, measurement, auditing and reporting and release of deliverables. To provide practical knowledge of a variety of ways to test software, an understanding of some of the trade-offs between testing techniques, and a feel for the practice of software testing.

title: Data Communications and Networking
description: Aim of this unit is to help learners understand the basics of data communications and networking. Topics that unit will cover include various aspects of data communications such as data transmission, transmission media, signal encoding, and digital data communication techniques. The unit will also explain the data networking with the help of topics including routing in the data networks, queuing theory, and flow control.

title: Computer Communications
description: This unit is an introduction to computer communications and networks technology. It covers fundamental knowledge on the design and implementation of networks and network protocols. The content of the unit covers the introduction to computer communications, physical layer, data link layer I, data link layer II, network layer I, network layer II, transport Layer I, transport layer II, application layer I, application layer II and security.

title: Introduction to Mergers and Acquisitions
description: This unit examines the motives and incentives for mergers, acquisitions and takeovers. It measures security price performance and the causes and consequences of takeovers. We look at corporate raiders and corporate governance through proxy contests. A comparison of the effects of share market repurchases versus cash dividends as forms of corporate payouts are studied. Other issues include anti-takeover defences, executive compensation structures, ownership and firm performance.

title: Advanced Digital Design
description: In this unit students learn how to use Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) and the VHDL hardware description language to implement embedded systems. FPGAs and VHDL are used in industry to develop high-performance digital systems. Students work in teams to develop a project involving the control of sensors and actuators. The laboratory component of this unit is intense and students have opportunities to further develop their professional identity.

title: Science Research Project
description: Review the research process. Formulate and design a research question/project relating to a science problem; construct a literature review using computer-based tools; perform systematic independent investigations; critically interpret results in the context of previous studies; communicate the body of research as a science paper

title: Extended Software Engineering Testing
description: An in-depth examination of unit, integration and system testing and the maintenance of large software-based systems. Topics include automated and manual techniques for generating and validating test data, the testing process, static vs. dynamic analysis, functional testing, inspections, and reliability assessments. Testing approaches based on graph theory, finite-state machines, formal specifications, logic and syntax based testing. Testing of graphical user interfaces, Stress testing. Development of a software configuration management plan encompassing tool selection, identification of artefacts, baseline and change control, measurement, auditing and reporting and release of deliverables. To provide practical knowledge of a variety of ways to test software, an understanding of some of the tradeoffs between testing techniques, and a feel for the practice of software testing.

title: CPU and GPU Architectures
description: This unit introduces students to the fundamentals of concurrent systems. Topics to be covered include basic concepts of concurrent process execution, modelling concurrency and common classes of concurrent algorithms, granularity of processes and communications, and race or hazard conditions and scheduling. Paradigms to be covered include both distributed and shared memory architectures.

title: Computational Transport Phenomena
description: This unit introduces the fundamental transport equations used to represent momentum, heat, and mass transfer in process systems. The boundary layer concept and the effect of drag and friction on flow behavior are discussed for various engineering scenarios. Concepts related to conductive and convective heat transport in different systems are covered. Fundamentals of mass transfer through diffusion and convection will be discussed, with and without chemical reaction. Case studies are presented on the analogies of viscosity, diffusivity, and thermal conductivity. Empirical correlations, dimensionless numbers, and their significance in solving transport phenomena problems are included. Further, this unit introduces computational fluid dynamic (CFD) technique to provide hands-on experience in using a state-of-the-art CFD solver based on the control volume approach for problems involving fluid flow, heat transfer and mass transfer.

title: Nutritional Biochemistry and Human Metabolism
description: In nutritional biochemistry and human metabolism, students expand on their knowledge of the metabolism of macronutrients in humans, and understand the role of tissue specific metabolism in whole body homeostasis. Amino acid and fatty acid metabolism are examined and their relationships with carbohydrate metabolism, and the maintenance of normal blood glucose concentrations is also investigated. The role and mechanisms by which insulin and glucagon control whole body metabolism following a meal, between meals, and during prolonged starvation is also examined along with the sources of energy during rest, moderate, and high intensity exercise.

title: Foundations of Cell Biology
description: In this unit, students will receive a comprehensive introduction to cell biology and build upon fundamental concepts presented in earlier units. Foundations of Cell Biology focuses on how cells regulate their activities to respond to the external environment.
