description: This unit delves deeply into the foundations of calculus and real analysis, and focuses on the development of critical thinking and logical reasoning skills which underpin mathematical methods and techniques used in solving problems that arise from science, engineering and business related fields. Emphasizing on rigorous mathematical reasoning, students will be exposed to the foundational aspects of mathematical logic, set theory (and their applications in mathematical analysis and problem-solving), real and complex numbers, limits-convergence-continuity (exploring these concepts from both intuitive and formal perspectives), differentiation (including Taylor series and its application to solving limits), integration (including the development of Riemann and Darboux integrals and their applications), and series. Through rigorous exploration and analysis, students will develop a profound understanding of the theoretical underpinnings of calculus and its applications across various disciplines. This unit is designed for those students who have passed WACE Mathematics Specialist ATAR or equivalent.

title: Professional Experience 1
description: This is the first in the suite of professional experience units that includes a practical component (a 10 day placement in a school). The unit will allow you to apply philosophies and theories related to teaching and learning. The unit also addresses professional responsibilities, effective communication and reflective practices to support your workplace learning. The professional experience practical assessment is a low-stakes observational work place learning opportunity intended to enable practical application of the knowledge and skills gained, along with providing students with insights into the complexity of the teacher’s role. All required clearances to work with children must be obtained and valid, and all other preparation requirements met prior to commencement of Professional Experience placement.

title: Regression and Nonparametric Inference
description: This unit begins with an introduction to nonparametric methods for hypothesis testing. These methods are distribution-free analogues of parametric methods such as one- and two-sample t-tests that have been presented in introductory statistics units. The main part of the unit is devoted to linear regression, and it will include topics such as simple and multiple linear regressions, estimation by the method of least squares, diagnostic checking of models, analysis of variance, conventional as well as more contemporary methods of variable selection. Throughout, students will be using the R language statistical computing environment to carry out and document analyses in a reproducible manner.

title: Stem Cells and Regenerative Medicine
description: In this unit, students will be introduced to key areas in current stem cell & regenerative medicine research and associated laboratory techniques. The unit begins with a basic introduction to stem cell biology and associated biomedical science. This is complemented by an examination of the theoretical application of stem cells across three broad themes: Stem Cells and Cancer Biology, Biotechnology, and Regenerative Medicine. The laboratory component will address various immunohistochemistry and cell assessment techniques, thereby developing student progression towards independent research skills. The ethical, legal and social implications of stem cell and regenerative medicine research and technologies will be discussed, and students are required to communicate professionally in a scientific manner.

title: Diversity and Cultural Planning
description: Addresses challenges related to access, equity, diversity and culture with a focus on providing students with a plurality of perspectives in planning.

title: Exercise Physiology
description: This unit aims to develop a deeper understanding of the physiological mechanisms underlying responses to acute exercise in apparently healthy individuals. Students will learn to conduct common laboratory- and field-based exercise physiological assessments, analyse, interpret and report collected data. The knowledge and practical skill competencies addressed in this unit are relevant to future careers in exercise science, sport science and clinical exercise physiology.

title: Cross-Cultural Communication
description: Learners engage with skills and concepts needed to practise public relations successfully in contemporary global and culturally-diverse communication environments, including recognition of ethical considerations and implications. The unit builds awareness and understanding of cross-cultural communication in international public relations and develops knowledge of public relations and corporate communication across cultural contexts and in specific regions, such as the Asia-Pacific.

title: Interior Architecture Honours Proposal
description: This unit encompasses the role and relevance of interdisciplinary and trans-disciplinary research in contemporary design practice, reflecting on, synthesising, and building discipline-related knowledge and expertise. Students select a topic of particular personal relevance and interest, to interrogate, position and develop a research project in consultation with their supervisor. The processes, including design as research, will demonstrate advanced theoretical and technical knowledge in one or more disciplines or areas of practice.

title: Pharmacokinetics and Pharmaceutical Analysis
description: This unit is intended to introduce the fundamental concepts of pharmacokinetics (i.e. the ‘passage/time course’ of drugs through the human body) and further extend student understanding of pharmaceutical analysis. This unit is divided into two learning modules. Module 1 includes drug bioanalysis, immunoassays, tracer techniques, fluorescence spectroscopy (fluorimetry), HPCE and mass spectrometry. Module 2 covers basic pharmacokinetic principles, drug absorption/distribution (including MRT), applied pharmacokinetics (including PK-PD relationships), hepatic/renal clearance, drug metabolism and bioequivalence.

title: International Study Abroad 3
description: n/a

title: Australian Studies
description: The Australian peoples: historical and cultural background; government, politics and law; myths, values, attitudes and language; popular culture and media; folklore, art and sport; and current affairs and issues.

title: Planetary and Minerals Geophysics
description: Minerals and in particular strategic minerals are critical for modern life, while the planets and other nearby celestial bodies, present future opportunity for humanity. This unit will focus on distribution of the minerals that sustain modern life and the geophysical methods used to delineate them. Students will explore petrophysical properties of rocks along with case studies focused on the geophysical strategies used for finding copper, gold, nickel, potash, Lithium, Iron Ore and many other deposits types from around the world. They will learn how to display and analyse multiple geophysical data sets over major deposits around the Australia.

title: Design For Manufacturing
description: The Design for Manufacturing unit focusses on the design of products to improve the ease of manufacture and the efficiency of assembly. This is achieved by adopting Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA) strategies and incorporating manufacturing methods and operation management such as Concurrent Engineering (CE), Flexible Manufacturing (FM), Just in Time (JIT), Lean Manufacturing (LM) and Automated Systems (AS) into the production facilities.

title: Narrative Nonfiction
description: This unit introduces you to narrative nonfiction, including its role and significance in telling true stories and reflecting contemporary issues. You will explore, analyse, and experiment with a range of written narrative nonfiction forms including feature articles and flash nonfiction. The aim of the unit is to provide you with a critical understanding of the influence of narrative nonfiction in contemporary life, to provide practice in writing in a variety of forms, and to enhance awareness of changing genres, styles, and issues.

title: Indigenous Reconciliation Action
description: This intensive unit of study is designed to challenge students to explore the complexities surrounding Indigenous reconciliation in Australia. Through a challenge-based approach, students will engage with the multifaceted matters, historical contexts, and contemporary efforts aimed at fostering reconciliation between Indigenous and non-Indigenous Australians. Emphasising critical analysis and reflection, students will explore the intersections of culture, politics, economics, and social justice within the reconciliation discourse. This unit will equip students with culturally appropriate ways to actively participate and make a difference to reconciliation in Australia.

title: Global Environmental Challenges
description: This unit provides an introduction to global environmental challenges including anthropogenic climate change, deforestation, resource depletion, and population growth. Current change scenarios and their impacts are examined globally, regionally and locally concerning freshwater and marine biodiversity; primary industries; water resources; human health; settlements and infrastructure; disaster management and emergency services and social economic and institutional dimensions. The sensitivity and adaptive capacity of affected systems will be examined, including adaptation and mitigation mechanisms to overcome barriers to change. National and international policy options associated with environmental sustainability and various forms of mitigation, adaptation and transformation will also be addressed.

title: Psychology Undergraduate Dissertation
description: Students jointly conduct the research planned in the associated unit PSYC4007 Psychology Undergraduate Dissertation Preparation and write up an individual account in the form of a dissertation.

title: Secondary Professional Teaching Practice 3
description: This unit is the third in a sequence of four professional teaching practice focused units. The unit will support your understanding and application of key education theories, concepts, and skills to develop your professional teaching practice. The first module will introduce evidence based learning design for secondary teachers to differentiate their instruction to meet the needs of diverse learners. The second module will continue to develop the theory and application of positive classroom management including positive learning environments and teacher-student conflict resolution. The third module will address communication with other teaching professionals, assessment differentiation, and rubric development. This unit is designed to provide a theoretical and practical foundation of essential skills you will need to demonstrate on the third school-based professional experience placement.

title: Business and Law International Experience 6
description: International mobility experience for undergraduate students.

title: Advanced Reservoir Engineering
description: Built upon the knowledge gained in the unit - Fundamentals of Reservoir Engineering (PEEN3001), this unit covers the practical, larger scale techniques used to analyse and make decisions about the long-term performance of hydrocarbon reservoirs. The unit starts with a discussion around well test analysis using a log-log Type Curve technique. Then the rest of the unit discusses in details the reservoir production management and foresting techniques such as the material balance calculations, aquifer modelling, immiscible displacement (Theory of Buckley-Leverett), production performance forecasting, generation and application of pseudo-functions and basics of enhanced oil recovery. Overall, this unit provides the petroleum reservoir engineers with the practical knowledge they need in forecasting and then managing and possibly enhancing recovery from hydrocarbon reservoirs.

title: Medical Radiation Special Topics 2
description: In this unit, students will explore selected special topics of relevance and currency to their Medical Radiation Sciences discipline, with a focus on advanced technology, MRS practice, or current professional issues. Students will investigate and appraise cutting-edge or specialised medical imaging or radiation therapy technology, explore and reflect on best clinical practice, and debate contemporary issues relevant to their profession. The special topics considered in this unit complement those of Medical Radiation Special Topics 1.

title: Climate Change, Health and Big Data
description: In this unit students will learn skills in research and assessment of climate change and health using big data. It gives students the training to understand health impact assessments of climate change. Data analysis skills will be taught using big data repositories of spatiotemporal gridded data on historical climate variables (i.e. heat, water resources, air pollution) and future projections under climate change scenarios. Statistical association modelling is used to estimate baseline risks using exposure modelling linked with health and population data. Evidence of the risks of impacts will be assessed in terms of at-risk populations such as Indigenous communities and disadvantaged socio economic groups. Students will explore case studies involving mortality, malaria and mental health. They will practice visualisation and strategies to communicate complex climate and health information for climate action plans by policy and research stakeholders.

title: Land Planning
description: This unit provides students with a brief overview of the history of land development in Australia. It identifies and discusses the roles of key stakeholders, consultants and government agencies involved in the land development process. The relationship between local infrastructure plans, local planning policies, town planning schemes and planning policies in Western Australia are examined, including their relationships within relevant jurisdictions. The application of R codes in conjunction with the Design Codes Policy in Western Australia are covered in detail, demonstrating their importance as principles for sound subdivision design. The land development process is documented from application to the approval of title, also covering economic and feasibility considerations for small-to-medium-scale subdivisions, achieving positive outcomes during the subdivision process and providing an overview of the lodgement procedure and conveyancing requirements. The unit also introduces students to the different types of land tenure.

title: Motor Learning
description: In this unit students will be introduced to motor skill acquisition from both theoretical and practical perspectives. It will build on fundamental knowledge of biomechanics, exercise physiology, motor control and psychology.

title: Sensory and Consumer Evaluation of Food
description: Insights into the physiological and psychological bases for sensory evaluation and consumer testing. Principles of sensory and consumer evaluation methods, theories, design, analysis and ethical practices. Sensory science links to quality management, food product evaluation and market and consumer trends. The future of sensory and consumer evaluation science.

title: Mechatronics Automation Project
description: Pneumatics actuators, gripper technology, control values and pneumatic circuit representation. Sequential control systems. Programmable logic controllers (PLC). Sequential control system representation, logic analysis and PLC programming. Sensor technology for sequence control, optical, capacitive, inductive and magnetic. Computer simulation of a programmable pneumatic positioning system.

title: Clinical Immunology
description: This unit builds on prerequisite units to apply knowledge of the immune system to a clinical setting. Students will compare innate and acquired immunity, discuss immune cell function and examine the MHC gene complex. Infection, inflammation and vaccine development are also covered and students will perform selected immunoassays used in medical laboratories.

title: Medical Radiation Pathology 2
description: Medical imaging diagnosis of the central nervous, gastrointestinal, hepatobiliary and genital-urinary systems. Various 2D and 3D imaging modalities including general x-ray, ultrasound, computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging that are commonly used in clinical practice for making diagnosis are presented and compared. The evaluation of disease processes on medical images enables medical radiation science professionals to identify and act on urgent/unexpected findings and gives them the ability to provide an informed opinion to a medical practitioner based on their knowledge of the scientific explanations underpinning disease and injuries affecting the human body.

title: Adaptive Reuse and Heritage
description: This unit introduces the concept of Adaptive Reuse and Heritage, the initiation of sustainable design responses to the adaptive re-use contemporary reuse of historic buildings with minimal impact on the heritage significance. Students will undertake research methods to synthesise knowledge and technical skills in ways that embrace history, and includes indigenous perspectives, in a contemporary context. Concepts such as culture, values, memory and identity are explored.

title: Design History and Culture
description: Designers should have a clear understanding and appreciation of the history of design, its development, theories and the major movements that have influenced its Evolution, and their reflection on human culture. The past informs the future and the ability to develop responsive designs requires creative opportunities and problems solving skills grounded in the lessons from the past. This unit will explore the historical and cultural practices underpinnings of the broader discipline area of design and enable you to develop and appreciation of its interconnectedness with social, political, cultural and economic issues of the Modern period to date. Learners will learn about the emergence of ‘Design’ as a field of practice and historical study through a thematic and chronological look at the past and present, covering ideas and concepts emergent from Design’s relationship with ideologies, technologies, materials, and human interactions.

title: Applied Anatomy
description: This unit introduces students to anatomical terminology and foundational systems in relation to functional human movement to inform clinical reasoning. Students will engage in understanding the neurovascular and musculoskeletal lower limb structures required for the development of physiotherapeutic skills. An understanding of underlying anatomical features will be explored to enable the identification of surface anatomy and palpation for clinical examination and imaging. This unit will involve peer learning, reflection, cadaveric specimens, imaging, problem-solving, and blended learning.

title: Indigenous Public Health and Health Promotion
description: The examination of Indigenous and non-Indigenous health promotion theories, models and strategies forms the bases of understanding the development of best practice in health promotion. Investigations of health education, health and social determinants, learning styles, principles of learning and values, beliefs and attitude identification in an Indigenous context is significant to developing and implementing improved health promotion outcomes and health behaviour.

title: Indigenous Australian Education
description: This unit focuses on complex cultural environments and roles interconnected with Indigenous Australian education. Students develop the skills to critically reflect and assess their own teaching abilities in an Indigenous Australian context.

title: Health Promotion in Challenging Contexts
description: The aim of this unit is to review the development and application of Health Promotion strategies in challenging and controversial areas. This will include exploring significant issues in areas such as sexuality, sexual and reproductive health, HIV/AIDS, mental health, alcohol and other drugs, prisoners and indigenous communities, the role of health promotion as a change agent in these areas; effective and ineffective strategies; useful and harmful approaches; ethical and political considerations; community engagement and advocacy; and national and international issues, experiences and perspectives.

title: Cultural Landscapes
description: This unit uses the concept of cultural landscapes, and the related concepts of place and territory, to understand and analyse the character and pressures on environments. The unit will equip students to understand, explain and apply geographical analysis to contemporary issues at different spatial scales. These issues include climate change, urbanisation, land use, human-nature relations, and ecological degradation. There is a strong emphasis on the development of technical skills using ESRI ArcGIS applications as they provide an excellent platform for exploring the layers of a landscape.

title: Advanced Clinical Biochemistry
description: This unit covers endocrine and other specialised clinical biochemistry tests. It includes the investigation of thyroid, hypothalamic/pituitary/adrenal disorders, as well as reproductive function, covering both male/female infertility, pregnancy, antenatal screening and assessment of foetal health. Other topics covered include inborn errors of metabolism, tumour markers, therapeutic drug monitoring, molecular diagnostics, iron metabolism, advanced immunoassay, measurement uncertainty, proficiency testing, and method and instrument evaluations and tumour markers.

title: Applied Paramedic Bioscience 2
description: In this unit, students integrate biomedical knowledge with patient-centred and culturally safe care to address cardiovascular and respiratory conditions commonly managed by paramedics. Emphasis is placed on discussing the aetiology, pathophysiology, and clinical manifestations of conditions commonly managed by paramedics, interpreting diagnostic strategies, and understanding pharmacotherapeutics and quality use of medicines. Students will also develop skills in evaluating and applying primary evidence and clinical standards to inform management strategies that are evidence-based, person-centred, and culturally safe.

title: Form and Structure
description: This introductory fashion unit focuses on developing foundation technical skills in pattern cutting and construction methods, using industrial machinery to develop commercial knowledge and skills. The unit examines the historical and cultural underpinnings of Western garment design and construction, using a practical and contextual framework for understanding contemporary fashion design.

title: Fine Art Studio Processes
description: This unit is designed to develop your capacity for research-based enquiry into skills, techniques, methods and processes of fine art that takes into account international and cultural contexts. You will undertake a practical engagement of studio-based research through staff and, or self-directed projects within a specified conceptual framework. You will work towards a studio research presentation and a developed body of artworks.

title: Intelligence and Strategic Risk
description: This unit will provide students with a critical understanding of intelligence, and its various processes, products and operating challenges. A particular emphasis of this unit is on how intelligence informs decision-making bodies within the context of strategic risk and those matters which can impact the state, national security and its institutions, which includes the intelligence community, military, law enforcement, border protection and health. Strategic intelligence and its methodological approaches will also be explored.

title: Integrated Applied Anatomy
description: This unit allows students to integrate anatomical terminology and foundational systems with the understanding of functional human movement to inform clinical reasoning. Students will engage in understanding the neurovascular and musculoskeletal upper limb and trunk anatomy required for the development of physiotherapeutic skills. An understanding of underlying anatomical features will be explored to enable the identification of surface anatomy and palpation for clinical examination and imaging. This unit will involve interactions between peer learning and reflection, cadaveric specimens, imaging, problem solving, and blended learning.

title: Teaching Indigenous Australian Community Education
description: Develop best practice in teaching and learning in a community education context. Development of community education resources for supporting groups for action, working for justice and social change. Application of Indigenous Terms of Reference to community education practice.

title: Indigenous Lifespan Development
description: An examination of the physical, social and cognitive human developmental milestones from preconception to adulthood. This will also include a consideration of the complications of trauma and adverse childhood experience on these milestones.

title: Korean Intermediate 4
description: This unit is an intermediate level unit suitable for students who have successfully completed Korean Intermediate 1 (KORE2000) or who have an equivalent level of competency. Taught through interactive and self-directed engaging learning approaches and materials, this unit will enable students to progress their Korean language competency and cultural literacy in various aspects of Korean society and culture to prepare them to live and work in Korea. On successful completion of this unit, students will be able to both read and produce intermediate level authentic materials in Korean and gain further confidence in using Korean language in everyday and workplace settings. Upon successful completion of Korean Intermediate 3 and 4 students will reach a level of competency equivalent to TOPIK (Test of Proficiency in Korean) scale of proficiency upper 2/ lower 3.

title: Petroleum Field Development Planning
description: Petroleum Field Development Planning is the capstone unit of the course, which relies on the reinforcement and applications of many of the principles and techniques learnt in previous units in order to develop a petroleum asset following a systematic approach. The students will be involved in working in an-open ended group project to study the exploration and production results associated with geology, geophysics, formation evaluation, reservoir engineering, drilling engineering, and petroleum production and operation; and develop a recommendation for an optimum field development plan. The project will be based on a representative field data set for a typical oil and gas field, and involves performing an assessment of exploration and production lifecycle, reservoir mapping, prospect generation and evaluation; reserve estimation; and reservoir performance evaluation; production forecasting; appraising the field including economics justification, recommendation of optimum development plan which includes: identification and selection of suitable technologies for drilling, completion and production of petroleum; development of a field-wide operation philosophy with a consideration of health, safety and environmental impacts; assessment of economic feasibility with scenario and sensitivity analyses; reservoir monitoring and management, and field abandonment strategy.

title: Clinical Neurophysiology
description: To obtain and interpret signals generated by the body, for the purpose of assessing function, clinical neurophysiologists must have a clear understanding of the technology and methods used to record and analyze signals, and understand the biological activity underlying these signals. This unit integrates the core anatomical and physiological knowledge required for the practice of clinical neurophysiology, examining the biology underlying signals generated by the body. Moreover, this unit introduces the technology and techniques for measuring and analyzing biological signals, and introduces the role of clinical neurophysiology in diagnosis.

title: Energy Transport
description: The Energy Transport unit is a comprehensive study of the movement of energy from its sources to end-users. This unit covers the technical, economic, environmental, and social aspects particularly related to Indigenous stakeholders of energy transport, including the infrastructure used to transport energy, the different types of energy sources, and the policies and regulations that govern the energy transport sector. Students learn about the infrastructure used to transport energy, including the electricity grid, pipelines, tank carriers and coal transport. The technical and economic factors that influence energy transport decision-making, including cost, reliability, efficiency, and regulatory requirements are covered. Students are introduced to the environmental impacts associated with different energy sources and transport modes, including greenhouse gas emissions, air and water pollution, and land use impacts. Students learn how these impacts are evaluated and how trade-offs between different impacts and energy benefits are made.Additionally, the course covers the national energy policy framework in Australia, including the role of energy market regulations and institutions, climate change policy, and renewable energy targets. Students learn about the opportunities and challenges associated with the transition to a low-carbon energy system, including the role of renewable energy sources and the decarbonisation of energy-intensive industries.

title: Supporting Literacy and Numeracy Development for Diverse Learners
description: This unit is one of three in a suite of undergraduate Option units designed to prepare Initial Teacher Educators (ITE) to specialise in the teaching of Literacy and Numeracy in diverse populations. Completing three of these units will provide graduates with a specialisation in this area. This unit introduces literacy and numeracy as dynamic and evolving concepts and understood by individuals with a variety of learning strengths and difficulties within their particular social, cultural and historical experiences. Students will explore literacy and numeracy conventions and demands across the entire curriculum, not limited to only English and Mathematics.  Students will begin to develop an awareness of the need for teachers to support opportunities for literacy and numeracy development holistically.

title: Project-based iSTEM Education
description: This unit is one of three undergraduate Option units in integrated science, technology, engineering and mathematics (iSTEM) offered by the School of Education. Completing all three units will provide a specialisation in iSTEM. This unit aims to equip students with content and pedagogical content knowledge in integrated STEM education in the context of project-based learning. Students will be scaffolded to use problem solving and collaboration skills, to think creatively and laterally, and to take initiatives as they engage with and reflect upon the projects. They will make explicit links to the science, mathematics and technologies curricula, whilst using various design processes. Pedagogical content knowledge will be developed by students creating and evaluating project plans and implementation approaches in a variety of educational settings as appropriate to their degree (ie ECE, Primary, or Secondary education)

title: Concepts in Occupational Therapy Practice
description: This unit offers an introduction to person-centeredness, foundational knowledge, skills and attitudes required to be an occupational therapist. Students are introduced to the occupational therapy process and understanding of occupational analysis, interviewing, grading and adapting. The unit guides students through the application of professional behaviours, interpersonal communication and ethics through a variety of practical and fieldwork experiences.

title: Introduction to Indigenous Australian Health Issues
description: Introduction to disease process: agent, host, environment, body systems affected and resistance of Indigenous people to disease. Social, biological and environmental determinants of common health problems. The structure and function of the systems of the human body.

title: Psychosocial Care for Health Instability
description: Apply knowledge of socio-cultural and biopsychosocial elements to practice in the context of life-long or life-limiting health conditions. Recognise and understanding of individual and family psychological responses to including personal skills and abilities, habitual behaviours, emotion and motivation. Recognise and assess psychological circumstances of the individual and family living with unstable health problems, such as stress, anxiety, depression and chronic pain and understand how these impact individuals and families. Apply transdisciplinary psychosocial approaches to person-centred practice to promote health and well-being, prevent illness, improve health care outcomes, and empower individuals and families.

title: Violence, Abuse and Trauma
description: The unit critically examines explanations for domestic and family violence and sexualised abuse. This unit explores how gender, age, cultural heritage, class, sexuality and (dis)ability mediate the lived experiences of violence, abuse and coercion, its impacts and the social responses. Students will explore current practice and policy responses and apply key approaches to working with perpetrators and survivors of violence, abuse and coercion including response-based practice, First Nations practice frameworks and trauma-violence informed practice.

title: Petroleum Geomechanics
description: This unit provides a background to rock mechanics principles and how they can be used for petroleum engineering applications like: wellbore stability, hydraulic fracturing, sand production, reservoir compaction and casing collapse.

title: Applied Complex Midwifery Bioscience
description: The focus of this unit is the applied pathophysiology and midwifery care and management of women and babies with complexities. Students will explore interdisciplinary collaborativemanagement of complex disorders over the continuum of midwifery care, along with the associated pharmacology.

title: Cross Institutional Study (within Australia)
description: Please refer to syllabus for the equivalent course

title: Seismic Methods
description: Seismic methods are cornerstone of modern energy exploration and are routinely deployed for, environmental, geothermal, groundwater, minerals, and engineering applications. Seismic methods are also fundamental in research as they can reveal the interior of our Earth's and neighbouring celestial bodies. This unit provides the theoretical and practical basis of surface and borehole seismic methods including essential aspects of acquisition and processing of seismic data. The workshops of this unit cover a diverse range of practical seismic acquisition and processing challenges through computer-based exercises using leading software and field demonstrations with modern and novel equipment

title: Digital Literacy in Indigenous contexts
description: This unit focuses on using contemporary digital communication tools to recognise and showcase Australian First Nations cultures. Students will learn about a variety of accessible digital tools that are currently in common usage. These tools will be used in a ‘cloud’ environment to enable greater data mobility and accessibility. They will be used to create multimedia artefacts that enhance First Nations cultures and recognises the contribution that First Nations people have made and continue to make to Australian culture. Students will have critical experiences of social media environments and learn to navigate these environments with a view to using them to appropriately publish digital artefacts that they have created.

title: Applied Laboratory Medicine Practice 2
description: This unit is the last of four clinical placements units. Students will participate in seven weeks of supervised professional practice in a "National Association of Testing Authorities" (NATA) accredited pathology laboratory. Students will be placed in a major analytical area of the laboratory developing skills and competencies in quality control and maintenance of laboratory equipment, data verification and validation, data interpretation and test reporting. Students will receive training in appraisal, evaluation and interpretation of analytical data and patient clinical history required for accurate diagnosis, aetiology, classification and monitoring of pathological processes.

title: Interior Architecture Studio - Well-being
description: In this design studio students will investigate the complexities of healing environments, and consider how the interior experience can contribute to a sense of well-being and the process of change. Design approaches to services integration, materiality and detailing will be informed by the user experience. Design methodologies and explorations are informed by research, resulting in a well-detailed, resolved spatial outcome. Cultural values and perspectives are explored and incorporated in the design proposal. Design prototyping and testing are to be done through digital fabrication and simulated environments.

title: Creative Design Studio
description: This unit introduces students to the design process as undertaken by those within the fields of Creative Advertising & Graphic Design. Through a series of practical projects, research reports and presentations, students will be introduced to creative practices through the production of innovative and appropriate design solutions.

title: Indigenous Australian Issues and Factors in Local Region
description: An introduction to historical factors that have impacted on Indigenous Australians in local and global contexts. Included in this historical overview are impacts of pre and post colonisation on community life. Federal and State legislation and policies will be unpacked in the context of local regions.

title: Fundamentals of Environmental Health Management
description: This unit introduces students to a variety of environmental health issues and examines their causes, health impacts and possible management strategies. It considers the current trends in environmental health and the roles of governments and international agencies in environmental health management.

title: Introduction to Journalism
description: This unit introduces students to the nature, history and function of journalism in Australia. Students will learn to think and communicate critically about journalism practice and journalism’s role in society, and as a crucial function of democracy. Students will develop practical reporting skills in a variety of mediums and platforms highlighting their ability to convey information and ideas effectively, concisely, creatively, and accurately.

title: Field Studies of Sedimentary Basins
description: A field camp of approximately 9 days to map sedimentary rocks, measure sections and study sequences in a selected basin. Students study areas under staff supervision and receive advanced training in observing, recording, and interpreting sedimentary rock and sequences of sedimentary basins.

title: Digital Public Relations and Storytelling
description: This unit engages students in the use of a range of digital media tools and encourages the application of writing, creative thinking and professional communication skills to tell a story across different digital platforms. The unit covers the principles and practice of ethical media relations, in local, national and international contexts. The unit develops students’ ability to write for a particular audience, understanding tone, relevance and resonance in communication.

title: Food Processing and Preservation Project
description: Food processing methods and their role in preservation of foods including thermal, chemical and physical processes used in the food industry. The effects of food processing methods and storage on the quality, safety and nutrient content of foods. Principles of food packaging and packaging requirements for preservation of foods.

title: Walking On-Country
description: Guided and taught by Indigenous rangers and Traditional Owners on Country, students will gain insights into, and participate in, the vital work rangers perform in caring for Country. Centred around a 1-week on Country immersion, the Walking On-Country unit will deepen students’ understanding of the desert, Country, Culture, Indigenous Ecological knowledge and community development from a First Nations' perspective. The Walking On-Country unit will build key intercultural capabilities whilst enabling students to understand how Indigenous land and sea management frameworks can be applied to regional, rural, and remote development contexts.

title: Advanced Science Capstone
description: This unit is for students enrolled in the Bachelor of Advanced Science (honours). The capstone unit is the culmination of the previous 3 years of study in a self-paced, self-directed project. The form of the project is dependent on the interest and aspirations of the student but will generally result in a product that adds to the scientific knowledge in the field of study or presents a technical solution to a problem. Alongside specialised discipline knowledge students develop research, technical, professional and communication skills. Through a process of inquiry involving the formulation of research questions and hypotheses; selection of appropriate methodology and experimental design; ethical consideration of the research process; critical review of scientific literature; effective scientific writing; development of a project proposal. The project is mentored by academic staff, industry partners or a combination of these.

title: Commercial Development and Valuation
description: This unit explores the development of commercial property including offices, retail and industrial space. It examines the building process including estimating the costs of construction and also the valuation techniques adopted in the commercial sector. Putting together valuation and costs, the unit investigates how to calculate the feasibility of commercial development projects and the residual land value.

title: Principles and Practice of Haematology
description: A systematic study through laboratory investigation of haematological disorders: blood counts, morphology and special tests.  Normal and aberrant haemostasis and control of anticoagulant therapy will be investigated, along with transfusion science and laboratory testing for compatibility.

title: Applied Health Promotion Planning and Evaluation
description: Evaluation designs and methods for health promotion programs. The role of evaluation in determining the short and long-term outcomes of health promotion programs. Ethics in health promotion planning and evaluation. Mixed methods for health promotion program evaluation. An introduction to multi-component and comprehensive planning and evaluation designs and systems approaches. Planning and evaluation methods for program replication and scale-up. Knowledge translation into practice and policy. Practical considerations in health promotion planning and evaluation, including funding, administration and resourcing.

title: Citizenship, Culture and Diversity
description: This unit explores how difference is constructed within understandings of citizenship; it introduces students to modernity and contemporary social theories and their intersection with everyday experiences of gender, sexualities, cultural heritage, socio-economic position and disabilities. Framings of colonialism, post colonialism and intersectionality are used to understand issues related to inclusion and exclusion.

title: Marine Biodiversity
description: An understanding of their biodiversity underpins the assessment and management of marine ecosystems. For those engaged in the prediction and assessment of anthropogenic impacts on marine and coastal environments the taxonomic skills related to the classification of marine biota and the ability quantitatively describe their biodiversity is critical. ZOOL2001 Marine Biodiversity will provide students with a sound understanding of the taxonomy of Australian marine life. The main marine botanical and zoological phyla will be investigated from a taxonomic stand-point. Students will use traditional and current to quantitative methods of describing and measuring biodiversity and assess their use in modern, scientific assessment of the impacts of anthropogenic activities in coastal and marine environments.

title: Functional Foods and Product Development
description: This innovative unit introduces the concept of functional food products, foods which make health claims, and product development in the food manufacturing sector. It covers the unique issues related to the development of functional food products including regulatory aspects, critical evaluation of the evidence for health claims, efficacy and safety considerations, food processing and shelf life stability challenges, as well as considering the consumer and marketing. Independent critical thought and self-directed learning are encouraged through evaluating the evidence for health effects from a range of bioactive components in food. Project management skills and various communication skills will be emphasised and developed through a collaborative food product development project.

title: Exercise Prescription
description: This capstone unit will provide students opportunities to create, implement and evaluate suitable exercise interventions for individuals and groups. A focus on general prescription principles for health, fitness and maintenance goals, as well as athletic performance, will be addressed. Special considerations for prescribing exercise in paediatric populations, females and older adults will also be emphasised. Active participation in the unit will allow students to foster a positive personal health and fitness ethos, while preparing students for their practical placements.

title: Paramedic Professional Practice
description: In this unit, students will build on previous knowledge to explore and solve complex legal, ethical and professional issues using a structured approach. Difficulties in determining capacity and consent in mental health, children and vulnerable populations will be explored. The role of the paramedic as a patient advocate for health equity and promoting diversity will be discussed. Students will then consider issues such as end-of-life care, recognition and reporting of abuse, evidence preservation, and victim support. Finally, students will consider the role of clinical governance and national safety frameworks in ensuring safe healthcare delivery. Students will also explore how their own mental health, empathy and self-compassion can impact clinical care.

title: Fundamentals of Clinical Pathophysiology
description: This unit expands understanding of the main pathophysiological processes that underpin common diseases and conditions managed by physiotherapists across all healthcare settings. A range of specific common acute / traumatic, non-traumatic and progressive conditions are explored, with students encouraged to examine similarities and differences between conditions in terms of underlying pathology, clinical presentation and the individual’s experience. Impact of specific physical and psychological conditions on an individual is explored using a biopsychosocial framework.

title: Interior Architecture Studio - Foundation
description: An introduction to the world of designing – the act and the outcomes with an emphasis on the domain of the ‘interior’ and its creation through design. The unit introduces the discipline of Interior Architecture and the role of the Interior Architect as a practitioner with particular attitudes and beliefs. Community settings within the city are explored as the context of the interior: the city as cultural artefact, its conditions, its histories and spaces. Students will study the relationship between idea, space, form and structure as it is related to human activities; analysis of the city as a representation of collective values; analysis, interpretation and creation of the elements of the city including interiors, pavilions, gardens, squares, streets, stairs, doors, gates and windows.

title: Medicinal Chemistry and Clinical Pharmacokinetics
description: This unit is intended to introduce the key concepts of medicinal chemistry, the fundamentals of drug toxicology and further extend student understanding of pharmacokinetics into the clinical/practice setting. This unit is divided into two learning modules. Module 1 includes drug discovery and design (including prodrugs), detailed synopses of the medicinal chemistry of a variety of important/current drug types and pharmaceutical toxicology. Module 2 covers therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM), hepatic and renal disease, pharmacogenetics, clinical pharmacokinetics of various major drug types and population PK.

title: Environmental Planning
description: Introduction to the environmental issues relevant to development and sustainable planning.

title: Research, Leadership and Entrepreneurship in Science 1
description: This unit is for students enrolled in the Bachelor of Advanced Science (Honours). It has been designed to allow students the flexibility to explore different dimensions of their chosen discipline. This is achieved through Independent Study Contracts (ISCs). ISCs are agreements between the Unit Coordinator, the student (or groups of students), and academic or industry mentors that details the tasks that students need to complete to achieve the learning outcomes of the unit. Students complete modules in Research Methodologies, Project Planning, Stakeholder Communication, Communicating Science and Leadership.

title: Language Analysis and Assessment
description: This unit develops students’ competence in the observation and assessment of people with developmental and acquired communication disorders using knowledge from a range of theoretical models. It introduces students to techniques for describing and analysing parameters of communication, including the use of standardised and non-standardised assessment.

title: Smart and Micro Grids
description: This unit will introduce the composition of a smart grid and how renewable energy sources can be integrated for environment-friendly operation of electric grid. The communication needs in a smart grid, demand management in particular through home area networks and smart meters, the inclusion of electric energy storages, and their applications in electric vehicles will be discussed. This unit will also present the composition of a microgrid with both renewable and non-renewable source, its ability to increase the penetration of renewable energy sources and how to design and control a microgrid in both grid-connected and stand-alone modes. The design of solar photovoltaic (PV) power systems for both grid-connected and stand-alone applications and the design of stand-alone micro-hydro systems are the other topics covered in this unit.

title: Radiation Physics and Instrumentation
description: Theoretical knowledge in the physical principles underpinning medical radiation science. The physics of electromagnetic, mechanical and particulate radiations including X-rays, ultrasound, charged particles and neutrons, their properties, productions, interactions with matter, detections and measurements. Basic instrumentation for medical radiation science covering components of linear accelerator, general X-ray and ultrasound systems, their image receptor technologies and image quality assessment parameters. Radiation safety and ALARA.

title: Advanced Coaching and Programming
description: In this unit students will build on their fundamental knowledge and skills in session design and apply it to the design of programs used for sport and exercise purposes. Theoretical concepts pertaining to program design, periodisation, load management and the development of perceptual motor and perceptual cognitive skills will be applied to team, individual and complex sports.

title: Medical Imaging Practice 2
description: Positioning theory, patient care, communication, radiographic or surface or applied anatomy, commonly encountered pathology or trauma, image acquisition and interpretation relevant to the intermediate beginner practitioner.

title: Quantum Mechanics
description: In this unit, students learn the basics of non-relativistic quantum mechanics. The unit starts by introducing the concept of the wave function, its interpretation, the Schrödinger equation and covers the topics of potential wells, potential barriers and quantum harmonic oscillator. Then a more formal approach to quantum mechanics is taken by introducing the postulates of quantum mechanics, quantum operators, Hilbert space, Heisenberg uncertainty principle, and Dirac notation. Next the unit considers topics covering the hydrogen atom, angular momentum, spin, the addition of angular momenta, and some basic aspects of many-body quantum mechanics, such as a system of identical particles and electron orbitals in atoms. The unit ends with the variational principle and its application to the helium atom and the hydrogen molecule.

title: Finite Element Analysis
description: Introduction to FEA. Direct method: stiffness matrices for spring element, tensile element and torsion element. Introduction to ANSYS, a general purpose FE package. Applications of the FE package to some common engineering problems. Element assembly and solution for unknowns. Influence of node numbers on element assembly. Programming with Excel. Spring in an arbitrary orientation. 2D transformation matrix. Direct method: stiffness matrix for a simple plane beam element. Formulation of stiffness matrices using Rayleigh-Ritz method. Interpolation function (or shape function) formulation. Lagrange’s interpolation formula and Hermitian interpolation formula. Finite Element Formulation for an Euler beam element. Higher order beam elements. Mass matrix, mass condensation and Guyan reduction. Finite elements in vibrations. Introduction to isoparametric elements. Finite elements for plates. Gauss quadrature.

title: Reflective Practice
description: A reflective practice unit forming a compulsory element of the Public Relations Institute of Australia’s (PRIA) accreditation requirements. The major activity is for students to critically reflect on their study experience within the context of an industry placement, covering a minimum of one month full-time, or part-time equivalent, with an employer in a public relations capacity.

title: Social Work Honours Field Education 2
description: Students will undertake 525 hours social work placement in a range of fields and sites of practice under the supervision of an approved supervisor. Integration and application of theoretical frameworks, social work skills and critically reflective practice are essential elements of the placement. Through the use of supervision students will develop competence in integrating personal values, professional values, ethics and frameworks into practice. Students will apply self-care strategies and undertake critical examination and evaluation of social work in practice. Students will be able to articulate social work skills in dynamic and diverse settings. This professional placement develops students’ skills to operate as beginning social workers in self-directed practice.

title: Introduction to Managing Indigenous Australian Projects
description: Introduction to Indigenous Project Management including needs analysis, project feasibility and development of a project proposal.

title: Earth Observation from Space
description: Satellite Earth Observation (EO) is used across most Earth science disciplines and their applications to real-world issues, from oceanography to meteorology, climate science, geophysics, ecology, forestry, agriculture, mining and many more. The wealth of information that the panoply of EO techniques provides allows addressing Earth system science as well as developing applications that can serve many economically significant Industries that rely on accurate and consistent information about the environment. This unit will provide an understanding of the basics of EO technology and applications. It will introduce fundamental concepts and theories underpinning EO, data capturing techniques and extraction of information from versatile satellite observations, and then will demonstrate application of EO to map and monitor Earth terrestrial and aquatic environments. The knowledge you will get from lectures and the skills learnt in your practicals will be applicable to multiple aforementioned disciplines.

title: Limb Anatomy and Biomechanics
description: The unit explores, in detail, the functional anatomy of the upper and lower limb and their associated girdles. Applications of anatomical and biomechanical principles in analysis of upper and lower limb function and dysfunction will also be covered.

title: Quantitative Biology
description: An introduction to a variety of statistical procedures which are frequently used in the biological sciences. Populations and samples, types of data, distributions, measures of central tendency and dispersion, graphing techniques, data screening, data transformation, diversity indices, one-way ANOVA, two-way ANOVA, post-hoc testing, dependent, independent and one-sample t-tests, simple linear regression and correlation, multiple linear regression, non-parametric procedures (Mann-Whitney U test, Kruskal Wallis, Spearman Rank Correlation, Chi-square and contingency tables), overview of multivariate ecological techniques. Experimental design, interpretation of analyses and report writing. Data analysis using R and RStudio

title: Advanced Econometrics
description: The unit starts with a brief overview on statistics, probability theories and linear regression models. It then moves to advanced econometric techniques for analysing data with complex structure, including: stationary/non-stationary time series models, discrete choice models, panel data analysis and spatial data analysis.

title: Applied Laboratory Medicine Practice 3
description: This unit is the third of four clinical placement units. Students will participate in seven weeks of supervised professional practice in a "National Association of Testing Authorities" (NATA) accredited pathology laboratory. Students will be placed in a major analytical area of the laboratory developing skills and competencies in quality control and maintenance of laboratory equipment, data verification and validation, data interpretation and test reporting. Students will receive training in appraisal, evaluation and interpretation of analytical data and patient clinical history required for accurate diagnosis, aetiology, classification and monitoring of pathological processes.

title: Working in Human Service Organisations
description: Students will explore strategies for navigating the diversity of structures and organisational cultures in Human Service Organisations. Students will focus on the purpose, policy and legislative contexts within Human Service Organisations. Students will also explore the social work role within these organisations including key social work values and ethics, particularly social justice. Socio-political analysis of how policy directives and other drivers shape Human Service Organisations will be considered as well as the role and impact of service users as key stakeholders. Students will engage with their emerging social work identity and the impact of working in a Human Service Organisation.

title: Occupational Therapy in Neuropsychiatry and Recovery
description: Mental health recovery approaches will be applied to explore mental health experiences across the lifespan. These mental health experiences will be explored in relation to the Mental Health Act of Western Australia. Recovery oriented assessment will be utilised to develop strategies to work alongside people in recovery. The use of the mental status exam and risk assessment will be explored; along with the utilisation of safety management plans. The recovery philosophy and medical model will be compared in the area of mental health. Skills in contemporary occupational therapy practice and service delivery will be developed

title: Innovative Speech Pathology Practice from Local to Global Communities
description: In this unit we introduce key concepts in public health in shaping our understanding about who is communicatively healthy and why, and the importance of prevention efforts in improving equity both globally and locally. We examine how health promotion frameworks are used in developing community-level interventions, focussing on prevention in response to an identified community need. We explore how speech pathologists can work collaboratively with communities to create authentic, inclusive supports to meet the needs of all people, including people with communication and swallowing needs. We highlight the need for systemic advocacy and change to promote local and global equity, and the role speech pathologists may play in this.

title: Interior Architecture Honours Project
description: Under the direction of a supervisor, students are offered a stimulative environment, which incorporates a breadth of practice and academic experiences relevant to the discipline of Interior Architecture. Each student will initiate and develop an individual project aimed at enhancing their design expertise. Core theory, technological strategies, and/or practices continue to be interrogated at an advanced level. Students are required to appropriately structure their research strategies in relation to the evolution of their particular topic, deploying appropriate methodologies and methods. Projects are expected to be framed within appropriate interdisciplinary and trans-disciplinary theoretical and practice-based discourse.

title: Paediatric Physiotherapy Practice
description: This unit applies understanding of evidence-informed theory and processes of typical child development across all developmental domains to inform the assessment, clinical reasoning and effective holistic management of common neurological, musculoskeletal and cardiopulmonary childhood conditions using an ICF model. There will be a focus on individualised communication and facilitation of function and participation, recognising the unique presentation, abilities and situation of each child and family. There is a focus on culturally-safe, family-centred practice and interprofessional teamwork as core philosophies in paediatric care, innovative technology to enhance management are explored.

title: Level Design Cinematics
description: This unit provides students the opportunity to explore the intersection of real-time technology, cinematography, and level design to craft cinematic sequences within both linear and non-linear digital experiences. It delves into the integration of techniques considering cinematic work from both traditional workflows, camera work and leverages on real time technology to produce compelling cinematic type sequences. Students will examine traditional and non-traditional workflows in cinematography, using theoretical frameworks to understand their boundaries while engaging with industry practices and production pipelines to create compelling narrative sequences.

title: Climate and the Biosphere
description: This unit introduces students to the deep-time history of our habitable planet, and evolution of its climate and life forms, demonstrating how interactions between the biosphere, geosphere and climate systems have been, and still are, key in shaping the world around us. Subjects covered include: the key stages in the evolution of life on earth from the Precambrian through to the Anthropocene; the geological context of climate change; how climate and life act as reciprocal controls on earth's surface systems; the recurring role of climate change in mass extinctions, their causes, precursors, and recovery; interpreting the fossil record; and the use of fossil preservation, morphology and chemistry to reconstruct past ecosystems, modes of life and environments. In the workshops, students will develop hands-on experience of examining, identifying and interpreting plant, invertebrate, and vertebrate fossil material and interpreting paleoenvironmental data.

title: Introductory Musculoskeletal Science
description: This unit provides an introductory biopsychosocial approach to musculoskeletal health across the life-span. Clinically-orientated anatomy and pathology are applied in the context of individuals with common musculoskeletal disorders in first-contact primary care settings. Evidence-informed, person-centred assessment and management based on a biopsychosocial framework is developed. Information is gathered from the individual using multidimensional screening tools, medical notes / referral letters, medical imaging, observation and physical assessment procedures. Clinical assessment findings are analysed and common patterns of clinical presentation identified. Principles of clinical decision-making about selection, rationalisation and application of treatment and management are considered, focused on evidence-based high-value care to achieve an optimised return to function. Principles include patient-centred education, graded movement exposure, exercise interventions and physical activity programs, manual therapy, facilitating healthy lifestyle behaviours and appropriate referral to other health care practitioners. Effective person-centred verbal and interprofessional digital communication skills are developed in a musculoskeletal context.

title: Health Planning and Evaluation
description: Planning in health care organisations, the planning environment, needs analysis, scope and feasibility, decision-making, cost management. Project evaluation, evaluation designs, perspectives of evaluation, data collection and analysis.

title: Professional Physiotherapy Practice
description: This unit develops professional clinical competencies across a range of healthcare settings using interprofessional team case-based learning. This includes developing empathetic, person-centred communication with diverse clients (including those from a gerontology context), based on theories of behavioural psychology, health beliefs and models of behaviour change. The ICF framework and biopsychosocial models will be applied in a physiotherapy clinical reasoning process. Skills including information gathering, collaborative person-centred goal-setting, methods for measuring outcomes and standard documentation strategies will be developed. Students will have the opportunity to engage in providing interventions in a clinical setting, guided by a health professional.

title: Numerical Optimisation
description: This unit introduces the fundamental techniques and methods for solving optimisation and numerical optimisation problems. Topics will cover optimisations models, one-dimensional search techniques, unconstrained optimisation techniques including steepest descent method, Newton’s method, conjugate gradient methods, and constrained optimisation techniques including Lagrangian multipliers, Kuhn-Tucker optimality conditions, sequential quadratic programming.

title: Clinical Medical Imaging Practice 4
description: This unit provides authentic medical imaging professional practice experience in the clinical setting, at the level appropriate for the advanced beginner reflective professional.

title: 3D Digital Production
description: The designer's responsibility is to understand, measure, respond to and minimise the adverse environmental effects of what they create. The emerging discipline of 'Circular Economy' is explored through an overview of knowledge, fundamentals, methods of measurement, leading applied fields of practice, and practitioners. A creative design-based project focusing on the circular economy as a framework to create a product able to benefit from the digital production technologies.

title: Speech Pathology Fieldwork 1
description: In this unit, students will undertake speech pathology clinical practice to develop competency according to Speech Pathology Australia Competency-Based Occupational Standards (CBOS). This unit will facilitate the development of skills in the management of paediatric or adult clients in community, health and/or education settings. Students will be expected to demonstrate competency relative to their stage of their fieldwork progression: They will demonstrate approaching intermediate competency at the end of their first placement and intermediate competency at the end of their second placement.

title: Exploring and Contesting Curriculum
description: This unit provides an introduction to the idea of curriculum including key terms, alternative models of curriculum and the processes and products of curriculum. Specific areas covered include: socio-cultural perspectives of curricula; curriculum integration; the development of early learning and school-based curricula; and the way in which teachers use curriculum documents for planning. This unit provides an introduction to the Early Years Learning Framework and the Australian Curriculum.

title: Contemporary Issues in Corporate Finance
description: A unit focusing on advanced corporate finance issues, including agency theory, capital structure, security offering and corporate takeovers. The content of this unit is applied and quantitative and the approach is analytical.

title: Risk Management
description: This unit provides a theoretical grounding in the management of risk and uncertainty for businesses. It develops frameworks and techniques for categorising, analysing and planning for risk and then applies them to situations faced by firms in a range of industry sectors.

title: Culture and Dress
description: This unit explores the language of garment and fashion through an examination of traditional dress and its impact on contemporary fashion culture. Students will be required to question preconceived ideas about the relationship between body, cloth and garment and explore the conceptual aspects of this relationship.

title: Medical Imaging Practice 3
description: Positioning theory, patient care, communication, radiographic or surface or applied anatomy, commonly encountered pathology or trauma, image acquisition and interpretation relevant to the immediate/advanced beginner practitioner.

title: Foundations of Medical Microbiology
description: This unit includes the study of prokaryotic cell structure and function with a focus on understanding the virulence properties of bacteria (including mechanisms of antibiotic resistance) and the influence these factors can have on the pathogenesis of infectious disease. The concept of the dynamic interrelationship between the human host’s defence mechanisms and the pathogenesis of microbial disease is introduced using examples of specific bacteria and viruses. The clinical diagnostic cycle for identifying microbial pathogens includes the collection of appropriate human clinical specimens, the laboratory processing of the specimens, the cultivation and/or taxonomic identification of pathogens and the susceptibility testing of medically important bacteria. This unit not only introduces each of these principles but also covers the important topic of antibiotic therapy including the mode of action of various antibiotics as well as the epidemiological basis for monitoring and controlling infectious diseases.

title: Proficient Japanese: Professional Interactions
description: This unit aims to develop and maintain an advanced competence in modern Japanese at JLPT N2 level. Learning materials are taken from a variety of up-to-date authentic media, TV, film, websites and digital media. The unit explores a number of issues in Japanese society and examines how they contribute to cultural and social identify. Students will learn to reflect critically on the complex intersection between language, identity, and society in Japan.

title: Financial Planning Internship
description: Students undertake a period of 120 hours in professional valuation practice under the supervision of a Licensed Financial Planner. Students are required to participate in the development of a full Statement of Advice and a work diary certified by the student mentor. Students must demonstrate the application of industry best practice in the construction of the Statement of Advice.

title: Residential Property Development
description: This unit examines the economics of residential property development as well as the process itself. We examine just how a decision to develop a property is made, the stages in the development process, the key actors involved and the role of the planning system. However, the main focus of the unit is on the financial viability of a development project. Students will use a variety of models to assess viability, measure risk and return and analyse and communicate modelling outcomes.

title: Network Optimisation
description: This unit will consider problems arising in business and industry. The students will learn the necessary skills to model and solve such problems through network optimisation. The topics covered include: Applied Graph Theory (basic definitions; applications of graph theory to network design and analysis; scheduling; facility layout design; various allocation and routing problems), Network Flows (basic concepts; application; Max- flow Min-cut Theorem; feasible flows and algorithms), Matchings (basic concepts; applications; algorithm for maximum matchings in bipartite graphs), Project Management (project planning; resource allocation problems; time constraints).

title: Urban Analysis
description: Examine changing form and function of central city areas using different theories and range of data.

title: Design Fabrication
description: This innovative unit examines narratives of occupation, of use, and of making, as embedded in designed products that constitute the interior. Through a series of explorations and testings, students use technology to create a prototype object that has purpose and feasibility for the design industry. Emphasis is placed upon future-thinking and finding simple ways to communicate narratives of construction, use, and occupation. Practices of environmental sustainability are also considered in students’ final products.

title: Traffic and Road Pavement Engineering
description: This unit comprises the road-used characteristics, measurement of traffic flow, geometric design of highways, highway types with their standards, and Highway capacities and design of intersections. This also includes road pavement structural design and materials.

title: Commerce Research Project Advanced
description: Students will investigate a complex business or research problem and synthesise findings or innovative solutions for a project embedded in business, community, industry or government. Students will compose a comprehensive professional report by conducting a fully integrated research project proposal with literature review, research design and methodology, data collection and analysis; and develop comprehensive findings or recommendations.

title: iSTEM Education through Digital Stories
description: This unit aims to equip students with content and pedagogical content knowledge in integrated STEM education through the context of digital storytelling. Students will engage in knowledge construction, innovative design and computational thinking to creatively communicate STEM concepts related to an issue that they are passionate about. In so doing they will make explicit links to the science, mathematics and technologies curricula. Pedagogical content knowledge will be developed by students through consideration regarding how they would adopt this approach in their future classroom by creating learning-experience implementation plans linked to STEM aspects of the curriculum and appropriate to their degree (i.e. ECE, Primary or Secondary).

title: Paramedic Clinical Practice 2
description: Within this unit, students will apply their theoretical knowledge to assess, diagnose, plan, manage, document, and evaluate patient care across the patient's lifespan (including scene safety, patient assessment, therapeutic management and diagnostic reasoning). Linked to the other semester 4 units, students will learn to assess and manage clinical conditions within a paramedic context. Advanced life support during out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, in line with national guidelines, will be introduced. Assessment skills will be expanded with a continued focus on identifying the deteriorating patient, performing diagnostic assessments, and using clinical reasoning to inform management. Students will learn to respond to and adapt management strategies in response to rapid and fluctuating changes in patient conditions. Clinical scope will continue to be expanded with further advanced skills (including intraosseous access) and therapeutic management options. All clinical practice will be grounded in relevant paramedic ethical, legal, professional, and person-centred frameworks, with a strong emphasis on reflective practice. Students will critically evaluate their experiences to develop self-awareness, enhance decision-making, and continuously improve the quality of care they provide.

title: Advances in Molecular Microbiology
description: An advanced course in the study of molecular biology and pathogenesis of major bacterial pathogens. There is an emphasis on new and emerging infections as well as those that have previously had major global impacts of clinical and economic relevance. Molecular microbiology and biotechnology uses this information to improve diagnosis, treatment, epidemiological analysis, control and prevention of infectious diseases. Core topics covered include bacterial genetics and the evolution of resistance to antimicrobial agents, the mechanisms of resistance to antimicrobial agents, and the spread and epidemiology of antimicrobial resistance genes. The lecture program will feature guest speakers from research and industry to highlight current aspects in microbiology. The practical component focusses on understanding the principles and practices of laboratory diagnostics using current molecular approaches. Seminars will be conducted as team presentations to explore current topics on infectious diseases in depth. This progressive unit aims to expose students to the multi-faceted approaches required when engaging issues in molecular microbiology.

title: Cyber Security Capstone Project 2
description: Students continue the projects that were designed and planned in Cyber Security Capstone Project 1. Each student will work in consultation with a member of the academic staff and with an industry partner. Projects are related to the professional practice of cyber security.
