This may include penetration testing, analysis of the safety of computer systems and/or research and application of security best practices for a particular situation, including the creation or adjustment of security policies. Students will have the chance to apply their learned knowledge in a real-world setting.

title: Developmental Neuroscience
description: This unit explores typical development of the nervous system’s structure and function. Somatosensory, autonomic and peripheral nervous systems. The unit covers motor systems and their role in controlling posture and coordinated movement. Students consider the role and integration of reflexes in relation to observation of typical motor development; identifying the role and integration of reflexes and reactions in relation to typical development. There is focus on understanding the development of cognition, perception, visual motor integration and language, developmental progressions and childhood occupations.

title: Podcasting
description: This unit examines the evolution of the podcast in the media environment, and the theory and practice of the medium in an ever-evolving media landscape. Students will examine the data surrounding podcasting’s growth, as well as its future. Students will examine and evaluate the many forms of podcast, from chat format to long-form investigative journalism pieces. They will hear from and speak to leading podcast content makers. They will learn about available technology for recording, editing, and distributing, examine business models, and seek to produce their own audio packages.

title: Interior Architecture Fundamentals
description: An introduction to fundamental aspects of interior architecture practice including building standards and codes, documentation drawings, and basic principles of construction and detailing. Floors, walls and ceilings are investigated as interior construction systems. Aspects of compliance to building codes are introduced to inform universally accessible solutions to interior environments. Computer aided drawing is introduced to form the communication tool for much of the assessment content.

title: Advanced Linear Algebra 1
description: This unit will introduce and develop the notions of vectors, lines and planes and their extensions into general n-dimensional space, through the study of vector spaces. This unit also covers matrices and their use for solving systems of linear equations through a study of a number of different of solution methods, as well as the calculation and application of eigenvalues and eigenvectors.

title: Curriculum and Instruction Lower Secondary: Humanities and Social Sciences
description: This unit is designed to prepare pre-service Lower Secondary Humanities and Social Sciences teachers. The focus of the unit is on curriculum planning, teaching strategies, evaluation, resources, the demonstration of positive impact on student learning and research relating to Lower Secondary Humanities and Social Sciences. Teaching and learning practices to support and challenge a diverse student cohort are explored.

title: Online Power and Resistance
description: The Internet has had a massive impact on our political systems, from grassroots activism through to global politics. This unit helps you to understand how and why this has happened, and why it matters. It explores the new challenges and possibilities for governance created by the Internet, as well as attempts to control the Internet by governments and others. Ultimately, you will come to understand how networked communications are intertwined with long-running political struggles around control and resistance.

title: Medical Radiation Instrumentation 2
description: The more advanced technological developments of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging modalities will be examined, along with supplementary and additional instruments used in medical radiation practice (portable, mobile and dental X-rays, fluoroscopy, angiography, and nuclear medicine). The theory covered will extend students' understanding of the equipment and/or systems, including their design, construction, operation, clinical applications, and relevant regulations and standards. Image post-processing and visualisation tools will be applied to the management and manipulation of 3D datasets for diagnostic applications. Safety and quality assurance requirements will also be considered, including those related to the use of contrast media.

title: Listening to Country: First Nations’ Perspectives
description: This unit gives you the opportunity to experience and listen on Country. It is a unique opportunity to develop your intercultural capabilities through an immersive learning experience led by Elders and senior First Nations people in a Western Australian context. You will be taught First Nations’ ways of being, doing and knowing so that whatever your discipline background, you will enrich your understanding of Country, community and self.

title: Contemporary Issues in Tourism Management
description: This unit has been designed for students to examine contemporary issues in international tourism, such as globalisation, climate change, threats of terrorism and natural disasters, mobility, technological innovations, demographic change, emerging consumer trends and new product developments. Students will consider the significant change these issues have brought to the tourism industry and necessitate new management strategies and policies to ensure its future success. The aim of the unit is to enable future managers and decision makers to recognise the most significant contemporary issues in tourism management and equip them with tools to effectively respond to these drivers of change.

title: Analytics for Experimental and Simulated Data
description: This unit explains the principles and practice of analysing data that were obtained under controlled conditions, such as a laboratory experiments or field trials. It covers the use of linear, generalised linear and non-linear models, emphasising practical techniques for data analysis. The key concept of 'sources of variability' and Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) serve as guiding principles. The unit also introduces elementary concepts in the design of experiments, such as confounding, and methods for design and analysis of computer simulated experiments.

title: Radio News
description: This unit equips students to work in a radio newsroom environment performing a range of tasks in the development of complex radio news stories. Students will undertake intensive tuition in digital recording, editing and production using industry standard equipment, ensuring they are able to react to the demands of the modern news environment. The unit will encourage students to develop critical thinking skills and establish professional practices within journalism's ethical and legal parameters, while working both independently and collaboratively within a news team.

title: Sustainable Property Markets
description: Residential and commercial property markets play a major role in shaping our cities and regions. Changing technologies and patterns of investment and development can contribute to sustainable cities and communities while the provision of affordable housing can reduce inequalities. This unit will examine how property markets are moving towards more sustainable outcomes, as defined by the UN sustainable development goals, and how policy can play a significant role in delivering a more sustainable future.

title: Social Interactive Experiences
description: This unit explores the methods and strategies for designing meaningful digital experiences that consider social connection, engagement and community. Building on foundational design principles and interaction design techniques, students will develop solutions that enhance social interaction while creating meaningful and beneficial experiences for users.

title: Statistical Inference
description: Point estimation. Properties of estimators - Fisher information. Bayesian inference and likelihood; Cramer Rao bound, consistency, sufficiency and Rao Blackwell theorem. Hypothesis testing: Neyman Pearson Lemma, likelihood ratio tests, power function and confidence tests. Review of matrix algebra random vectors and covariance matrices Multivariate normal and its associated distributions. Monte Carlo, boot strap and resampling methods. Estimation of regressions.

title: Special Topic in Clinical Education
description: Practicum experience that meets the requirements of the World Federation of Occupational Therapists. Integration of occupational therapy theoretical frameworks. Development of essential clinical and ethical reasoning. Practical demonstration of essential skills in planning, assessment, intervention, communication, documentation and management functions.

title: Advanced Japanese: Engagement with the Japanese Community
description: This unit develops high level of competence that enables advanced students to communicate with explicit knowledge of Japanese society and culture. Topics include current socio-cultural issues such as the decrease in the number of children, unsolved mysteries, and education problems. These skills would be demonstrated by application of complex vocabulary and grammatical techniques. The unit activities include organizing and presenting a video recorded speech in Japanese.

title: Style Hunting
description: This unit introduces students to the concepts of Cool Hunting & Trend Spotting within the context of contemporary culture. It involves research into major international social, cultural and economic factors affecting current and future changes in consumer behaviour. Students analyse the process of trend emergence and dissemination, looking at both street style, sub-cultural fashions and high end couture and designer driven fashions.

title: Indigenous Australian Professional Practice and Leadership
description: Development of professional behaviour and ethics as an Indigenous health professional in multi-disciplinary settings. Examination of Indigenous leadership in the context of health care including theoretical approaches to leadership and contemporary issues in relation to health care. Promotion of Indigenous self-determination and governance.

title: Clinical Pharmacotherapeutics
description: In this capstone unit, students integrate current knowledge and evidence in pharmacology and pharmacotherapy to manage a range of medical conditions and complications in specific patient groups. Students demonstrate their ability to consider the evidence behind both sides of an argument in complex patient cases with clinical uncertainty and work towards a collaborative solution. This unit comprises 4 modules: Paediatrics, Gender and Reproductive Health, Geriatrics and Nutrition.

title: Exercise Delivery
description: This unit aims to develop practical competencies in effective and safe exercise instruction for apparently healthy individuals and groups. Using hands-on, practical and authentic learning activities, students will have the opportunity to design, deliver, modify and monitor basic exercise interventions targeting a variety of exercise domains. A client-centred focus will be reinforced with a case-based approach to learning.

title: Systems Storytelling for Bioregional Impact
description: With a focus on Western Australia, Systems Thinking for Regional Impact allows you to develop a systems thinking approach, and learn deep mapping techniques, to understand the pivotal role of regions when addressing the world’s most complex environmental, societal, and governance (ESG) sustainability challenges. On completion of the unit, you will be equipped with knowledge and skills to understand complex challenges and how to build partnerships with regional, rural, and remote communities and industries to co-create regenerative strategies and solutions.

title: Topics in Medical Science
description: In this unit, students will continue to develop competencies in core aspects of Medical Science. The unit will encompass three modules: Professional Development, Molecular Pathology, and Analytical Techniques.

title: Health Sciences Studies Abroad Topic 2
description: Observation of specific activities in the field in both government and community settings, geopolitical, social and cultural issues in the particular field and comparison of activities in the participant's country of origin with those activities in the work experience location. A formal program and learning contract will be negotiated for each practicum or fieldwork offered. The purpose and objectives will vary depending upon the designated field experience, however, cultural implications of activities should be considered.

title: Contemporary Advertising Practice
description: This is a strategic advertising management unit exploring theories associated with and the socio-cultural influences on the development of marketing communication campaigns. Specifically, students will develop an understanding of the advertising industry and the way in which advertising agencies approach their craft, from taking into consideration brand positioning, through to understanding target audiences through to developing creative strategies. Students will also be exposed to contemporary issues impacting advertising agencies and their clients.

title: Adult Developmental Psychology
description: This unit follows on from PSYC2003 Child Development Psychology and explores the psychological development theories through adulthood. The development of cognitive, social and personality are examined. In addition this unit covers the psychology of vocation and career development; the role of family; death and dying; and mental health in older adults.

title: Energy Management and Climate Change
description: This unit introduces climate change issues and explores strategies for mitigation and energy management. The climate change section covers adaptation and mitigation to overcome the issues due to anthropogenic climate change, including the greenhouse effect, global warming, and sea-level rise. Carbon emission, reforestation, renewable energy, food security, water resources, and marine biodiversity at the local, regional and global levels will be examined. The relevant environmental policies and legislations will be highlighted in addressing the climate change issues to achieve sustainability. The energy management section covers the fundamentals of energy conservation and the key procedures for effective energy management, including energy audits, billing analysis, and economic assessment. It addresses energy management strategies for process industries and explores approaches such as energy integration, ways to create sustainable cities, and the adoption of new renewable energy sources.

title: Reflection and Research in Education
description: This unit will provide students with knowledge and skills of critical reflection and action research to support the transition into being education professionals. Critical reflective frameworks and the application of these will be explored. An action research plan will be devised based on a selected educational issue. The concepts of professional identity of educators, resilience and wellbeing will be examined and a toolkit of resources to support growth in these areas will be developed.

title: Animal Diversity and Evolution
description: Investigates the diversity of animal life, both invertebrate and vertebrate in their phylogenetic context. The taxonomy, evolutionary background, anatomy, ecology, ethology (vertebrates) and physiology of the major groups of animals are examined. The unit highlights the integration of structure and function and examines patterns of organisation from an evolutionary perspective. Specialisations and adaptations of animals to their environment will be investigated in lectures and laboratory sessions, to enable students to appreciate the wide diversity of biological mechanisms, processes and responses found in the Animal Kingdom.

title: Visualisation and Communication of Health Data
description: This unit will provide student with the opportunity to practice effective communication of health data across different media types. Students will analyse how individuals and groups process visual information. They will be introduced to a range of data visualisations techniques in order to create appropriate and reproducible representations of health data. Students will also explore the needs of audiences ranging from lay audiences to professional groups.

title: Earth Resources and Sustainability
description: Earth’s resources are essential in supporting human life – from the water we drink and the soil in which we grow our food, the fossil fuel we burn to keep ourselves warm and maintain industrial activities to the periodic table we employ for the vehicles and electronics of our modern, globalised, and fast-paced digital world, including the entire house we live in. In this unit, we will explore various geological resources that support society and entire economies and consider how these finite resources can be managed sustainably in a changing world. Topics include the key earth resources and their geological context - what they are, where we find and how we exploit them; energy transitions – from fossil fuels to a low carbon world based on renewable technologies; weighing up costs vs benefits in resource exploitation; and the impact to the environment and its sustainable management. Students will work across theoretical lectures and practical workshops to identify environmental, social and governance issues (ESG) in earth resource exploration and extraction, and evaluate and develop solutions to these key challenges that will allow human progress in the 21st century. It won't come as a surprise that this unit covers more than half of the 17 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) as core content: SDG3 (health), SDG6 (clean water), SDG7 (clean energy), SDG9 (sustainable infrastructure), SDG11 (sustainable cities), SDG12 (responsible consumption), SDG13 (climate action), SDG14 (life below water), and SDG15 (life on land).

title: Urban Regeneration
description: The evolution of contemporary cities and the impact of change on land use, structure and functions of cities. Heritage and cultural planning. Methods of urban renewal and role of redevelopment agencies.

title: Clinical Medical Imaging Practice 5
description: This unit provides authentic medical imaging professional practice experience in the clinical setting, at the level appropriate for the advanced beginner/competent reflective professional. Students will have the opportunity to advance their capacity for culturally safe practice.

title: Business Web and Mobile Technologies
description: In this unit, students will learn to design, develop, and evaluate effective business websites and mobile applications using modern technologies. Through practical projects and real-world examples, students will gain project management experience and develop professional skills sought after by employers. By analysing stakeholder needs, students will create user-friendly designs that meet business requirements. In the unit, students will have the opportunity to select and integrate technologies to present business data visually across websites and mobile apps. Students will also evaluate current and emerging web and mobile technologies, making informed recommendations. Upon completion, students will possess a skill set that includes communication, digital proficiency, and the ability to apply knowledge to solve business challenges creatively. This unit emphasises industry relevance and career readiness, preparing students to become globally engaged professionals in the field of business web and mobile technologies.

title: Foundations of Pathology
description: The unit covers the basic mechanisms of disease that include a series of lectures, tutorials and online practical sessions made up of three modules, Cellular pathology, System pathology and Neoplasia. Module one covers cell injury/death including apoptosis, atrophy, hypertrophy, and necrosis. Module two covers organ system pathology in respiratory, GIT and cardiovascular organs. Module three is an introduction to carcinogenesis, covering benign and malignant entities. The relationship of pathology to laboratory diagnostic testing will be utilised through the tutorial sessions within the unit.

title: Collaborative Theatre Practice
description: This unit investigates how collaborative theatre practice has evolved through a focus on Greek theatre, Commedia dell'arte, and Shakespeare. The student will consider cultural and performance contexts, performative processes and skills within the original context as well as contemporary approaches. The student will be introduced to dramaturgical principles and processes to support their own collaborative practice. They will generate production concepts for contemporary versions or adaptations of the original texts.

title: Principles and Practices of Counselling
description: Exploration of the current psychological and counselling theories necessary to develop a successful counselling relationship. This includes the methods used to work professionally and ethically in support of a culturally safe and secure environment for clients. Students develop an applied understanding of counselling skills, with attention to self-awareness, reflecting the influence of values, attitudes, personal biases and power relations in the counselling space. Students will also develop their knowledge and skills to conduct culturally safe basic interviews, assessment in counselling sessions and ongoing support within a multidisciplinary setting.

title: Molecular Cytogenetics and Diagnostics
description: Students will learn basic identification of all chromosomes in the human genome, laboratory techniques for culture and preparation of human tissues for cytogenetic studies, and methods used to identify and analyse molecular and cytogenetic alterations. In addition, students will learn about molecular and cytogenetic mechanisms of disease expression, and how these relate to clinical phenotype. Molecular and cytogenetic changes in cancer will also be discussed.

title: Business and Law International Study Abroad 2
description: International mobility experience for undergraduate students.

title: Geophysics Project
description: In this unit, you will apply industry-standard geophysical methods in "real world" settings by completing a range of geophysical surveys and by writing a report summarising the project background, including health, safety and environment requirements, the problems addressed, data acquisition methodologies, data processing approaches, data analysis, interpretation methodology and project outcomes.

title: Communication Skills for Educators
description: This unit is designed to introduce you to the learning, thinking and communication processes you need to succeed in your studies as an education undergraduate at Curtin University. The unit will develop skills in research, thinking critically and reflecting on your personal levels of literacy and numeracy competencies in preparation for the LANTITE. You will be encouraged to write at the required university standard and communicate effectively in the academic and professional context of teacher professional standards.

title: Environmental and Groundwater Geophysics
description: This unit examines how geophysical methods help resolve global food, environmental and water supply challenges. Digital versions of complex groundwater and environmental systems are needed to understand/ balance current and future needs. Effects of lakes, rivers, the seawater interface, groundwater flow and hydrodynamics in large basins wioll be examined. Attention will be paid to define seawater interface, environmental applications, methods used in aquifer replenishment, building basin scale groundwater models, methods for geological sequestration of CO2, characterization for mine tailings and soil classification for agriculture/engineering.

title: Energy Storage
description: This unit introduces students to energy storage forms and systems and provides a broad understanding and appreciation of the scientific principles that underpin the operation of such systems. The emphasis is on energy storage in the form of electron, gas, liquids and solids at different scales. This unit introduces energy storage for power systems, overview of energy storage technologies, e.g., thermal, mechanical, chemical, electrochemical efficiency of energy storage systems. This unit highlights the storage for renewable energy systems in a sustainable manner, e.g., solar energy, wind energy, pumped hydro energy, fuel cells, energy storage in micro-grid and smart grid, and scalable and large-scale energy storage of hydrogen energy. Smaller energy storage systems are also discussed for benchmarking and comparison, with consideration for the opportunities and impacts on First Nations people.. Topics covered include electrical, chemical, thermal, mechanical, electrochemical, thermochemical and thermomechanical energy storage systems as well as grid integration issues.

title: Neuroanatomy
description: Gross organisation of the human brain in relation to its embryological development; Functional anatomy of the musculoskeletal structures, viscera and nerves of the cranium; Investigation of the neural systems that serve the senses and command voluntary movement; How changes to the internal and external environment influences the brain; Exploration of the neurobiology of human behaviour. Integration of the role of structures of the head with human development and survival. Neurovascular and musculoskeletal components of the head are explored, with reference to functional control mechanisms.

title: Extended Cyber Crime and Security Enhanced Programming
description: The most common threats to a system ranging from organised attacks to viruses and malware. This unit provides the knowledge needed to handle these threats with a focus on major network threats and vulnerabilities to an enterprise network as well as covering detailed knowledge of computer forensics (both approaches and tools) for Linux/Windows. Approaches used in massed network attacks and evaluate the methods to address these types of attacks. The basis of viruses and malware and security deficiencies that are typically exploited by viruses and web based malware. In the last part of the unit, the student will cover in detail the tools available under Windows and Unix based systems to detect and trace hacking attacks.

title: Applied Laboratory Medicine Practice 1
description: Seven weeks of supervised professional practice in a 'National Association of Testing Authorities' (NATA) accredited medical laboratory. Students will undertake discipline specific clinical laboratory placement gaining competency, skills and knowledge in the systems and processes documented in the laboratory’s Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) related to a discipline specific set of elements outlined in Unit 3 of the Competency based standards for Medical Scientists published in Dec 2009.

title: Negotiation, Mediation and Advocacy
description: This unit will develop students’ theoretical understandings of dispute resolution approaches, negotiation and advocacy in the area of employment relations. The unit also develops students as practitioners with the practical skills and knowledge to navigate disputes consistent with best practice and the legislation.

title: Pharmacy Practice 4
description: In this unit, students further develop effective inter- and intra-professional communication in relation to patients with complex histories. Students learn to accurately perform complex pharmaceutical calculations and medicines reconciliation, and to research and interpret medical information including therapeutic guidelines, medical notes, and the National Inpatient Medical Chart. This unit covers the diversification of pharmacists' roles, including rural pharmaceutical services (including to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander peoples) and the provision of Mental Health First Aid. Clinical, ethical, and legal reasoning in complex clinical cases, pharmacoeconomic decision-making, and the evaluation and application of risk management strategies in complex cases form important elements of this unit.

title: Creating and Responding to Literature
description: This unit is one of a set of 3 undergraduate option units to prepare Initial Teacher Educators (ITE) to specialise in teaching literacy and English. This unit introduces a range of literary texts applicable to students from Foundation to Year 10, including: short stories, novels, poetry, prose, plays, film and multimodal texts, in spoken, print and digital online form. The unit explores how texts reflect the historical and socio-cultural context of their creation and how different readers respond to them through the lenses of their own personal and socio-cultural context. The text–to-life and life-to-text significance of literature will be explored. In addition to the analysis of linguistic, literary and multimodal devices available to authors, students will investigate how these devices are applied in the process of textual creation. A diverse range of texts, valued for their aesthetic, social and cultural significance, will be at the heart of the unit and will include literature spanning from Australia (including the oral traditions and written texts of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders); Asia and the world, as well as sustainability. The unit will explore the dynamic, constantly evolving and polysemic nature of genres of literature.                  The expectation is that students will have completed two mandatory (non-option) units in English/Literacy before taking this unit.

title: Technology, Innovation and Societies
description: This unit explores the relationship between society and technology, equipping students with theoretical tools to critically analyse digital innovation and its social impact. Drawing on theories of the social shaping of technology, students will apply these to real-world case studies, exploring how social, political, and economic forces shape technological development and innovation. The unit covers historical and contemporary examples of innovation, disruption, and crises, enabling students to assess the wider implications of emerging technologies. Through the assessments, students learn to present well-researched arguments and communicate their analysis of socio-technological developments to diverse audiences, preparing them to contribute thoughtfully to the future of digital and social media communication.

title: Integrated Medical Science
description: Students in this unit will analyse genomic test results via the evaluation of symptoms, contemporary databases, variant pathogenicity, literature and biochemical pathways, in order to generate probable outcomes of clinical/diagnostic/biological significance. Develop and enhance critical thinking capabilities by applying inherent laboratory knowledge and skills to the analysis, evaluation and review of scientific literature and other sources of information, with the intention of developing new ideas, engaging in creative thinking/innovation as well as the promotion of socially responsible communication/truth telling.

title: Principles and Practice of Anatomical Pathology
description: This unit prepares students for employment in a contemporary anatomical pathology laboratory. Students will engage with the principles of how anatomical pathology is used in the investigation of disorders of health and understand the features of normal structures and alterations resultant from underlying pathophysiological changes. Students learn a range of intermediate skills regarding the preparation of cells, fluids and tissue for microscopy and allied histology and cytology investigations

title: Advanced Drilling Engineering
description: The role of advanced drilling in petroleum development including: Casing design, cement and cementing equipment, pore and fracture pressure gradients, directional drilling, offshore drilling and well control.

title: Integrated Speech Pathology Professional Practice
description: This unit will provide students with the opportunity to demonstrate integration of the theoretical, and practical knowledge acquired during the course, and consider this in light of legislative and ethical complexities. The unit will also prepare graduates to work within a range of contemporary settings.

title: Classical Mechanics and Quantum Physics
description: This unit will apply the Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formalism to Classical Mechanics and Quantum Physics. Applications include to circular and oscillatory motion, and an introduction to treating systems on a very small scale. The theoretical component will be supplemented by related experimental techniques.

title: Medicine 5
description: This unit builds on the knowledge, skills and attitudes developed over the previous four years of the course in a series of work based clinical placements with an emphasis on pre-intern training to be fully work ready on graduation. Students will develop a competent level of practice demonstrating skill development and an integrated body of knowledge derived from the physical, biological, behavioural and social sciences. Students will show empathy for patients and have recognition of their own limitations. The placements will enable students to integrate health promotion and disease prevention with the management of illness and injury as well as give consideration to patient safety and quality of care. In the unit, students will learn to practise with due regard to available resources and cost effective measures in a manner which encourages patients to assume increasing responsibility for their own health and to participate in decisions about their health care. Students will understand the need for lifelong learning in the practice of medicine and medical education including further training and medical research.

title: Advanced Biomedical Science Honours
description: Students will undertake original research and gain in-depth knowledge in a particular field of biomedical and/or clinical science under the guidance of an academic supervisor. Students will learn and be assessed on their scientific communication skills in both oral and written presentations of their research. Through the year-long program, students will gain understanding of biomedical or clinical science research, and develop their ability to evaluate literature, perform independent research, identify and solve complex issues, and communicate effectively. Emphasis will also be placed on developing research skills applicable across the healthcare sector and by Medical graduates in diverse clinical environments, including general practice and/or rural or remote locations. Examples of such research skills include epidemiology, population studies and clinical data analysis. The research skills developed within this program will provide an attractive credential for students seeking employment in the public or private sectors, and will ensure they are highly competitive for entry into a higher degree research program.

title: Medical Radiation Pathology 1
description: The section of introductory pathology covers disease and body defence mechanisms, carcinogenesis and neoplasia. The section of systematic pathology deals with the musculoskeletal, respiratory and cardiovascular systems. Various 2D and 3D imaging modalities including general x-ray, ultrasound, computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging that are commonly used in clinical practice for making diagnoses are presented and compared. The evaluation of disease processes on medical images enables medical radiation science professionals to identify and act on urgent/unexpected findings and gives them the ability to provide an informed opinion to a medical practitioner based on their knowledge of the scientific explanations underpinning disease and injuries affecting the human body.

title: Food Safety and Microbiology
description: This unit examines the source, types, growth and effects of microbes in food and their impact on food safety, food processing and preservation. Food-borne pathogens and the epidemiology of food-borne illness. Procedures for monitoring, food recall and general procedures of food hygiene. The principles of hazard assessment critical control point (HACCP). Local, national and international standards, statutes and codes.

title: Professional Practice in Employment Relations
description: This unit allows the student to put into practice the learning they have gained in the course of their degree studies and helps prepare them for the challenges ahead in their chosen career. The student is required to conduct a project with a relevant workplace, and submit a written report upon completion of the professional placement. It offers an opportunity for some guided independent study in a real workplace setting.

title: Culinary Nutrition Practice
description: In this unit, students will learn the principles of culinary nutrition, focusing on the integration of nutrition science with culinary practices. Students will gain practical knowledge and skills in food selection, preparation, and cooking aimed at enhancing the sensory appeal of meals while improving health outcomes. Through a “farm to fork” approach, the unit will also explore factors that influence food choices, examining food systems and food production through to sustainable consumption, household food waste, and the impact on climate.

title: Introduction to Tort Law
description: This unit introduces the basic principles of negligence, trespass and workers compensation law. It also develops oral communication skills necessary for lawyers, including small group presentations, oral argument, and client interviewing.

title: Multimedia News Production
description: This unit underpins the production of the student news website The Western Independent. Working collaboratively and independently students will undertake roles as reporters, producers and editorial leaders in a converged, dynamic, newsroom environment.

title: Interior Architecture Practice 1
description: This unit introduces the reality of contemporary professional practice, and allows students to consider and prepare for opportunities for future industry employment. Contemporary local, national and international transdisciplinary realities of Interior Architecture practice are the foci of this unit, which investigates and simulates real-life issues, complexities and opportunities in practice. The challenge is to work effectively within a group to meet the brief while at the same time producing individual output which mirrors authentic design practice.

title: Introduction to Screenwriting
description: The unit examines screenwriting techniques and practices in how to develop and create a narrative screenplay for drama production.

title: Introduction to Energy Engineering
description: This unit introduces important concepts related to energy, including the definition of energy and its different forms, units of energy, energy conversion and efficiency, magnitudes of energy and energy density; current patterns and trends in energy consumption; key sources of available energy; introduction of methods for the generation of energy including fossil fuels, geothermal energy, biomass and biofuels, solar energy, wind energy, ocean energy, hydropower, nuclear energy, natural hydrogen, salinity gradient potential; assessment of relative advantages and drawbacks of the energy sources available; impacts of different energy sources on society, environment, economy and articulate sensitivity towards the First Nations on energy policy and program.

title: Planning for Sustainable Urban Development
description: The examination of sustainability principles and urban form, including the study of interest groups, sustainable development , global and local environmental issues and responses, policies and agreements, indicators and audits.

title: Health Promotion in Action
description: Practical introduction to health promotion projects, steps involved in planning, implementation and evaluation of a project. Conducting surveys. Practical implementation and evaluation of the use of appropriate individual, group and population strategies for health promotion interventions. Meetings. Working in groups, work integrated learning, reflective practice.

title: Industrial Modelling and Optimisation
description: This unit considers optimisation problems arising in the industry. The students will learn the necessary skills to model the problems mathematically and solve them using operations research techniques. The unit focuses on the industry problems that can be formulated as integer programming models. The topics covered include problem formulation, solution methods, and the use of a mathematical solver.1-	Problem formulation: Formulating business problems (such as facility location, production planning, workforce scheduling and supply chain) as integer programming models.2-	Solution methods: Simplex, dual simplex, simplex method for upper-bounded variables, branch and bound, and cutting planes.3-	Solver implementation: Python and one integer programming solver such as CBC, Gurobi, or Cplex.

title: Fundamentals of Thermodynamics
description: The objective of this unit is to learn the basic concepts of thermodynamics and apply them to relevant mechanical engineering situations. Initially, students will learn the fundamental concepts of thermodynamic systems and control volumes to analyse closed and open systems. This will be followed by the derivation of mathematical relations for various thermodynamic properties of pure substances and ideal gases. Analysis of the interactions between work and heat flow leads into the First Law of Thermodynamics, considered for both closed systems (non-flow energy equation) and open systems (steady flow energy equation). Finally, students will be introduced to the Second Law of Thermodynamics using the concepts of heat engines and heat pumps, considering reversibility and irreversibility of processes, the Clausius Inequality, entropy and measure of irreversibility.

title: Advanced Anatomical Pathology
description: This unit involves the advanced study of cytology and histopathology and builds on the knowledge and skills introduced on clinical placement. It covers the pathogenesis and a range of diagnostic cellular features of benign, inflammatory and neoplastic conditions in major body systems. Ancillary testing including special stains, immunohistochemical and molecular methods for the purpose of diagnosis and clinical patient management are introduced.

title: Child Language Disorders
description: This unit develops students’ competence in applying theoretical knowledge and the evidence base in interpreting and reporting assessment data, and planning intervention for children with developmental communication disorders from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds. It also introduces students to the process of evaluating the effectiveness of intervention.

title: Medical Radiation Science Research Methodologies
description: Students will learn about the common types of medical radiation science research and their associated methodologies. This will include major stages of conducting research including literature review, topic formulation, proposal development, ethics and other clearances, data collection and analysis, results presentation and dissemination of outcomes. Research critique and application of findings for evidence-based practice in medical radiation science will also be covered in this unit.

title: Introduction to Digital Creative Practice
description: This unit provides a comprehensive introduction to the various cognate disciplines within the digital creative industry. Students will explore the contributions of influential practitioners and significant milestones that have shaped these disciplines. They will identify and analyse roles, principles, techniques, and approaches pertinent to their specific interests within the digital creative sector. Additionally, students will engage in prototyping creative outcomes using methodologies and tools relevant to fields such as animation, motion graphics, game design, and digital user experience. The curriculum emphasises the foundational principles of digital design that are integral to these mediums. Through this, students will develop a nuanced understanding of how to effectively engage and communicate with audiences in their creative roles and determine the most appropriate contexts for employing these principles.

title: Professional Practice in Urban and Regional Planning 1
description: Explore institutions and principles governing professional conduct in planning practice, and develop specific professional communication skills applied in industry.

title: Technologies: Coding for Teachers
description: This unit is one in a suite of three undergraduate Option units designed to provide a specialisation in the use of technologies for learning and learning design. This unit aims to develop a student’s content and pedagogical knowledge related to using coding as part of the Technologies curriculum. Students will cultivate content knowledge through developing an understanding of computational thinking, sequence, branching, and iteration as they design algorithms and code their solutions using programming environments commonly used in schools. Pedagogical content knowledge will be developed through students developing learning–experience implementation plans in the Technologies area for their own future students and appropriate to their degree (i.e. early childhood, primary or secondary).

title: Introduction to Nutrition Science
description: Introduction to Nutrition Science provides a foundational understanding of the scientific principles that underpin human nutrition. The unit examines dietary guidelines, nutrient reference values, and food and nutrition policies that shape public health recommendations. Students will explore components of food, their physiological roles, and the biological processes involved in digestion and absorption. The unit also introduces methods for assessing dietary intake and the broader implications of nutrition for individual health, sustainability, and career pathways in nutrition and health sciences.

title: Editing
description: This unit provides a practical introduction to editing. Students learn about the editor’s role and profession, the publishing process, and editorial project management; and they learn and practice the skills needed for professional proofreading and copyediting, including language skills, on the page and the screen. Student learning is graduated through a series of successively higher-level editing tasks, which students practice thoroughly in workshops, and are assessed in before moving to a higher level.

title: Industrial Ecology
description: The course is broadly organised in four learning units, with some unavoidable overlap between them (see also annex I) 1. Industrial Ecology: a discipline based on parallels: the roots of the recent steep rise in interest for Industrial Ecology are investigated, and the scope of Industrial Ecology is explored by looking at specific features in which it augments the mainstream interpretation of Cleaner Production and Eco-Efficiency. Furthermore, this learning unit focuses on the parallel between natural and industrial ecology, i.e. co-location of (processing) industries to achieve regional resource efficiency synergies in Eco Industrial Parks in which the waste of one facility becomes input to another facility (this is also known as Industrial Symbiosis). 2. Indicators, Conditions and Objectives: carrying capacity is another fundamental concept in natural ecology. It is also used in Industrial Ecology to set the direction for sustainable production and consumption. This learning unit starts with a discussion of indicators for carrying capacity, based on the material and energy flows in a society. 3. Sustainable Use of Materials and Technology: material flows (and the embodied energy contained therein) drive the industrial ecosystem and technology is being employed to alter and transform material flows for the benefit of society. 4. Sustainable Societies and Communities: this learning unit covers blueprints for equitable management of material and energy resources and flows by societies and communities. It also covers the results of recent global sustainability assessments of selected industry sectors, to investigate how sectors like mining, minerals and transport can best contribute to achieving the sustainable development of the communities they operate in.

title: Planning for Housing
description: An appreciation of the social, cultural and economic dynamics underpinning housing policy and the housing market in general. Exploration of the strategic and statutory planning instruments affecting housing.

title: Literacy and Numeracy for First Nations Peoples of Australia
description: This unit is one of three offered in the Literacy and Numeracy in Diverse Populations suite in the undergraduate Bachelor of Education course. Completing three of these units will provide graduates with a specialisation in this area. This unit has a focus on and embraces the histories, cultures, linguistic and social aspects that impact First Nations students’ literacy and numeracy learning in today’s classrooms. Students will examine a variety of strategies to effectively engage First Nations learners in literacy and numeracy learning with a focus on pedagogy that recognises the importance of place and community.

title: Integrated Pharmacology and Therapeutics 3
description: In this unit, students learn about the pathophysiology, pharmacology and pharmacotherapy for the management of respiratory, musculoskeletal, endocrine, inflammatory gastrointestinal and skin disorders, anaemia, and the use of antineoplastic agents in the treatment of cancers. The unit will focus on the application of current evidence to resolve clinical problems. The unit comprises 6 modules. Module 1: Respiratory disorders including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and pneumonia. Module 2: Musculoskeletal disorders including rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis and gout. Module 3: Conditions associated with the endocrine system including thyroid and adrenal disorders. Module 4: Cancers and complications with use of antineoplastic agents. Module 5: Inflammatory gastrointestinal disorders, and anaemia. Module 6: Skin conditions including psoriasis, acne, herpes zoster and drug eruptions.

title: Curriculum and Instruction Senior Secondary: Health and Physical Education
description: This unit is designed to prepare pre-service teachers to teach the Senior Secondary Health and Physical Education curriculum. The focus of the unit is on curriculum planning, teaching strategies, assessment, reporting, the demonstration of positive impact on student learning and research relating to Senior Secondary Health and Physical Education (HPE). The unit examines moderation, the provision of feedback and responding to individual student needs. It will explore learning practices to support and challenge a diverse student cohort.

title: Advanced Animation Studio
description: This unit provides students with an opportunity to further develop their skills and conceptual approach in the areas of animation, 3D and motion graphics. It encourages students to explore established conventions, visual styles, animation techniques, audio design, narrative structures, and screen language in their own work.

title: Introduction to Mining and Digital Applications
description: In this unit students will be introduced to the concepts of ‘value chain’ and ‘life of mine’ and will learn about main mining methods currently used in the industry and how they evolved over time. They will also gain an understanding of how new approaches to the collection and use of data are transforming mining across the value chain. Students will be introduced to the use of advanced sensor data analytics to inform decision-making in the mining context. There will also be opportunities to learn about state-of-the-art developments in digital mining systems through field visits and engagement with industry experts.

title: Introduction to Innovation Principles
description: We are in the midst of a technological revolution that integrates billions of people and devices into interconnected systems, where emergent ideas create value and resolve constraints, and where new opportunities arise. This technological revolution underlines the importance of innovation within our society. This foundation unit provides a systems approach to innovation investigating the underlying innovation principles and contexts within which innovation occurs, types of and approaches to innovation, and development of innovation and technological capabilities and mindset in the age of the Fourth Industrial Revolution. This knowledge will help you understand and later apply the underlying principles that drive technological and social progress and the development of a GRIT (global, responsible, innovative and technology) mindset.

title: Technology and Dress
description: Examines the relationship between technology, design and application. Technology relevant to fashion design is introduced and allows students to creatively explore the process and the resulting impact on aesthetics.

title: Foundations of Physiotherapy Practice
description: This unit aims to develop student physiotherapists’ professionalism, agency and identity within an inter-professional setting, through the application of professional skills and problem solving within varied settings. Students will learn to adapt their communication and clinical reasoning for an individual with pain and inflammation, whilst maintaining a person-centred approach. Students will develop their ability to safely assist individuals during more complex movement tasks and in more diverse settings.

title: Geodata Processing
description: In this unit students will solve basic and advanced spatial problems with computer programming. The unit is structured as follows: identified spatial problems will be investigated, structured into smaller problems, and for each problem students will design and implement a computer program as a solution. In this unit students will learn the algorithmic fundamentals, data manipulation techniques and approach to translate their algorithms into a computer language. In addition, students will learn how to debug a program written in the selected language.

title: Screening and Diagnostics for Midwives
description: This unit covers screening and diagnostics informed by comprehensive, relevant and holistic health assessment and Diagnostics Reasoning. There is a focus on accountable clinical practice for ordering and interpretation of radiological and laboratory tests informed by legislation, regulations, evidence and scope of practice. Clinical decision-making is informed by cultural and socioeconomic factors.

title: Interpretation and Machine Learning in Geophysics
description: Interpretation of geophysical data is needed to; (i) construct an accurate, high value representation of the subsurface or (ii) achieved an environmental, engineering or exploration objective. A core element of this unit is seismic interpretation. Students will learn theoretical and applied seismic interpretation. Students will learn to interpret 2D and 3D seismic data in a number of settings with state of the art software. Modern geophysical acquisition systems are able to stream tremendous quantities of data from conventional or new distributed sensor systems. At the same time machine learning is becoming an integral part of interpretation. This unit will also cover methods of interpretation of seismic, electromagnetic and potential field data and introduce application of machine learning that involve integration of multiple geoscience data sets

title: International Political Economy
description: The unit studies the role of political and economic relations between states, between non-state actors (NGOs, community groups, business) and between states and non-state actors in the creation and maintenance of global economic, financial and environmental structures and policy. Topics include theoretical approaches to IPE, international trade, the global financial system, the integrating power of information technologies, the relationship between states, markets and communities, global environmental governance regimes, environmental sustainability and global population and demographic trends, the role of international institutions, theories of accumulations, and the political economy of international development. The unit will be comparative and draw on case materials from a wide range of societies and states.

title: Medical Anatomy
description: Medical Anatomy integrates surface anatomy and 2D imaging of head, trunk and limbs into a 3D understanding of body structure and organ relationships. In this unit bones, joints, muscles, nerves and blood vessels are explored to learn how they function and are related in 3 dimensions. Correct use of anatomical terminology will be used to examine and communicate anatomical structures, positions and movement. An understanding of the role of anatomical features will help predict function and relate underlying anatomical structures to surface anatomy for clinical examination and imaging.

title: Applied Research and Biostatistics
description: In this applied research and biostatistics unit, students will learn ethical application of mixed research methodologies. You will learn to critically evaluate scientific evidence provided by the scientific community alongside evidence created elsewhere, such as Artificial Intelligence. Working in groups to review scientific evidence and apply ethical considerations and statistical reasoning, you will identify research gaps and design a research proposal that assesses research hypotheses related to an area of the United Nation Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDG), such as food produce, improved nutrition, sustainable food consumption (UN SDG2); mental health, accidents prevention, tobacco control (UN SDG3); low carbon, sustainable energy use (UN SDG7); and food waste, electric vehicles, recycling, reduce waste generation/wasteful consumption (UN SDG12). You will learn to prepare UN SDG-related data in an appropriate format to suit the requirement of certain statistical packages and test the proposed quantitative research questions using appropriate techniques, such as regression models. Finally, you will practise interpreting and communicating your findings that provides answer(s) to progressing the UN SDG.

title: Intermediate Japanese: Everyday Contexts
description: This unit has an emphasis on the interactive use of the Japanese language and is aimed at increasing student communicative competence in listening, speaking, reading and writing. It provides students with opportunities to establish essential skills with a focus on practical, everyday use of the Japanese language. Students are able to compare and contrast Japanese culture with their own, and other cultures through situating the use of the Japanese language in relevant social and cultural contexts.

title: Physical Activity, Exercise and Fitness Assessment
description: This unit builds on an understanding of the fundamentals of physiology and develops students' knowledge of physical activity and exercise and their relationship to individuals and populations health. The knowledge and skills gained through this unit will enable students to assess an individual’s physical fitness safely, analyse and interpret results and provide basic exercise prescription based on current physical activity guidelines and practices and explain the rationale.

title: Graphic Design 4
description: A focus on research and visual development, production techniques and professional practice that will produce relevant solutions to graphic design problems. Graphic design practice will include understanding the relationship between problem-solving and idea generation as well as applying design principles to create solutions. This unit will also deal with presentation practices including the designer/client relationship. Projects undertaken in this unit will form part of a graduate portfolio.

title: Quantitative Methods for Business Research
description: This unit aims to provide students with foundational knowledge to develop their own learning process to acquire data analysis and data analytics techniques as required. It exposes students to common quantitative techniques in business research including elements in regression analysis, multivariate analysis, discrete choice models, structural equation modelling and other techniques in supervised and unsupervised learning. These elements will be demonstrated via practical examples using open source software, such as R, Python or Julia. It will also cover issues surrounding research data best practice, such as the FAIR principle and other related topics in data science.

title: Introduction to Geophysical Exploration Methods
description: This unit provides an introduction to geophysics, which is the main technique used to investigate the physical nature of the ground directly beneath the Earth's surface and consequently is a valuable tool for the non-invasive exploration of the Earth's sub-surface. This unit provides students with basic knowledge about the theory and application of the magnetic, gravity, seismic, electrical, electromagnetic, radiometric and borehole geophysical methods for exploration. Students will undertake and be assessed on appropriate laboratory and practical activities to acquire geophysical data relevant geophysical equipment; and apply geophysical processing, analysis and interpretation techniques using relevant software.

title: Advanced Concrete Design and Construction
description: This unit focuses on the design and construction of advanced concrete sections. The topics include basic concept of prestressing, prestressing technology, capacity of prestressed concrete sections, post tensioned slabs, composite concrete sections, design and construction integration. Computer software is used for analysis and design of advanced concrete structures.

title: Landscapes, Soils and Surface Environments
description: Landscapes, soils and surface environments shape the ecosystems that we depend on, playing a critical role in sustaining biodiversity, regulating climate, and supporting human life. Via class and field activities, this unit will equip students with an understanding of landscape processes, focusing on soil formation, hydrology, ecosystem functions, and their spatial variation. Students will explore how soil, water, and vegetation interact in shaping landscapes and regulating key processes such as carbon storage and nutrient cycling. Climate change and its impact on landscape resilience and environmental systems will also be addressed, alongside techniques for monitoring change, and the importance of integrating country-appropriate cultural approaches for sustainable land management.

title: Advanced Biomedical Science Research Project 1
description: Students will further develop and contextualise foundational research, critical analysis, evaluation and formal research skills within the biomedical sciences. They will develop competence in exploring and applying analytical and research skills whilst evaluating literature of a relevant topic. Students will consolidate their scientific written and verbal communication skills, in both individual and group work.

title: Agricultural Production Systems
description: This unit examines animal and plant production as both integrated and separate systems, emphasising production and management principles. It focuses on the application of scientific principles to cropping and animal management and production systems. Knowledge will be developed in the context of the animal production and crop production year through workshops, discussions and field visits.

title: Architecture Design Studio 3B - Civic
description: This studio is the capstone design unit being the culmination of the architectural studios for the Bachelor of Applied Science. It explores a civic building of medium rise complexity and scale. The unit emphasises the integration of architectural, cultural and technological considerations like structure, services, envelop and environmental strategies in relation to site. Work integrated learning is incorporated through a range of strategies and decision making processes pertinent to design and construction in architectural practice.

title: Safety and Environmental Health Law
description: The common law legal system, including parliamentary, government and court systems. Specific areas of law in Western Australia including negligence, employer's liability for injuries to workers, workers compensation, occupational health and safety laws and environmental laws.

title: Business Clinic
description: The FBL Business Clinic is an experiential, Practice-Based Learning (PBL) and Work Integrated Learning (WIL) unit where students will have the opportunity to engage in real-world business consulting for eligible clients, including individuals, small businesses, and startups. Through hands-on experience in the clinic, students will develop their understanding of key business concepts, problem-solving techniques, and ethical decision-making, gaining valuable insights into the challenges and opportunities of modern business practice. By working directly with clients, students will be better prepared to navigate the complexities of the business world upon graduation.

title: Project Risk and Development Appraisal
description: This unit introduces students to building and infrastructure project development processes as well as urban planning processes. This will include project finance and appraisal methods, financial feasibility analysis of project development, risk management, life cycle costing principles and practice.

title: Bioprocess Engineering
description: This unit applies engineering principles to biological systems and emphasizes the integration of biology and chemical engineering.  Important biological concepts most relevant to bioprocessing are introduced. These include enzymes, cell growth and metabolic pathways. The basic concepts and kinetics of enzymes, enzyme inhibition and immobilization will be examined. Engineering principles are applied to bioprocesses for the purpose of selection, design, scale up, control, and operation of bioreactors as well as downstream processing; that is, the separation and purification of the bio- products.

title: Perception
description: The biological and psychological basis of perception. Students are introduced to traditional as well as contemporary theories of perception and action.

title: Relativistic Astrophysics and Cosmology
description: This unit begins with a detailed, mathematical treatment of Einstein's special theory of relativity and its implications for observational astronomy. These include apparent superluminal motion in the jets of active galactic nuclei, Doppler boosting, stellar aberration and so on. This leads into a qualitative description of the structure of space-time and Einstein's general theory of relativity. Basic concepts such as the space-time metric and its curvature in the presence of mass or energy are introduced, but detailed mathematical details are left for 4th year units. Various cosmological concepts are discussed, including how the ultimate fate of the universe is linked to its energy density. Current models of the evolution of the universe are explored, including the idea of an inflationary period shortly after the big bang. Observational measurements of the rate of expansion of the universe throughout its history are discussed, including recent evidence that suggests the rate of expansion is accelerating.Sources of uncertainty in these data are also considered.

title: Computer Graphics
description: The unit is an introductory unit on computer graphics concepts and techniques. It covers fundamental knowledge on modelling, transformation and rendering for computer generation of three dimensional graphics. The contents of the unit include 2D & 3D transformations, projection, OpenGL introduction, graphical objects representation, visible surface detection, illumination & shading, texture mapping, and virtual & augmented reality.

title: Accounting Modelling and Data Visualisation
description: In this unit, students will develop practical data analytic and visualisation skills using advanced functions of Excel, Microsoft Power BI and Tableau. Students will learn project management skills and develop interactive dashboards that can support problem-solving and decision making.

title: Advanced Digital Media Planning
description: This advanced unit is designed to give insight and hands on experience in the area of digital communication planning, where students use data, together with their knowledge of digital media platforms to engage in communication planning.  The advanced nature of this unit encourages students to integrate their previous digital knowledge with insight from industry database(s) to plan and implement and track a digital communication campaign.

title: Agriculture and Food Science Dissertation
description: Students will conduct an independent research project under the guidance of an academic supervisor, resulting in the preparation, submission, presentation and defence of a dissertation. Students will develop research, technical, professional and communication skills along with specialised discipline knowledge through a process of inquiry. Completing their dissertation will involve critical review of scientific literature, the formulation of research questions and hypotheses, selection of appropriate methodology and experimental design, social and ethical consideration of the research process; collection, analysis and interpretation of scientific data, and effective scientific writing to produce a professional-standard manuscript.

title: Process Simulation and Data Analytics
description: This unit covers methods used for the numerical solution and analysis of process flowsheets. After an introduction to process engineering software and revision of flowsheet concepts, the topics discussed include the numerical solution of algebraic and ordinary differential equations; spreadsheet functions for data analysis and optimisation; flowsheet tear analysis; introductory process simulation using Excel/VBA (Visual Basic for Applications). Process flowsheets are also solved using a commercial process simulator, such as Aspen Hysys. Students cover the selection of species, thermodynamic property package and unit models; techniques for successful process simulation; conducting sensitivity studies and optimisation; and dealing with uncertain information. Students will be introduced to the fundamentals and scope of data analytics, and gain skills in interpreting large data sets and building performance dashboards for engineering processes. The unit emphasises the need to set out simulations and analyses clearly, justify the approach taken and evaluate the computed results. Students develop teamwork and communication skills in the context of solving and analysing process flowsheets.

title: Data Communications and Network Management
description: This unit teaches the topics defining data communications standards including Physical layer and Data link layer standards, encoding, error detection, and protocols for both wired and wireless communications. Using practical approach, the unit also covers the network design principles of TCP/IP including routing protocols, routing algorithms, flow and congestion control algorithms, application layer protocols and network management with an introduction to Software Defined Networking for modern data networks.

title: Evidence Informed Health Practice
description: The role of empirical evidence in making decisions in health practice. Introduction to different types of research methodologies; measurement; observation; data collection; research ethics; bio-statistical analysis; strategies to understand, question and evaluate evidence.

title: Network Engineering
description: Network Security. Authentication Technologies. Institute of Electrical and Electronic Engineers (IEEE) 802.1x. Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA)Servers Configuration. Identity-Based Networking Services (IBNS). Context Based Access Control (CBAC). Encryption Basics. Remote Access.

title: Data Mining
description: This unit will cover the key concepts of data mining with an emphasis on unstructured data analysis and interpretation. The first part of the unit covers the fundamental techniques used to pre-process unstructured data. Next, association rule mining concepts and techniques are reviewed and evaluated. Classification and cluster analysis is then covered in detail. Finally, stream data mining techniques are evaluated in the context of image and network traffic data analysis.

title: Extended Distributed Computing
description: This unit introduces students to Distributed Computing and its associated complexities. Topics covered include remote procedure calls and asynchronous calls, Multi-tiered architectures for distributed computing and XML serialisation and passing objects by value over the network. In addition the unit covers Serverside Web scripting with CGI based approaches. Further topics include Service oriented architectures, Web services as a SOA Framework and modern Internet applications with Ajax and Web Services.

title: Computing Honours Dissertation
description: Students will be required to conduct an independent research project under the guidance of a supervisor, resulting in the preparation, submission, presentation and defence of a dissertation. Students will develop research, technical and professional and communication skills, research autonomy and specialised knowledge through a process of inquiry involving the formulation of research questions and hypotheses; selection of appropriate methodology and experimental design; ethical consideration of the research process; critical review of scientific literature; effective scientific writing; development of a project proposal, and the preparation of a dissertation.

title: Web Application Frameworks
description: Explores the use of modern client-side and server-side application frameworks for development of sophisticated web applications. The unit first covers in-depth how to work within client-side frameworks to develop complex, usable and high-performance application front ends. Second, the unit discusses and explores back-end technologies for securely implementing server-side business logic and data storage.

title: Chemical Reactions and Mechanisms
description: Building on first-year studies of the reactions of organic molecules, this unit will demonstrate how the mechanism of each reaction can affect the 3D outcome of the product. Reactions involving substitutions, additions, eliminations, radicals and acid/base chemistry will be examined in relation to common functional groups. The reaction of carbonyol compounds will be emphasised in relation to keto/enrol tautomerism., enol/ enolate chemistry and carbon-carbon bond forming reactions. Aromaticity and the reactivity of aromatic compound will be explored. Particular emphasis will be placed on how substituents influence reactivity and regiochemistry. These skills will lead to the design of synthetic pathways to simple organic molecules. An introduction to organometallic chemistry: bonding, ligands.

title: Accounting - The Fundamentals of Business
description: The unit aims to provide students with knowledge of accounting transactions. It applies the conceptual framework and the objectives of the financial statement. It focuses on understanding, defining and recognising various elements of financial statements and the use of a computerised accounting software. In addition, the unit teaches the application of selected international financial reporting standards and underlying accounting theories.

title: Mobile Radio Communications
description: Introduction to land-mobile radio communication systems. Mobile radio environments: propagation mechanisms, path loss, fading and multipath, and statistical models. Cellular concept: architecture, frequency reuse, handoff, interference and capacity, grade of service. Multiple access methods: conflict-free and non-conflict-free, frequency, time, code and space division multiple access. Spread spectrum techniques.  Intermodulation and noise performance of a radio receiver.

title: Communications Engineering
description: The first part of the unit provides an overview of a communication system and an introduction to random processes. Next, digital encoding of time-continuous analogue signals and pulse-code modulation (PCM) are discussed. Baseband and passband digital transmissions are then covered in detail including Nyquist’s criteria, intersymbol interference, eye diagram, multidimensional digital modulation, and probability of error. This is followed by optimum receiver design, error control coding and waveform equalisation. Finally, orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) communication is discussed.

title: Human Rights and Social Justice
description: This unit focuses on anthropological and sociological approaches to the provision of human rights for peoples and cultures in Australia, Asia and beyond in some of the following areas: political and socio economic spheres, ethnicity and indigeneity, gender and sexuality, religion, environment, migration and war. The unit addresses claims to human rights, their maintenance and protection and uses a social justice framework to evaluate conflicts between rights.

title: Radio Frequency and Microwave Systems
description: Radio Frequency, microwave systems, deep space communications and remote sensing, including radio astronomy and radar, share a number of major electronic engineering challenges driven primarily by the very long distances and low signal levels involved. This course addresses the relevant disciplines, including radio frequency and microwave engineering. Some related topics, including radar, orbital dynamics and space situational awareness, will also be addressed.

title: Business Inquiry Lab
description: This core unit introduces students to essential information, knowledge, and foundational academic and professional skills, including ethical reasoning, as they commence their Bachelor of Advanced Commerce (Honours) degree. The unit introduces the research culture within the Faculty of Business and Law. Students will engage with research centres, interact with academic staff, and explore current research themes, building early awareness of how research informs business, law, society and policy. Through reflective and exploratory tasks, students will begin to identify their academic interests and develop a sense of identity as emerging researchers and future professionals.

title: Sustainability and Structures in Architecture
