description: This unit addresses the sphere of aspects that are related to the role of financial institutions in a dynamic financial technology driven global environment. The content provides students with an understanding of the financial statements of financial institutions; how to measure their overall performance; different risks that they are exposed to; and the application of different financial models and methodologies to manage these risks.

title: Process Instrumentation and Control
description: This unit covers Piping and Instrumentation Diagram, as well as the theory and practice of the automatic control of process systems. Students are introduced to the terminology, basic components, configurations, and engineering representations of process control loops and control system synthesis. The mathematical modelling of chemical processes for control purposes is then examined using both first principles and data driven approaches. The models are represented in the frequency domain through Laplace transforms. Different types of typical dynamic process behaviour are subsequently explored: first order, second order andsimilar. This is followed by the design of single-loop feedback control systems for Proportional, Proportional Integral and Proportional Integral Derivative controller types. Control loop design includes techniques for controller tuning and for stability analysis using root locus and Bode diagrams. The unit has a laboratory component in which students conduct experiments on process control rigs to help link theory with practice.

title: Foundations of Computer Science
description: This unit introduces the mathematical theory that underlies the computing profession. It introduces proof and logic concepts central to computer science and programming methodology, including an introduction to set theory and mathematical relations, graph theory. Computational and mathematical recursion is also addressed, along with the paired concept of induction proofs. Finally, the analysis of software using discrete statistics is also addressed, including univariate statistics and confidence intervals.

title: Advanced Thermodynamics and Reactor Engineering
description: This unit will equip students in the analysis of processes using advanced knowledge in thermodynamics and reaction engineering. The concepts of chemical and physical exergies will be used to perform exergy efficiency calculations. Multi-reaction equilibria will be applied to reactor design. Thermodynamics cycles will be analysed in relation to power generation, with a particular focus on nuclear power sources. Students will be introduced to unsteady-state reactor design and analysis, non-ideal reactors, and catalytic and non-catalytic gas-liquid reaction, non-catalytic gas-solid reaction and three-phase reaction.

title: Financial Decision Making
description: This unit develops skills and knowledge that enable students across all disciplines to make informed and responsible decisions using accounting and financial information. The unit explores different forms of business and financing options and how these affect business decisions through the understanding of financial statements. Students will learn about basic accounting and financial terminologies; cash and accrual accounting, capital investment decisions, business financing, time value of money, triple bottom line reporting and business budgeting. Students will also learn how to interpret financial statements and how global events impact on business decisions.

title: Introduction to Chemistry
description: This unit is an introduction to the fundamental nature of matter for students who have not previously studied chemistry. Students who have passed WACE Chemistry 3A/3B or equivalent should instead take CHEM1000 Principles and Processes in Chemistry or CHEM1001 Biological Chemistry. A range of chemical processes that underpin a broad array of disciplines will illustrate the importance of and differences between chemical and mathematical representations of reactions and reactivity. The physical phenomena resulting from bond types and their resulting intermolecular forces will explain the properties of natural and man-made processes and materials. Using examples from nature and biology the role of the certain groups in ascribing reactivity and function of organic molecules will be highlighted.

title: Auditing, Assurance and Risk Assessment
description: An overview of assurance and ethics, independence and corporate governance. Understanding of the company audit process including audit planning - the concepts of materiality and audit risk. The evaluation and testing of internal control systems and substantive audit testing of transactions and balances. The finalisation of the audit and audit reporting.

title: Object Oriented Software Engineering
description: This unit equips students to develop and communicate complex object oriented (OO) design structures for a given set of software requirements. The unit focuses on selected polymorphic design patterns to impart a set of techniques for creating highly cohesive and loosely-coupled designs. It takes students from high-level Unified Modelling Language (UML) design notations to their practical implementation in OO programming languages. Students also learn about the Model View Controller (MVC) architecture to help promote separation of concerns, containers and generics to promote design reuse, and factories and dependency injection to help address design testability.

title: Virtual Design and Construction
description: This unit is an introduction to virtual design and construction (VDC) and integrated concurrent engineering (ICE). Students will learn the components of VDC, including associated hardware and software, as well as the application of VDC processes to support ICE to improve construction project performance in terms of time and cost.

title: Asian Media in Transition
description: Theoretical and methodological issues that need to inform any understanding of Asian media and culture and how these issues can be seen in practice, concentrating on specific case studies.

title: Business Valuation Using Accounting Analytics
description: Theory, application and interpretation of financial statement analysis. Objectives of financial statement analysis from viewpoints of equity investors, management, acquisition and merger analysts, and short and long-term debt holders. Case studies in comprehensive statement analysis.

title: Econometric Principles
description: The unit will cover the following topics: Review of elementary statistics and introduction of the simple regression model; the multiple regression model; hypothesis testing; non-linearity; functional form and dummy variables. The usefulness of the techniques will be illustrated by applications to problems in business, economics and finance.

title: Computing Topics
description: This unit covers new developments in selected topics in computing science. Students will participate in practical and theoretical activities to increase their knowledge and equip them with the skills to remain current in the selected topics.

title: Culture to Cultures
description: This unit investigates culture, communication and representation. We examine the complexity of culture and our engagement with other cultures and culturally diverse thinking and perspectives. As part of this, we explore Indigenous cultures, histories, knowledge, perspectives and values. The unit also explores the relationship between media and culture, critically analysing media representations that inform our ideas about particular topics, other cultures and people. We examine the effects and consequences of representation by analysing the ideological role played by global media, and how this connects with power.

title: Facilities and Asset Management
description: This unit examines the scope and importance of facilities and asset management. The history, common terms and attributes of facilities and asset management are explored. This is so that students gain the understanding, knowledge and skills necessary to effectively perform the roles of either a facilities or asset manager.

title: Macroeconomic Theory
description: This unit builds on the skills and competencies students have acquired in their study of ECON2001 Macroeconomic Principles. In ECON3004 Macroeconomic Theory we aim to develop students critical awareness in three key areas of macroeconomics: 1) The factors determining long run growth outcomes for the macroeconomy. 2) The causes and consequences of cyclical fluctuations. 3) The economics of the exchange rate and of policy making in open economy environment.

title: Microeconomic Theory
description: The unit will provide a thorough grounding in microeconomics at an advanced level. Topics include mathematical tools for microeconomics, profit maximization and cost minimization, monopoly, oligopoly, general equilibrium and the use of Pareto optimality to analyse the performance of markets including market failure.

title: Machine Learning
description: This unit introduces the foundational concepts, algorithms, and applications of Machine Learning (ML). Students will gain hands-on experience with diverse data types including tabular, image, text, and time series, and will learn to develop ML models such as linear models, SVM, decision trees, and neural networks. Covering a broad spectrum of topics within supervised and unsupervised learning, self-supervised learning, and deep learning, the unit also focuses on practical applications in computer vision and natural language processing, equipping students with the skills to implement ML solutions and solve real-world problems effectively.

title: Creating and Presenting Media Stories
description: This unit develops the skills and confidence to create content (stories), and present the stories authentically and effectively, using modern technology, especially smartphones. Students will develop skills in the software and hardware involved in mobile storytelling, alongside the principles and creative practices of established and emerging media content generation. Students will learn how to develop confidence and capabilities in presentation skills.

title: Software Architecture and Extensible Design
description: This unit equips students to evaluate architectural problems and solutions in software engineering, and to develop highly extensible designs to help implement them. Students learn advanced design structures for multithreading in object oriented languages, the use of build systems for creating modular software, the design and implementation of application programming interfaces (APIs), plugin systems and domain-specific languages (DSLs) for fostering communities of developers, and approaches to internationalisation (I18N) to create globally-relevant software.

title: Media, Culture and Consumption
description: This unit aims to deepen students understanding of the receiving end of communications media- consumers, audiences, publics and users. It will familiarise students with the social and cultural consequences of media consumption and provide a strong grounding in competing perspectives in audiences studies and the role of media usage in the formation of subcultures, public spheres, and national communities.

title: Industrial Chemistry and Achieving Sustainability
description: Chemistry has an important role to play in increasing the sustainability of many industries In this unit, some of the chemical industries in WA will be presented and their actions towards sustainability will be discussed. The principles of sustainability will be used to assess industrial practices. In addition, this unit will study future technologies and materials for increased efficiency of resources development,sustainable energy technologies and transition to a circular economy focussed on harnessing waste as a resource. Students will apply their knowledge to propose solutions for challenges of sustainability in chemical industries.

title: Understanding Social Research A
description: This unit examines contemporary theory and practice in anthropology and sociology, specifically in the anthropology and sociology of public problems. These focus on the construction of a public problem and its conversion from private concern to public issue. Public problems can range from concerns over the global economic recession, climate change and terrorism to those of obesity, cigarette smoking, town planning or graffiti. Students will consider several research projects in order to develop a reflexive awareness of contemporary anthropological and sociological practices and methods. This unit also involves undertaking a project which may be textually based and/or involve the collection and analysis of empirical materials.

title: Business Technologies and Data Management for Accountants
description: Examination of the Internet and its importance to accounting, including electronic payment systems, electronic commerce, web accounting reporting, and emerging technologies. Provides a review of hardware, software and data communication systems including networks, web browsers, file transfer protocol, mail and newsgroups.

title: Accounting, Behaviour and Control
description: This unit builds upon foundational knowledge of management systems including performance management and control systems aligned with organisational strategy.

title: Oral Pathology, Oral Medicine and Pharmacology
description: In this unit you will gain pharmacological knowledge relevant to the clinical management of adults and children. You will learn the importance of pharmacology in patient treatment; and how to recognise side effects, medication interactions and the importance of understanding the limitations of medications. You will also study the science behind anti-microbial mouthwashes, toothpaste ingredients and other over the counter therapeutic goods. Oral health therapists should be able to recognise different oral pathologies, so this unit will describe different oral pathologies and the possible causes and explain the role of the oral health therapist in clinical management. You will also explore different clinical manifestations in problem-based learning tasks and be introduced to the specialty of oral medicine. The specialty of oral medicine is concerned with the oral health care of patients with medically related disorders of the oral and maxillofacial region. You learn how to interpret certain clinical characteristics (within your scope of practice) and prepare professional referrals.

title: Advanced Applied Economics
description: This unit comprises a series of specialist sessions that demonstrate the wide range of economic and social issues that require economic analysis and highlight, from an industry/practitioner perspective, the challenges involved in applied economic analysis. The topics of the lectures vary from year to year but all have current policy relevance.

title: Early Learning Through the Humanities and Social Sciences
description: This unit is designed to investigate the knowledge, skills and understandings young children need as they connect with their world and continue to grow as active and contributing citizens. An inquiry approach underpins the development of an integrated teaching plan and collaborative inquiry from the Humanities and Social Sciences (HASS) learning areas and includes Aboriginal culture, knowledge and understandings. The unit examines pedagogical approaches, theoretical perspectives and research which assist students to plan and implement teaching and learning programs to support children (birth – 8 years) as they build their sense of belonging and citizenship in the family and community. Students will critically reflect on the meaning of the educator as global citizen and explore how children's culture, heritage, and traditions can be valued within a variety of learning contexts.

title: Applied Economics
description: In this unit students will apply microeconomic and macroeconomic theory to a number of real world issues. Students will be introduced to the challenges involved in applied economics, including: the selection and/or development of theories and models for particular markets or issues; the identification, collection and analysis of relevant sources of data; and the presentation of results.

title: Energy Economics, Management & Markets
description: This unit introduces students the fundamentals of energy economics. While engineering decisions are contemplated after assessing numerous technical parameters and potential outcomes, no final decision is ever made without giving due consideration to the likely economic outcome of that decision, and how that decision will economically impact or be impacted by the wider market. Students are exposed to the following topics: macro and micro economics, markets (including supply and demand), income determination (product pricing and forecasting tools, exchange rates), costs determination (top-down, bottom-up, fixed and variable, estimating) and capital expenditure (estimating methods) & working capital. These factors are then used to compile a simple cash flow model where Students will be required to determine discounted cash flow-derived net present value incorporating: depreciation and amortisation schedules, royalties, free- or carried- interests, appropriate taxation and discounting. Students will be introduced to discounting (weighted average cost of capital, incorporating the cost of equity and the cost of debt) and variable (differential) discounting, as well as to the debt and equity costs of funding capital projects, and will be introduced to calculating project investment returns on projects. The unit provides an insight into the way in which projects and their associated companies are explicitly and comparatively economically evaluated.

title: Advanced Macroeconomics
description: Recent developments in macroeconomic theory and policy implications. Neo-Keynesian and neo-classical theory. Dynamic macroeconomic theory. Business cycle theory. Open economy macroeconomics. New growth theory. International policy coordination.

title: Microeconomic Principles
description: This intermediate level unit further develops students’ understanding of a variety of topics in Microeconomics such as utility and preference, consumer choice, production and cost, the firm and industry, market structure, game theory, factor markets, distribution of income and market failure.

title: Behavioural Economics and Finance
description: This unit examines the key concepts, research methods and major findings of behavioural economics and finance. A key objective is to provide students with a solid knowledge base of the core theoretical concepts in behavioural economics and finance, including the field’s connections with psychology and neuroscience, bounded rationality, heuristics and biases, framing, self-control and mental accounting. A further aim is to provide students with an appreciation of the various practical and policy applications of these concepts in the real world. The unit provides students opportunities to develop a range of skills relating to the design, conduct and evaluation of experiments in economics and finance, in addition to critical evaluation and communication skills. Students will engage in hands-on activities associated with experiments and problem-solving, as well as participate in classroom discussions and debates. The unit will cover a range of important topics including, the role of emotions in decision-making, stereotypes and other biases, self-control, nudges and public policy, trust and participation in collective action, neuro-economics, overconfidence, and financial market anomalies.

title: Complex Corporate Issues
description: This unit aims to provide students with an advanced knowledge of corporate transactions and business combinations. It will also address current issues in business and how these impact accounting.

title: Advanced Microeconomics
description: An examination of the core areas of modern microeconomic theory. The unit is examined at a higher level of analytical rigour than ECON3000 Microeconomic Theory. This unit covers the following essential concepts: Consumer theory, preferences, utility functions, indirect utility and expenditure functions, properties of consumer demand, consumer's surplus, duality in consumer theory, uncertainty, technology and production, cost functions, duality in production, theory of the firm and market structures, and game theory.

title: Intermediate Chinese: Everyday Contexts
description: This unit develops students' communicative competence in the Chinese language over a wider range of real-life situations. Conversation, readings, discussions and report writing will be conducted on topics in relation to the contemporary Chinese society and culture. The cultural significance of language usage will be examined, together with systematic discussion of appropriate manners and social etiquette to enable effective communication

title: Emerging Digital Experience Studio
description: In this unit students will work on projects that are directly linked with real-world practice. Projects based on simulated client briefs, real client briefs, or studio placements give students direct experience in working in professional environments. Students will have the opportunity to document and reflect on their experiences, as well as forge industry connections in the 3D visualisation, visual effects, education, simulation and game design industries.

title: Molecular Virology
description: This unit examines the molecular biology of viruses, with the aim of increasing student understanding of gene regulation and nucleic acid replication to an advanced level. Animal, plant, insect and bacterial viruses are studied, along with strategies for the development of antiviral agents and vaccines, cloning and expression vectors, biological control of insects and pests, strategies for studying oncogenesis and cell apoptosis and tools for diagnosing viral infection and analysing the epidemiology of viral disease.

title: Land and Development Economics
description: Critical examination of the property development process and the economics underpinning land use, land development, and built form outcomes.

title: Introduction to Health Psychology
description: This unit provides an introduction to health psychology in the Australian context. You will learn about how psychological theory can be applied to understanding health enhancing behaviours and health risk behaviours. In addition you will explore the impact of living with illness and pain and strategies for improving health and quality of life.

title: Cadastral Surveying
description: In this unit, students will apply theory and principles of cadastral surveying to determine the location of land boundaries. They will develop their skills in field surveying through experiencing cadastral surveying for boundary redefinition and subdivision. They will identify and evaluate historical survey records and conduct office calculations. Students will assess land boundary evidence from field surveys, carrying out calculations so that land boundaries can be re-established in their original position. The cadastral surveying process is covered from start to finish and experienced through a Work Integrated Learning (WIL) industry work placement.

title: Sustainable Fashion
description: In a contemporary environment of global economic, social, cultural and environmental concerns, sustainability has become a major consideration within design. It is a consideration which impacts on all aspects of the development and lifecycle of a product and has become increasingly important within fashion design because of its associations with excessive consumption and waste. This unit examines the issue of sustainability within fashion design and engages you in the development of garments that reassess the design process within this context.

title: Motion Design and Compositing
description: This unit develops students’ skills and conceptual approaches in the art of digital compositing. Compositing is the act of blending various visual elements together into a seamless video form. It can be seen in special effects for film, web site banners, TV title sequences, TV commercials, architectural walkthroughs and training simulations. Students will have the opportunity to develop their conceptual approaches and explore the technical possibilities of motion and special effects compositing through hands-on production experimentation.

title: Image Design Culture
description: With an emphasis on visual analysis and image interpretation, Image Cultures develops students’ understanding of core principles and theories that underpin effective visual communication and the creation of meaningful images.

title: Business, Law and Regulation
description: This unit introduces basic principles of business law and regulation. It discusses business structures and introduces the relationships that a business enterprise has with government, employees, suppliers, competitors, customers and the broader community. The unit identifies key Australian regulatory bodies and considers a range of regulatory approaches from the prescriptive to self regulatory.

title: Provisioning Techniques
description: The aim of this unit to continue building on the principles of financial economics, particularly for determining provisions. Provisioning techniques such as ruin theory and run-off triangles are explored. Practical, hands-on modelling experience is developed through the use of EXCEL spreadsheets (students are assumed to have functional EXCEL skills prior to commencement of this unit).

title: Advertising Design 3
description: This unit explores creative advertising design practice, with a focus on concept and communication design process. The conceptual process component addresses the development of advertising ideas and concepts, and the communication design component deals with the communication craft skills of copywriting and art direction. Students will apply conceptual and advertising communication design principles through a series of exercises and practical design projects.

title: Medicine 4
description: This unit comprises supervised practicum experience in the disciplines of Medicine, Surgery, Paediatrics, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, General Practice and Psychiatry. A range of learning activities will be experienced in clinical settings, and will focus on important knowledge and skills in each of the clinical disciplines. Students will develop skills in diagnosis and management of common clinical problems.  Communication and clinical skills learned in previous years are extended further and applied within clinical settings. Skills related to patient interaction, physical examinations and performing procedures in medicine, surgery, obstetrics and gynaecology, general practice and psychiatry will be developed in various settings including ward attachments, outpatient clinics, community settings and in general practice clinics.

title: Health and Physical Education
description: This unit introduces students to health and physical education in the contemporary Australian primary school curriculum, where emphasis is on developing children’s health and physical literacies within safe and lifelong learning frameworks so they are able to flourish as healthy and active citizens. With attention to diversity and social justice, children’s rights to develop health and physical literacies within their personal, physical and socio-cultural contexts are explored, and relevant teaching approaches identified. Given the emphasis on evidence-based curriculum design, students will investigate the research that underpins the contemporary curriculum rationale and focus. This unit reviews ongoing, developmentally appropriate and explicit teaching about health and movement, where children participate safely to develop the knowledge, skills, dispositions and understandings to make healthy and active choices for the wellbeing of themselves and others. In this regard, the importance of physical skills in the early childhood years, including observation and practise of fundamental motor skills (FMS), assessment of FMS and appropriate interventions, is addressed. Advanced movement skills and strategies, components of personal, social and community health, fitness, spatial awareness and games-based teaching models are also explored.

title: Children as Mathematical Learners
description: This is the second in the suite of units on mathematics education. It delves deeper into the Australian Mathematics Curriculum, with a particular emphasis on fostering a deeper understanding of the structure and content within the Number and Algebra strands (F-6). There is a strong emphasis on developing and valuing conceptual understanding. Emphasis is placed on enhancing both mathematical and pedagogical content knowledge (MCK and PCK), enabling pre-service teachers to make informed professional judgments and effectively diagnose and plan for children’s mathematical needs. You will develop, implement, analyse and moderate diagnostic assessment tasks effectively to elicit children’s mathematical knowledge and understanding in the Number and Algebra strands (F-6). Through critiquing a range of contemporary pedagogies, you will design and design learning, planning for teaching and learning in mathematics.

title: Policy in Practice: The Classroom in Context
description: This unit delves into the complexities of educational policy and its practical application within classroom and school environments. Students explore legislative, administrative, and organisational policies relevant to teaching. They critically analyse the challenges of translating written policies into effective classroom practices, with a specific focus on meeting the needs of diverse student populations. Additionally, students evaluate policy theory and its impact on teaching practices, considering differences and diversity. The unit encourages students to develop informed perspectives on educational issues and create actionable plans aligned with relevant policies.

title: Theory in Practice: Inclusion and Differentiation
description: This unit explores the core principles and practices of inclusive education, emphasising the importance of understanding and responding to the diverse needs of students. It delves into contemporary perspectives on human learning and the historical and philosophical foundations of inclusive education. The unit focuses on effective differentiation strategies and assessment methods to foster an inclusive and supportive learning environment. Through critical analysis and practical application, students will be equipped to create equitable learning experiences for students of diverse abilities.

title: Inquiry in the Mathematics Classroom
description: Participants will continue to develop a variety of approaches to teaching and learning mathematics, including social constructivist. There is an emphasis on the deep understanding of the Geometry, Measurement and Probability strands of the Australian Curriculum: Mathematics. There is continued development of teachers' mathematical content knowledge with particular reference to knowledge of spatial and measurement concepts for effective teaching, as well as those related to financial literacy and mathematical modelling. Development of pedagogical content knowledge is centred on the investigation of appropriate use of a wide range of resources, including technologies, and their application to learning and teaching.

title: Unix Systems Programming
description: This unit develops fundamental Unix/Linux concepts: process management, inter-process communication, threads, file systems, memory management, virtual memory and the I/O subsystem. The unit further develops C language knowledge with the ANSI and POSIX standards from previous units to enable competent C programming at the system level. Parallel to this the student is introduced to Unix/Linux scripting and systems administration.

title: Language, Literacy and Literature for 3 to 5-Year-Olds
description: This unit explores the diverse nature of literacy and language development in 3-5 year olds. Students will analyse theoretical perspectives and differing pedagogies underpinning teaching and learning of language and literacy. Students will examine research relating to a variety of teaching approaches to establish strong literacy learning environments that support children who are beginning to read and write. The unit highlights the linguistic and cultural backgrounds children and families bring to early learning environments and consider how learning environments for 3–5-year-olds can value individual, and cultural diversity in relation to home and school literacy practices. The unit will build on the students’ knowledge base about teaching, assessing and planning for language and literacy learning.

title: Mathematics for the Early Years
description: The focus of this unit is on making connections between what young children know about mathematics, what children need to know and the role of the educator in developing children’s mathematical understanding. This includes identification of children’s knowledge and developing and using assessment and intervention strategies. The unit is an introduction to social constructivist learning of mathematics and social cultural theory of learning and their application to early childhood learning environments. The unit develops educator knowledge of mathematics content areas; number, algebra, geometry, measurement and statistics and probability. There is a strong emphasis on integrating mathematics into everyday teaching.

title: Leadership in Early Childhood Education
description: This unit provides the opportunity to develop foundational leadership skills and knowledge expected of contemporary early years educators. The unit examines the theory and practice of leadership in early childhood education, and students use an enquiry process to investigate and reflect on the leadership roles and responsibilities of early childhood educators across a range of dimensions. These include ethical approaches to leadership, regulatory requirements, advocacy, pedagogical leadership, and working in partnership with colleagues, families and the wider community.

title: Early Childhood Professional Experience: Formal Learning Environments for 5 to 8-year-olds
description: This professional experience unit includes both theory and practice to work with children aged 5-8 years in a school setting. This unit covers a comprehensive overview of theory and practices in establishing and creating emotionally supportive, equitable, healthy, safe and effective learning environments for diverse groups of children including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. This includes developing the skills needed to guide children’s behaviour and offer feedback. Students will also learn about planning their teaching and children’s learning. Students are supported in both the theory and practical components of the unit to become reflective educators who critique and apply their knowledge of multiple pedagogies, the curriculum, their role as a teacher, design elements of a rich learning environment, and a range of approaches to authentically practise, document and assess learning. The professional experience practical assessment is a three (3) week full-time block placement with children aged five to eight years old in a school-based setting intended to enable practical application of knowledge and skills covered in the theory, along with providing further insights into the complexity of the role of teacher. All required clearances to work with children must be obtained and current, and all other professional experience requirements met. Both theory and practical components must be passed in order to pass the unit.

title: Social Justice and Diversity in Early Childhood
description: This unit explores contemporary issues of culture, equity, values and social justice in early childhood pedagogy. The unit proposes an image of the child as a citizen with rights and students analyse the impact of this image in curriculum decision-making. The unit promotes a view of early childhood settings as democratic forums: students critically examine approaches to building relationships with children, families, and communities. Students consider how to redress inequalities and create welcoming spaces for children, educators and families of diverse cultural backgrounds, beliefs, and practices. Students articulate their roles as advocates for children’s rights and are encouraged to reconceptualise their views on families, gender, language and sexual identity to further consolidate an ethical approach to the profession of educator.

title: Pedagogical Contexts for Play
description: This unit examines the value of play in early childhood pedagogy, and invites students to become advocates for children’s right to play. The unit explores historical and current theoretical perspectives on pedagogy and play, and offers opportunities to discuss examples of current local, national, and international play-based curriculum in learning settings from birth - 8 years. The unit emphasises planning of physical environments for play and includes a focus on the outdoors as a pedagogical space. Students will learn to plan with intent, observe, interpret, and assess children’s learning through play. Students will critically review contemporary issues impacting on time and opportunity for play, and explore possibilities for and approaches to establishing shared understandings between educators and families on the value of play in children’s learning.

title: Primary Professional Experience 2: Classroom Skills for Diversity and Inclusion
description: This is the second in the suite of professional experience units that includes a practical component (15 days of placement in a school). The unit will allow you to extend your developing knowledge and skills in the classroom by considering lesson planning and classroom management by considering diverse students’ needs and the ways teachers respond to these needs, both through a theoretical and a practical lens. The professional experience practical assessment assesses your emerging ability to engage with practical application of the knowledge and skills gained working towards classrooms where all students can thrive. All required clearances to work with children must be obtained and valid, and all other preparation requirements met. All assessment components must be passed in order to pass the unit.

title: Introductory Economics
description: This unit provides some powerful tools for understanding how economies work. It introduces the concepts and methods of experimental and behavioural economics; models of economic growth, business cycles, and financial crises; macroeconomic indicators of economic growth, unemployment, and inflation; and tools to understand and evaluate monetary, fiscal, and other economic policies. Economics affects everything in our lives—what we earn, how we work, where we learn, what we consume, how much we waste; the list goes on. An understanding of economics is critical in an uncertain world, where market forces have such a significant influence on our lives. Any student undertaking a course in commerce or business at the undergraduate level requires an understanding of economics—how people make decisions (rational or otherwise), economic policy, challenges caused by the COVID-19 pandemic on global economic recovery and decent work progress, sustainable economic growth and productivity, climate change dilemmas and so on. A good grasp of introductory principles of economics is crucial if we, as student collaborators and critical social-ecological observers, are to make informed judgements about solving real-world problems.

title: Analytics for Decision Making
description: This unit will develop analytical capabilities, equipping students with knowledge about basic data analysis to derive essential information from numerical, textual and visual datasets. As consumers and producers of data, students will learn about data management and security practices, as well as developing an understanding of legal and ethical issues relating to the collection and use of data. Students will develop their analytic capabilities by understanding and interpreting a range of data types including macroeconomic data, which will be used as a base case study where students will examine how macroeconomic conditions affect business decisions across a variety of disciplines including marketing, management, and finance. Students will have the opportunity to personalise their learning experience as they examine case study data sets relating to a range of business disciplines including economics, marketing, human resources and finance. Students will also develop skills to effectively communicate the results of their analysis to an audience and recommend business actions from a considered range of alternatives.

title: Quantitative Techniques for Business
description: This unit introduces mathematical concepts relevant to business and economic applications. The unit begins with a review of foundational concepts in algebra, progressing to elementary calculus used in applications of constrained and unconstrained optimisation. The second half of the unit reviews elementary statistical concepts and techniques for statistical inference.

title: Curriculum Integration and Differentiation
description: This unit provides opportunities to consolidate professional knowledge and skills related to curriculum, teaching and assessment. Curriculum integration emphasises multi-subject approaches to teaching children in school, particularly literacy and numeracy. Curriculum differentiation emphasises adjusting teaching and learning methods to accommodate each child's individual needs and preferences in order to maximum learning. Curriculum integration and differentiation are often achieved in the context of inquiry-based instructional approaches.

title: Inquiry in the Humanities and Social Sciences Classroom
description: This unit introduces each of the HASS discipline areas and the pedagogy and theory – including inquiry learning and curriculum integration – which can assist students to develop teaching, learning and assessment strategies for HASS in the Primary classroom. Students will explore the knowledge, skills, attitudes and values that enable children to become active and informed citizens as they connect with their local and global communities. Students will reflect on the role of the educator as a global citizen. Through the thematic of contested histories, they will explore how difference – cultural and otherwise – is valued and respected in the HASS classroom; and how that can empower children from diverse backgrounds, while laying the basis for sustainable communities.

title: Primary Professional Experience 1: Introduction to Classroom Skills
description: This is the first in the suite of professional experience units that includes a practical component (a 10 day placement in a school). The unit will allow you to apply philosophies and theories related to teaching and learning. The unit also addresses professional responsibilities, effective communication and reflective practices to support your workplace learning. The professional experience practical assessment is a low-stakes work place learning opportunity intended to enable practical application of the knowledge and skills gained, along with providing students with insights into the complexity of the teacher’s role. All required clearances to work with children must be obtained and valid, and all other preparation requirements met. All assessment components must be passed in order to pass the unit.

title: Inquiry in the Science Classroom
description: What does it look like, feel like and smell like? In this unit the inquiry process provides the framework through which students investigate science in the primary classroom. Students will create and participate in inquiry-focused hands-on activities across the science learning areas of the Australian Curriculum. This unit will focus on fostering a positive, engaging and safe environment to promote students’ scientific literacy and will consider lesson planning, teaching strategies and assessment forms in the context of the science classroom. The unit will curate a raft of science resources and evaluate technologies available for primary classrooms. There is a focus on promoting students’ ability to develop primary school learners’ knowledge and skills to work scientifically, and to foster a positive attitude to science, as well as apply science knowledge to better understand the world around them.

title: Visual and Media Arts Education
description: Planning and pedagogy of authentic forms of arts education are addressed through the curriculum subjects of Media and Visual Arts. The school curriculum provides the framework for planning sequential, inquiry-based and engaging learning opportunities for primary school children. Experiential learning opportunities and reflective practices facilitate the development of practical understanding of the scope and nature of arts learning across the primary school years. Personal media and visual arts literacy are promoted as the foundation for teaching within a lifelong learning framework. Pedagogical understandings and practices that support the development of children’s identities and agency through their creativity, self-expression, meaning-making and communication of ideas are studied, practised with children, and reviewed using an improvement cycle framework.

title: Early Childhood Professional Experience: Learning Environments for 3 to 5-year-olds
description: This professional experience unit includes both a theory and a practical component (a placement with children aged 3 - 5 years). Throughout the unit, approaches for creating emotionally supportive, equitable, healthy, safe and effective learning environments are critically examined. The design of supportive environments is contextualised within collaborative partnerships and positive reciprocal relationships with children, families, and communities. The unit emphasises the application of differentiated learning, teaching and assessment approaches to meet the diverse needs of children in this age group. The examination of data relevant to early childhood education and the implications for learning and teaching are explored. The professional experience practical assessment is a 4-week full-time block placement intended to enable practical application of knowledge and skills covered in the theory, along with providing further insights into the complexity of the teacher’s role. All required clearances to work with children must be obtained and valid, and all other professional experience requirements met. Both theory and practical components must be passed in order to pass the unit.

title: Nutrient Metabolism
description: Nutrient Metabolism builds on your foundation in the Biochemistry of Nutrition, exploring the science of key micronutrients with a focus on bioavailability, mechanisms of action, and excretion. Since we consume food rather than isolated nutrients, this unit emphasises the connection between nutrient metabolism, food-based guidelines, and broader dietary patterns. Through laboratory work including nutritional status assessments and engagement with current scientific literature, you will develop a deeper understanding of how metabolic principles inform dietary recommendations. By the end of this unit, you will be able to translate complex scientific concepts into real-world applications, enhancing your ability to evaluate and communicate nutritional information effectively.

title: Regional Industry Internship
description: Regional Industry Internship gives you the opportunity to undertake a passion informed, project-based industry internship in regional Western Australia. You will tackle real-world challenges, integrate Indigenous Knowledge Systems, ideate strategies and solutions, and experience work and life in a regional community. You will gain experience in co-creating environmentally responsible, socially just and economically sustainable regional communities and industries. On completion of this unit, you will be empowered with the tools and insights necessary to actively contribute to positive change and innovation in a diverse range of professional settings.

title: Social Work Field Education 2
description: Students will undertake 525 hours social work placement in a range of fields and sites of practice under the supervision of an approved supervisor. Integration and application of theoretical frameworks, social work skills and critically reflective practice are essential elements of the placement. Through the use of supervision students will develop competence in integrating personal values, professional values, ethics and frameworks into practice. Students will apply self-care strategies and undertake critical examination and evaluation of social work in practice. Students will be able to articulate social work skills in dynamic and diverse settings. This professional placement develops students’ skills to operate as beginning social workers in self-directed practice.

title: Planning Analytics
description: To develop skills for the preparation, undertaking and presentation of individual research on a planning topic. Dividing research into discrete tasks that collectively produce a competent planning report. To encourage critical self reflection of research preparation and outcomes.

title: 3D Design Practice
description: This unit introduces knowledge and required skills in 3D digital modelling and producing prototypes. Parametric solid modelling software CAD is used to create designs as forms, scale drawings, and images. Then, 3D digital modelling techniques are utilised to produce the created designs.

title: Introductory Actuarial Practices
description: This unit is an introduction to the use of Excel, one of the fundamental tools of business, with an emphasis upon financial applications. The unit will provide a mix of the theoretical framework of key financial concepts, such as accumulated value and discounted present value, alongside practical application. The basic and financial functions of Excel will be used to solve business problems such as the preparation of a loan amortisation schedule and determination of discounted present value and internal rate of return for a series of fixed cash flows. The importance of clarity, structure and flexibility in the development of Excel spreadsheets will also be covered.

title: Photography Core Principles
description: This unit introduces students to the core principles of photographic production. Emphasis is placed on developing student proficiency in photographic process, technique and practice to advance their emergence as innovative visual communicators.

title: Design Computing
description: Through a series of practical design projects and exercises, held within a digital environment, this unit introduces students to industry standard design technologies and software.

title: Natural Hazards
description: This unit examines the political ecologies of hazards from a geographical perspective. The concepts of risk, vulnerability and adaptation to select hazards are examined at the global, regional and local scale. The spatial distribution, severity of hazard impacts and strategies to minimize vulnerability are examined in the context of climate change, sustainable development, public policy and the vulnerability of communities in both developing and developed countries.

title: Foundations of Clinical Exercise
description: This unit explores the foundational principles related to the safe assessment, prescription and monitoring of exercise and rehabilitation across the lifespan and in selected clinical populations. Understanding of the physiological changes offered by physical activity, including aerobic and resistance exercise, is progressed to include the evidence-based effects of exercise on clinical populations. The basic principles related to implementing aerobic, strength and conditioning, motor control and range of movement exercise are applied to clinical case examples in the areas of musculoskeletal, cardiopulmonary, neurological and other physiotherapy settings. Factors that influence implementation success will be considered, including shared decision-making and motivational factors, biomechanical and physiological factors, desired functional goals and accessibility to resources needed for exercise. Students will develop their skills in shared decision-making with clients and effective verbal and digital communication with fellow health professionals working within a range of rehabilitation contexts.

title: Advanced Radiation Therapy Care
description: In this unit, students will critically evaluate the role of adjuvant oncology treatments, and the management of complex patient care situations. Students will investigate complex and emerging radiation therapy technologies and techniques. Students will engage with peers in interactive sessions to facilitate critical reflection and clinical decision making.

title: Child Development for Educators
description: Situated in the context of theory and research, this unit provides an overview of typical and atypical human development from conception to adulthood across physical, cognitive, social and emotional domains. Biological and environmental influences on development are examined. Implications for contemporary educators are explored with a focus on maximizing developmental outcomes from birth through young adulthood. In addition to emphasis on knowing your students and how they learn, this unit focuses on effective engagement and interaction with parents/carers and maintaining safe school and care environments for children and adolescents. This includes developing awareness of child development services in the community.

title: Skills in Professional Writing
description: This unit introduces students to foundational skills in professional writing. It offers development of critical and analytical reading and writing skills and develops an understanding of the use of argument and persuasion in the field of public discourse.

title: Structural Analysis of Indeterminate Structures
description: This unit introduces classical and computer methods of structural analysis to enable students to assess, quantify and communicate an understanding of statically indeterminate structures’ behaviours. The syllabus includes application of the key concepts of compatibility, stiffness and flexibility to conduct analysis of structures by the force method, slope deflection method, moment distribution method and computer software.

title: Photogrammetry for Mining Operation
description: This unit is an introduction into Photogrammetry with a special focus on applications in mining operation. The fundamentals of photogrammetry, the photogrammetric workflow and its products will be introduced, and applied to tasks related to underground and open pit mining operation. Applications including the mapping of mine sites, the estimation of stock pile volumes as well as geotechnical analysis. The learned theory in the lectures is reinforced during tutorials and practical laboratories.

title: Creative Arts Professional Practicum
description: This unit allows students to access authentic work experiences in the creative industries. Coordination of placements to specific  environments with designated reputable organisations will be facilitated and supervised.

title: Fine Art Project Advanced
description: This unit is designed to further develop your capacity to refine, resolve, present and critique self-directed studio practice. You will contextualise your practice within a broader cultural, social and international context and prepare a body of work for exhibition through group discussion and ongoing presentations.

title: Introduction to Indigenous Australians
description: Introduction to the cultural, historical and social conditions and major issues which have shaped and continue to shape the lives of Indigenous people in Australia, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander identity, culture, diversity and worldview; pre and post colonization in Australia; Indigenous achievement; and reconciliation.

title: Linear Algebra 1
description: This unit will consider problems arising from science, engineering and business related fields. Students will learn the necessary skills to model and solve such problems through the introduction of mathematical techniques of linear algebra as well as complex analysis. Students will be introduced to idea of a complex number together with their applications and use in solutions to polynomial equations. This unit will cover vectors, lines and planes and their extension into n-dimension space. This unit also covers matrices and their use for solving systems of linear equations through a study of a number of different types of solution methods. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors will be considered. This unit is designed for those students who have passed WACE Mathematical Applications or Mathematical Methods or equivalent.

title: Corporate and Community Media Production
description: This unit aims to develop students’ communication, creative and entrepreneurial skills, while working with real-world clients on advanced media production projects.

title: UX Business Optimisation
description: User experience (UX) is the end-to-end experience a user has with a product, system, platform or service, and it has become integral to contemporary business practice. UX is an increasingly important tenant of digital marketing and technology interaction and is critical to effectively solving problems at many scales, including persons, users, businesses, and those facing society as addressed through the UN Sustainable Development Goals. In this unit, you will deeply explore real-world problems from a Systems Thinking perspective, implementing a range of industry-driven methods, techniques, and methodologies to design creative and innovative solutions to real-world problems.

title: Big Data and Health
description: This unit will provide the opportunity for students to learn how to use big data to comprehend complex real-world health challenges. It provides an introduction to how data are generated and used in health contexts. It gives students the opportunity to investigate the major sources of data relevant to health and explore how this information can be used to create evidence for policy, research and individual behaviour change.

title: Property Investment Analysis
description: Income producing properties play a vital role as an asset class for both households and corporate entities. In this unit students examine the time value of money, investment decisions, debt financing, components of income, accounting procedures and taxation relevant to income producing properties. Students will construct complex cash flow analysis spreadsheets and calculate the investment value of income producing properties to assist in making informed decisions.

title: Introduction to Contract Law
description: This unit focuses on contractual formation, including, agreement, intention, consideration and estoppel; the limits on the enforceability of contracts, including privity & formalities; and the substantive content of contracts, including oral statements, the incorporation of terms & express and implied terms. Study of this unit also enables a student to develop their communication skills via the negotiation exercise.

title: Mechatronics Design Project
description: Problem-based learning to develop knowledge and skills of designing and building autonomous machines are covered. Students sketch and analyse block diagrams and schematic drawings. Lab activities include design, analysis and construction of analogue and digital systems and pulse-width modulated voltage control circuits. Applications of feedback and timers in linear systems are introduced. Principles of top-down software design are also covered. Sensor selection and deployment are demonstrated.

title: Leadership and Evidence Based Practice in Physiotherapy
description: This unit develops students’ understanding of World Health Organisation social determinants of health and current Australian national health priorities in the context of evidence-based physiotherapy practice. Specifically, social determinants of health and Australian national health priorities will be integrated through the three pillars of leadership, evidence-based practice and cultural security. To facilitate critical thinking skills and collaborative behaviours, students will engage in a participatory action research project.

title: Manufacturing Processes
description: This unit introduces different manufacturing processes such machining, casting, metal forming, powder metallurgy, welding, and additive manufacturing with the special attention on production planning and computer numerical control (CNC) simulation. The students will also have hands-on experience to apply the knowledge in different manufacturing processes.

title: Power, Politics and Government
description: This unit introduces students to the role of power and politics in the public sphere. It investigates the origins, forms, distribution and control of power, the tension between cooperation, competition and conflict, and the role and function of the modern democratic state as a sovereign political community operating in a defined territorial area.

title: Introductory Neuroscience
description: This unit introduces students to physiotherapy assessment and management principles for people with pathologies resulting in neurological impairments across the adult lifespan. The unit explores holistic, person-centred care using the ICF framework for subjective and objective assessment and physiotherapy treatment and management. Decision-making and inter-professional team-work is applied in a neurological context, with a focus on problem-solving and clinical reasoning. Professional written and verbal communication skills are also developed in this context.

title: Health Promotion Methods
description: Critically assessing the selection of health promotion strategies, methods and activities. Applying models of behaviour change, group process, community development and population-based theories to health promotion. Utilising health education, learning styles, principles of learning, group formation, facilitation, values, beliefs and attitude identification, environmental adaptations, negotiation and conflict resolution for health promotion practice.

title: Statistical Modelling
description: This unit will introduce students to different aspects of statistical modelling, estimation, and inference. Generalized linear modelling (GLM) extends Normal linear model theory to encompass distributions from the exponential family of distributions, including binomial (logistic regression) and Poisson distributions (loglinear models). Analysis of GLMs will also include formulation, estimation, model selection, diagnostic-checking, and evaluation of predictive ability. GLM will be extended to include extreme value theory and distributions. In time series analysis, the focus shifts to the analysis of data collected or observed sequentially in time. Students will be introduced to the modelling of different types of time series using autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models. Topics to be covered include exploratory data analysis, identification of ARIMA models, estimation, diagnostic checking, and forecasting.

title: Geological Field Mapping
description: Geological mapping in the field, and application of appropriate field techniques to support the generation of a field map. Map preparation, core logging and report writing.

title: Photography Studio Processes
description: This unit explores the theory, history and applied professional practices of studio based photography. This unit will introduce students to sophisticated lighting techniques that facilitate the production of choreographed lighting in photographic practice. A professional photographic approach to digital outcomes will also be examined in this unit. Students will be required to develop photographic outcomes through a series of projects that demonstrate a disciplined engagement with professional studio based photographic practice.

title: Industrial Fluid Mechanics
description: This unit is designed in three blocks. The first block promotes the general knowledge of fluid mechanics for system analyses. This section provides insight into sources of energy loss, pumps and other turbomachinery equipment. The second block combines some of the essential subjects in particulate flow and elaborates on particle-flow interactions. The section is continued with granular beds and porous media engineering. The section on particulate flow is concluded with fundamentals and application of discrete element modelling (DEM) to be used as numerical tools for particle-flow simulations.The third block introduces the non-Newtonian fluids, including slurries and dives into understanding rheological behaviours. Multiple methods of pressure drop, unique characteristics and design implications are discussed.

title: A History of the Modern Middle East
description: This unit examines the modern political history of the Middle East from the late Ottoman Empire to the present and the region’s global significance. It traces the effects of colonialism, authoritarianism and democratisation on the region. Students who complete the unit will develop a broad understanding of the historical forces that have shaped the Middle East and North Africa. In so doing, students will also gain a strong understanding of some of the key phenomena in the region, such as the tensions between Arab Nationalism and Islamism, the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, and militant Islam.

title: Petrology
description: Students will learn to describe and classify of igneous and metamorphic rocks in hand specimen and thin section. We will cover the generation of primary magmas in the mantle and crust, the mechanisms by which those magmas are emplaced as intrusions and lavas, and the processes that lead to magmatic differentiation. Students will learn how to interpret igneous and metamorphic rocks through the use of simple phase diagrams and the role of whole-rock chemistry, temperature and pressure on mineral assemblages, with implications for constraining tectonic settings.

title: Studies in Language Development
description: Development of communication, language and speech in infancy, early, middle and late childhood, adolescence and adulthood. Observing, describing, analysing and documenting communication, language and speech behaviours.

title: Integrated Gerontology
description: In this unit, students learn about the pathophysiologic and psychosocial changes associated with ageing. The impact of global ageing, burden of care, ethical, and medicolegal issues in gerontology are considered in relation to occupational therapy frameworks (Person Environment Occupation Performance/Participation (PEOP)). The unit is strongly focused on the development of Occupational Therapy skills within all practice contexts relevant in Western Australia (community, tertiary and residential aged care) with a specific focus on learning through application in residential aged care. Furthermore, integrated gerontology explores personal, cultural and societal understandings of ageing. Assessment, treatment, rehabilitation, illness prevention and health promotion of age related health conditions is a focus of learning in this unit.

title: Advanced Pharmacology
description: In this unit students will compare and contrast the pharmacology of drugs acting on the cardiovascular, renal, endocrine and central nervous system (CNS). This unit of learning will investigate drugs affecting lipoprotein metabolism, diuretics, vasodilators calcium channel blockers and antithrombotics, including drugs affecting heart rhythm. Psychostimulants and drugs of abuse are also discussed, including drugs for Parkinson’s and other neurodegenerative disorders, epilepsy, and drugs used to treat behavioural disorders. The unit includes discussions on the chloride ion-GABA receptor complex, benzodiazepine receptor agonists and antagonists. Cancer progression will be investigated with the antineoplastic drugs currently used to treat cancers in multiple organ systems. Absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion (ADME), mechanisms of action, adverse effects and detailed drug interaction potential including drugs covered in all previous pharmacology units will be examined.

title: Trunk Anatomy and Embryology
description: Explores the relationships between structure, function and embryological development of the somatic and visceral components of the neck, thorax, abdomen and pelvis.

title: Business Analysis for Investment
description: The aim of this unit is to equip students with necessary tools and techniques to assess the financial health of a company. Students will further develop their ability to interpret both financial and other information to evaluate business performance and value companies. The financial analysis skills acquired in the unit will be instrumental in making successful decisions in numerous business contexts, including: the evaluation of financial performance, the identification of sources of value creation, risk and credit assessment, and in assessing the achievement of financial targets and strategic goals. Topics discussed: Introduction to the financial statement analysis, understanding financial statements and supplementary information, financial analysis techniques and applications, evaluating financial reporting quality, analysis of financial statement for forecasting, valuation and risk analysis purposes.

title: Ethics and Sustainability in Engineering
description: This unit focuses on how the Profession of Engineering can support people and the planet by providing future Engineers with appropriate tools, ways of thinking, and a sense of responsibility and agency to lead for change. The unit includes the importance of the context in which Engineering is practised, which incorporates an appreciation of diverse perspectives and societal values in considering sustainability, including reflecting on the values of traditional First Nations Peoples. The unit content is broadly organised into three clusters: (1) Engineering Ethics and Sustainable Development: an introduction to the sustainable development agenda and debate and ethical responsibilities of the Profession of Engineering. (2) Resource Management Tools and Practices: the 'nuts and bolts' of efficient resource utilisation in 'industrial' operations, including life cycle assessment, ecoefficiency analysis, triple bottom line analysis, and environmental management system. (3) Sustainable Technology: an exploration of technology's role (engineering) in achieving sustainable development.

title: Introduction to Business Programming
description: This unit is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in basic programming and computational concepts, regardless of their previous coding experience. Through a variety of interactive learning activities, students will gain the knowledge and skills necessary to confidently apply programming tools and techniques to solve problems in a range of fields, such as business, science, and engineering. By the end of the unit, students will be able to develop and implement effective programs using appropriate programming languages and apply best practices in program design and development.

title: Engineering Professionalism and Communication
description: This unit is focused on developing the awareness of the Engineering Profession for students, covering professional behaviour and image. Professional institutions, engineering ethics and qualifications are introduced and after graduation activities such as recruitment and career progression are practised. Communications skills are developed, with emphasis on negotiation and presentation techniques as well as Indigenous Perspectives. Occupational health and safety including legislation is covered. The unit also covers an introduction to Law including the Australian Legal System, Intellectual Property and Employment laws. There is a focus on leadership, technological change, and marketing with a view to preparation for future careers. Work Experience requirements including reflections are covered. Group presentations are an integral part of the syllabus.

title: Digital Signal Processing
description: Due to an ever-increasing advances in digital technology, there is now a greater ability to manipulate and extract information from signals digitally. This unit aims to introduce students to some of the concepts and techniques of digital signal processing and their applications. These include Discrete-time signal and system theory; Sampling; Design of Finite Impulse Response (FIR) and Infinite Impulse Response (IIR) digital filters; Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). Additionally, students will be introduced to discrete-time random signals and to Spectrum estimation and analysis.

title: Tectonics and the Dynamic Earth
description: The mechanical, thermal and chemical structure of the earth. Lithospheric plates, and the driving mechanism for their relative movement. Evolution and dynamics of the Earth's core and mantle. Rifting, stretching and loading of continental crust, continental margins, ocean tectonics, mid ocean ridges, mantle plumes and continental flood basalts. Subduction zone and arc mechanics, magmatism, metamorphism and sedimentary basins. Collisional orogens, granites, channel flow and exhumation. Craytons, mobile belts and tectonic processes in Precambrian and Phanerozoic orogens. Continental growth through time. Palaeomagnetism, plate reconstruction and the supercontinent cycle.

title: Environmental Applications of Geographic Information Science and Remote Sensing
description: Developed for Environmental Scientists, this unit teaches principles of Geographic Information Science (GISc) and Remote Sensing (RS) with a large emphasis on enabling students to explore practical and contemporary environmental issues interactively. The GISc content focuses on LiDAR point cloud processing, terrain analysis (geomorphometry, potential incoming solar radiation, hydrology) for use in species distribution modelling, spatial pattern analysis and geostatistics. The RS portion includes the use of satellites and UAVs (drones) for capturing imagery of the Earth’s surface. Students will use the different image sources to learn rectification, mosaicking and a variety of image processing techniques (e.g. spectral indices, classification algorithms).

title: International Study Abroad - Australian Experience
description: A formal program and learning contract for international study abroad students coming to Australia will be negotiated for each practicum/fieldwork offered.  The purpose and objectives will vary depending upon the designated field experience; however; students should consider the cross-cultural implications of their activities.

title: Physics 2
description: Physics 2 assumes that students have passed Physics ATAR and Mathematics Methods ATAR or equivalent (or higher). Students who have not passed these units or equivalent should enrol in PHYS1006 Foundations of Physics. The unit begins with an introduction to the basic laws of electricity and magnetism and their applications. It includes consideration of electrostatic fields in free space, magnetic fields due to steady currents, and electromagnetic induction, leading to an understanding of the basic properties of Maxwell's equations. The course then explores two pillars of modern physics: quantum mechanics and relativity. The study of quantum mechanics begins with its origins in the photoelectric effect and leads up to the time independent solution of Schrodinger's wave equation. An introduction to both general and special relativity is included. This course includes a laboratory component which will involve experiments and computer simulations that are linked to the lecture material and will give students experience and understanding in measurement and uncertainties, physical data analysis and report writing.

title: Advanced Marine Science and Technology
description: Advances in science and technology used in coastal and marine research improves the efficiency and accuracy of data collection, the scope and applicability of results, and ultimately, sustainable resource management. MARI3000 Advanced Marine Science and Technology exposes students to the technology currently used in coastal and marine research and the science it underpins. Guest lecturers will present their current work using particular technologies and will pose real-life problems that can be addressed using these methods. Students will intensively workshop solutions to these problems, and present their work in a variety of highly contextualised formats. Examples of topics that may be covered are advances in remote sensing, remote and autonomous underwater vehicles, oceanographic instrumentation, genomics, acoustic tagging and ecological modelling.

title: Illustration Fundamentals
description: This unit introduces students to the fundamental principles and technical processes of illustration design. Students will learn how to visualise and communicate narrative concepts, developing their abilities as skilled technical practitioners and visual communicators.

title: Introductory Mathematics
description: In this unit students will revise the necessary numerical skills and basic algebraic skills to solve pre-calculus problems found in science, engineering and business-related fields through the application of commonly occurring simple mathematical functions and techniques of linear algebra. The unit covers the properties, manipulations and solutions of algebraic equations and inequalities as well as polynomial, exponential, logarithmic and rational functions. Students will learn trigonometry of the triangle and its use in the solution of right angle and acute triangles and also trigonometry of the circle including angular velocity and acceleration. Students will be introduced to idea of a complex number and use in solutions to polynomial equations. This unit will cover basic vectors and their applications. This unit also covers matrices and their use for solving systems of linear equations through a study of a number of different types of solution methods. This unit is designed for those students who only have the rudimentary maths knowledge so that no real prerequisite is required.

title: Taxation Administration
description: The aims of Taxation Administration are to give you a basic understanding of the administration of the Australian Taxation system and the role various authorities play in the administration of taxation laws. The unit introduces you to the requirements to lodge an annual income tax return and associated elections, which then result in the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) issuing an assessment.
