We will consider the various means by which outstanding taxation payments can be collected by the ATO. Disputes are common regarding the imposition of taxation and a review of the objection and appeals process will be considered. As the administrator of the Australian taxation system we will consider in depth the role of the Australian Taxation Office including their legislated powers. As a means of deterring taxpayers from not complying with their taxation affairs a strict penalty regime is imposed. Other areas we will consider will be the use of ATO Rulings and the role of a Tax Professional. We will also consider the Commissioner’s remedial power, some state taxation administration powers and topical issues in taxation administration. This unit also includes a field trip to the Perth offices of the ATO.

title: Health Promotion, Media and Advocacy
description: Media use as a health communication / health promotion strategy. The measurable impact on public health of: news reporting (e.g. causes of death, celebrity diagnoses); advertising of unhealthy products (e.g. tobacco, alcohol, junk food); entertainment programming (e.g. representation of violence, mental health and suicide on TV); and entertainment-education. Health communication via: social and online media; mass media (e.g. newspapers, TV, radio); folk media (e.g. theatre, song); and limited reach media (e.g. pamphlets, posters). How to plan, develop, test, implement and evaluate health communication media. Getting to know your audience. Co-design with your audience. Literacy, health literacy and media literacy. Unintended media effects, misinformation and disinformation. Marketing and social marketing. Managing a social marketing campaign. Advocacy and media advocacy strategies: planning and implementation. Giving interviews, writing media releases and working with journalists.

title: Mental Health Research Evaluation
description: This unit evaluates ethical research practice and develops and integrates evaluation research concepts within Indigenous mental health practice frameworks. Students will review Indigenous community principles and practice within Indigenous Terms of Reference. Attention will be given to the establishment of a Critical Reference Group (CRG) and other stakeholders in the project.

title: Engineering Electromagnetics
description: Engineering electromagnetics is a fundamental branch of electrical engineering that combines physical reasoning and mathematical analysis to describe and explain the behaviour of key electrical quantities and components such as voltage, current, resistors, capacitors and inductors. While circuit theory enables us to calculate system-level responses, electromagnetics reveals the physical principles that govern component behaviour. You will learn how capacitors store energy in electric fields, how inductors store energy in magnetic fields, and how time-varying fields lead to coupling between electric and magnetic phenomena. These principles will be applied to the analysis of transmission lines, the transfer of power and information and the propagation of electromagnetic waves, the foundation of wireless communication and sensing technologies. To support your learning, the unit incorporates programming exercises to visualise complex equations, hands-on experiments using industry-standard measurement equipment and specialised electromagnetic simulation software to design and analyse matching networks. These tools will deepen your conceptual understanding and provide valuable practical skills aligned with professional engineering practice.

title: Science, Technology and Global Problems
description: Science and Technology are critical tools for addressing global problems. This unit investigates the nature of knowledge, science, data and problems with a global focus. Working in inter-disciplinary teams, students focus on the development of practical and theoretical solutions to real global problems using current and emerging scientific fields. In doing so they develop important skills in defining problems, scientific inquiry, building and working effectively in teams.

title: Curriculum and Instruction Senior Secondary: English
description: This unit is designed to prepare pre-service teachers to teach the Senior Secondary English curriculum. The focus of the unit is on curriculum planning, teaching strategies, assessment, reporting, the demonstration of positive impact on student learning and research relating to Senior Secondary English. The unit examines moderation, the provision of feedback and responding to individual student needs.

title: Medical Imaging Practice 1
description: Positioning theory, patient care, communication, radiographic or surface or applied anatomy, commonly encountered pathology or trauma, image acquisition and interpretation relevant to the beginner practitioner.

title: Fit, Form and Function
description: Contemporary fashion design is built on the foundations of fit, form and function. This unit engages students in a re-examination of the traditional application of these three components of design. The classic design of the three pieces suit forms the primary focus for investigation into the parameters of fit form and function in garment, and the application of deconstructionist theory.

title: Network Optimisation for Transport and Logistics
description: The unit focuses on 4 core topics in network optimisation: minimum-cost flow problems, optimal fleet sizing, arc routing problems, and node routing problems. For minimum-cost flow problems, areas covered include the standard problem formulation, shortest path problems, maximum flow problems, transportation problems, assignment problems, and the network simplex algorithm. For optimal fleet sizing, areas covered include deterministic and stochastic formulations, left and right derivatives, convex analysis, and the golden section method. For arc routing problems, the areas covered include the Chinese postman problem, Fluery's algorithm, Floyd-Warshall algorithm, matchings, and Euler tours. Finally, for node routing problems, the areas covered include the travelling salesman problem, heuristic methods and lower bound techniques.

title: Journalism Industry Placement
description: This unit presents students with the opportunity to hone their journalistic skills while undertaking a placement at a Western Australian media organisation. Students will validate their theoretical and professional knowledge in news room situations, filing copy, attending media and press conferences while working in a collaborative environment. Students will apply that knowledge within the legal and ethical parameters which apply to the profession. This unit will measure how well students understand the nexus between professional practice and academic theories.

title: Web Media
description: For at least twenty years, we have seen a trend towards 'convergence' in the media, as new social understandings and new business models emerge that break down the distinction between traditional media forms (print and broadcast news, films and games, and so on). We have also seen the development of social or participatory media, without rigid boundaries between consumers, creators and producers. The Internet has played a critical role in these processes, becoming the key frame of reference for discussions of the future of converging and participatory media. In particular, the World Wide Web enables the production, distribution, remixing and remediation of an extraordinary array of digital media content and the linking together of otherwise separate media forms. In this unit, you will investigate why and how media are transforming in the era of convergence and participation, and then put these insights into practice by creating web-based media content.

title: Clinical Exercise and Sports Injury
description: This unit examines the role of exercise in the management of chronic health conditions and the prevention and acute management of sports injuries. The pathophysiology of common chronic health conditions will be explored together with the role that exercise (and exercise scientists) play in managing these conditions. Common sports injuries will be explored in the context of the injury cycle with a particular focus on the role of the exercise scientist in injury prevention, acute management and referral procedures, and return to sport.

title: Personal Finance
description: An introduction to personal financial management. This unit covers important aspects of personal financial planning including understanding the regulatory environment in Australia, ethics, and basic financial planning skills required by an individual or future planner. This unit also explores direct and indirect investment opportunities offered by contemporary financial markets and their characteristics. In addition, risk management and insurance, superannuation and estate planning are covered to provide broader understanding of constructing a financial plan.

title: Paramedic Clinical Practice 1
description: Within this unit, students will apply their theoretical knowledge to assess, diagnose, plan, manage, document, and evaluate patient care across the patient's lifespan (including scene safety, patient assessment, therapeutic management and diagnostic reasoning). Linked to the other semester 3 units, students will learn to assess and manage clinical conditions within a paramedic context. Assessment skills will be expanded with a key focus on identifying the deteriorating patient, performing diagnostic assessments, and using clinical reasoning to inform management. Additional airway skills will be introduced alongside increased medication options and intravenous access. All clinical practice will be grounded in relevant paramedic ethical, legal, professional, and person-centred frameworks, with a strong emphasis on reflective practice. Students will critically evaluate their experiences to develop self-awareness, enhance decision-making, and continuously improve the quality of care they provide.

title: Advanced Tort Law
description: This unit provides advanced coverage of the law of negligence, focusing on the duty of care in a range of novel fact situations. The unit also examines vicarious liability, breach of statutory duty, the assessment of damages, defamation, and private nuisance actions, and will touch upon non-delegable duties of care.

title: Integrated Neuroscience
description: This unit continues to develop students’ skills in neurological physiotherapy applying an evidence-informed approach to more complex presentations including stroke, traumatic brain injury, and spinal cord injury. Students will apply principles learned in Introductory Neuroscience to a variety of conditions across a range of acuities, using clinical reasoning, problem-solving and person-centred approaches. Effective verbal and digital communication skills will continue to be developed in an interprofessional neurological context, including person-centred goal-setting and discharge planning. Student will also explore innovative technologies and consider the management of long-term chronic neurological conditions with the goal of optimising ability and quality of life.

title: Interior Architecture Project Studio 2
description: Under the direction of experienced Interior Design practitioners students are offered a professional environment which incorporates a breadth of practice and academic experiences relevant to the discipline of interior architecture. Each student will initiate and develop an individual Interior Architecture design project aimed at developing their design expertise. Students are required to identify, explore and extend their chosen project, testing spatial ideas and concepts in relation to human occupation beyond pre-existing and embedded assumptions and inclusive of cultural and international perspectives. Students are encouraged to demonstrate innovative, reflective design practice, drawing from their existing body of work to demonstrate an emerging identity as a designer, while demonstrating command over relevant practice conventions and communication techniques and strategies. Design prototyping and testing are to be done through digital fabrication and simulated environments.

title: Illustration Concepts and Processes
description: Illustration practice involves the exploration and development of ideas by using a wide range of skills, techniques and processes. Throughout this unit students are encouraged to experiment with as many different techniques as possible. This enables students to convey messages in appropriate and effective ways to a series of design briefs.

title: Health and Safety Professional Practice
description: Development and expansion of professional and practical skills within a workplace situation. A major component is the design and completion of a workplace-based project in a field of interest and appropriate to career development.

title: Online Games and Play
description: This unit explores the broader spaces and nature of play online, and how it relates to the development of digital forms of gaming. The nature of immersion, and its relationship to interactivity, is examined, investigating how narrative is constructed and communicated through game play. The unit provides critical perspectives on the notion of gamification and the growing area of research centred around videogame streamers and the labour ecosystem of eSports. It examines a series of gaming tropes and themes, games as texts, and the ways that games enter social frameworks to convey, refract, engage with, and resist power structures. An ongoing focus is on the function of rules in framing play, particularly in relation to how players cheat, hack and mod their games to break those rules.

title: Development Outcomes
description: Introduction to the character of the development control process, to understand its role in the broader planning process, and to develop the necessary skills to apply development assessment to a range of typical development proposals to produce 'quality' development outcomes.

title: Midwifery Clinical Practice
description: The focus of this unit is on increasing midwifery skills and experience, including quality use of medicines and medication administration, through clinical experience. This unit includes clinical experience in woman-centred care as part of midwifery continuity of care practice with individual women. The Midwife Standards for Practice (2018) inform the scope and purpose of this unit.

title: International Experience 8
description: n/a

title: Managing Operations
description: Operations management is a core activity within all organisations, critical to business strategy, performance outcomes, competitiveness and sustainability. This unit examines the role of operations in service and manufacturing, profit and non-profit and small and medium organisations. A strategic approach to understanding operations is employed, with innovation and excellence examined to create sustainable competitive advantage. The unit provides conceptual, analytical and practical learning into the management, challenges and opportunities of operations.

title: International Study Abroad 7
description: n/a

title: Clinical Decision Making in Paramedicine
description: In this unit, students will explore theories and models of clinical decision-making and their relevance in the paramedic setting. Cognitive bias and its impact on patient safety will be explored. Frameworks to guide clinical decision-making will be introduced, and their efficacy will be evaluated. The role of social and economic factors, safety netting and patient values will also be explored in clinical decision-making. Effective communication, including verbal and written communication, as influences on bias and patient safety throughout the patient journey will also be explored. Finally, students will consider non-medical factors and available referral pathways to develop management plans for acute patients of all acuity types.

title: Physical Metallurgy
description: In this unit, the relationship between the microstructure of metals and other materials and their mechanical properties is studied. Following this, the control of material microstructures in order to control the mechanical properties of metals is investigated, including mechanical testing, strain hardening and annealing, solidification strengthening, solid solution and dispersion strengthening, as well as strengthening by phase transformation and heat treatment. In addition, corrosion, wear and static and dynamic failure of metals are investigated. Finally, ferrous and non-ferrous metal alloys and their roles in industry and society are treated in more depth.

title: Small Business Growth
description: This unit focuses on integration and analysis of key functions, concepts and strategies for growth-oriented Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs). The unit has a significant fieldwork component where students work in teams to identify a small business owner who agrees to engage with the students throughout semester as they analyse and evaluate aspects of the business. Students conclude this Unit by producing a tailored report which focuses on and applies key functions, strategies and concepts gathered throughout the Unit. The owners are invited to provide input into the assessment of the report to retain the reality-based approach of this live case.

title: Social Work Integrity and Accountability in Practice
description: This unit engages students in an exploration of integrity and accountability within legal, ethical and values frameworks. It provides an introduction to key legal discourses and frameworks. Students will develop competence in accessing and interpreting legal information and gain knowledge of key legal concepts relevant to social work practice. Ethics is considered within the Australian Association of Social Work (AASW). Students will gain an introduction to social work values and undertake critical comparisons of personal and cultural values with social work values.

title: Sociocultural Perspectives of Sustainability
description: This unit examines what people of diverse cultural and social backgrounds understand by sustainability. It looks at how they are affected by and respond to state, market and wider community strategies to bring about more sustainable ways of living. Some of the main topics may include: the idea of sustainability in social science; the relationship between social, cultural and environmental notions of sustainability; how people understand and relate to the natural world; the social and cultural meaning of sustainable development; and sustainable bodies. Case materials will be drawn from various sociocultural contexts around the world.

title: Electric Power Generation, Transmission and Distribution
description: This unit explains the foundation of generation, transmission and distribution networks. The unit covers the principal operation of various types of generations including thermal, hydraulic, nuclear, natural gas and renewable energy sources. The application of FACTS and storage devices in power systems along with system stability and transmission line compensation are covered. The unit also covers the main steps of designing an overhead transmission line with supporting structure and insulation strings. Corona, travelling waves and fault location in overhead lines are also covered.

title: Mineral Exploration Techniques
description: This project style unit will cover modern mineral exploration strategies, concepts and techniques with a practical on approach within an environmental, social and governance (ESG) framework. The unit will introduce different types of ore deposits and application of the mineral systems approach to select areas, explore and define targets for different deposit types using geological, geochemical and geophysical methods and modern data acquisition techniques. Students will learn about the drilling methods, analytical and QAQC procedures, acquisition using modern geophysical, analytical and scanning techniques, visualisation and interpretation of geological, geochemical and geophysical data in GIS and industry standard 3D software, culminating in a real world mineral exploration project. The role of technological advances in achieving sustainable practises in mineral exploration will also be introduced.

title: Indigenous Health Data Interpretation
description: This unit aims to show how qualitative and quantitative data can be used as evidence to make decisions in Indigenous healthcare practice. The focus is on data interpretation rather than analysis. Students will also develop skills to calculate simple descriptive statistics. It will also examine global and local Indigenous perspectives and the role that evidence-based practice plays in planning for better health outcomes.

title: Supply Chain Modelling and Optimisation
description: This unit introduces key concepts and activities in the areas of logistics and supply chain management and establishes the distinct role each plays in industrial modelling and optimisation. Basic skills in analysing, classifying and solving the fundamental components of inventory systems are developed using both single and multi-commodity deterministic and stochastic models. Forecasting techniques and practices are introduced. Case studies are used to highlight and expand the understanding and application of the topics discussed in the unit.

title: Relationships and Sexuality Education
description: This unit is designed to prepare students to deliver relationships and sexuality education (RSE), within a school or community-based setting. RSE is learning about the emotional, social and physical aspects of growing up, relationships, sex, sexuality and sexual health. Students will apply pedagogical approaches: acquiring knowledge, skills and positive attitudes towards RSE; and examine, plan, deliver and assess current RSE content. Other topics include the importance of a safe and supportive classroom environment, overcoming perceived barriers to RSE delivery, innovative teaching strategies, engagement with key stakeholders, affirming diversity, and working competently and confidently in a multicultural environment.

title: Japanese for Beginners
description: This unit introduces basic communicative skills in Japanese at an elementary level. Students acquire the four essential language skills of speaking, listening, reading and writing characters (Hiragana, Katakana, and Kanji) through ample practice in communicative activities supported by digital technology. Students will also be introduced to Japanese society and culture through mini-lectures, audio-visual presentations and virtual real-time classroom-based or online tutorials.

title: Strategic and Defence Planning
description: This unit introduces the key fundamentals of contemporary policy making and planning. Students will be introduced to a six-step national strategic planning process; the foundations of contemporary defence planning as an evolving process. They will become familiar with conceptual understanding of national purposes and national security interests. Students will learn about meaningful strategies, plans, programs and operations. Students will acquire core skills associated with contemporary strategic thinking, systematic planning, and the art of management of different assets.

title: Professional Practice in Public Health
description: Students will apply discipline, specific knowledge and skills during a relevant professional placement within their specific discipline area. They will also develop their professionalism, communication skills and their understanding of occupational health and safety and ethics in the workplace. They will learn to prepare documents to demonstrate employability.

title: Art and Design Fundamentals
description: This unit introduces students to the fundamentals common to art and design practices. The aim of the unit is to increase awareness of possibilities and to equip students with conceptual tools that can be used for generating, developing and refining art and design ideas. As well the unit develops analytical skills for trouble-shooting when an art or design work is not developing as intended.

title: Medical Radiation Special Topics 1
description: In this unit, students will explore selected special topics of relevance and currency to their Medical Radiation Sciences discipline, with a focus on advanced technology, MRS practice, or current professional issues. Students will investigate and appraise cutting-edge or specialised medical imaging or radiation therapy technology, explore and reflect on best clinical practice, and debate contemporary issues relevant to their profession. The special topics considered in this unit complement those of Medical Radiation Special Topics 2.

title: Behavioural Neuroscience
description: This unit examines the foundations and relationship of the brain, the central nervous system structure and function, and cognition. It also examines the relationship between neurophysiology and behaviours, including reference to contemporary addiction theories.

title: Art Visual Research 1
description: This unit is designed to develop skills in the visual arts through processes, techniques and research concepts relevant to contemporary art practice. You will develop research methodologies that will support and strengthen your investigation in contemporary art practice, through drawing or other media.

title: Sustainable Event Development
description: This unit takes a strategic approach to examine the impacts of events and festivals from a sustainability perspective. The unit considers ethical, responsible and sustainable concepts and theories when assessing and evaluating the economic, environmental and social-cultural impacts of local, national and international events. Sustainable event tools and techniques are examined, and challenges and opportunities are considered.

title: Cyber Security Concepts
description: An introduction to information security and management and cover the basic ISO27000 standard - how to build a security program and develop the appropriate security controls (administrative, logical and physical control); how to develop a set of policy to ensure effective risk management and resource usage verification. Industry standard for information security - ISO27000. Procedures used to secure data and resources at all levels in an ICT organization. Risk assessment and management.

title: Robot Manipulation Project
description: This unit introduces terminology, construction and geometries of industrial manipulators. Students learn forward and inverse kinematics and application of transformation methods and homogeneous matrices. Mathematical principles of robot velocity analysis are also introduced. The lab component of this unit introduces robot simulation software structure, robot middleware and use of analytical systems in simulated and real environments.

title: Fine Art Concepts and Contexts
description: Exploration of contemporary art practice from local, national and international perspectives. Examination of Western assumptions in contemporary art practice. This unit explores the relationship between research and practice.

title: Digital User Experience Design
description: This unit provides students with foundational knowledge and skills in user experience (UX) design. Through a combination of theoretical study and practical application, students will explore universal design principles, foundational UX theory, usability heuristics and the impact of technology on user experience.

title: English: Teaching Reading and Writing
description: This unit is about teaching English in the Primary years. The focus of this unit is on pre-service teachers developing an in-depth understanding of teaching children to read and write. Teaching reading and writing will be situated in the context of understanding different perspectives and theories about how children become literate. This unit will prepare pre-service teachers with knowledge of the multiple components to inform the comprehensive identification of children’s skills as readers and writers at various stages of their development. In addition, the unit will provide pre-service teachers with the basis for creating rich learning experiences for children.

title: Fine Art Theory and Criticism
description: In this unit students will examine the issues concerning contemporary and twentieth century art theory and practice from local and international perspectives. Issues and theories will be evaluated and critiqued through discourse, reviewing literature and in written format.

title: Supply Chain Technology and Systems
description: Management of supply chains for the organisation - organisational, functional and financial elements; using supply chains to improve customer service and competitive advantage; financial control of the overall supply chain; supply chain decision making and business planning; critical elements of supply chain design and operations - logistics, transportation, warehousing, inventory management, material management, purchasing, order processing; designing and optimising logistics and supply networks including outsourcing and process design; setting up and managing supply and distribution channels; supply chain information and decision support systems; supply chain master planning including demand forecasting; new supply chain challenges and opportunities - globalisation, e-business, new technologies, and corporate and social responsibilities.

title: Wastewater Treatment Principles and Design
description: This unit covers theory and conceptual design of systems for treating municipal wastewater. An overview of the characteristics of wastewater, treatment standards, and wastewater treatment processes are discussed. Physical and biological processes are presented, including sedimentation, biological treatment and sludge treatment. This unit includes a laboratory component for analysis of wastewater.

title: Virtual Production and Cinematography
description: This unit offers an industry-centric exploration of the virtual production pipeline, aimed at crafting motion-based creative outcomes. It delves into the integration of virtual production techniques with traditional cinematography to produce captivating and immersive narrative sequences. Throughout the unit, students will acquire a comprehensive understanding of virtual production, leveraging both technical and creative processes in relation to cinematography. Students will engage with industry practices and production pipelines, while synthesizing relevant theoretical frameworks in cinematography to create compelling narrative sequences. This unit equips students with the requisite skills to enhance their creative output and utilise industry-standard production techniques effectively.

title: Medical Radiation Sectional Anatomy
description: This unit enables students to advance their knowledge and skills in anatomical identification and relationships using 2D multiplanar reformatted views (axial, sagittal, coronal and oblique) of the head, neck, chest, abdomen pelvis, and limbs using Computed Tomography (CT) and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) images.

title: Decolonising Place
description: In this unit students will engage with critical race theory and the history of Western expansion through concepts of colonialism, modernity and globalisation. Students will investigate key texts in literature, film and theory to explore the distribution of political and economic power in the specific places in the world throughout history. Through a study of texts, including World and Indigenous texts, this unit investigates critical and aesthetic responses to colonialism.

title: Interactive Platforms
description: This unit introduces students to interaction design principles and the concepts, skills and tools required to produce a range of interactive experiences. Through practical projects and theoretical exploration, students build upon knowledge of prototyping and motion design techniques. Students develop an advanced understanding of interaction design principles for various digital modalities.

title: Building a Sustainable Workforce
description: This unit provides an analysis of the theoretical frameworks and contemporary practices which lead to building a sustainable workforce within complex internal and external environments. Within this context, the critical human capital recruitment, selection and retention practices and processes are discussed and analysed, with an emphasis on current and future challenges and trends. Special attention is paid to the practical implications of working towards sustainable workforces across a range of industries and national contexts, including implications for HR planning initiatives.

title: Physiotherapy Clinics 5
description: This fieldwork unit covers physiotherapy practice, to entry level standard according to the physiotherapy practice thresholds in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand.

title: Business Application Development
description: This unit explores contemporary programming concepts, emphasising their global application and role in fostering responsible technological innovation. It encourages students to design and develop globally relevant business applications, focusing on resolving unique problems using innovative technologies, while adhering to ethical software development practices.The unit emphasises software design techniques, visual development, event processing, file processing, and database interaction in a modern integrated development environment (IDE). Students will critically evaluate programming solutions, optimising logical and functional outcomes while being mindful of the global impact and ethical implications of their chosen development methods.

title: Elementary Australian Taxation Law
description: A general study of the taxes applicable to business entities, proprietors and shareholders - payroll tax, stamp duty, income tax, including capital gains tax, goods and services tax and fringe benefits tax.

title: Professional Midwifery Studies
description: This introductory midwifery unit will develop students’ academic writing and knowledge of the role and scope of practice of the midwife, models of maternity care, professional bodies and cultural perspectives. The unit will explore the historical, political, legal, ethical, quality and safety aspects of midwifery from local, national and international perspectives.

title: Petroleum Production Technology
description: An introduction to petroleum production systems including reservoir’s inflow performance and well’s outflow performance concepts, formation damage mechanisms, and nodal analysis; Basic well completions including options, types, properties, and selection based on producing scenarios, and familiarization of different downhole completion equipment; An overview of artificial lift systems including technologies, equipment and fundamental mechanisms of each system, and artificial lift selection criteria; Analysis and optimization of total petroleum production systems using conventional and nodal analysis.

title: Design Thinking and Visual Narrative
description: This unit provides an in-depth introduction to design thinking, the design thinking process, and several research methods that are commonly used in design thinking. You will be taken through the stages of the design thinking process and learn how to: (a) collect data using research methods; (b) analyse the data collected; and (c) apply the findings from your analysis to develop a solution to a brief. You will use the design thinking process to develop solutions. You will be required to work both individually and in a team.

title: Electromechanical Energy Systems
description: Electromechanical Energy Systems considers multiple aspects of energy transformation and distribution, mainly focusing on mechanical engineering-related aspects of electrical systems. From an electricity generation perspective, systems incorporating steam, hydraulic and gas turbines will be examined, using thermal input from solar energy or combustion with associated emissions controls, and cooling through psychrometric processes. Other forms of generation including nuclear energy, fuel cells, solar PV, wind, wave and geothermal energy will also be briefly considered, along with energy storage including batteries, pumped hydropower, and thermal storage. Electrical fundamentals include circuits and single phase, three phase transformers and auto transformers, equivalent circuits, phasor diagrams, testing, and parallel operation. Principle of operation characteristics and control of DC, single phase and three phase induction machines and synchronous machines will be presented, with applications to mechanical plant. There will also be an introduction to induction motors, stepper motors, brushless DC machines, and permanent magnetic machines, with an overall focus on energy efficiency.

title: Applied Geodetic Surveying
description: This unit comprises a surveying field camp in authentic conditions, involving teamwork and organisational skills development in order to complete 3D geodetic surveys to prescribed precision and accuracy. The unit will include planning, field surveying using discipline-specific equipment and techniques, analysis of surveying data, and report preparation for hypothetical clients in set timeframes.

title: Publishing
description: This unit provides advanced practical editing instruction, and allows students to build on existing knowledge and skills. They learn and practice the skills of editing to a real-world publishing project in which project management skills, high-level editing skills, and professional writing skills are utilised. The capacity to work independently and collaboratively to take a written text from submission to publication is developed. Students also learn to analyse and reflect on issues relevant to contemporary publishing industries.

title: Physics Project 2
description: This unit is designed to increase students' understanding and skills in physics research. The specific scientific 	project objectives are determined by the student and supervisor. The work carried out in PHYS3004 will most commonly carry on from what was completed in PHYS3003 and focus on tasks such as experimental work, data analysis, and report writing

title: Electrical Machines
description: In this unit, a review of fundamental concepts of three-phase circuits, singly and doubly excited electromagnetic systems, magnetic circuits, single- and three-phase transformers, single- and three-phase induction motors, DC motors, as well as an introduction to fractional horse power motors are presented.

title: Advanced Structural Analysis
description: This unit is on application of the matrix methods, computer software and approximate approaches to analysis of statically indeterminate structures. The contents include stiffness and flexibility concepts of truss and beam members, procedures of full and direct stiffness methods applied to trusses, beams and frames, flexibility methods applied to trusses, beams and frames, self-straining of structures, and analysis using commercial software and by approximate methods.

title: Curriculum and Instruction Lower Secondary: English
description: This unit is designed to prepare pre-service Lower Secondary English teachers (Years 7-10). Focus will be on curriculum planning, teaching strategies, evaluation, resources, the demonstration of positive impact on student learning and research relating to Lower Secondary English. Teaching and learning practices to support and challenge a diverse student cohort are explored.

title: Teaching and Learning in the Digital World
description: This unit provides an overview of technology enhanced resources commonly used to support teaching and learning. Fundamental skills, attitudes, and approaches that educators require to make effective personal and professional use of such resources in varied educational contexts will be addressed. A key focus will be effective integration of technology to enhance learning, teaching and management processes. Approaches for working in technology-rich educational contexts by which possible harm to one’s self and to others may be minimised through systematic assessment of risk, adoption of safe practices, and ethical behaviour will be explored.

title: Spatial Mapping
description: Application of basic topographic and cartographic principles. Application of CAD software packages to represent spatial data in two dimensions including but not limited to - coordinate systems, element placement and manipulation, editing, reference files and precision plotting. Field camp involving teamwork and organisational skills in order to plan, execute and present results of a topographic survey. The field camp includes but is not limited to - reconnaissance, traversing, levelling, detail survey, topographic mapping and report presentation of results.

title: Quality Assurance in Psychological Research
description: Key theoretical and research developments in pure and applied areas of psychology. Critique of theoretical and empirical bases of key concepts in psychology. Generation of methodological improvements in experimental, correlational and qualitative psychological research.

title: Sustainability and Durability of Concrete Structures
description: This unit focuses on the sustainable issues in concrete and materials and methods to improve the durability of concrete. Students will be introduced to various ways and methods to make concrete more sustainable using supplementary cementitious materials and recycled concrete. Basic mechanisms causing deterioration (reasons for repair) of concrete structures will be discussed. Tests for assessing durability of concrete structures, repair/restoration methods/techniques will also be discussed. Students will be introduced to Life Cycle assessment/analysis of concrete. Case studies of structures in service will be discussed and analysed.

title: Wildlife Conservation
description: This unit introduces the core principles of conservation biology with a focus on wildlife, exploring the causes and consequences of global biodiversity loss and the multidisciplinary approaches, including traditional Indigenous practices and modern scientific techniques, applied to maintain and restore this diversity. These themes will be developed through interactive workshops and practical classes, preparation of conservation relevant reports, and field visits to relevant organisations involved in conservation.

title: Introduction to Midwifery Bioscience
description: This unit focuses on the anatomy, applied physiology, assessment and support of well women and babies across the continuum of midwifery care. Students explore health promotion and education strategies for women with reference to preconception health, pregnancy, labour and birth, the puerperium and early neonatal care, breastfeeding and bio-psychosocial factors pertinent to midwifery practice.

title: International Study Abroad 5
description: n/a

title: Foundations of Pharmaceutical Sciences
description: This unit provides students with an introduction to the core concepts in pharmaceutical sciences, delivered across three modules with theoretical and practical components.Module 1: Pharmaceutical Calculations comprises essential skills and concepts, such as unit conversions, molar equivalence, concentration, density, dilution, pH and preparation of pharmaceutical solutions, including buffers. This module includes an introduction to laboratory safety and medicinal dosage forms in clinical use.Module 2: Pharmaceutical Analysis comprises general knowledge and practical skills for the quantitative analysis of medicinal substances via titrimetric and spectrophotometric techniques. This module includes an introduction to common and important functional groups within drug molecules.Module 3: Pharmaceutical Biochemistry introduces essential biomolecules and metabolic pathways. This module also explores enzyme function and energy metabolism, and considers the pharmaceutical relevance of these biochemical processes and their role in the molecular basis of disease.

title: X-Ray Diffraction and Electron Microscopy
description: Fundamental principles of electron microscopy and x-ray analysis. This will include fundamentals of the interaction of electrons with solids, theoretical and practical understanding of scanning electron microscopes (SEM), transmission electron microscopes (TEM), energy dispersive x-ray analysis. Sample preparation, operational modes, image analysis and signal processing. The advantages and disadvantages of different types of instruments. X-Ray topics will include x-ray fundamentals, absorption of x-rays, x-ray analysis, wavelength effects and relevant techniques. Theory of diffraction of x-rays and details of modern x-ray diffractometers. Introduction to crystallography, crystal structure, Bravais lattices, Miller indices. Phase identification and quantitative analysis.

title: Design Capstone Project
description: This unit will enable you to consolidate and apply the diverse skills and knowledge gained in your degree in preparation for entry into professional practice. Working in teams on an industry or applied academic project will afford you with the opportunity to extend your design, collaboration and project management skills. In addition to exposing you to the rigor of the design processes used in industry, the unit will challenge you to bridge the research/theory/practice nexus to deliver innovative, implementable designs showing a high level of resolution.

title: Leadership in Indigenous Australian Contexts
description: An exploration of a range of leadership models and theories. Students will apply professional and ethical practices and behaviours in Indigenous organisations and community settings. Students will determine appropriate and effective leadership qualities when engaging in professional and community contexts.

title: Consumer Law and Policy
description: This unit focuses on the development, sources and regulation of fair trading and consumer protection law in Australia, including its application to small business, at both State and Federal levels. Topics include consumer credit, misleading or deceptive conduct, statutory unconscionability provisions, unfair contractual terms in consumer contracts, consumer guarantees, and product liability and safety regulation. This unit develops students' capacities to communicate cogently and critically in a consumer law context.

title: Planning for Regions
description: Investigates the theories, processes and methods of regional planning including the links between theory and practice. Includes comparison of regional spatial forms, city regions and plans, systems, agencies and legislation.

title: Biochemical Principles in Pharmacology
description: This unit introduces important concepts for the understanding of the molecular basis of drug action within the human body. Normal and disease state processes at the cellular and molecular level are explored including; the genomics, proteomics, lipidomics and glycomics of living systems. Students investigate the normal regulation of biochemical pathways and the mode of action of related exogenous compounds used in deficiencies/disease states including inflammation: Topics include: Antibody and immunoglobulin structure and function plus local mediators; Signalling molecules and propagation of a signal: receptors and second messengers; Regulation of essential nutrients (vitamins and minerals): including iron and the production of necessary co-factors; Endogenous and exogenous “antioxidants”; Regulation of blood glucose levels and diabetes mellitus; Lipid relevance to atherosclerosis: regulation of lipoprotein metabolism, dyslipidaemia and drugs; Amino acids and urea synthesis including related diseases; Nucleic acid metabolism, gout and its treatments; and, Molecular and population genetics.

title: Systems Engineering Design
description: This unit provides students with a foundation of knowledge and skills necessary to use model-based systems engineering (MBSE) to support and manage systems engineering design activities, process interfaces and the whole design process. Students will learn concepts of modelling, systems thinking, and systems engineering within the framework of the engineering project life cycle. Emphasis is placed on identification of stakeholders needs, project management and speciality engineering supports, extending through concept development, requirement development, functional analysis and formulations (functional, physical and logical architectures), preliminary design (low-level requirement allocation to define system/subsystem configuration), detailed design (design synthesis, implementation), integration, verification, validation, operation, support, phase-out and disposal. Three pillars of MBSE: language (System Modelling Language (SysML)), Tool (software) and Approach (process to build the model) and how to use each to meet objectives during the systems engineering process design will be introduced with a focus on traceability and cross-cutting relationships. Students will be given an opportunity to develop practical skills in systems engineering through laboratories and projects.

title: Species Evolution Over Time
description: This unit is designed to prepare pre-service teachers to teach evolution in Senior Secondary Biology and Human Biology. It is an in-depth exploration into the theory of the evolution of life beginning with the history of evolution, evolutionary processes and changes over time starting at the genome level up to ecological communities, and finally it will conclude with the evolutionary story of humans. Conceptual and theoretical knowledge of evolutionary changes in species will build the necessary skills within the context of Senior Science curriculum planning, teaching strategies and assessment.

title: Fundamental Concepts of Data Security
description: This unit will cover the core information security principles of confidentiality, integrity and availability. These core principles will be applied to the concepts of information risk management, and the analysis and handling of compromised systems. The ethics around computer crime, privacy, and intellectual property are covered in detail. Finally, the unit will cover the criteria and controls for information classification.

title: Perinatal Mental Health for Midwifery Studies
description: This unit introduces the student to important aspects of perinatal mental health and midwifery practice. Students will develop their understanding of mental health and mental illness during pregnancy, birth and the postnatal period in order to provide sensitive, evidence-based midwifery care to women and their families.

title: Superannuation and Retirement Planning
description: The primary aim of this unit is to introduce students to the Australian Superannuation system and legislation. This unit is a taxation unit which aims to give a basic understanding of the practical application of income tax law and the superannuation legislation to regulate retirement savings in superannuation.

title: Foundations of Japanese
description: This unit covers both written and spoken Japanese at an introductory level that builds on prior knowledge gained in Beginning Japanese. A communication-oriented approach is used to help students develop confidence in speaking, listening, reading and writing Standard Japanese so that they will be able to interact with speakers of Japanese in simple day-to-day situations. A wider range of topics on Japanese society and culture will also be introduced through mini-lectures, audio-visual presentations and real-time classroom-based or online tutorials.

title: Foundations of Psychology
description: Broad outline of the study of mental processes. Introduction to perception, thinking, language, intelligence, consciousness, psychological disorders, and psychological therapies.

title: Indirect, State and Employment Taxes
description: By studying this unit you will be building upon your existing knowledge obtained from TAXA2000 and expanding this knowledge into Western Australian state taxes as well as employment taxes. On completion of this unit you will have obtained the knowledge to distinguish between Commonwealth and State tax systems and be able to demonstrate this through research methods, expand on understanding the language of taxing statutes in order to apply their provisions to situations you may come across in your career and to obtain the ultimate aim of achieving a high level of competency in reading and using tax legislation which is paramount for any tax career. As well as state taxes we will consider taxes and concepts associated with employment such as Fringe Benefits Tax, Superannuation, Salary Packaging and how payouts are taxed on cessation of employment. We will look at the concessional taxing of an important Australian industry that of primary production (farming) to assist them with the fluctuating income they face due to ongoing issues outside of their control, to highlight the important work undertaken by farmers we will participate in a trip to a farm for some practical and fun activities.

title: Science and Engineering Study Tour Experience
description: Take on a real-life industry project, explore a local, national or international destination, and immerse yourself in the local culture of the host destination. Before commencing the study tour, students will participate in seminars covering unit requirements, health and safety, assessments, and cultural competency training. During the tour component of the unit, students will undertake multimodal learning through lectures, seminars, workshops, and site visits, as well as informal experiential learning through cultural activities, group discussions and frequent debriefing with teaching staff. On their return, a final debriefing seminar will be held. Additional costs to attend the study tour are involved in addition to standard unit fees.

title: Clinical Medical Imaging Practice 2
description: This unit provides authentic medical imaging professional practice experience in the clinical setting, at the level appropriate for the intermediate beginner reflective professional.

title: Responsible Tourism Management
description: This unit provides students with the opportunity to recognise how tourism, hospitality, and events sectors increasingly understand the need to adopt responsible tourism policies and practices globally. The aim of responsible tourism is to develop tourism that makes the destination better for the community, and the environment while offering quality tourism experiences. Students will examine responsible tourism innovative approaches to better understand and manage the new complex realities of contemporary tourism development in domestic and international destination contexts. The unit will enable students to incorporate sustainable, ethical, and indigenous perspectives, critically explore community-based tourism issues around local economic development, community empowerment, and poverty reduction, as well as review responsible marketing practices and how technology is assisting in creating more responsible tourism.

title: Introduction to Planning
description: The origins, evolution and development of the planning of settlements and cities, from indigenous planning to 21st Century planning. The emergence of modern planning as a profession and as a response to the health issues and problems associated with the industrial city. Utopian ideas and pioneer thinkers in planning. An overview of key planning theories, the evaluation of planning documentation and the ethics of planning practice.

title: Professional Teaching Practice 1
description: This unit is the first in a sequence of four professional teaching practice focused units. The unit will support your understanding and application of key education theories, concepts and skills to develop your professional teaching practice. The first module will introduce evidence-based learning design for secondary teachers to meet the needs of diverse learners. The second module will introduce the theory and application of positive classroom management and the third module will address professional conduct behaviours and effective communication strategies for teachers. This unit is designed to provide a theoretical and practical foundation of essential skills you will need to demonstrate on a school-based professional experience placement. All required clearances to work with children must be obtained and valid, and all other preparation requirements met.

title: Video News
description: This unit introduces students to the theory and practice of video news production for the web and television. It equips students with the capacity to develop research, writing, interviewing and presentation skills for video news productions across platforms. This unit also introduces basic competencies in camerawork and editing.

title: A History of Terrorism and Insurgency
description: This unit focuses on the phenomena of terrorism and insurgency throughout the course of history up until the contemporary period. Students will explore the definitions, theories and driving forces behind these issues, seeking to develop an understanding of their historical continuities and how and why they have emerged as a threat to international security in the post-Cold War Environment. Drawing on an array of case studies, the unit will cover a diverse range of topics relating to political violence, including: ideology; the influence of globalisation; foreign fighters; countering violent extremism; and counterinsurgency.

title: Speech Sound Disorders
description: This unit focuses on assessment, analysis and intervention for speech sound disorders.

title: History and Theory of Art and Design 2
description: Theoretical perspectives that underpin historical twentieth century and contemporary art practice with a focus on different international and Indigenous perspectives.

title: Medicine 3
description: In this unit students extend their understanding of the human body and the pathophysiology of human disease at the individual, societal and global levels.Normal anatomy and physiology, pathological processes and disease manifestation, psychosocial factors, public health, principles of evidence-based practice, professionalism, ethical and legal considerations and rural Indigenous health are studied in an integrated manner through the exploration of clinical cases and interactive supportive seminars. Self-directed and peer led learning are complemented by expert guidance. Communication skills, clinical examination and procedural skills are taught alongside the scientific content.The first half of the year addresses in detail the Gastrointestinal system, Musculoskeletal system, and the Neurological system including Psychiatry.The second half of the year provides the opportunity for integrated extension and spaced revision of cumulative content.Professional behaviours and awareness and strategies for personal well-being appropriate to the medical workforce are also fostered, and observational placement opportunities within allied health and clinical settings complement the structured content, forming a sound base for the transition to clinical practice.

title: Pharmaceutical Technology
description: This unit introduces students to pharmaceutical technology, good manufacturing practice (GMP) and risk assessments in the production of sterile and non-sterile pharmaceutical products. Principles of parenteral formulation and heat sterilisation technology in the production of sterile products. Drug stability analysis in pharmaceutical product development, pharmaceutical packaging technology, and cold chain delivery. Controlled oral release technology in patient compliance and chronotherapeutics.

title: Korean Beginners 2
description: This unit builds on the learning outcomes of Korean Beginners 1. Focusing on a supportive and scaffolded approach to language learning, this unit will build on the basic written and spoken Korean communication skills achieved through the successful completion of Korean Beginners 1. On successful completion of this unit students will be able to extend their knowledge of the basic communication skills required when travelling or working in Korea. Through readings and classroom exercises, students will also be introduced to polite formal language registers required in the Korean workplace and learn further key grammatical structures while learning about Korean education system, workplace cultures food cultures to contextualise their language learning.On successful completion of Korean Beginners 1 and 2, students will reach a level of competency equivalent to the National Institute of Korean Language’s Standard Curriculum for Korean Language TOPIK-I Level 2 lower level proficiency.The study of Korean language and culture is highly recommended for students planning on a career in engineering, science, commerce, international relations, creative arts or teaching. Competence in an Asian language gives a competitive advantage in the labour market.

title: Emergency Management and Incident Investigation
description: This unit will equip students with the knowledge and skills required to plan for and manage occupational and environmental incidents and investigate the incidents to prevent a recurrence.

title: Injury Management and Workers Compensation
description: This unit explores individual, organisational, social and institutional responses to the management of occupational injury and disease. Specific consideration is given to the consequences of injury and disease, and the complex processes of workers compensation, injury management and prevention programs.

title: Curriculum and Instruction Lower Secondary: Health and Physical Education
description: This unit is designed to prepare preservice teachers to teach the Lower Secondary Health and Physical Education curriculum. The focus of the unit is on curriculum planning, teaching strategies, evaluation, resources, the demonstration of positive impact on student learning and research relating to Health and Physical Education in Lower Secondary Teaching. The unit will explore learning practices to support and challenge a diverse student cohort.

title: Water Resource Management and Treatment Principles
description: This unit covers underlying principles and design techniques related to water quality and potable water treatment including physical and chemical unit processes. Flow of water through unit processes of coagulation, flocculation, softening, sedimentation, filtration and disinfection are presented. An overview of water resources management options is discussed considering environmental and societal requirements as well as potential impacts of climate change. This unit includes a laboratory component for analysis of source water to optimise treatment processes.

title: Mentoring, Coaching and Tutoring
description: Examination of the activities of mentoring, coaching and tutoring - their conceptual underpinning, similarities and differences. Research on effective programs and strategies. Development of personal skills and reflection through practical application during the semester.

title: High Performance Computing
description: This unit is designed as an adjunct to the Honours Research Dissertation.  The unit is intended for scientists and engineers interested in applying high performance computing in the solution of problems in their field. The following topics are considered: Architecture and parallel programming, Message Passing Interface (MPI), Serial Optimisation, OpenMP programming,  GPU acceleration, large scale I/O, Python for HPC, Workflows and Containers.

title: Introduction to Indigenous Australian Ways of Working
description: Introduction to Indigenous Australian identities, Indigenous cultures, and local ways of working. Development of consultative practices associated with the Indigenous Terms of Reference conceptual framework.

title: Statistical Mechanics and Thermodynamics
description: This unit is designed for students who have successfully studied WACE Physics 3A/3B or equivalent, and have taken 1st year Physics or Chemistry units (preferably both), together with the mathematics unit specified above. The unit begins with a comparison of the ways of describing a physical system in terms of both macroscopic and microscopic viewpoints, and simple relations between them, such as temperature. The unit explores the zeroth, and first Laws of thermodynamics, including the concepts of heat capacity and enthalpy. Exploration of the second law of thermodynamics is used to describe the operation of heat engines and Carnot cycles. The concept of entropy is introduced, and some of its properties are examined using the third law of thermodynamics. It then examines thermodynamic potentials and phase changes in substances. The final part of the unit explores the kinetic theory of gases and statistical mechanics. We start with simple probabilistic descriptions of how energy is distributed in macroscopic systems, and derive the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution function. Applying this to ideal gases, we explore the concepts of pressure, viscosity, thermal conductivity and diffusion. Finally, we extend the classical treatment of energy distribution to include the effects of quantum mechanics, deriving the distribution functions of blackbody radiation and matter that are subject to either Bose-Einstein or Fermi-Dirac statistics.

title: Interior Architecture Project Studio 1
description: Under the direction of experienced Design practitioners, this studio unit offers a professional environment which incorporates a breadth of practice and academic experiences relevant to the discipline of interior architecture. Each student will initiate and develop an individual Interior Architecture design project aimed at developing their design expertise. Students are required to identify, explore and extend their chosen project, testing spatial ideas and concepts in relation to human occupation beyond pre-existing and embedded assumptions. Students will engage in innovative, reflective design practice, drawing from their existing body of work, skills and knowledge to demonstrate an emerging identity as a designer, while demonstrating command over relevant practice conventions and communication techniques and strategies. Design prototyping and testing are to be done through digital fabrication and simulated environments.

title: Life Cycle Management
description: The unit is divided into four learning modules. Module 1 consists of Cleaner Production Assessment, which is the systematic procedure for generating and implementing Cleaner Production options for a production facility. Module 2 discusses Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), providing a sustainability framework for identifying environmental, economic, and social interventions taking place in the different stages of the product’s lifecycle, and allocating these to units of product functionality. The LCA procedure follows ISO 14040 series of standards. Module 3 introduces to ISO14001-4 guideline for Environmental Management Systems (EMS). The purpose of an EMS is to provide a procedure for the systematic planning, implementation, and evaluation of environmental actions in a company. It is not specifically designed to promote Cleaner Production, but the environmental management system has sufficient flexibility to incorporate Cleaner Production activities. Module 4 discusses the integration of Tools (Industrial Ecology Toolbox), focusing on parallels between the tools that are being used in the three procedures discussed above. It is intended that this will enable the selection of the most appropriate sustainability assessment tools for a particular industrial setting.

title: Advanced Computational Quantum Mechanics
description: This Unit provides both theoretical and computational methods in Quantum Mechanics. The content covered includes analytical solution of the hydrogen atom, usage of Dirac notation, understanding the mathematical foundation of Stern-Gerlach experiments, the concepts of structure and dynamics, diagonalising Hamiltonians, contour integration, definition of scattering amplitudes, advanced theoretical and computation Quantum scattering theory

title: Sustainable Livelihoods
description: The unit is concerned with the practice of sustainable livelihoods in the developing world. The range of approaches to designing, implementing and evaluating development projects for sustainable livelihoods is critically examined. Topics include: project planning, understanding the project environment, logical framework analysis, participatory and control-oriented management techniques. Through case studies from the Asia-Pacific region these approaches are examined in the context of the socio-economic, cultural and environmental factors that influence the vulnerability and resilience of communities and their capacity to respond to global and local processes of change.

title: Communicating with Japan
description: This unit is designed to promote awareness and understanding of communicative patterns and behaviours in Japanese culture. The unit deals with Japanese cultural key words, language-specific rules and customs, and the relationship between culture and language. Focus will be on an analysis and exploration of similarities and differences in communication between Japanese and other cultures.

title: Environmental Geoscience
description: This unit introduces the student to the geochemical principles underlying the ecosphere and the impact human activity has on it. Areas of study include an introduction to the matter/nutrient cycle in different environmental compartments, followed by a discussion of the diverse manifestations of matter disequilibria caused by human activities (acid rain, ozone hole, eutrophication). Another fundamental part of this unit is a quantitative geochemical examination of environmental contamination illustrated with examples from water pollution, acid mine drainage, tailings dams and their failure, heavy metals and toxicity, and contaminant transport. By covering these subjects, the unit actively embeds United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 3 (SDG3) (good health), SDG6 (clean water), SDG14 (life below water), and SDG15 (life on land) as core content. Discipline based problem solving with data analysis, interpretation and evaluation will extend fundamental knowledge in environmental geoscience.

title: Power Grid Infrastructure and Protection Systems
description: This unit covers power system fault mechanisms, introducing fundamental principles and the protection and control in substations to understand modern power grids. Next, it explores practical aspects of protection, including primary and secondary methods. This section bridges theory and real-world applications in Generation, Transmission, and Distribution Networks. Finally, it examines advanced technologies in power systems, such as Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs), IEC 61850 standard and cybersecurity.

title: Creative Design Project
description: This unit allows students to engage in self-directed or industry driven individual or group projects of a practical and/or theoretical nature.

title: Risk Analysis
description: This unit introduces the student to the use of Bayesian statistics in credibility theory and to the applications of loss distributions, including compound distributions, in risk modelling. Copulas are introduced to account for tail dependencies in distributions. Practical, hands-on modelling experience is developed through the use of R and EXCEL (students are assumed to have functional R and EXCEL skills prior to commencement of this unit).

title: Social Work Philosophy, Policy and Context
description: This unit introduces students to the dynamic landscape of social work, both in its contemporary context and its development as a profession through time, space and place. The relationship between social work and social policy will be explored by looking at the historical development of social work, including the values and ethics of the profession and through an introduction to advocacy and community.

title: Food and Nutrition Sociology
description: In this unit, students will apply the concepts of sociology to the study of food and nutrition, by exploring links between social organisation and individual behaviour. Students will analyse the interactions between the sociological (social, cultural, economic and political) and biomedical influences on food selection for a range of population sub-groups, both nationally and globally. Reflective practice will be used to investigate how students’ own lived experience shapes their perspectives, and they will apply newfound understanding to their development as emerging health professionals.

title: Planning Dissertation Preparation
description: Examines the appropriateness and design of quantitative and qualitative research methodologies and critical thinking skills and literature reviews. Design of an individual research program for a topic to be undertaken in a dissertation.

title: Design Innovation and Smart Technology
description: The design process is expanded in this unit in response to integrate smart technology, current trends, fashions, fads, enhance human wellbeing and socio group niche demands. Research requirements are to identify and explore the work of practitioners of excellence and design market drivers within a defined area, e.g. inclusive design, design for elders, sustainable design, and wearable technology. The student's design proposal will relate to research findings and utilise creative techniques including combination, rearrangement, improvement and invention.

title: Indigenous Australians in the 21st Century
description: Consideration of issues relevant to contemporary Indigenous Australians located in rural, remote and urban communities, including health initiatives; cultural security; governance and leadership; community compensation; role of mining companies: Indigenous Australian business and enterprise; developing partnerships; similar issues with other First Nations; responses to 'The Apology' of 2008; and Indigenous achievements.

title: Promoting Mental Health and Social Inclusion
description: This unit will focus on mental health promotion, prevention and early intervention and will also examine processes by which individuals and groups are included or excluded in society. Students will be introduced to social inclusion as a determinant of health, a public health approach to the prevention of mental health problems and the promotion of mental health. National and international strategic directions and theory and frameworks to underpin effective action will be considered. Evidence-informed case studies will focus on contemporary and emerging issues impacting populations and groups with a focus on socio-ecological influences and disadvantage. Examples may include a focus on specific settings such as workplaces, schools and community; groups across the lifespan; and priority populations including Indigenous peoples and people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds.

title: Diplomacy and Conflict in the Indo-Pacific
description: This unit provides a survey of the key points of diplomatic friction in the Indo-Pacific. Emphasis will be given to critical analysis of specific disputes and problems such as the presence of US forces in the region, the rise of China, the South China Sea, the Taiwan Strait, and the Korean Peninsula. It will also examine a variety of bilateral and multilateral relations important to managing conflict within the Indo-Pacific region, including ANZUS, ASEAN, and the Quadrilateral dialogue. Furthermore, it provides a look at the Indo-Pacific region from Australia’s strategic perspective geographically located at its southern edge.

title: Advanced Japanese: Cultural Connections
description: This unit is a continuation of JAPN3000 to increase students’ skills in intercultural communication, at level N3 of the Japanese Language Proficiency Test. Reading materials include authentic texts on Japanese culture containing complex sentence structures, highly idiomatic expressions and an additional 100 Japanese characters (Kanji). Interactive tutorials include practice on how to make predictions, give compliments, and engage in a debate or discussion. Honorific forms are also introduced.

title: Vital Physiology
description: Physiology is the study of the functions of an organism. This unit looks at the physiological underpinning of the supply and removal of oxygen, water and waste products to and from tissues, and the mechanisms that regulate these within homeostatic limits.

title: Forensic Advocacy
description: This unit will build upon the basic advocacy skills developed in first and second year units. Students will learn how to run a complete trial from beginning to end, spending time specifically developing skills for each component of the trial and culminating with their participation in a full mock trial.

title: Counselling and Collaborative Practice in Speech Pathology
description: In this unit students will develop an understanding of theories of counselling, and apply this knowledge to a diverse range of clients and contexts. Students will also develop an understanding of coaching models and how these apply within a speech pathology contexts, including working with parents, allied health assistants or carers. Students will continue to develop their understanding of working with a team context, and apply learning of collaborative practice (team work) to the role of speech pathologists in a diverse range of workplace contexts, considering the Speech Pathology Australia Code of Ethics and medico-legal responsibilities.

title: History of Warfare and the Evolution of Conflict
description: This unit provides students with a comprehensive overview of the key determinants of the causes of war, as well as the history of conflicts and wars, starting from the Persian-Greek wars and ending with the latest inter-state and intra-state conflicts of the first half of the twenty-first century.

title: Introduction to Counselling
description: Introduction to a range of psychological interventions. The nature of these psychological interventions is investigated in the social and historical context. A second aim is to establish the basic counselling skills involved in interview and consultation processes in a conceptual framework that allows flexibility and understanding of the helping and change processes and the acquisition of basic helping and interpersonal communication skills that underpin the majority of the main theoretical systems.

title: Noongar- Awakening an Endangered Indigenous Language
description: This unit aims to develop an understanding and knowledge of an Indigenous language and culture through a practical introduction to the Noongar language. The unit addresses the questions: What is the Noongar language? Why is it endangered? Why is this important? Students will also have the opportunity to develop their skills in listening, speaking, reading, writing and cultural knowledge.

title: Mathematical Computing
