description: This unit introduces the fundamentals of fortran, including arithmetic computations, control structures, formatted input/output, array processing, user defined functions, subroutines, and modules. It also covers numerical methods for solving various mathematical problems, including systems of linear equations, nonlinear equations, interpolation, and integration.

title: Clinical Medical Imaging Practice 3
description: This unit provides authentic medical imaging professional practice experience in the clinical setting, at the level appropriate for the intermediate/advanced beginner reflective professional. Students will have the opportunity to develop their capacity for mentoring.

title: International Experience 1
description: n/a

title: Environment and Marine Science Dissertation
description: Students will conduct an independent research project under the guidance of an academic supervisor, resulting in the preparation, submission, presentation and defence of a dissertation. Students will develop research, technical, professional and communication skills along with specialised discipline knowledge through a process of inquiry. Completing their dissertation will involve critical review of scientific literature, the formulation of research questions and hypotheses, selection of appropriate methodology and experimental design, social and ethical consideration of the research process; collection, analysis and interpretation of scientific data, and effective scientific writing to produce a professional-standard manuscript.

title: Psychosocial Perspectives Across the Life Course
description: Stages of development within the life course with reference to biological, psychological, (including emotional and cognitive) and social capabilities. Transdisciplinary, sociocultural perspectives on development and significant life events and person-centred application to nursing and paramedic practice. Concepts of: gene expression, brain plasticity, stress reactivity, emotional, attention, social regulation, cognition, adaptability, agency, context and structure with reference to the unstable person and their family.

title: Risk Assessment and Risk Management
description: This unit will build knowledge and develop competence and skills in the techniques that support hazard recognition and the assessment and control of risks associated with workplace settings. It also includes practical frameworks for the application of occupational and environmental health risk assessment and detailed examination of the roles of risk perception and risk communication in risk control and management.

title: Advertising Account Planning
description: This unit aims to establish an understanding of Account Planning and to build essential skills critical for Account Planners such as the ability to gather consumer insights, to synthesise insights gathered, to develop a creative brief from the findings to achieve clients' objectives and to inspire the creative team. The key marketing ingredients are extracted from all areas of marketing subjects such as segmentation, branding, IMC, qualitative marketing research and students taught to amalgamate these ingredients to uncover and pitch 'the big idea' to inspire the creative team.

title: Introduction to Research Methods for Honours
description: This unit provides an introduction to research methods and prepares students for conducting their own independent research project. This unit covers the whole research process from the identification of research questions through to writing up the project. Students learn how alternative research paradigms and philosophies lead to decisions about the relevant method to use to address an identified gap in the current literature for their own research topic.

title: Software Engineering Project A
description: Software engineering projects are selected and undertaken in consultation with a member of the academic staff working in small groups in conjunction with an industry partner or client. Projects are related to the design, implementation and testing of computing systems with associated literature reviews. Team-oriented software engineering processes are applied during all phases of the project. Management activities are undertaken and a range of software engineering tools are applied to resolve problems arising during the execution of the software development process.

title: Materials Engineering
description: This unit will provide a short review of basic ferrous metallurgy, general materials specifications and certification, with a further analysis of Alloy Steel and Tool Steel. Stainless Steels (SS) will be covered including the different classifications, properties and applications of this group. In addition, the evolution of High Nickel Alloys (HNA) from the established SS showing the metallurgical characteristics, properties and the applications in more severe environments and functions. The functional requirements of Superalloys, specifically for creep resistance will be demonstrated. An overview of Cobalt based alloys with an emphasis on tribological properties will be given. Surface Conditioning and Hardening processes for steels will be summarised and Failure and Defect Analysis using case studies will be undertaken. The next part of the unit deals with non-metals, namely Polymeric Materials, Ceramics and Glasses and the development of Composite Materials. The analysis will cover specifications and standards, and mechanical behaviour. The final part of the unit will cover the technology and applications of Smart Materials. General Materials Selection and Design and criteria will be considered throughout the unit with the inclusion of case studies.

title: Technical Theatre Fundamentals
description: The acquisition and application of technical production skills for performance. This highly practical unit is closely linked to the production program at Curtin’s Hayman Theatre.

title: Sustainable Future and the Built Environment
description: This theory informed unit aims to synthesise and stretch the students' understanding and application of design methodologies towards speculating on and imagining new visions for the sustainable future. It focuses on extreme, complex and bizarre environments. Philosophical and theoretical readings are explored as other ways of thinking and seeing the world. Similarly, possibilities for geographic, built and spatial typologies and material realities are investigated.

title: Systems Pharmacology
description: In this unit students will compare and contrast the pharmacology of drugs acting on the autonomic nervous system (ANS), respiratory, musculoskeletal and gastrointestinal systems. Students will investigate drugs for pain, local hormones that are mediators of inflammation, drugs affecting blood glucose, thyroid function, bone metabolism and the immune response which will include drugs having immunosuppressive or immunostimulant characteristics. Mechanisms of drug action, adverse effects, drug interactions and general ADME (absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion) properties will be examined.

title: Automatic Control Systems
description: This unit introduces the concept of feedback control systems, including an overview of some relevant historical examples. Modelling and linearisation of physical systems are reviewed, and the concept of stability is introduced. Students will apply stability assessment techniques, including the Routh criterion and the root-locus method. Control systems design approaches will consider time response characteristics as well as frequency-domain properties including phase and gain margin. Proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controllers and lead-lag controllers will be utilised in control design examples.

title: Mooting
description: This unit is a legal skills unit, which is designed to develop legal research and written and oral communication and advocacy skills. This unit will also help those students wishing to become involved in local, national and international mooting competitions to develop the skills necessary for participation. Students will participate in a number of workshops and seminars on various aspect of mooting. They will also undertake a ‘short’ moot assignment to develop and reflect upon their advocacy skills before moving on to work as part of a team to develop written submissions for an appeal concerning a complex legal scenario. These written submissions will require detailed and strategic research into the relevant grounds of the appeal and will form the basis of arguments that the students, as part of a team, will advance before a simulated appellate court on behalf of their team’s client. The unit will also facilitate students’ engagement with the profession, through guest lectures, networking and other associated opportunities.

title: Advanced Haematology
description: A review of advanced haematology including clinical investigation of haematological disorders, coagulation disorders and transfusion science through a combination of didactic lectures, case studies, critical paper reviews and presentations.

title: Graphic Design 1
description: This unit deals with the concept and design of 'The Brand' and its role within Creative Advertising and Graphic Design communication.

title: Pharmacy Practice 2
description: This unit covers contemporary models of patient consultation including; inter and intra-professional communication, taking into consideration patient health literacy, cultural awareness and patient counselling for a range of dosage forms. Students will continue to hone their skills in the provision of primary care (history/examination/diagnosis/management/monitoring) of minor skin disorders including dry skin, eczema, acne, sunburn and fungal skin infections. Bites and stings, infestations, foot care and personal care will also be discussed. Students are introduced to systems of governance and risk management including medicine supply, administration, dispensing and prescribing legislation, pharmacy premises legislation, national privacy and confidentiality principles, codes of conduct and ethics. Students are required to obtain S2/S3 certification as part of this unit. This unit requires students to accurately perform applied pharmaceutical calculations.

title: Design Technology and User Experience
description: The fundamental designer's knowledge, purpose and required skills of digital modelling and fabrication are studied in this unit. Parametric Solid modelling software CAD is used to create form, scale drawings, and render images. The required application of technical communication to Australian and international standards is established. The design potential of digital fabrication is studied through the examination of iconic designs, human sensory experiences, research and creative experimentation.

title: Ore Deposits
description: Ore deposits provide essential raw materials for the net zero transition and economic livelihoods worldwide. In this unit, students are introduced to the principal types of ore deposits and the processes of ore formation. Magmatic, hydrothermal and sedimentary deposits are investigated through the use of deposit models and other techniques from mineral exploration, research and mining geology. A special emphasis is placed on commodities relevant to the energy transition and high-tech applications. Lecture topics are examined in parallel in the practical component, which employs traditional reflected light microscopy for the identification of ore minerals, ore textures and associations, but also modern tools available to resource geologists.

title: Sustainable Procurement
description: This unit focuses on contemporary business procurement and demonstrates an ethical approach to purchasing and supply chain sourcing practices. The unit includes rethinking supply management strategies to include green purchasing, inclusive procurement and social responsibility. The unit will assess ways in which organisations’ recycle, remanufacture, recondition and reuse materials. Ethical and internationally recognised environmental standards, and fair trade certifications for social and ethical performance are appraised for sustainable procurement in supply chains. This unit will examine ways in which supply chains take advantage of opportunities to innovate in the interest of fostering change and improvement through procurement.

title: Domestic Study Tour
description: This is a national study tour and allows students to follow the taxation cycle within the Australia taxation system. Over a 10 day period students will visit a Canberra and Sydney and will visit a number of organisations including government agencies such as the ATO, Treasury, Tax Practitioners Board, as well as various professional organisations. The aim of the study tour is that students will immerse themselves in learning to understand and appreciate the roles of everyone involved in the smooth running of the Australian Taxation System. As well the study tour will allow students to research the background of business practices study tour location; eg., cultural, religious, economic, political, historical and geographical.

title: Electronic Design
description: High frequency models for the Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT) and the Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor (MOSFET) will be introduced and incorporated into transistor circuits. Methods for analytical analysis and simulation for these transistor circuits will then be given. Analysis and simulation will be used to determine transfer functions of standard single stage transistor amplifiers. Multistage transistor amplifiers including output stage amplifiers will then be examined. Non ideal operational amplifier characteristics will be introduced and methods for their circuit analysis examined. Theory and design of feedback amplifiers including stability criteria will be examined and applied to common operational amplifier circuits. Extensive use of MAPLE/MATLAB and PSPICE simulation tools is made throughout the unit activities.

title: Structural Geology
description: Stress and its relationship to brittle failure of rocks. Visualising stress using Mohr circles. Fault initiation and development. Application of stereographic projections in structural geology. Concepts, models and quantitative techniques for analysing for strain in rocks. Kinematic analysis of shear zones and fold mechanisms. Analysis of superposed deformation and refolded folds. Rheology and the mechanical properties of rocks. Deformation processes, mechanisms and microstructure. Construction of deformation histories.

title: International Study Abroad
description: The primary goal of the unit is the integration of international students into local cultures, and the development of an ability to appreciate the cultural values around which local people organise their daily tasks. Students with their Project Coordinator develop structured, hands-on learning experiences that reflect academic, career, or extracurricular interests. Occasionally students complete apprentice styled internships, develop visual exhibits or arrange and give performances.  The unit is an experiential learning opportunity for students to undertake a project with three major components—the prospectus, the field experience and the reflective essay.  The project goals are rooted in the ethnography methodology which emphasises experiential learning and involvement of local people in analysis and interpretation. Ethnographies are cultural descriptions that include analysis of visual and material culture. The methods for collecting and documenting information most commonly employed with this methodology are interviewing and participant observation.

title: Mineralogy and Geochemistry
description: Geochemical classification and distribution of the elements. The Solar System, meteorites and Earth differentiation. Chemistry of the solid Earth, atmosphere, hydrosphere and biosphere. Basic thermodynamics, equilibria, phase relationships and kinetics. Major and trace element fractionation and partitioning. Stable and radiogenic isotopes and their applications. Fluid-rock interaction. Eh and pH of natural systems. Organic geochemistry and the carbon cycle. Analytical methods and geochemical data presentation. Crystal chemistry of rock-forming minerals. Optical properties of minerals. Introduction to transmitted light microscopy.

title: Urban Transport Systems
description: Examine the relationship between land use, urban form and travel behaviour, including the policy and institutional contexts related to the planning and regulation of multi-modal urban transport systems. Review integrated land use and transport planning approaches to achieve more sustainable cities and development.

title: Present and Future Mathematics
description: This unit extends undergraduate engagement in mathematics by examining a range of contemporary mathematical ideas and applications such as blockchain, fractal geometry, data mining and recent developments in proof; along with other current and emerging fields of mathematical research. In this examination, mathematics is situated within a broad economic and socio-cultural context which considers authentic vocational applications, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander mathematics, integration within STEM, and the challenges facing the globally-connected financial world. A blended learning approach will be taken to delivery.

title: Business Innovation Lab
description: This unit helps students apply entrepreneurial and problem solving skills to develop viable business ideas and create potential start-up opportunities or innovations for existing businesses. The unit combines academic instruction and industry mentoring from specialists active in the start-up community. Drawing on academic and industry mentors, students develop business proposals and formulate persuasive pitching skills to respond to global market opportunities in dynamic business environments.

title: Voice for the Actor
description: This unit develops awareness of vocal strengths, weaknesses and habits and explores a range of exercises to help develop the performer’s voice. Students will also apply vocal technique to spoken language, verse and dialogue.

title: Implementing and Monitoring Indigenous Australian Community Projects
description: Apply Indigenous project management principles and ethical framework to the implementation and monitoring of a community development project.

title: Engineering Research Project 1
description: In the Engineering Research Project units, students have to demonstrate they have acquired and can apply advanced knowledge and skills to solve complex problems in their discipline. In this unit students will: identify a problem, propose and plan a solution that meets the requirements, do a literature review to investigate existing solutions, make design decisions and assumptions to develop their solution, keep a logbook, and give an oral and written progress report at the end of semester.

title: Integrated Clinical Case Management
description: This unit allows students to integrate prior learning with clinical reasoning frameworks using holistic, person-centred, inter and intra-professional management. Clinical case examples will be drawn from a range of lifespan, stages of recovery, levels of disability, cultural backgrounds, and diverse urban and regional/remote community settings. This will include gerontology, gender/pelvic health, and dizziness case examples. The unit will focus on developing inclusive shared decision-making skills to empower individuals with person-centred, evidence-informed knowledge and self-management skills to restore their function and optimise their health. Students will develop skills in reflective practice, collaboration, and working in an interprofessional team, to achieve optimal patient outcomes. Students will be developing the safety awareness required for a first-contact practitioner and will consider the challenges of managing an individual in geographical isolation using digital technology. The unit encompasses three Masterclasses taught by expert clinicians. The unit has a clinical focus culminating in a simulated clinical placement to consolidate learning.

title: Media Law and Ethics
description: This unit equips students to identify and apply laws governing publication that concern media professionals, including journalists and others employed in the various media streams. Students are equipped to identify, analyse and apply these laws when seeking and preparing material for publication to avoid legal liability while exploiting the limits of freedom of speech. In addition, the unit explores key theories and concepts in ethical reasoning and develops skills in critical thinking on issues of professional ethics in journalism and the media. Students will develop a toolkit of concepts and strategies with which ethical questions and dilemmas can be addressed.

title: Inquiry for Clinical Practice
description: Students investigate the nurse's role within the health care team through the application of relevant professional standards governing the practice of registered nurses. Students engage in problem-solving, communication skills and decision making with reference to the nursing process; assessment; planning; implementation; evaluation; discharge planning and documentation; relevant to scope of practice. Planning of care is based on best practice nursing evidence with a focus on person centred and integrated health care.

title: Nursing Honours Dissertation
description: A continuation of attributes learnt from Nursing Honours Preparation, students will develop competencies in the research process and interpretation of data from their research project. Students will develop skills in: oral presentations communicating the results and significance of their research; preparing a research article and dissertation; as well as responding to examiners’ comments.

title: Introduction to Probability and Data Analysis
description: This unit is an introduction to methods of statistical analysis and their role in scientific inference - drawing conclusions about the world using data. It begins with an introduction to probability, which provides a foundation for understanding randomness, uncertainty, chance, and most important of all, for statistical inference. We start with an introduction to definitions of probability and probability models, and then go on to discuss probability distributions, and tools and techniques that can be used to model a wide range of phenomena, as well as those that are useful in statistical inference. In the second part of the unit, we discuss descriptive statistics and inferential statistics. Throughout, we will emphasize that how data are collected determines the nature of the conclusions that we are entitled to draw from any study. Students will be introduced to the R language statistical environment, which they will use for exploring, displaying, and analysing data, and for carrying out and reporting the results of statistical inference. This unit is designed for those students who have passed WACE Mathematics Methods or equivalent.

title: International Experience 4
description: n/a

title: Mechanics for Energy Engineering
description: To achieve sustainable energy supply, it is essential to utilize solutions such as geothermal energy, underground energy storage, onshore and offshore wind, solar farms, geologic energy/carbon storage, hydroelectricity, and nuclear energy. However, designing, installing, and maintaining such facilities requires knowledge of the behavior of solid materials in different environments, including composite materials. This course aims to provide students with a understanding of this subject. Specifically, students will learn about stress, strength, and failure in solids, as well as how different types of stress and strain affect solid behavior. They will also gain insight into solid mechanical strength parameters, the various types of failure, and how cyclic loading and temperature fluctuations impact solid mechanical behavior. Additionally, this course covers the analysis of stresses and strains for plane stress problems, fluid statics, hydrostatic pressure, pore pressure, and Mohr's circle. Finally, students will learn about basic stress analysis of beams and how to design pressure vessels. By the end of this course, students will have a thorough understanding of the various factors that influence the mechanical aspect of the design and maintenance of facilities that contribute to meet sustainable energy supply. Students will conduct laboratory experiments to reinforce their theoretical understanding of various concepts. The learning outcome of this unit will meet United Nations SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

title: Nyungar Culture and Identity
description: Examines significant historical, cultural and contemporary issues which have shaped and continue to shape the lives of Nyungar people in Western Australia. This includes Nyungar history pre-colonisation, the experience of Nyungar peoples post-colonisation, and how Nyungar culture is perceived in contemporary settings.

title: Radiation Therapy Practice 2
description: This unit provides a comprehensive development of the theoretical knowledge and practical skills underpinning intermediate beginning radiation therapy practice, including the principles, technology, patient positioning and approaches associated with simulation, planning and treatment. This unit provides further development of the intermediate beginning radiation therapist’s capacity for culturally safe person-centred care, effective communication, safe and ethical practice, and reflective thinking.

title: Electronic Fundamentals
description: Topics to be addressed in this unit will include semiconductor doping, PN junction, diodes and circuits, physics of bipolar junction transistor, introduction on field effect transistor, elementary transistor amplification circuits, transistor biasing, device modelling, analysis and design of linear (small signal) single-stage amplifiers.

title: Introduction to Public Health
description: Introduction to public health theory. Recent trends in public health practice. Environmental and nutritional factors that impact on health. Major causes of morbidity and mortality in Australia. National health priority areas. Indigenous health issues. Application of primary, secondary and tertiary levels of prevention in public health.

title: Child Developmental Psychology
description: This unit introduces students to the psychological development of children from birth through adolescence. Major theoretical frameworks and research addressing cognitive, social, emotional and physical development are examined.

title: Foundations of Haematology
description: A study of basic haematological concepts including blood film morphology for the clinical laboratory investigation of  common haematological disorders. Blood transfusion practice, blood group systems including serological techniques. Major blood coagulation pathways, anticoagulant therapy and associated laboratory techniques.

title: Engineering Design Methodology
description: This unit will provide students with the ability to understand the stages of engineering design for mechanical systems and devices and able to choose tools appropriate for each stage with the aim of optimising the design process. The students will be able to use classical design optimization methods such as linear programming, simplex algorithm and geometric programming for design optimisation. In addition, students will apply modern design methodologies such as parametric design, robust design and axiomatic design for parts and systems.

title: Eco-Efficiency Strategies
description: The first module provides an introduction to the concepts and strategies under the Eco-Efficiency umbrella. The second module covers the oldest and still most common application area for Eco-Efficiency, production processes and systems. The third module deals with the rapidly expanding body of Eco-Efficiency experience in product and service development and delivery. The fourth module deals with the management implications of Eco-Efficiency. The fifth module looks at the current level of uptake on Eco-Efficiency and Cleaner Production in different parts of the world.

title: Image Concepts
description: Image Concepts examines key historical, theoretical and conceptual issues that underpin contemporary photographic and illustration practice, and explores how these issues reflect cultural preoccupations and concerns. With a focus on developing an integrative and scholarly study of theory and criticism, students will develop their own photographic and/or illustration research project that systematically explores photography and illustration's relationship to contemporary existence. Encouraged to follow both measured and intuitive sequences of scholarly investigation, students will be challenged to develop new forms and insights into photography and/or illustration theory and criticism in a manner that recognises cultural influences on photography and illustration, as well as the impact photography and illustration has on culture.

title: Mathematical Sciences Honours Dissertation
description: Students will be required to conduct an independent research project under the guidance of a supervisor, resulting in the preparation, submission, presentation and defence of a dissertation. Students will develop research, technical and professional and communication skills, research autonomy and specialised knowledge through a process of inquiry involving the formulation of research questions and hypotheses; selection of appropriate methodology and experimental design; ethical consideration of the research process; critical review of scientific literature; effective scientific writing; development of a project proposal, and the preparation of a dissertation.

title: 3D Environment and Prop Design
description: This unit teaches students how to build high quality 3D props and environments for use in film, video games and other digital media. Students will continue to build on the skills acquired in Introduction to 3D Modelling, learning industry standard tools, advanced techniques and efficient workflows which will enable them to achieve high quality outcomes for their portfolio and future projects. They will collect and analyse reference and utilise design principles to develop their own environment. Students will block out and iterate on their environment design before starting final production. They will explore modular and procedural approaches to advanced modelling, lighting, texturing and material development in creating a complete and engaging digital environment.

title: Engineering Surveying
description: This unit covers the theoretical and practical aspects of engineering surveying including geometric aspects of road design, it’s set-out, planning and surveying of local control networks for construction surveying and as-constructed surveys, set-out techniques for construction surveying and sewerage. In addition, computation of volumes of earthworks and checking verticality of structures are included. The unit demonstrates adjustment, maintenance and calibration of total stations. It includes comprehensive practical and software training.

title: Electronics
description: Introduction to electrical and magnetic phenomena, electrical circuits, circuit analysis, Kirchoff’s Voltage Law, Kirchoff’s Current Law, nodal and mesh analysis, equivalent circuits. Introduction to electronics: the operational amplifier, PN junction, transistor and applications. Introduction to PSPICE simulator.

title: Introduction to Human Communication Science
description: Introduction to normal communication, language and speech. Components of language. Psycholinguistic models of normal language and speech. Pragmatic and sociological factors affecting human communication. Introduction to the profession of Speech Pathology, and the role of Speech Pathologists in a variety of settings.

title: Industrial Project
description: Under the supervision of an academic staff member, students will work independently to apply core subject knowledge in mathematics and statistics to solve an industrial, mathematical, or statistical problem, or problems in related areas such as education and teaching & learning.

title: Fieldwork Skills
description: This unit provides practical experience in preparing, conducting and analysing fieldwork from a geographical perspective. Skills in qualitative and quantitative data selection, collection and analysis will be developed together with training in the preparation and presentation of research results for a range of clients.

title: Integrated Structural Design
description: Combination of reinforced concrete, steel and timber design principles underpinning Australian design codes are examined and utilised in the design of structures with reinforced concrete, steel and timber members. Reinforced concrete and steel design principles are extended with their application to the design of portal frame structures. An integrated structural design project is to be undertaken, using a combination of timber, steel and reinforced concrete elements. Students will work in groups to develop concept designs for comparison. The detailed design of one concept design will be carried out (individually), including estimation of material quantities and a cost analysis utilising construction engineering approaches.

title: Integrated Marketing Communications
description: This is an introductory unit which explores the importance of marketing communication, the concepts underlying effective marketing communication and the skills needed to create simple integrated marketing communication (IMC) campaigns.

title: Psychopharmacology in Indigenous Mental Health
description: This unit gives an overview of the uses and dynamics of commonly prescribed medicines for the treatment of mental health disorders. The major families of medications are reviewed along with their biopsychosocial and holistic impacts. More commonly used bush medicines will also be covered.

title: Microcontroller Project
description: This unit introduces structure and functional design of microcontroller-supported mechatronic systems. Major components of a typical mechatronic systems are reviewed. Attributes and role of each major component of mechatronic systems are discussed. Students work in teams to program and build a mechatronic system controller and partake in an end of semester competition to demonstrate their controller systems. Major components of mechatronic system such as Sensors, Actuators, Timers and interrupts, Darlington drivers, Protection diodes; H-bridge, Voltage regulated power supply, Servomotors, Stepper motors, PWM-controlled DC motors, Analog-to-Digital converters, Keypads and, LCD displays are covered. Students also learn to program, compile, simulate and download embedded microcontrollers. Binary and bitwise programming techniques are also covered.

title: Indigenous Mental Health
description: An examination of factors that contribute to mental health for Indigenous people from the perspectives of social determinants of health, management of mental health in the family and community, and the application of holistic practice that enables best care and treatment for Indigenous peoples.

title: Mental Health 2
description: This unit is designed to introduce students to knowledge, skills and attitudes to equip them to provide psychosocial care in a variety of health settings to people who are experiencing chronic mental health conditions. Using an evidence-based approach, the unit will explore and discuss mental health nursing in Australia, and focus on the importance of biopsychosocial assessments, person-centred and trauma-informed care, and active participation of consumers and carers in mental health assessment and recovery planning. The unit will also explore contemporary challenges such as suicide prevention, postvention, and the management of high-prevalence disorders, including anxiety and depression. Additionally, students will gain insights into psychopharmacology and other treatments, and the crucial role of psychoeducation and self-management in managing emerging mental health challenges.

title: Voice and Speech Science
description: This unit develops students’ skills in objective assessment focusing on applied issues using speech science instrumentation. This unit addresses assessment and intervention for voice disorders across the lifespan. The relationship of voice disorders with other communication disorders is explored.

title: Mathematical Modelling
description: Mathematical Modelling is an introduction to mathematical modelling and optimisation that aims to enhance the student’s problem solving skills. This unit comprises three parts: Networks, Optimisation, and Combinatorics. Modern society is dominated by a system of networks for the transmission of information, the transportation of people and the distribution of goods and energy. Students will acquire skills in modelling a network with a graph; designing optimal networks (Kruskal’s algorithm); project networks (Critical path method); network routing (Dijkstra’s algorithm); and switching networks. In part two, students will discover that decision making using optimisation technology assures that the best possible outcome is achieved within the constraints applying to the system under investigation. Here, we will cover inventory models; and linear programming modelling including the use of computer packages for solving problems. Finally, Combinatorics is concerned with the study of arrangements, patterns, designs, etc. To do this, we will take a closer look at counting techniques; solution of linear equations; recurrence relations; and logic with application to circuit designs. Some applications will also be given.

title: Research, Leadership and Entrepreneurship in Science 2
description: This unit is for students enrolled in the Bachelor of Advanced Science (Honours). It has been designed to allow students the flexibility to explore different dimensions of their chosen discipline. This is achieved through Independent Study Contracts (ISCs). ISCs are an agreement between the Unit Coordinator, the student (or groups of students), and academic or industry mentors that details the tasks that students need to complete to achieve the learning outcomes of the unit. Students complete modules in translational science, entrepreneurship, science marketing, funding research (grant writing).

title: Surface Design
description: This unit introduces students to the creative process and simple production techniques, utilised in the design and printing of surface imagery for material application. Students will experiment with print processes to create unique design solutions and apply them using reproduction techniques to a variety of surfaces.

title: Applied Bioscience for Health Complexity 2
description: This unit covers pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnosis, pharmacology and clinical decision making for individuals with critical instable conditions including; trauma, burns, sepsis, haematological dysfunction, cardiovascular failure, cardiac arrhythmias (AF, VT, VF, Heart Block, PEA, Asystole), respiratory failure, acid base imbalance, acute kidney injury, spinal injury, cerebrovascular accidents and quality use of medicines

title: Indigenous Australian Research Positioning
description: Focus on the positions and positioning of researchers past and present. Students are required to negotiate and articulate their own position/s and standpoints as well as gain understanding of others’ positions. Examines the historical patterns of research undertaken in Aboriginal contexts, and considers the politics and power relations of past and present research.

title: Inquiry for Legal and Ethical Nursing Practice
description: Students learn ethical and legal frameworks for professional practice exploring the function of law and regulation and how the law effects and guides professional practice. Professional practice frameworks, professional rights and responsibilities, ethical and legal health related dilemmas across the life span and cultural contexts are reviewed. Students apply ethical principles and analyse medico legal contemporary issues in holistic nursing and healthcare.

title: Crisis Intervention and Recovery
description: This unit explores the theories and strategies for intervention and management within crisis situations. A key focus of this unit is evidence based trauma informed approaches to healing and recovery within an Indigenous Australian historic, generational trauma, context. Students will critically consider the multi-dimensional nature of trauma and the human responses to traumatic experiences. Themes addressed include: self-care, the helper/client relationship, suicide intervention, recovery and aftermath of trauma, crisis related to substance abuse, illness, death and loss, and community programs for crisis intervention.

title: Engineering Management and Professional Practice
description: This unit introduces the fundamentals of engineering management. Key topics include organisational management, managing project teams, engineering ethics and sustainable engineering practice. A major focus is on project management, including the project life cycle, project planning, scope, scheduling, budgeting, work breakdown structures and resource allocation. This unit also introduces key concepts in contract law for engineers, quality and risk management, as well as strategic planning.

title: Digital Creation Futures
description: Explore how co-creative digital and social media practices can help shape the future of online culture in ethical and socially meaningful ways. This capstone unit consolidates your prior learning - especially in Web Media - by connecting theoretical principles to applied practice through a socially engaged digital project. You'll begin by writing a solo proposal on an issue or opportunity that matters to you, while exploring ideas like design justice (creating media with equity and inclusion in mind), civic imagination (using media to imagine better futures), and critical creation (thoughtful, purposeful digital making). Next, in small teams, you’ll select, design, and produce a public-facing digital project. Finally, you’ll heighten engagement and participation with a focused outreach that draws on the participatory and algorithmic practices that shape digital culture.

title: Physiological Processes
description: Physiology is the study of the functions of an organism. This unit examines several fundamental body functions, e.g., absorption, secretion, communication, transport and movement, from a physiological perspective. These themes are addressed within five modules: cellular physiology; nerve & muscle physiology; cellular communication; endocrine physiology and energy metabolism.

title: Dynamic Modelling and Control
description: Overview and history of feedback control. Mathematical modelling of physical systems including thermal, fluid, electromechanical and mechanical. Interpretation of the dynamic response of low order systems in both the time, frequency and s domain. Feedback and stability. Stability assessment techniques, root locus analysis. Response specifications, time and (mention of) frequency. Introduction to controllers. PID algorithms and tuning. Sampled data systems and digital control systems.

title: Functional Anatomy
description: In this unit, students will learn the foundational terminology and concepts related to neuromusculoskeletal anatomy. The bony structure, joints and muscles of the human body will be explored in detail, along with as an introduction to motor nerves. Students will be required to apply this knowledge in analysing everyday functional movements and exercises.

title: Extremism in Global Politics
description: This unit explores the (re)emergence of extremist thought and influence in contemporary global affairs. It begins by examining periods in 20th century international politics, with particular focus on understanding the causal factors behind the extremism periods during this timeframe. With this information in hand, it then turns to growing extremist challenges witnessed today including new forms of ethnonationalism, populism, conspiracy theory and conspirituality, neomasculine anti-feminism, and other forms of militant neoreaction. Emphasis is placed on understanding the underlying material, economic and sociological influences driving this resurgence: including the impacts of social media and other forms of communications technology; globalisation; growing ecological and environmental degradation; shifting cultural, racial, religious and gender norms; and the long-term impacts of neoliberal capitalism. Students will finish the unit with an understanding of the complex interrelations of these various factors and their role in driving political extremism, as well as how they as individuals and members of society can confront this challenge.

title: Principles of Tourism, Hospitality and Events
description: This unit provides an introduction to the underlying principles of tourism, hospitality and events, three closely related sectors which together constitute one of the largest industries globally. The aim of this unit is to provide an understanding of the nature and elements of these sectors with specific reference to the concept of sustainability. The unit examines the sectors’ sustainability in theory and practice with case examples from Australia and overseas.

title: Graphic Design 2
description: Through a series of structured exercises and activities, students will apply the design process model to strengthen their understanding of its purpose, while developing creative problem solving and practical design skills. The principal objectives of each project will be research, interpretation and development of original and innovative design solutions to set briefs.

title: Business Ethics
description: Business and its operations increasingly raise ethical issues that affect all of us, including in new and emerging areas. This unit considers many of these issues, such as:Should employers be able to access the social media accounts of job applicants? Do we have a right to know when companies use artificial intelligence to make decisions about us?Should social media platforms ban hate speech and opinions that are harmful to others, or should they allow total freedom of speech?Should businesses use child labour in countries where the law allows it? Or bribes in countries where these are expected?Should there be any limits on the treatment that businesses can subject animals to in producing food or medicines? Should those in business only be guided by profit or are there some things that are too unethical to be done even if they are profitable? If there are ethical obligations in business, how can we decide and agree on these? This unit explores prevailing views on ethical theories and ethical thinking and invites students to explore their own views on these questions and discuss ethical and moral dilemmas that arise in business contexts.Students will learn and apply critical thinking skills related to the practice of business within the framework of societal values.

title: Toxicology and Diseases
description: This unit outlines a conceptual framework for toxicology and related impacts on human health from environmental and occupational exposures, reveals mechanisms by which toxicants initiate pathological dysfunction or disease, and introduces methods to identify toxicants and their adverse health effects associated with environmental and occupational exposures. Topics include toxicological terminology, basic principles of toxicology, toxicological testing methods, toxicity of common hazardous substances, adverse consequences to human health that result from environmental and occupational exposures, and risk communication. The unit supports healthy lives and well-being for all by providing a grounding in understanding the adverse effects of common toxicants, strategies for identifying health effects, and treatment options. Additionally, it fosters inclusive and equitable quality education through offering a range of learning opportunities and styles in toxicology, promoting access to learning for diverse populations as part of the foundation for public health.

title: Managing Tourism Destinations
description: This unit is designed for students to explore and critique the theory and practice of tourism destination management in an international context. Tourism destinations are a constantly evolving combination of products and services, attractions and activities, accommodation and amenities. Understanding how and why destinations form and develop in particular ways, and why they decline in popularity provides insights into effective strategies for their successful and sustainable development. This unit also provides future managers with the theoretical and practical basis for effective international destination management.

title: Marketing for Tourism, Hospitality and Events
description: Students are provided the opportunity to develop an in-depth knowledge of aspects relating to the role of marketing in tourism, hospitality, and events. The unit provides students with an understanding of the applications of marketing principles in a range of global and local tourism environments. Broadly, students will focus on areas such as developing tourism marketing opportunities and strategies, using effective communication to use and adapt information and technology relating to segmenting consumers, and marketing tourism destinations, in alignment with ethical and responsible practices and insight into the future of tourism.

title: Neuroscience for Occupational Therapy
description: The main focus of this unit is the planning and implementation of occupational therapy assessment and intervention for adults with neurological conditions such as acquired brain injury or neurodegenerative conditions. Students integrate knowledge relating to the pathophysiology of these neurological conditions, an occupational therapy model of choice and evidence-based theories/practices to plan and implement occupational therapy assessment and intervention in different practice contexts. The occupational therapy assessment results will guide the development and implementation of occupational therapy intervention and will follow a remedial and/or compensatory approach to address the impact of the neurological condition on the person's occupational performance and participation.

title: Great Power Competition
description: This unit explores the importance of great powers, including superpowers, and their role and place in the contemporary international system. It will analyse strategic behaviour of great powers and the factors that shape national strategies, and it will consider how relations between great powers and the competition for power affects the international security environment as well as the Australian national security and defence.

title: Interior Lighting Design
description: This unit provides an introduction to principles of interior lighting design and its application techniques in order to develop fundamental specialist knowledge. Special focus is given to the exploration of various aspects of human inhabitation and lived experience in the built environment - well-being, comfort, perception and colour - through the implementation and use of science and technology.

title: Public Health Honours Preparation
description: Fundamental competencies to enable students to develop an appreciation of the ethics and principles of research and research design; critically appraise and interpret scientific literature; as well as develop skills in planning and writing a research proposal.

title: Fine Art Studio Strategies
description: This unit is designed to develop your capacity for research-based enquiry into skills, techniques, methods and processes of fine art. You will undertake a practical engagement of studio-based research through staff and/or student-directed projects. You will work towards presenting a body of artworks that investigate art making strategies and material exploration.

title: Fundamentals of Geographic Information Systems
description: This unit is an introduction to the application, structure and function of geographic information systems (GIS). Students will develop skills and knowledge around the input and management, analysis and presentation of geographic data and relationships. They will also develop expertise in the storage and simple manipulation of spatial data together with the integration and management of spatial and attribute data. There will be a particular focus in this unit on the application of the principles of academic integrity and academic referencing conventions.

title: Advanced Investment Analysis
description: This unit covers advanced topics in investment finance including asset pricing, behavioural finance, financial return predictability and momentum. Examples of topics to be covered include: portfolio theory, asset pricing theory, the efficient markets hypothesis, empirical asset pricing, and behavioural finance.

title: Exercise Science Professional Practice
description: Students will develop specific professional practice skills necessary to gain employment following graduation. Relevant professional placements will be completed to allow the application of discipline specific knowledge and skills. Students will develop their understanding of quality practice, ethics, and safety in the workplace, whilst developing their communication skills and professionalism.

title: Advanced Topics in Astrophysics
description: This unit is designed as an adjunct to the Honours Research Dissertation. Students will further develop their research, technical, professional and communication skills, and specialised knowledge through the exploration of advanced concepts in the field of Physics.

title: Business and Law International Experience 4
description: International mobility experience for undergraduate students.

title: Design Principles and Process
description: An introduction to design process and principles. Through lectures, tutorials, and various projects, the unit addresses the purpose, sequence, major stages and application of design process to synthesize solutions relevant to the fields of Design. Students will learn how to research, ideate, develop and refine a design to a professional standard. They will also learn how to apply design principles such as balance, hierarchy and proximity to their work.

title: Go Practice - Internship 1
description: This unit provides students with internship opportunities in becoming job-ready graduates. Students in courses without professional work experience are strongly encouraged to enrol in this unit.

title: Physiotherapy Clinics 2
description: This fieldwork unit will cover physiotherapy clinical practice, to entry level standard according to the Physiotherapy practice thresholds in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand for Physiotherapy, managing clients in a rehabilitation setting with a range of caseloads and model/s of intervention and service delivery.

title: Linear Algebra and Statistics for Engineers
description: This unit will consider problems arising from engineering related fields. Students will learn the necessary skills to model and solve such problems through the introduction of mathematical techniques of linear algebra, data analysis as well as statistical inference. This unit will cover vectors, lines and planes and their extension into n-dimension space. This unit also covers matrices and their use for solving systems of linear equations through a study of a number of different types of solution methods. Students will be introduced to the world of statistics by looking at the concepts of descriptive statistics and inferential statistics. This unit is designed for those students who have passed WACE Mathematical Methods or equivalent.

title: Engineering Science Studio
description: This unit enables students to engage in the design process as undertaken in the field of Engineering. Through practical projects, students will produce innovative and appropriate design solutions documented through their design portfolio, research reports and presentations. Design prototyping and testing are to be done through physical and/or digital fabrication and simulated and/or real environments depending upon the projects. Students will reflect on their own cultural values and world views, and the implications for culturally safe engineering professional practice. This unit requires students to create design solutions that engage with a place-specific landscape or site. Opportunities for cultural and interdisciplinary engagement will be encouraged. Work Integrated Learning is incorporated through the design of projects (such as the projects’ challenges, sites, stakeholders etc.).

title: Radiation Therapy Practice 1
description: 1.1)	This unit provides a comprehensive introduction to the theoretical knowledge and practical skills underpinning beginning radiation therapy practice, including the principles, technology, patient positioning and approaches associated with simulation, planning and treatment. This unit provides opportunity for further development of the beginning radiation therapist’s capacity for culturally safe person-centred care, effective communication, safe and ethical practice, and reflective thinking.

title: Pharmaceutical Formulation
description: This unit introduces students to the pharmaceutical science and formulation of liquid-in-liquid, solid-in-liquid, solid and semi-solid dosage forms. Pharmaceutical Science aspects: surface phenomena, surface and interfacial tension; surfactants, micelle formation; properties of colloids and rheology. Formulation Aspects: Formulation, preparation and evaluation of semi-solid dosage forms, suppositories and two phase liquid-based preparations. Preservation of two phase systems.

title: Collection Development
description: The unit places a strong emphasis on the acquisition and demonstration of a high level of understanding of the professional practices, technology and skills appropriate to the fashion textile design industry. An emphasis is placed on the development of independent research skills leading to the design and production of a collection of textiles and/or garments which demonstrate appropriateness in a contemporary industry context.

title: Introduction to Health, Safety and Environment
description: This unit introduces students to fundamental concepts and practices in occupational health, safety and environment (HSE). It covers a broad range of topics within selected HSE disciplines, including identifying, evaluating and managing risks to human health in workplace and environmental contexts; understanding relevant HSE legislation; and exploring strategies to promote safety and sustainability in various occupational and environmental settings.

title: Go Practice - Internship 2
description: This unit provides students with internship opportunities in becoming job-ready graduates. Students in courses without professional work experience are strongly encouraged to enrol in this unit.

title: Medicine 1
description: In this unit, clinical cases and patient scenarios provide context for learning foundational concepts in biomedical and clinical sciences using a body systems-based approach. The relationship between human structure and function in health and adaptive physiological responses to changes in the internal and external environment are explored. The unit introduces clinical consultation and the doctor-patient relationship with a focus on developing effective communication and history-taking skills. Basic examination and procedural skills are introduced and interpreted within the context of the clinical consult in a healthy individual.Students explore health advocacy, health behaviours, health promotion and social determinants of health, promoting a holistic patient-centred approach to health in society. Students develop a broad understanding of Aboriginal culture and the specific impact of colonisation on health outcomes in Aboriginal people and communities. This unit serves as the foundation for the study of medicine and equips students with the necessary skills as they adjust to both the university and medical school learning environment and begin to develop their individual professional identities as current medical students and future doctors in society.

title: Community Psychology
description: Approaches to psychological issues at an individual, family, organisational and community level form the basis of this unit. This unit adopts an ecological and substantive approach to theory and practice. The unit also covers the major legislative frameworks.

title: Physiotherapy Clinics 4
description: This fieldwork unit will cover physiotherapy clinical practice, to entry level standard according to the physiotherapy practice thresholds in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand, managing clients across the human lifespan in any setting or range of settings with a range of caseloads and model/s of intervention and service delivery.

title: Korean Beginners 1
description: This unit is suitable for students with no or very limited experience in foreign language learning and is designed to support the learning needs of a university student with no or very limited knowledge of the Korean language. With a focus on supportive and scaffolded approach to language learning, this unit will introduce students to basic written and spoken Korean communication skills needed in daily life in Korea. On successful completion of this unit students will be able to master basic communication skills required when travelling or working in Korea, such as greetings, introductions, talking about past events, asking and giving permission as well as asking and giving directions. Students will also be introduced to the Korean writing system hangeul, and learn skills in writing basic emails, text messages and SMS messages in Korean while learning about Korean society, culture and history to contextualise their learning.On successful completion of Korean Beginners 1 and 2, students will reach a level of competency equivalent to the National Institute of Korean Language’s Standard Curriculum for Korean Language TOPIK-I Level 2 lower level proficiency.Korean language study is highly recommended for students planning a career in engineering, science, commerce, international relations, creative arts or teaching. Competence in an Asian language gives a competitive advantage in the careers market.

title: Introduction to Psychology
description: Broad outline of the nature, methods, and fields of psychology. Introduction to psychology and methodological issues related to the study of human beings and the relevance of both for interactions with individuals and groups. Introduction to social psychology, personality, development, learning, memory, and motivation.

title: Power Electronics
description: AC-DC Converters, DC-DC Converters, DC-AC Converters, AC-AC Converters, Switching Mode Power Supplies, DC Drives, AC Drives, Application of Power Electronics in Power Systems, Application of Power Electronics in Renewable Energies, Application of Power Electronics in Smart Grids.

title: Automatic Control
description: Analysis of automatic control systems in the frequency domain. Compensation techniques using time and frequency methods. Case study in control system design and performance criteria. State space representation and ‘modern’ control.

title: Australia Taxation Law Cases
description: Taxation is a law, it's created and passed in the Parliament and given Royal Assent thus becoming legislated laws taxpayers must abide by, but the interpretation of the law may be seen differently by the taxpayers and the ATO, so here enters the courts where cases on tax laws are determined. Within this unit of study, you get to interpret and review seminal cases and legislation that form the foundation of the Australian taxation system in which everyone participates. We will teach you to obtain the necessary skills to become an expert in examining and applying relevant case law to taxation problems and showcasing as we go the famous cases of the past and highlight current ones as they come to light during your study in this unit.

title: Event Management
description: This unit focuses on integrating theory, knowledge, and ethical, responsible, and sustainable practice for event planning and management. It investigates the temporal and spatial characteristics of a range of event types, managing operations and logistics, resources and stakeholders, and the role of events in the development of communities. Work-integrated learning is undertaken through the planning and evaluation of an event.

title: Environmental Systems Management
description: This unit provides students with a functional understanding of environmental management system frameworks and principles, focusing on industry applications and certification processes for sustainable environmental performance. It will introduce techniques for identifying environmental aspects and impacts, along with methods for applying sustainable corrective actions to promote continuous improvement to environmental performance. Students will explore key environmental topics including air pollution and water quality, waste management, contaminated sites and their remediation, and odour management. Other more contemporary themes will focus on industry adaptions to climate change to promote industry resilience, and environmental impacts of industry on Indigenous Australian communities and culture.

title: Hospitality Experience
description: This unit represents an exciting and innovative opportunity for students to combine theory with practice while simultaneously developing operational and functional management skills required in the hospitality industry. The unit is designed to provide students with an overview of the key issues in commercial food and beverage operations, lodging operations, recreation, and entertainment. The learning environment is structured to facilitate interaction to stimulate discussions and analysis.

title: Entrepreneurship
description: This unit shines a critical light on the practice and theory of entrepreneurship, enabling students to model future entrepreneurial practice that considers the social, environmental and economic possibilities of a regenerative future. Exploring the fundamentals of entrepreneurship in light of rapid technological advancement, environmental degradation and social inequality, the unit will inspire students to understand and imagine their own – or others’ – entrepreneurial actions and how to get there.

title: Korean Popular Culture
description: This unit offers students an opportunity to gain a deep understanding of South Korean society and history through the study of Korean popular culture, music and film. From trot to K-pop, this unit traces the development of Korean popular music, cinema and other creative industries in Korea. The focus will be on examining the political, cultural, economic and social significance of creative industries in modern Korea, through examining global idol cultures, gaming and fandom communities, the world of South Korean cinema, TV dramas and webtoons, and the role screen cultures have played in Korean society in the past. This unit will also cover North Korean public and popular culture, focusing on the political and social importance of culture in North Korea. Through a range of interactive assessments, students gain advanced skills of critical cultural analysis, as well as an understanding of how culture intersects with national identity and international relations.This unit is taught in English, no prior knowledge of Korean language is required.

title: Facilitation Processes in Indigenous Australian Contexts
description: In this unit students will engage community members in dialogue to facilitate participatory enquiry through planning, design, problem solving and evaluation within an Indigenous setting using culturally appropriate protocols. Students will develop, integrate and apply conceptual frameworks, processes and skills related to learning about local issues in a community context.

title: Introduction to Microbiology and Biohazards
description: An introduction to theory and practical aspects of basic microbiology. Growth requirements of micro organisms. Communicable disease incidence and transmission in various occupational settings. Identification, management and control of biohazards in the workplace

title: Design of Foundations
description: This unit covers the engineering design and construction of shallow foundations (pad, strip, combined, strap and raft) and deep foundations, including single and group pile foundations, as well as the special design of stiffened slab footings on expansive soils. Students will learn how to choose the best type of foundations for certain structures, and will also develop an understanding of the fundamental design aspects and the corresponding affecting parameters.

title: Spatial Sciences Project
description: Students develop their independent learning skills in researching, defining, designing, implementing, managing and presenting a spatial sciences problem and solution. Students will conduct an independent investigation with the primary liaison being their supervisor, Additionally, there will be some lectures (information sessions) and online resources available. Students have the responsibility to maintain regular contact with their supervisor and ensure they meet deadlines and attend project-related activities.

title: Legal Foundations
description: This unit provides foundational knowledge of law and the Australian legal system, including its historical development and constitutional framework. It contrasts common law and other forms of legal system and introduces students to the key sources of law while developing the skills of case analysis, statutory interpretation and legal reasoning required to access those sources of law and interpret and apply them to the resolution of legal disputes.

title: Earth and Planetary Sciences Honours Dissertation
description: Students will be required to plan and conduct an independent research project in an area of Earth and Planetary Sciences under the guidance of a supervisor, resulting in the preparation, submission, presentation and defence of a dissertation. Students will develop a project proposal involving the formulation of research questions and hypotheses; selection of appropriate methodology and experimental design; ethical consideration of the research process; critical review of scientific literature. Students will develop research and technical skills in data acquisition and interpretation, research autonomy, and specialised knowledge through a process of scientific inquiry. Students will develop professional and communication skills by presenting and defending research findings orally to an audience, and effective scientific writing via the preparation of a dissertation that utilises professional academic approaches and standards to avoid plagiarism and uphold academic integrity.

title: Community Nutrition
description: This unit builds on first and second-level units with new knowledge and critical thinking skills relating to nutrition assessment and intervention design and the application of these concepts across a diverse range of groups and settings. Students will develop skills to select relevant data to collect and identify the associated methods, techniques and standards to use. Students will process, analyse and interpret nutrition assessment data to identify and prioritise nutrition problems and the associated nutrition-related causes. Students will develop skills in the design of nutrition interventions to address nutrition problems and associated causes, and the selection of appropriate criteria for evaluation and monitoring of outcomes.

title: International Experience 9
description: n/a

title: Web Communications
description: The Internet has dramatically changed the way people and organisations communicate, whether for better or worse. For many, online communication through digital and social media is now one of their most significant forms of interaction with others. Digital and social media also underpin collaboration between people, either in formal groups or loose networks. Understanding how the Internet affords us new and different ways of communicating is, therefore, essential. This unit will enable you to become an effective and sophisticated user of digital and social media, able to deploy techniques, technologies and underlying concepts for online communication, collaboration and media creation.

title: Health Promotion, Equity and Social Justice
description: Health promotion seeks fairer and more equitable societies. In this unit equity and social justice will be considered with particular reference to processes, institutions and determinants which influence health and living conditions through the distribution of power, money and resources. Power will be examined as it relates to structure and agency. Contemporary and emerging health promotion issues relevant to policy and practice will be considered across a variety of issues, settings and populations. Case studies of social change that positively impact health will be explored.

title: Performance Analysis and Introductory Data Science
description: This unit delves into the pivotal role of performance analysts within the realm of sports. Students examine data-centric frameworks and tools used for performance analysis, tackling various challenges encountered by coaches and sport scientists. They evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of prevalent analytical methods and scrutinize the customary metrics gathered on a daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly basis. Exploring data visualization and presentation techniques to effectively communicate empirical findings to diverse stakeholders. The communication methods will encompass acute decision-making aspects, as well as those pertaining to player growth and athlete recruitment. To ensure alignment with current industry standards, this module incorporates a wealth of contemporary research and exposes students to various methodologies prevalent in the field. A cornerstone of this course involves a rigorous assessment task, necessitating students to analyse a dataset meticulously and present an integrated solution aimed at enhancing athlete readiness.

title: Virtual Production
description: This unit focuses on developing students' skills and expanding their conceptual approaches in the art of digital virtual production. Virtual production utilises game-engine enabled technologies to blend digital and real life elements, resulting in a captivating motion image sequence. Students will utilise industry standard workflows to refine and develop their conceptual approaches and explore the technical possibilities of virtual production through production experimentation.

title: Science and Professional Practice in Psychology
description: Introduces the scientist-practitioner model for psychology. Explores the historical origins of psychology, the scientific mindset and the role of ethics in psychological research and practice. Examines the manner in which theory, research and practice are mutually informed. Reviews psychology career pathways in the discipline, profession and related areas.

title: Curtin Taxation Clinic
description: The Curtin Tax Clinic is an experiential, Work Integrated Learning (WIL) course where students will have the opportunity to undertake advice and representation work for eligible taxpayers (individuals and small businesses). Through their work in the clinic, students will develop their understanding of substantive and procedural tax and ethical issues and be better equipped to deal with the realities of tax practice upon graduation.

title: Central Nervous System (CNS) Pharmacology and Therapeutics
description: In this unit, students learn about the pathophysiology, pharmacology and pharmacotherapy for the management of medical conditions and complications that affect the central nervous system (CNS) and apply current evidence to resolve clinical problems. This unit comprises 4 modules. Module 1: Mental health conditions including major depressive disorder, anxiety disorders, sleep disorders, bipolar disorder and schizophrenia. Module 2: Pain disorders including use of opioid analgesics, local and general anaesthetics. Module 3: Substance abuse and addiction. Module 4: Neurodegenerative disorders including Parkinson’s disease, multiple sclerosis, dementia and epilepsy.

title: Advanced Pharmacokinetics and Drug Bioanalysis
description: In this unit students will build upon prior course content based upon pharmacokinetics (PK) and drug analysis. This unit comprises two learning modules: Module 1 (drug bioanalysis) - fundamentals of drug bioanalysis, high pressure liquid chromatography for drug bioanalysis, immunoassays, tracer techniques and labelled drug studies, fluorimetry and mass spectrometry. Module 2 (advanced PK) - drug metabolism and metabolite kinetics, PK in renal and hepatic disease, PK variability, therapeutic drug monitoring, prediction of human kinetics and PK research principles.

title: Responsible Innovation and Leadership
description: This unit helps students apply innovative thinking skills to create novel business models and solutions to global challenges facing society today and that achieve UN Sustainable Development Goals for a better future for all. A key objective of the unit is to aid students in building a responsible mindset so they can become leaders who make decisions around innovative solutions that consider the needs of all stakeholders. Through this unit, students will build competencies aimed at developing a global, responsible, innovative and technology (GRIT) mindset.

title: Supply Chain Project
description: This unit explores the application of skills, processes and technology in supply chain management, and examines a variety of critical issues in procurement, logistics and supply chain. Best practices of leading companies around the world are analysed. Innovative and collaborative decisions to solve problems are examined to achieve goals within a wide range of complex supply chain management issues faced by organisations. The unit provides an understanding of value-maximising solutions and identifies how management and the application of processes of logistics, procurement and the supply chains of the future will be structured.

title: Satellite and Space Positioning
description: Who uses GPS (Global Positioning System)? Pretty much everyone in one way or another. Satellite and Space Positioning unit provides you with the knowledge and basic skills needed to collect and process data for positioning using Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS; comprising the US-GPS, Russian-GLONASS, EU-Galileo and Chinese-Beidou). Need for positions derived from GNSS are now required in most fields.
