For example, whereas Surveyors need to provide accurate three-dimensional coordinates in space and time, Civil and Mine Engineers use Real Time Kinematic (RTK) to obtain positions during construction and mining activities. Geologists, on the other hand, need precise locations of their rocks while Agriculturalists require accurate positions for precision farming. With climate change increasingly being of global concern, its monitoring is now being undertaken using GPS atmospheric sounding. In this unit, you will not only be introduced to a modern surveying positioning tool but also to the state-of-the-art space missions currently in operation, such as GPS radio occultation and Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE). Assuming no prior knowledge, the unit provides the basics of GPS, its positioning methods (static, RTK, Real Time Extended (RTX), etc.), and the processing techniques (Trimble Business Center (TBC) and AUSPOS Online Service). In addition, the unit considers other space-based positioning techniques such as VLBI (very long baseline interferometry), LLR (lunar laser ranging) and SLR (satellite laser ranging). It is hoped that once you have completed this unit, you will be prepared to meet future challenges requiring knowledge and skills of satellite and space positioning, which is not only essential, but which you will find very useful and use regularly in your future careers.

title: Introduction to Scientific Data Analysis
description: Computing, data collection, and data analysis are an essential part of a contemporary scientist’s toolkit. In this unit, students will learn about the collection, storage, manipulation, interrogation, analysis and presentation of scientific data using contemporary computing environments. In the first part of the unit, the emphasis will be on using Microsoft Excel to store, manipulate, and display data. In the second part, students will be introduced to the visualisation and analysis of large scientific datasets using R (programming language), a contemporary statistical environment. Using both these computing environments, students will also learn descriptive and inferential methods that they will require to draw conclusions from scientific data, along with tools and techniques that will allow them to communicate their findings in a manner appropriate to scientific reports, articles, dissertations, and other modes of communication.

title: Formation Evaluation
description: Borehole environment and logging procedure, Log data QC, Log editing and calliper logs, Spontaneous potential (SP) logs, principles and applications, Gamma ray and spectral gamma ray, Principles of sonic logging and applications, Density logging and litho-density, principles and applications, Neutron logging, principles and quantitative interpretation, Applications of combined density and neutron logging data, Resistivity logging and measurement principles, Electrical properties of reservoir rocks and Archie's relationships, Log interpretation procedure in clean formations, Log interpretation in shaly formations.

title: Educators Inquiring About the World
description: This unit provides an introduction to systematic processes of inquiry which lay the foundation for meaningful interpretation and implementation of curriculum. Students will learn the principles of inquiry and be introduced to inquiry methodologies as well as discipline specific inquiry approaches for Science and HASS. A cross-curriculum priority will be chosen as the thematic focus for the unit. This will assist students when they are selecting a global and local issue as the topic of their inquiry project. The inquiry project will require students to use and develop skills in critical and creative thinking, analysis and evaluation, problem identification and problem solving, ICT, and collaborative participation, which are important WIL skills and 21st century competencies.

title: Humanities Honours Project 1
description: This unit extends skills acquired during a relevant Bachelor of Arts Degree. Students will acquire new knowledge and develop a research approach through the development of a project. Through independent research and guided supervision students will produce work for review and examination at the end of semester.

title: Fluid Mechanics
description: This unit introduces the fundamental properties of fluids and characteristics of fluid motion. It establishes basic concepts, such as Bernoulli equation and the control-volume analysis applied to mass conservation and momentum equation to characterise flow systems theoretically and experimentally and evaluate flow properties and fluid forces on solid bodies. It introduces models and techniques to analyse internal and external flows for the laminar and turbulent regimes and develop an understanding of the operation of fluid systems. Students will draw on their fundamental knowledge of fluid mechanics to perform design calculations for engineering applications such as dams, turbines and propellers, flow around structures, piping systems and pumps.

title: 3D Character Studio
description: This unit develops students' skills and conceptual approaches in areas that are critical to the character creation pipeline. Students will explore industry standard approaches and technology to complete a project ready character asset.

title: Commerce in Indigenous Australian Contexts
description: Development of knowledge and skills in Indigenous related business practices including: socio-economic concepts, governance, organisational management and leadership, wealth creation for Indigenous communities using Indigenous Terms of Reference. Students will examine business models to identify and develop appropriate best practice frameworks within Indigenous settings.

title: Nursing Honours Preparation
description: Fundamental competencies to enable students to develop an appreciation of the ethics and principles of research and research design; critically appraise and interpret scientific literature; as well as develop skills in planning and writing a research proposal.

title: International Experience 3
description: n/a

title: Capstone Computing Project 1
description: Software engineering projects are selected and undertaken in consultation with a member of the academic staff, usually working in a small group in conjunction with an industry partner or a designated client. Projects are related to the design, implementation and testing of software systems with associated literature reviews. Team-oriented software engineering processes are applied during all phases of the project. Management activities are undertaken and a range of software engineering tools are applied to resolve problems arising during the execution of the software development process. The main focus of this unit is problem identification and the development of a project proposal.Students from each degree and major will be given tasks specific to that degree and major as part of their project work.

title: Energy Conversion and Sustainable Management
description: This unit aims to provide students with an overarching view of energy conversion technologies and their application to sustainable management practices. Students will explore how energy is converted from various energy sources into useful forms; and can be managed sustainably. Topics include a broad understanding of the principles and practices of sustainable energy management, energy conversion and energy storage technologies, and sustainable energy management strategies.

title: Surveying and Geo-Informatics
description: This unit introduces the applications of surveying and geographic information systems (GIS) methods to mining. Students will be introduced to key surveying techniques used in open cut and underground mining environments. The unit explores the role of the mine surveyor in underground control, supporting unmanned machine guidance systems, and the application of satellite positioning technologies. Students will gain hands-on experience by collecting and processing surveying data, including levelling and traversing, using instruments and methods simulated for a mine site environment. Students will be also introduced to the fundamentals of GIS and its use in analysing, processing, and presenting data collected by surveying and other mapping techniques. This will entail utilising GIS software for data processing, input and representation of data, storage and manipulation of geospatial data, and data dissemination with maps. Students will also develop their collaborative and communication skills through fieldwork activities.

title: Brand Management
description: This unit extends on the various aspects of advertising and marketing and applies these concepts to a brand equity perspective. The topics will be built around the product/brand management decisions and through seminars, case analyses and a brand audit project. The unit examines specific advertising and marketing topics related to building, measuring, and managing brand equity. Specifically, the unit examines various brand management decisions and the strategies and tactics to build measure and manage brand equity. These include (a) direct and indirect measures of brand equity, (b) structures of desired brand knowledge, (c) choice of brand elements, (d) development of supporting marketing programs, (e) introduction of new products naming, corporate perspectives and (f) management of brands over time and geographical boundaries.

title: Fine Art Project
description: This unit is designed to introduce you to research methods relevant to contemporary art. You will develop skills in writing proposals, initiating your own studio practice and presenting a body of artworks. You will engage in regular ongoing dialogue with staff and peers to discuss the progress and direction of studio project work.

title: Entertainment Industry Essentials
description: This unit will introduce students to the intricacies of developing, managing and marketing in the entertainment industry. As a starting point, students will learn about the myriad of businesses that make up the entertainment industry. Then, students will explore the managerial and marketing practices of entertainment businesses. This encompasses (1) developing, branding and marketing entertainment products for specific audiences; (2) producing and managing entertainment product portfolios; and (3) delivering authentic entertainment experiences. The unit also delves into sustainable entertainment product management with a specific focus on the triple bottom line as well as innovative business orientations. Entertainment Industry Essentials aims to deliver a vibrant learning experience through interactive lectures and seminar activities, guest lectures and a field trip. Students taking the unit can expect to develop a theoretical and practical understanding of this exciting multi-billion dollar industry.

title: Indigenous and Cross Cultural Psychology
description: Examination of people in broad cultural contexts. The role of culture, world view and ecological factors that play a role in shaping our realities, and subsequently our adaptations to contexts is explored. It promotes the development of a psychology that is sensitive to cultural diversity.

title: Real-Time Effects and Compositing
description: This unit focuses on developing students' skills and expanding their conceptual approaches in production methods for real-time effects and compositing which are utilised in moving image sequences. Real-time visual effects focus on real-time methodologies, such as utilising game-engines or other tools that augment real-time work production. In this unit students will learn the basic industry workflows for real-time visual effects production and the relevant techniques in compositing to blend various visual elements and create a compelling moving image sequence. Students will learn to utilise industry standard workflows to refine and develop their conceptual approaches.

title: Physiotherapy Clinics 1
description: This fieldwork unit will cover physiotherapy clinical practice, to entry level standard according to the Physiotherapy practice thresholds in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand for Physiotherapy, managing clients in an acute care setting with a range of caseloads and model/s of intervention and service delivery.

title: Advanced Narrative Nonfiction
description: Narrative non-fiction is a hybrid of literature and non-fiction. It includes narrative non-fiction, memoir, personal essay and literary journalism, and combines the diligence of the journalist, the analysis of the essayist, and the story telling techniques of the novelist. The genre encompasses a broad range of topics in which the narrative events and experiences are used to explore more complex themes and issues, and in which ethical and cross-cultural issues are addressed. In this unit, you will read and analyse works of narrative non-fiction and write an original work of your own.

title: Sustainability Communication and Action
description: This unit aims to engage students with sustainability concepts and frameworks including planetary boundaries and the United Nation's Sustainable Development Goals through the critical study of environmental issues and solutions. Students will develop essential professional writing, presenting, and academic referencing skills, learn effective academic and professional communication, and use technology tools to enhance their research on sustainability topics.

title: Go Practice Internship 5
description: This unit provides students with fieldwork opportunities through internships or industry and community engagement opportunities in simulated work-based environments. Independent student learning will be supported by academics and industry advisors, and students in courses without professional work experience are encouraged to apply.

title: Advanced Biomechanics
description: This unit is designed to leverage off the knowledge base acquired in REHT2002 Biomechanics to enable acquisition, analysis and interpretation of kinematic, kinetic and electromyographic data, to measure movement both optimal and pathological. The instrumentation and methodologies to acquire these data will allow a number of specific skilled movements to be analysed and the pathomechanics of injury detected. The strengths and weaknesses and limitations of the methodologies will be evaluated.

title: Medical Pathophysiology
description: Principles of disease processes, causes, medical procedures, cell injury, inflammation and tissue repair, abnormal growth patterns. International systems for classification and coding of diseases. Diseases of the muscular, endocrine, cardiovascular, pulmonary, digestive and nervous systems. Correlation between mechanisms of disease and clinical aspects (disease phenotype, signs and symptoms).

title: Cyber Security- Intrusion Detection System and Incident Handling
description: This unit introduces the technology behind intrusion detection and examines the approaches taken by intrusion detection systems, both at the network and host level. It examines the differences between using host-based and network-based IDSs and how each of them can be implemented. Students learn how to analyse the different responses required, depending on the risk/threat to the system and how to handle intrusions. The unit will first examine in detail the different approaches in Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS). Next, the unit will cover how an intrusion detection system responds to an alarm and how to design and deploy an IDS to fit the requirements of differing organisations ranging from small LAN based systems to multi-level distributed systems.

title: Managing Social Media Platforms
description: This unit provides students with both a theoretical and applied understanding of managing social media platforms. The unit reviews social media platforms, critical research and agency best practice in social media marketing. Students will develop an understanding of the social media landscape, social media platforms, develop digital literacy as well as an understanding of ethical and regulatory conduct in the social media space.

title: Introduction to Speech Pathology Practice
description: This unit develops students’ understanding of professional practice and the application of speech pathology theories and concepts. This unit supports students to develop the skills relevant to speech pathology practice, providing an introduction to the application of skills through simulated experiences which develop skills in interacting with clients. Students will also have the opportunity to complete an early intervention experience and observe a practicing Speech Pathologist. The introduction and use of the clinical portfolio allows students to link experiences to speech pathology competency standards and develop an understanding of the competencies required in developing clinical competence.

title: Introduction to Occupational Therapy
description: This unit introduces students to the profession of occupational therapy and the role of occupational therapists in a variety of settings. Students will understand the impact that participating in meaningful occupations and occupational roles has on a person’s health and well-being. The unit introduces occupational therapy models used to understand humans as occupational beings. Students will analyse how injury, acute and chronic health conditions and disability might impact a person’s occupational performance and engagement.

title: Structural Mechanics
description: This unit examines methods of calculating stresses and strains in materials under a range of different loading conditions. Geometric and material properties are examined and utilised to calculate normal and shear stresses and strains due to applied axial, bending, shear and torsion actions. The basic relationships between normal stress and strain are expanded upon with investigation into general beam equations and general strain equations, enabling the solution of problems involving compatibility, composite beams, unsymmetrical bending, plastic behaviour of beams and combined actions. Techniques to determine shear stresses and strains due to shear forces and torsion actions in circular and non-circular sections are introduced. Biaxial Stress systems, and the combination of normal and shear stresses, are analysed using Mohr’s circle and stress transformation methods.

title: Measurement and Adjustment Analysis
description: Functional and stochastic models. Linearisation by Taylor's series. Review of variance propagation. Correlated observations. The parametric, condition and combined adjustment models. Adjustment of survey networks. Introduction to datum definition. Least squares coordinate transformations. Statistical assessment of adjustment results. Assignment of class and order to networks. Introduction to pre-analysis and network design. Sequential least squares estimation. Parameter constraints and observations.

title: Pharmacy Practice 5
description: In this unit, students learn how to communicate with and provide pharmaceutical services to special patient groups including patients who are terminally ill and those with mental health issues. Students will extend their communication skills by giving oral presentations and providing evidence-informed written disease management care plans in patient cases with health-related issues. Students will evaluate and apply error risk reduction strategies in pharmacy practice with the aim of providing continuous quality improvement and quality assurance. There will be further opportunities for students to become more familiar with information technology for pharmacists including electronic prescribing and electronic medication management records. Students will extend their performance of pharmaceutical calculations to include complex pharmaceutical calculations in patients with multiple morbidities. Students will also develop policies and guidelines for new pharmaceutical services and will investigate and reflect on evolving roles and new models of care for pharmacists. Students will apply clinical, ethical, economic and legal reasoning to resolve complex professional dilemmas.

title: Visual Communication
description: In this unit, students will refine their skills in research and academic writing. The three assessments outlined, encourage students to apply design theories in analysing specific topics. The unit focuses on semiotics, material culture and icons of popular culture. This is relevant to all visual communicators, and was specifically constructed for those studying creative advertising, graphic design, illustration and photography.

title: Introduction to Australian Taxation Law
description: Studying this unit will introduce you to the Australian Taxation System and get you to critically consider the various aspects of the taxation legislation with a focus on Income Tax, Fringe Benefit Tax, Goods and Services Tax and Capital Gains Tax as well as a detailed investigation into the taxing of various tax entities used in Australia. You will be exposed to considering the global aspect of taxation and how foreign companies and individuals are treated for tax purposes in Australia. Being a tax professional is a privileged position but it comes with both social and ethical responsibilities and in this unit we will identify these as well as taking a detailed looked at the various bodies associated with the administration and review of the Australian Taxation System such as the Australia Taxation Office, Inspector General of Taxation and the Tax Practitioners Board. Whilst this unit is an introductory unit of taxation the detailed material and passion and enthusiasm of the teaching staff will ensure that you leave the unit will an appreciation for the complexity of the Australian Taxation System and more importantly the vast array of career opportunities that exist in this profession.

title: Services Marketing
description: Explosive growth in service-focused business has propelled the importance of this sector for marketing professionals. The strategic frameworks designed for marketing of physical goods do not effectively transfer into the services marketing environment. The inherent relationship between service businesses and their customers places greater demands on these firms to manage complex processes. For example, service delivery, potential service failure, service recovery, staff culture and managing customer satisfaction pose distinct challenges to service marketers. An expanded services marketing mix addresses the pressure on service businesses to remain competitive in advancing their business outcomes. Moreover, the dramatic increase in E-commerce service-focused enterprise has accelerated the need for services marketing initiatives across online environments. Managing virtual relationships within an ever-changing online services landscape poses new challenges within the marketing profession.

title: Mine Surveying
description: Open cut and underground mine surveys. Transfer of directions through mine shafts. Gyrotheodolite. Underground traverse networks. Design, measurement and processing of three dimensional mine deformation survey networks. Precise electronic theodolites and total stations for use in Deformation type surveys. Precise Levelling. Introduction to mine surveying software such as Surpac and its use in the mining industry.

title: Management and Teamwork in Allied Health
description: In this unit students will be introduced to principles of case management, including funding sources, service delivery models, and evidence-based practice. The unit explores establishment and management of human, financial, and physical resources relevant to practice. Responsibilities for staff and student supervision, mentoring, and professional development, legislative compliance, and impacts of health economics will be explored using scenarios promoting innovation, inclusion, and collaboration. Clinical reasoning and decision making will be applied to diverse contexts using case scenarios.

title: Common Mental Health Disorders
description: An analysis and application of knowledge of common mental health disorders, the signs and symptoms of mood affective disorders including depression, bipolar and anxiety disorders. The association between trans-generational trauma and depression among stolen generation people is also explored. Students critically examine these maladaptive behaviours and categorise them from a mental health perspective that includes concurrent conditions, classification of the disorder and appropriate referral.

title: Psychosocial Care for Complex Mental Health
description: Critical appraisal of mainstream diagnostic classification of major mental illness and psychopathology from a transdisciplinary perspective. Sociocultural and temporal context of mental wellness and illness. Psychosocial partnership in care in the formulation of assessment, treatment and management of mental health and illness behaviours. Strength-based psychosocial interventions to empower wellbeing in people living with complex and critically unstable mental health problems and the application to person-centred practice in nursing 	and paramedicine. Accountability and social justice issues within mental health contexts.

title: Integrating Indigenous Science and STEM
description: Students will be introduced to Indigenous science, history, culture, knowledge and practices, and the value of integrating different knowledge systems to address global challenges. This unit focuses on developing the capacity of students to research, evaluate and communicate scientific and cultural information and arguments using written, visual and oral presentation techniques, while demonstrating inter-cultural awareness, scientific standards and academic integrity. In tandem, related ethical issues within STEM are explored, and particularly, the historic use of scientific ideas to justify social and political actions. The nature of science and scientific behaviours, the role and relevance of science and other knowledge systems in society, and methods of scientific inquiry are introduced to foster students' professional identities as scientists in Science Technology Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) fields in the 21st century.

title: Motion Design Studio
description: This unit introduces students to the process of developing creative outcomes through motion design. A large percentage of information we see in our everyday lives is conveyed through moving graphics, particularly in television commercials, television program title sequences, movie special effects and music video clips. This unit focuses on the design process of creating motion design. It aims to provide a foundational understanding of visual and theoretical principles that impact motion graphics. This includes typography, layouts, storyboarding and aesthetics. In the motion design projects, students will learn skills in basic motion graphics and digital production techniques.

title: Functional Analysis
description: This unit covers advanced topics in Functional Analysis and Advanced Calculus which are important in several areas of applied mathematics, physics, and engineering. The first part of this unit deals with functional spaces, which are infinite-dimensional vector spaces whose elements are, as the name suggests, functions. To develop the adequate background for the study of these spaces, we will introduce the notions of normed and metric spaces, Banach and Hilbert spaces. These have immense relevance in contexts like applied optimisation and quantum physics. We will then introduce the theory of generalised functions, also known as distributions. Distributions are routinely employed in science and engineering to model impulsive behaviours: the classical example is the Dirac delta distribution, which is used to model, for example, a point charge, point mass or electron point. Enlarging the classical Lebesgue functional spaces to include distributions allows us to define the appropriate set of solutions of linear partial differential equations. To address this topic, which is one of the pivotal ones in modern theoretical and applied mathematics, we will introduce and develop the theory of the Fourier transform, not only for functions, but also for tempered distributions, and we will apply it to the solution of important partial differential equations arising in mathematical physics, including the heat equation, the Laplace equation and the Schroedinger equation.

title: Business and Law International Experience 5
description: International mobility experience for undergraduate students.

title: Mental Health 3
description: The unit is designed for students to develop a comprehensive understanding of the multifaceted aspects of mental health care in acute settings. Through a combination of theoretical knowledge and practical skills, students will explore the structure, policies, and standards guiding acute mental health services in Australia, gain insights into diagnostic systems, therapeutic alliance, case management, and legal and ethical considerations. Emphasis will be placed on the lived experience and the recovery framework, recognizing the importance of holistic care in addressing co-occurring chronic diseases and complex social issues. Students will be introduced to psychopharmacology for low prevalence disorders and assisted to navigate personal and professional challenges they may encounter in mental health settings.

title: Advanced Structural Modelling
description: The concept of elasticity in 2D and 3D continua will be introduced with particular focus on plane stress and plane strain problems. Finite element (FE) method will be introduced with particular focus on the formulation of stiffness matrix equations for bar, truss, beam and plate elements. Shape functions will also be introduced in the formation of FE stiffness equations. The use of commercial FE software to model and analyse different structural problems will also be covered. Non-linear FE analysis techniques will also be introduced in this unit. The theory of buckling analysis of plates and frames will also be covered. Basic principles and industry practices for the analysis and design of bulk material handling support systems used in the mining sector provide an industry context for modelling.

title: Strategic Management
description: This unit focuses on the practice and concepts of sustainable strategic management through the introduction of appropriate theoretical models, frameworks and practices of sustainable organisational strategies. The central issue of the unit is the achievement of competitive advantage: internal and external drivers of competitive advantage, the link between strategy formulation and implementation, the role of strategic leadership in formulating and implementing strategy for creating and sustaining competitive advantage.

title: Indigenous Australian Healing Practices
description: Introduction to cultural and spiritual expressions of health and illness in Indigenous and non-Indigenous contexts. Conceptual understanding of and cultural sensitivity to different methods of healing practices in Indigenous communities inclusive of social and emotional wellbeing. Use of various bush medicines and ways of working with Indigenous healers in non-Indigenous health systems.

title: Curriculum and Instruction Senior Secondary: Humanities and Social Sciences
description: This unit is designed to prepare pre-service teachers to teach the Senior Secondary Humanities and Social Sciences curriculum. The focus of the unit is on curriculum planning, teaching strategies, assessment, reporting, the demonstration of positive impact on student learning and research relating to Senior Secondary Humanities and Social Sciences. The unit examines moderation, the provision of feedback and responding to individual student needs.

title: Fine Art Studio Practice
description: This unit is designed to further develop your capacity for reflection and research-based enquiry into skills, techniques, methods and processes of visual art. You will gain further skills in articulating the studio research process and further develop conceptual frameworks that support artistic practice.

title: Campaign Planning and Evaluation
description: This is an applied research unit, structured around a real-life client who challenges students to develop solutions to a contemporary communication challenge. Throughout the semester learners explore different qualitative and quantitative research methods, critically examine ‘best practice’ examples and are exposed to the latest developments and standards in measurement and evaluation, which will enable them to demonstrate the communication function’s return on investment (or return on expectations) to key decision-makers.

title: Special Topics in Law
description: This unit will focus on a specialised area of law, which will vary from year to year. The specific materials that will be covered depend upon the subject of the special topic(s) and the academic undertaking the teaching of the unit. Students will be required to undertake intensive reading and research on the specialised topic(s), and will develop an in depth knowledge and critical thinking skills with respect to the subject matter of the topic(s). The unit develops students capacities to communicate through oral and written means as appropriate to working within a complex field of law.

title: Social Psychology
description: Exploring the history of social psychology and the implications for fundamental understanding of social situations, including groups.

title: Introduction to Occupational Therapy Professional Practice
description: This unit develops students’ understanding of professional practice—the integration of ethical behaviour, accountability, interpersonal communication, and the application of occupational therapy knowledge and frameworks in alignment with the Occupational Therapy Competency Standards. It consolidates the application of theories and concepts by drawing on occupational therapy models and frameworks, applying client- and person-centred approaches, engaging in reflective practice and clinical reasoning, and supporting the development of professional behaviours—including verbal and non-verbal communication skills identified in the Occupational Therapy Competency Standards as essential for interprofessional collaboration and safe, respectful practice. Through learning activities, students begin to apply the competency standards with a particular focus on accountability, ethical practice, and interpersonal communication. Students will undertake a one-week fieldwork placement, offering opportunities to observe and appropriately engage in professional practice within the scope of a second-year student. A reflective portfolio supports this process, enabling students to capture their growth in relation to the Occupational Therapy Competency Standards and to recognise that professional behaviours, communication, and ethical practice are skills that continue to develop throughout their studies and future practice.

title: Integrated Surveying
description: Integration of terrestrial surveying techniques, equipment and processing software to provide accurate mapping information of structures on the earth’s surface. Principles, operational aspects and applications of laser scanning. In-field calibration of total stations and levels as well as theory of calibration and adjustment of terrestrial laser scanners. Observational and equipment requirements to meet various classes of SP1 accuracies for control networks. Introductory least-squares adjustment of control networks. Trigonometric heighting.

title: Food Science Professional Placement
description: Application of discipline specific knowledge and skills during a professional placement in the food industry. Development of professionalism, multicultural communication skills, problem solving skills and ethics in the workplace. Preparation of documents to demonstrate employability including job applications and resumes.

title: Introduction to Derivative Securities
description: This unit covers the theoretical foundations of derivative securities, financial forwards and futures, forward rate agreements (FRAs) and swaps, model-independent option valuation, geometric Brownian motion, Black-Scholes- Merton model, binomial model, option Greeks, and model risk. This unit also discusses the impact of quantum Fintech on derivatives market. This unit includes analyzing a business case study and use Eikon real derivatives market data to solve work integrated problems.

title: Introduction to Financial Management in Indigenous Australian Contexts
description: An introduction to financial management practices including budgeting, funding applications and acquittals in an Indigenous context. Students will learn about organisational leadership models and financial management of resources which impact on professional practices. Financial regulatory frameworks and corporate governance in Indigenous communities and organisations will also be explored.

title: Digital Marketing and E-Commerce
description: This unit offers an in-depth understanding of the non-technical aspects of the internet and its strategic marketing applications. It covers how the digital environment affects marketing decisions through identifying web-based opportunities and threats for firms. It also focuses on major digital marketing and e-commerce strategies (e.g., SEO, SEM, etc.) that a firm or brand can adopt to engage with consumers across their purchase journey using various digital channels such as paid, owned, and earned media. The unit will sharpen students’ digital competencies and will strengthen their GRIT (Global, Responsible, Innovative and Technological) mindset.

title: Introduction to Laboratory Medicine Practice
description: Seven weeks of supervised professional practice in a 'National Association of Testing Authorities' (NATA) accredited medical laboratory. Students will be orientated to the Professional Standards of Occupational Health and Safety and Good Laboratory Practice as described in 'Competency based standards for Medical Scientists'. Placement will be in the specimen reception/collection area of the laboratory gaining competency and knowledge in the systems and processes documented in the laboratory's Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) related to pre-examination and examination of primary samples.

title: Marine Ecology
description: This unit will cover the ecological processes that drive temperate and tropical marine communities, and the quantitative methods used to describe them. Students will acquire practical skills in developing hypotheses and research questions, collection of field data, and the various univariate and multivariate analyses used to measure ecological data. There will be particular emphasis on long-term monitoring and experimental design and how these are used to measure natural and anthropogenic disturbances. Topics covered include; population dynamics and processes; gene flow and connectivity; biogeography and distribution patterns; life-history attributes; biodiversity patterns in marine habitats and methods used to study community structure including diversity indices and ordination. Students are assumed to have a working knowledge of basic statistics.

title: Primary Care Nursing Practice
description: The unit builds on the fundamentals of nursing practice and continues to explore assessment and care of the stable person from the context of primary care. Topics covered include cultural care, physical and mental health assessment; therapeutic communication with people in a range of settings, including changes in cognition and perception; and principles of primary health care; health screening and health promotion across the life span. Students apply best practice nursing care to support wellbeing and person-centred care including the importance of working in partnership with those receiving care. Medication preparation, administration, dosage calculations, legislative control and applied pharmacology in the context of the stable person is reinforced.

title: Introduction to Business Information Systems
description: In this unit, the focus is on understanding the significance of Business Information Systems (BIS) and Business Information Technology (BIT) in promoting global, responsible, innovative, and technology-driven success in organisations. The unit offers an overview of the different types of information systems and technology, and how they support and enhance business processes through the appropriate use of technology. It also introduces the activities and tools used to develop, maintain, and operate effective BIS. By the end of this unit, students will have a foundational understanding of how BIS and BIT can contribute to organisational success in a global, responsible, innovative, and technology-driven manner.

title: Human Resources Management Introduction
description: In this unit, you will learn about the contemporary role of human resources management (HRM) and its impact on the economic performance of organisations and societies globally. You will explore key HRM functions, challenges and issues within a complex and turbulent global working future as well as the critical influence HRM has on the decent work and economic growth agenda, both nationally and internationally. You will develop the critical knowledge and skills necessary to become an HR professional through engaging with the relevant and current literature and unit content, listening to industry professionals and working on real world case studies and scenarios. As the unit content has been developed in collaboration with industry professionals, you will develop a comprehensive understanding of the strategic and integrated nature of HRM within organisations. This unit will prepare you for a career in HRM or related fields, as well as enhance your employability capability.

title: Operations Research
description: This until will consider problems arising in business and industry. The students will learn the necessary skills to model and solve such problems through mathematical modelling and operations research techniques. The topics covered include: Linear programming (LP): Linear Programming models, Two-variable LP problems, Basic theory of linear systems, The Simplex algorithm, Duality, Sensitivity Analysis. Transportation Problem: basic concepts, applications, algorithm. Project Planning: Basic concept, formulation and application of LP to analyse project scheduling). Quadratic Programming: Basic concepts, application, algorithm. Game Theory: basic concepts, application, modelling through LP.

title: Consumer Behaviour
description: Introduces the role of consumer behaviour and how it is shaped by the social and cultural environment and the psychological foundations. The unit in essence focuses on the decision processes in consumption behaviour in different buying situations. This develops the student's ability to integrate marketing processes at a higher level. For marketers, an understanding of how a consumer selects, purchases, uses and disposes of products and services is pertinent to successfully managing the marketing function. Concepts drawn from various disciplines such as psychology, economics and anthropology are also examined.

title: Property Valuation Practice
description: Students undertake a period of 120 hours in professional valuation practice under the supervision of a Licensed Valuer. Students are required to prepare and submit three valuation reports, two residential and one commercial, a work diary and timesheet all certified by their mentor.

title: Local Planning
description: Examines the framework for local plan-making.  Tools and mechanisms including data systems, local planning, strategies and schemes, legislation and the implementation of local planning are explored.

title: Discovering Marketing
description: Understanding the role marketing plays in business and society; The global marketing environment; Consumer buyer behaviour; Market segmentation, target marketing and positioning; New product development and the product life cycle; Marketing Strategies (the 4 P's) - product, price, place and promotion; Ethics in marketing.

title: Transportation Engineering and Earthworks
description: This unit provides an introduction to highway engineering, railway engineering and airport engineering. It examines principles of geometric design of highways, railways, airports and ports, including basic principles of vehicle performance for road pavement design. It introduces earthworks construction with the consideration of earthmoving types, earthwork volumes, mass haul diagrams, soil volume properties, grade and rolling resistance, and assessment of main earthwork equipment and machines with optimisation techniques.

title: iSTEM: Social Issues
description: This unit is one of three undergraduate Option units in integrated science, technology, engineering and mathematics (iSTEM) offered by the School of Education. Completing all three units will provide a specialisation in iSTEM. This unit aims to equip students with content and pedagogical content knowledge in integrated STEM education in the context of an inquiry based approach. Students will develop, create and reflect upon a contextual problem, make explicit links to the science, mathematics and technologies curricula and 21st century learning skills. Pedagogical content knowledge will be developed by students creating and evaluating project plans and implementation approaches in a variety of educational settings as appropriate to their degree (ie ECE, Primary or Secondary).

title: International Experience 7
description: n/a

title: Introduction to Screen Practice
description: Introduction to national and global cinematic and broadcast industries. Students study historical and contemporary business models and screen audiences while simultaneously developing their professional practice, technical and teamwork skills as creators of screen works. This unit combines critical studies and creative practice through action/reflection and production/analysis tasks.

title: Engineering Connections
description: In this unit students will study major engineering projects throughout history to make connections between the projects and non-technical aspects of engineering, namely: ethical behaviour, health and safety, historical context, risk management and social environment. Students will use critical thinking to engage in conversations about projects in different disciplines. Students will submit their work using written, oral and multimedia formats.

title: Advanced Topics in Mathematical Sciences A
description: Australian Mathematical Sciences Institute (AMSI) is the collaborative enterprise of Australia’s mathematical sciences, of which Curtin is a member. AMSI Advanced Collaborative Environment (ACE) Network offers a wide selection of honours level Mathematical Sciences subjects in online mode. Within this unit, you will enrol in one of the ACE subjects available for your period of study. A detailed subject guide and pre-enrolment quizzes are available for each subject under ACE network tab of AMSI. The subject may be selected to complement your existing strengths and knowledge. You will be completing this unit alongside other fellow students from Australian and New Zealand universities.

title: International Experience 2
description: n/a

title: International Management
description: This unit acquaints students with current international management theory and practice, encouraging interest and enthusiasm for an international business career. It provides students with an introduction to methodologies for studying management from a comparative perspective and highlights the emerging issues for an international manager. The practical issues of adaptation needed in cross-cultural or cross-national managerial interfaces are considered extensively and students learn to analyse management problems and generate solutions to real-life issues and problems. This unit provides students with the opportunity to develop Global and Responsible Mindsets. Utilising various case studies across different cultural contexts, students are able to develop their cross-cultural communication and engagement through extensive in-depth analysis, discussion, and application of contemporary global practices.

title: Enhancing Your Business Mind
description: This unit has been designed by industry to help give students the confidence and abilities that industry want. The unit will take students through different team thinking techniques used in many varying industries in order to broaden their own discipline knowledge. The unit will also focus on self; the students overall interpretation of the value they can bring to an organisation. The unit will help prepare students for their transition into the workplace by equipping them with the resilience necessary to succeed.

title: Fundamentals of Strength of Materials
description: This unit focuses on studying and analysing different loading conditions of structural elements. This understanding provides skills to better select materials, design elements and structures, and assess safety issues. This unit will focus mainly on mechanical engineering applications. Various strategies will be utilised to gain an in-depth understanding and solve common engineering problems for simple as well as complex structures.

title: Renewable Energy Principles
description: This unit will first give an overview of energy transition and the role of renewable energy in addressing environmental impacts by the use of fossil fuels. The unit will cover in detail three renewable energy types most commonly used. i.e. solar, wind and hydro. Under the topic of solar power, calculation of sun’s position angles and solar radiation components are introduced. Furthermore, it will focus on solar PV cells, modules and arrays and their electrical characteristics. Under the topic of wind power, the students will learn the fundamentals of wind resource, types of turbines and their control, wind speed assessment, types of generators and control methods in grid-connected application. The sections covered under hydro power are the calculation of power in water, types of hydro power plants, types of turbines, generators and their control methods in grid-connected application. The last topic covered in this unit is on the emerging alternative energy source of hydrogen. The fundamentals of energy conversion in fuel cells, the types of fuel cells, methods of generating hydrogen, non-idealities of fuel cells, power conditioning needs are all discussed under this topic.

title: Introduction to Software Engineering
description: This unit explores the broad range of software engineering practices over the course of the software development life cycle. The unit covers simple software project management techniques, leading into the specification of functional and non-functional requirements. It demonstrates how to use version control systems to manage coding projects, and how to identify maintainability problems in source code. Finally, it addresses the development of unit testing from a simple theoretical basis and also a highly practical level.

title: International Business Ethics
description: It is critical for organisations to be ethical and socially responsible in contemporary international business. This unit provides various settings for students to engage and discuss ethical, social and environmental issues in the decisions made within the international business context. Students will apply enhanced skills to justify the ethical business decisions made related to stakeholders across different countries.

title: Foundations of Nursing Practice
description: This unit introduces the fundamental concepts of relevant theories, history and practice development that relate to nursing. The unit provides an introduction to communication, reflective practice, a systematic process approach, scope of practice and decision making frameworks in an interprofessional context. Students are introduced to medication mathematics and applied pharmacology. There is a focus on 	fundamental and core principles of patient care based on current best practice, quality outcomes, self care/independence relating to person-centred care and primary health care and the reciprocal relationship between physical and mental health. There is a focus on physical and mental wellbeing and cultural perspectives and considerations for care. Core skills include health assessment; hand hygiene; standard precautions and non-touch-techniques, simple wound dressing, manual handling, end of life care, professional communication and cultural safety. Professional competence and regulatory practice are developed according to the requirements of the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA), Australian Nurses and Midwifery Accreditation Council (ANMAC) and the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia.

title: Geoscience Project
description: A supervised study of a problem or issue of relevance to geology, geophysics or environmental geoscience. The project will include a component of literature review as well as a practical or fieldwork component.  It may or may not be undertaken in collaboration with an industry partner.  Project results will be presented as a formal report and a seminar.

title: Engineering Industry Research Project 2
description: In this unit students will continue the development of the research project begun in Engineering Industry Research Project 1, drawing it to the conclusion and presenting the project findings and solutions in a variety of media, including an individual dissertation.

title: Epidemiology and Biostatistics Practice
description: This unit is a follow up unit from MEDS4003 Principles of Epidemiology and Biostatistics. Statistical and epidemiological methods commonly used in health research will be applied using real examples and case scenarios. There will be elements of critical appraisal on the methods, evidence-based recommendation and knowledge translation.

title: Radiobiology and Fractionation
description: This unit will cover the biological effects of ionising and non-ionising radiation at the cellular level and the resulting effects on organs, tissues and the whole body. Students will gain an in-depth knowledge on mechanisms of repair to biological damage; systemic & total body responses to early/late effects of radiation; hereditary effects; and effects on the embryo & foetus. Students will then apply this fundamental knowledge to critically consider the principles of fractionation and the justifications for the various treatment schedules.

title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Health
description: This unit introduces students to the fundamental concepts of machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI). Students will have the opportunity to explore the uses and impact of machine learning and artificial intelligence in public health and health care. They will address the advantages, limitations and scope of ML/AI from a health perspective. The unit will also have a practical component in which students use the data generated by ML/AI to explore contemporary health issues.

title: Initiating and Planning Indigenous Australian Community Projects
description: Students will initiate and plan an Indigenous Community Development project that will incorporate project management concepts and skills in needs analysis, Indigenous Ways of Working, and an understanding of Professional Development Group processes.

title: Clinical Radiation Therapy Practice 1
description: This unit provides authentic radiation therapy professional practice experience in the clinical setting, at the level appropriate for the beginning reflective professional.

title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Mental Health First Aid
description: This unit provides students with skills to assist a person who may be developing a mental health crisis. The unit also explores Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander social and emotional wellbeing, mental health concerns within communities and professional health teams, and mental health first aid strategies for working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities. Unit content also includes: recognising depression, anxiety, gradual onset psychosis, substance misuse, eating disorders, suicidal thoughts and behaviours, panic attacks and severe effects of drug or alcohol use.

title: Inquiry for Evidence based Clinical Practice
description: Students engage in a review of quantitative and qualitative methodology in the context of clinical research. Students apply the research process: research problems/hypotheses; literature review; theoretical frameworks; sampling; data collection; data analysis; descriptive and inferential statistics; reliability and validity; trustworthiness; research ethics. Critique of research underlying evidence-based practice is critical to this unit of study.

title: Fine Art Project Development
description: This unit is designed to develop your capacity to refine, resolve, present, and critique a self-directed studio practice. Considering a variety of international perspectives, you will develop a project proposal, engage in group discussion and ongoing presentation of works to peers.

title: Foundations of Calculus
description: This unit introduces and establishes the ideas of calculus and how the techniques of calculus can be used in solving problems in science, engineering and business-related fields. Students will learn the necessary skills to solve such problems through the application and techniques of both differential and integral calculus. This unit will cover a variety of techniques of differentiation and integration, and by using these methods of calculus students will learn to solve a range of applications. This unit will also build upon the students’ knowledge of trigonometry, extending into the areas of identities, solving trigonometric equations as well as applying calculus to the trigonometric functions.

title: Calculus 2
description: This unit introduces some fundamental theories and methods for the solution of differential equations and multivariable integral and vector calculus problems. It aims for students to develop their mathematical skills for modelling and solving real world problems by using differential equations and multivariable calculus. Topics covered include first-order differential equations, second and higher order constant coefficient linear equations, power series solutions, Fourier series, partial differential equations, gradient and directional derivatives, maxima and minima, double and triple integrals, line and surface integrals, div and curl, path independence, Green’s theorem, divergence theorem and Stokes theorem.

title: Immunology and Infectious Diseases for Pharmacists
description: This unit is an introduction to the biology of infectious disease and the immune system, particularly as it applies to the practice of Pharmacy, and covers the fundamentals of Microbiology and Immunology, as well as a comprehensive coverage of the medically important infectious diseases. The unit explores the structure and nature of microorganisms with an emphasis on bacteriology, including the identification of common medically important bacteria. Virology and eukaryotic microorganisms are also covered including fungi and protozoa. Through this unit of learning you will also gain knowledge in the structure and function of the immune system with an emphasis on the major innate and adaptive immune mechanisms and how these interact to create an effective defence system against pathogenic microorganisms: both in stopping infection and removal of infectious agents. You will also acquire understanding of the mechanisms of hypersensitivity, autoimmunity and tissue rejection. The causative agents of major diseases are dealt with from a body systems perspective, with a focus on their disease-causing properties that enable them to invade tissues and evade immune defences. These include, but are not limited to, the respiratory system and gastrointestinal tract diseases, the skin and central nervous system diseases, urinary and sexually transmitted infections, vector-borne and emerging infectious diseases. We investigate the role of vaccination in the prevention and control of disease as well as the vaccines which are currently recommended by national and state vaccination schedules.

title: Current Topics in Food Science
description: This unit develops students’ insights into global food systems and the influence of current issues linked to public health on integrated food industries, policy, regulation and global communities. Students explore the production of food commodities from plant and animal sources and their properties and applications in food processing. The unit incorporates current research and industry developments in food science and new technologies in agricultural science, horticulture, animal welfare and traceability.

title: Playful Interactive Experiences
description: This unit helps students to understand key considerations when designing for playful user experiences. Focusing on diverse mediums and multi-platform experiences, students explore emergent technologies for the evolving digital landscape. Projects emphasise mastery of techniques that engage the audience in play as a vehicle for learning, connection and engagement, equipping students with skills to design experiences that delight users across various modes of interactivity.

title: Advanced Psychological Science Qualitative Methods
description: Qualitative design and data analysis in psychological research.

title: International Ethics
description: The aim of this advanced level unit is to help students think systematically about the ethical aspects of statecraft (i.e. the art of conducting state affairs). It examines the moral responsibilities that flow from the management of national decision-making in order to arrive at principled frameworks that ought to guide political action in the international arena. The unit will engage with a series of challenging moral questions on important dimensions of world politics. It examines a range of normative perspectives on what should be done in any given circumstance, drawing upon concrete examples to help students become aware of and improve their own ethical commitments via in-class discussion and thought-provoking written assignments.

title: Indigenous Australian Research Techniques and Methods
description: Develops applied research skills (methods and techniques) that enable students to plan and undertake ethical, effective and culturally sensitive research in Indigenous Australian contexts, and that give priority to Indigenous perspectives, and benefit Indigenous people. Students examine and critique structured and unstructured interviews, focus groups, questionnaires, document analysis and observational data collection skills and techniques, and consider strengths and weaknesses of each.

title: Signals and Systems
description: The course will cover continuous-time and discrete-time signals, specifically their mathematical representations, properties and classifications, such as power and energy signals.  Special attention is devoted to Linear time-invariant systems, where concepts such as impulse response, convolution are developed. The course also cover the Fourier series representation of periodic signals, which leads to continuous-time Fourier transform (and discrete-time Fourier transform), Laplace transform and  Sampling theorem. Students will be introduced to Matlab.

title: Individual Differences
description: This unit introduces students to the major themes and issues underpinning the study of individual differences. It covers influential philosophical, theoretical and empirical approaches to understanding personality and mental abilities.

title: Linear Systems and Vibrations
description: This unit introduces the topic of natural and forced vibration in single and multi-degree of freedom systems. Students will be taught how to simplify a variety of linear and torsional systems into mass-spring-damper systems with different force excitations. These systems will include torsional systems with varying cross sections, stiffness, and multiple rotors, as well as beams vibrating transversely with concentrated and distributed masses. Students will then learn how to create and solve these systems' differential equations. Concepts in math, such as Fourier Series, Laplace Transform, and Linear Systems of ordinary differential equations, will be taught to aid in solving the differential equations. The concept of damping and how it affects the system will be introduced. Since systems that are analysed are often part of a larger system, or are not found in isolation from their environment, concepts such as transmissibility, whirling, rotor balancing, and geared systems will be investigated. Instrumentation and methods of measuring and analysing the vibration of these systems will be introduced.

title: International Study Abroad 4
description: n/a

title: Design Theory in Practice
description: This is an introductory unit that should be completed in a student’s first semester of study at Curtin. This unit aims to prepare students in design-focused disciplines for the requirements of both academia and industry practice. Students will be required to develop and demonstrate skills in referencing, research, communication (written and oral), and thinking (critical, evaluative, and reflective). Students will be prepared to use these skills not just for academic contexts, but also in ways that are unique to design-focused disciplines (e.g. writing and presenting a design report). To enable students to practise and apply these skills, as well as provide the core foundational knowledge required in design disciplines for both academic and industry contexts, this unit will also engage students in the exploration and discussion of key design theories over the course of the semester.

title: Comparative Medical Imaging Science
description: This unit builds on two previous units to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the role of different imaging modalities including general radiography, fluoroscopy, computed tomography, angiography, magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasound and mammography in diagnosis according to the suspected pathology, or its stage of progression. Cost effectiveness and radiation dose are considered throughout as is availability of resources.

title: Applied Physical Rehabilitation
description: The unit focuses on the application of the occupational therapy process including assessment, intervention and evaluation for people with physical activity limitations and participation restrictions within the frameworks of the International Classification of Functioning (ICF) and Person Environment Occupation (PEO). Practical occupational therapy skills to enhance occupational performance for people with physical limitations are part of the learning experience. Case studies are used to develop students’ critical thinking, professional and practical knowledge using occupational therapy models.

title: Foundations of Biostatistics and Epidemiology
description: Foundations of Biostatistics and Epidemiology enables students to learn core skills in epidemiology and biostatistics. Students critically appraise public health and clinical epidemiological research literature and perform basic statistical analysis. Students will encounter basic statistical and graphical description and analysis of epidemiological and biomedical data with appropriate graphs, tables, and summary measures; statistical inference and statistical hypothesis testing applied to problems in health and clinical medicine using parametric and non-parametric tests; calculation of common epidemiological measures of disease frequency and association such as incidence rate, prevalence, attributable risk, risk ratios and odds ratio; role and significance of inferential statistics such as confidence intervals and probability values. Various epidemiological research designs and their strengths and limitations as well as threats to the internal validity; role of chance, bias and confounding are included.

title: Engineering Research Project 2
description: In the Engineering Research Project units, students have an opportunity to demonstrate they have acquired and can apply advanced knowledge and skills to solve complex problems in their discipline. In this unit students will: complete implementation of the solution they proposed in the previous unit, verify their solution against requirements, keep a logbook, and effectively report and present the project in a variety of media, including an individual thesis.

title: History in Practice
description: This unit trains students in practical research and analytical skills that equip them to complete an advanced research project in the field of history. Students are exposed to practical applications of the historian’s skills, engaging with and reflecting on diverse historical practices, research methodologies, and dealing with primary sources. Students can expect to learn about practices such as archival research, digital history, local history, oral history, material culture, and/or quantitative methods (specific practices may vary between offerings). The unit offers students an opportunity to reflect on the theoretical frameworks regularly used by historians that, in turn, guide them in their practice as creators of history, including through site visits and real-world historical projects.

title: Performing Arts for Educators
description: This is the first of two Arts Education units. It introduces The Arts Learning Area through performing arts and places The Arts in a cultural context. The centrality of contemporary arts practices, techniques, processes and pedagogies centre praxis-led learning. This unit emphasises creative thinking, self-expression, meaning-making and communicating ideas. Performing-arts praxis, reflection and appreciation activities provide experiential learning opportunities designed to promote personal confidence, arts literacy and presentation and communication skills in the performing arts and for teaching.

title: Inquiry for Nursing and Midwifery Leadership
description: Students incorporate evidence informed clinical practice in critical environments. Collaboration, clinical reasoning, decision making and communication to prioritise care in critical situations are key skills developed. There is a focusing on the development of leadership, team approaches to care, preceptor/ mentor relationships; accountability, self-care, resilience and managing challenging situations. Skills for enhancing therapeutic interactions, negotiation and problem solving, conflict management and handling difficult conversations are further explored in this unit.

title: Industrial and Systems Engineering Research Project 1
description: Students undertake a significant research project that either develops new knowledge or addresses an engineering problem of interest. Students are free to choose from a range of projects offered by the faculty members as well as by external partners. In this unit students will: identify a problem, propose and plan a solution that meets the requirements, do a literature review to investigate existing solutions, make design decisions and assumptions to develop their solution, keep a logbook, and submit a written progress report at the end of semester. Projects involve engineering research methodologies, including analytical, numerical or experimental investigation or design, carried out over a period of one year. The students submit their final project work in the form of an undergraduate thesis at the end of the subsequent unit Industrial and Systems Engineering Research Project 2.

title: Business and Sustainable Development
description: This unit focuses on the principles and practices of regenerative business, going beyond the concept of sustainability to explore how businesses can become forces for positive change. Students will gain an understanding of regenerative business by examining the principles, strategies, and tools used to create systems that restore and regenerate ecosystems, minimise waste, and promote positive impacts on the environment, society, and the economy. By embracing a holistic approach underpinned through systems thinking, students learn how businesses can shift their focus from growth and profit to emphasising resilience, abundance and regeneration.

title: Design and Built Environment Research Methods
description: In this unit students are introduced to the concepts, methods, tools and techniques of research and investigation in design and built environment. Identification and formulation of a research problem, a research design and methodology and a literature review are expected outcomes of this unit.

title: Foundations of Acute Care
description: This unit applies foundational pathophysiology and anatomy knowledge, communication, professional and manual handling skills to individuals presenting in an acute care clinical setting. Concepts of medical stability, post-operative protocols, and risk management are included within the context of acute trauma, gerontology, medical and surgical patients. There is a focus on person-centred management, guided by accurate assessment processes, including gathering and documenting accurate information from the patient, medical notes, charts, investigations (including X-Rays), and simple physical or physiological testing. Principles of acute care, including positioning, mobilisation with attachments, transfers, walking aids, selection and prescription of early rehab exercises, and engagement of the patient in the recovery process are considered and practiced. Common discharge issues are considered.

title: Theory of Interest
description: This unit develops the student’s understanding of the fundamental concepts of financial mathematics, and how these concepts are applied in calculating present and accumulated values for a stream of cashflows. Practical, hands-on modelling experience is developed through the use of EXCEL spreadsheets (students are assumed to have functional EXCEL skills prior to commencement of this unit).

title: Fundamentals of Heat Transfer
description: This unit introduces the fundamental heat transfer concepts and their applied relevance to thermal devices and systems in mechanical engineering. Based on energy conservation principles, the unit will enable the student to acquire analytical and modelling skills for characterising thermal systems behaviour and developing solutions to evaluate heat transfer rates in thermal processes. The unit will thus facilitate and impart thermal design capabilities in students in devices such as insulation systems, fins, and heat exchangers.

title: Rural Geographies
description: Understanding complex issues and challenges affecting rural and remote peoples and environments in Australia and exploring solutions.

title: Creative Arts Advanced Project
description: Students will develop and produce a creative arts project through this 50-credit point capstone unit. This project will be a culmination and synthesis of learned skills and methods from their chosen major. The culmination of this unit is the publication of final works to an audience in the form of exhibition, performance or screening. Learning experiences in the unit will also facilitate the development of each student’s professional portfolio and equip them with relevant knowledge and skills pertaining to the career of a creative arts practitioner.

title: Social Work with Older People
description: This unit explores how experiences of ageing are mediated by gender, age, sexuality, cultural heritage, lived experience and the human body. Students will be required to analyse current discourses about ageing, care, risk and resilience and examine their impact on shaping policy and practice. The unit will evaluate theoretical approaches to understanding experiences of ageing and integrate assessment and intervention skills for working effectively with older people.

title: Educating Adolescents: Diversity, Differentiation and Inclusion
description: This unit is designed to build upon the foundation of Child Development for Educators. The unit will specifically focus on adolescents with regard to their physical, intellectual, social and emotional development and will address factors that influence learning in the secondary school context. The unit will address contemporary theoretical and evidence based perspectives of inclusion to account for cultural, linguistic, neurological, physical, behavioural, gender, sexual and First Nation diversity. The unit will support your development of skills in meeting the diverse needs of learners through the differentiation of teaching practices.

title: Precise Engineering and Deformation Surveys
description: Directed study and research. Special topics related to advanced engineering surveying. High-precision coordination methods for industrial applications: instrumentation, calibration, observing procedures and accuracy assessment. Electronic triangulation, Laser tracking. Laser Radar. Precise Levelling. Mechanical, optical and laser alignment. Optical tooling. Plumbing and verticality measurements. Integrated analysis of deformations: deformation measurement on natural and man-made structures. Least squares adjustment, sensitivity analysis, stability analysis, statistical testing for deformation.

title: Planning Law
description: Examines law relevant to planning in Western Australia from its origins in the United Kingdom environmental planning law to the current day. The relationship between planning law and environmental law, land law and land tenure is explored.

title: Computer Aided Drawing and Engineering Modelling
description: This unit deals with the principles, rules and standards that govern the creation and interpretation of engineering drawings. Students learn and apply the concept of orthographic projection to describe three dimensional objects and concepts two dimensionally. Through the study of drawing standards, conventions and abbreviations, students develop their capacity to produce and interpret multi-view drawings that include auxiliary and sectional views. Students learn and use computer-aided drafting to produce detail and assembly drawings. Students will also be taught how to create 3D models of parts and assemblies. The 3D modelling will include 3D sectional views, extracting orthogonal views, animation and CAD/CAM integration.

title: Foundations of Forensic Science
description: Foundations of Forensic Science is a general introduction to the history, underlying principles and contemporary issues in forensic science. It will provide an overview of the forensic process from crime scene to court and the role of the forensic scientist as an expert witness. It also includes an introduction to forensic analysis and interpretation as illustrated by selected case studies. Students attend a two-hour seminar per week and a one-hour workshop fortnightly with supporting online material.

title: Advanced Japanese: Intercultural Communication
