description: This unit develops interactive skills to enable communication and conversation in Japanese. It introduces grammar, vocabulary and kanji which are equivalent to level N3 of the Japanese Language Proficiency Test. Students discuss a wide range of topics such as Japanese ambiguity and indirectness. This unit also focuses on strengthening students’ skills in intercultural communication. Authentic texts are used to analyse modern Japanese culture and society.

title: Intermediate Japanese: Extending Everyday Contexts
description: This unit has an emphasis on the interactive use of the Japanese language and further develops communicative competence in speaking, listening, reading, writing and cultural knowledge. It provides students with opportunities to apply and extend skills with a focus on practical, everyday use of the Japanese language. Students are able to compare and contrast Japanese culture with their own, and other cultures through situating the use of the Japanese language in relevant social and cultural contexts.

title: Frontiers in Immunology
description: In this unit students will explore fundamental concepts and current advances in immunology. This may include (but not be limited to) cancer immunotherapeutic strategies, how ageing impacts immune function, and vaccines. Practical work will involve designing and conducting immunology-based assays. Students will undertake a directed research component in order to apply fundamental knowledge to “real-life scenarios”.

title: Interior Architecture Studio - Workplace
description: The aim of this design studio is to explore relevant theory to inform, translate and synthesise relevant aspects of human occupation in relation to a design proposition. The focus of this unit is on contemporary spatial typologies of work that are in significant transition catalysed by new technologies. Students consider future projections of occupation to generate a design proposition and project. Design prototyping and testing are to be done through digital fabrication and simulated environments. Site analysis is a component of this unit.

title: Feature Journalism
description: Feature Journalism develops and extends the research, interviewing and writing skills acquired in earlier units. The unit explores long form storytelling and considers how different storytelling techniques such as anecdotes, description and character development work with factual and explanatory material to construct powerful journalism. Students develop their own long form ideas and produce engaging and relevant written and/or audio stories and photos for the Western Independent website. The unit explains and evaluates different forms, styles and structures that features can take. Students will analyse and learn from outstanding long form journalism from around the world, and consider the complexities of the journalist-source relationship. Feature Journalism explains the importance of, and encourages a reflective and ethical approach, to interviewing, research and writing techniques for long form journalism.

title: Art Visual Research 3
description: You will develop a self-directed visual art practice project by negotiated proposal to progress skills in the techniques and processes of various specialisations within contemporary art practice, through drawing or other media.

title: Engineering Mechanics
description: Through the activities of lectures, tutorials and practical laboratories, you will study introductory Statics, Dynamics and Fluid Mechanics. Statics considers bodies in equilibrium and this requires the application of Newton's Laws along with the understanding and manipulation of vector quantities: forces, equilibrium and couples. Free-body diagrams are applied to the analysis of simple trusses and internal actions within beams. Internal axial stress and strain are studied in relation to Hooke’s Law and material properties. The principle of compatibility is applied to statically indeterminate problems. The properties of area required for beam bending analysis are covered. Dynamics is addressed via kinematics and kinetics of particles and rigid bodies but limited to two-dimensions. Rectilinear, curvilinear and relative motion are described in x-y and n-t coordinates. Newton's second law is applied directly and also via work-energy principles and impulse-momentum principles. Kinetics of rigid bodies and rotation about a fixed axis are studied. Fluid mechanics commences with fluid statics, hydrostatic pressure and fluid forces on simple structures. Fluid dynamics is studied via Bernoulli’s equation and momentum flux. This unit is designed for those students who have passed WACE Mathematics Methods or equivalent.

title: Electrical Circuits
description: This unit first reviews the fundamentals of Direct Current (DC) circuit analysis using various methods such as Nodal Voltage and Mesh Current methods and other circuit theorems such as the superposition, Thevenin’s and Norton’s theorems. The circuit analysis is then extended to Alternating Current (AC) circuits energised by time-varying voltage or current sources. Here, the circuits with sinusoidal sources are first transformed into the frequency domain using phasor concepts and then analysed to obtain the steady-state responses using the circuit analysis methods learnt for DC circuits. Power associated with AC circuits is then covered defining the relationships to one another of instantaneous power, average (real) power, reactive power, complex power and power factor. The transient analysis of first order and second order circuits are then followed. Frequency responses of Resistive-Inductive-Capacitive (R-L-C) circuits are covered introducing the Bode plots for magnitude and phase responses. To complete the picture, Laplace transform in circuit analysis is introduced. Finally, the balanced three phase circuits and their power calculations, and the two port networks are discussed.

title: Go Practice - Internship 3
description: This unit provides students with fieldwork opportunities through internships or industry and community engagement opportunities in simulated work-based environments. Independent student learning will be supported by academics and industry advisors, and students in courses without professional work experience are encouraged to apply.

title: Introduction to Autonomous Robots
description: This unit concentrates on both theoretical foundations and practical skills of developing autonomous mobile robots. Topics covered are localisation, mapping, navigation, and control of mobile robots. Students will gain the deep understanding and programme skills of essential algorithms for autonomous robots, through developing the software for a mobile robot operating in both a high-fidelity simulation environment and in a real-world lab environment.

title: Privacy and Cyber Security: Health Data Governance
description: This unit will introduce students to health data governance, including relevant legislation and the importance of cyber security in keeping health data safe. Students will explore contemporary concerns about the collection, linkage, storage and use of health data including transparency, informed consent, confidentiality, third party access and the application of artificial intelligence. They will also engage with issues of data privacy and protection which encompasses cyber security and cyber risk management.

title: Food Chemistry
description: In this unit you will learn about how the various food components such as starch protein and fat influence the properties in the food products in which they reside.

title: Advanced Contract Law
description: The unit covers the discharge of contracts, whether by performance, agreement, frustration, or termination; contractual remedies, including damages, equitable remedies, and restitutionary forms of remedy; and invalidating factors, including misrepresentation, mistake, duress, undue Influence, unconscionability and illegality.

title: International Experience 6
description: n/a

title: Primary Professional Experience 3: Advanced Classroom Skills
description: This is the third in the suite of professional experience units that includes a practical component (20 days of placement in a school). The unit will allow you to extend your developing knowledge and skills in the classroom by considering advanced assessment practices, managing challenging behaviour and extending existing classroom skills, both through a theoretical and a practical lens. The professional experience practical assessment assesses your ability to further refine your knowledge and skills required for working in classrooms. All required clearances to work with children must be obtained and valid, and all other preparation requirements met. All assessment components must be passed in order to pass the unit.

title: Space Exploration: Science, Technology and Industry
description: Space has captured the human imagination for millennia, from the earliest use of stars for navigation through to planning to put the first human on Mars. This unit introduces the underlying concepts of space exploration, and the scientific, technical and social drivers of the space industry. Students will explore the solar system from the Sun, terrestrial and outer planets and moons, asteroids, comets, and beyond. We will cover the history of human and robotic space exploration, including the scientific objectives, payload considerations and earth and space-based approaches. We explore relationship between science, technology and industry, looking at how space science leads to technical advancements that spin out into innovations across a range of sectors on Earth. The unit supports students in understanding how space exploration exists in a social context, including economic factors and political and cultural drivers. The ethics of space exploration will be considered, including multi-cultural and Indigenous perceptions of and cultural connections to the night sky, and the need for responsible exploration, embedding sustainability principles.

title: Law, Ethics and Mental Health
description: An examination of general legal principles with reference to the Mental Health Act of WA in relation to Indigenous rights and culturally responsible mental health care delivery. Students will examine: ethical practice in relation to ways of working in an Indigenous context as part of a multidisciplinary healthcare team; and, ethical and professional practice in the context of human rights, social justice and equity as part of comprehensive mental healthcare delivery.

title: Assistive Technology & Environmental Design for Occupational Therapy
description: Occupational therapy role of assessment, prescription, technology selection and advocacy in relation to environmental design and assistive technology. Contemporary models and frameworks for matching consumer needs with assistive technology and environmental designs. Standards, risk and regulation applied to environmental design and assistive technology. Accessing funding for assistive technology and environmental design and modification.

title: Hydrogen Energy
description: The Hydrogen Energy unit offers a comprehensive examination of hydrogen's role in sustainable energy transition aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goals. The unit begins with an introduction to hydrogen energy and its role in sustainable development, including an overview of global energy demands, the hydrogen cycle, and comparative analysis with other energy sources. It covers the thermodynamics and physical properties of hydrogen, addressing safety, energy content, and innovative materials for handling hydrogen. Hydrogen production technologies are explored in depth, including electrolysis, photolytic water splitting, biological methods, steam methane reforming, and emerging technologies. Students will evaluate the economic and environmental aspects of these technologies, along with advancements in modular and decentralized production. The unit also delves into storage, transportation methods, and the fundamentals of hydrogen liquefaction.

title: Integrated Systems Anatomy and Physiology
description: An integrated approach to the study of body systems correlating structure and function of the musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, respiratory, digestive, urinary and reproductive systems together with their endocrine and neural control. Students will investigate the interaction of these systems in normal body functioning and in selected altered body states.

title: Transitional Nursing Practice
description: This unit consolidates prior learning across the curricula as the student transitions to the role of a Registered Nurse. Comprehensive care of the unconscious patient and management of a deteriorating patient are addressed along with medication and pharmacology knowledge. The consolidation and integration of professional development culminates in a continuing portfolio for professional practice as an RN.

title: Devising Fundamentals
description: This unit introduces both practical and theoretical approaches to understanding and creating contemporary theatre specifically focussing on devising. Students will incorporate practical processes and theoretical material to gain a critical understanding of devising techniques and processes and will apply them to the rehearsal and presentation of an original devised work. Attending performances at the Hayman Theatre will be central to the experience of this unit. Students will apply the processes and skills of contemporary theatre practitioners to the rehearsal and presentation of an original devised work. They will extend their performance practice through active participation in the Hayman Theatre Company performance season and will attend a variety of performance pieces. They will develop a critical mind enabling them to offer sophisticated critique and analysis of their own and a range of different theatre-making processes.

title: Foundations of Anatomical Pathology
description: This unit covers the histology and cytology of the body systems. Students will study the principles and applications of histological and cytological methods for the investigation of disorders of health. Students will be introduced to the preparation and microscopic interpretation of selected tissues and fluids using histological and cytological methods.

title: Computational Fluid Dynamics and Heat Transfer
description: This unit introduces a range of numerical methods widely employed for thermo-fluids engineering, such as the Finite Difference Method and Finite Volume Method. From the fundamental algebraic concepts to applied case studies, the unit will enable students to develop an understanding of the challenges of numerical techniques and to acquire analytical and modelling skills to generate relevant numerical solutions. Through hands-on activities, students will gain engineering capabilities to assess modelling strategies, design effective computational simulations and characterise common situations encountered in the fields of fluid mechanics and heat transfer.

title: Engineering Noise Control
description: This unit provides an introduction to acoustics and the practice of engineering noise control. There is an increasing need for engineers to improve the management of noise as we become more aware of the impact of noise in our environment. The awareness of this impact is also reflected in the regulatory requirements, which are becoming progressively more stringent. Hence, minimizing the impact of noise on our global acoustic soundscape is becoming increasingly important in a more populated world. This unit is intended for future engineers involved in the design of equipment, processes and infrastructure so as to provide a solid understanding of the practice of engineering noise management. Practical approaches to engineering noise management are included, considering noise management at the source, along the transmission path and at the receiver.

title: Public International Law
description: The unit explores the basic principles and practices of public international law. The unit provides a preliminary understanding of how international law shapes global governance and is also shaped by the ideas and institutions of global governance. It will focus on the architecture of international law including its sources and power. It will examine a range of concepts including states and non-state entities, sovereignty, jurisdiction, responsibility, the UN and peaceful settlement of disputes. The unit will address some areas of international law in action including modern warfare and humanitarianism.

title: Psychosocial Care for Health Complexity
description: Psychosocial factors influencing individual and family responses to complex health conditions. Students develop an advanced understanding of sociocultural factors influencing social support and structure and function of the individual and family with critically unstable health.. Person-centred psychosocial interventions to empower wellbeing and adaptive responses to complex health concerns. Communication strategies and interventions applied by paramedics or nurses to empower well-being. Transdisciplinary communication in complex health care settings.

title: Paramedicine Honours Dissertation
description: A continuation of attributes learnt from Paramedicine Honours Preparation, students will develop competencies in the research process and interpretation of data from their research project. Students will develop skills in: oral presentations communicating the results and significance of their research; preparing a research article and dissertation; as well as responding to examiners’ comments.

title: Geology Mapping Project
description: A field camp of approximately two weeks duration, the location of which varies from year to year. Students undertake independent mapping of an assigned area, and receive advanced training in structural and lithological mapping techniques and in the compilation of a geological map and report.

title: Business and Law International Experience 3
description: International mobility experience for undergraduate students.

title: Introductory Physiotherapy Practice
description: In this unit students will be introduced to the scope and limits of physiotherapy and the notion of professional and ethical practice. They will explore and practice the development of a therapeutic alliance through safe person-centred therapeutic touch and respectful communication. There will be a strong focus on developing empathetic communication skills, in particular the skill of listening with understanding. The concepts of biopsychosocial frameworks of care will be introduced. Students will be introduced to clinical reasoning as a problem-solving process, applying simple assessment and management strategies. Blended learning (online and face to face) and practical classes will be based around several vignettes of patients followed through their hospital stay. This will introduce students to the scope of movement problems and how to apply effective therapeutic touch and manual strategies to assist functional movement recovery. Students will also start to engage in reflective practice, providing self and peer feedback in order to build agency in learning.

title: Contemporary and Comparative Social Policy
description: In this unit students will engage with social policy as it relates to social work practice. This unit encompasses the key characteristics of social policy, including core concepts and terminology. Students will analyse the form, content and direction of social policy debates and arenas in Australia and internationally.

title: Drone Mapping & Applications
description: This unit is an introduction into mapping and applications using drones and associated technologies. The fundamentals of field data capture, mapping and photogrammetry will be introduced including pre-fieldtrip planning of drone flights based on best practice and job specifications, in-field data capture, basics of positioning, photogrammetric workflows, processing of images, corrections, geo-referencing and the production of point clouds, 3D models, Digital Surface Models (DSM), Digital Terrain Models (DTM) and ortho-images. Further, the post-processing of photogrammetric outputs including data analytics, classification and geo-visualisation will be introduced. Application in multiple disciplines including Agriculture/Ecology/Health, Built Environment as well as Mining/Geology/Geophysics will be discussed. The theory learned in the lectures is applied during practical exercises.

title: Financial Engineering 2
description: The aim of this unit is to build on the principles of financial economics for application in finance and investments, with a particular emphasis on stochastic calculus and its use in valuing options. Practical, hands-on modelling experience is developed through the use of EXCEL spreadsheets (students are assumed to have functional EXCEL skills prior to commencement of this unit).

title: Electromagnetics and Potential Methods
description: Electromagnetic and potential field methods are used to reveal the interior of our earth and other celestial bodies from surface to hundreds of kilometres depth below surface. This unit will span theory, acquisition, processing and interpretation of electrical, radar, time domain electromagnetic, frequency domain electromagnetic, gravity and magnetic methods. Students will develop the specific skills set required to apply these methods for large scale industry, environmental, groundwater, strategic minerals discovery, environmental or energy related applications

title: Governance for Planning
description: Governance in Australia - Federal, State and Local Government. The location of planning activity within the spheres of government. Introduction to planning and related law and its interpretation in planning and development practice.

title: Taxation of Business Structures
description: Taxpayers in business often have a choice to which business entity they will use to run their business operations through, there are several choices available to them including sole trader, partnerships, trusts and companies and with all of them come different tax issues and decisions that need to be made. You will be exposed into looking at complex taxation matters surrounding these entities such as Division 7A and the recently debated Sec 100A which has been contentious, as well as Small Business Concessions and Capital Gains Tax Concessions which all tax professional must have an understanding of. Cryptocurrency and crowd funding are new forms of financing businesses and we look at the tax consequences associated with them along with more traditional forms of financing, we use an expert tax professional in the area of crypto to help you with these concepts. You will also have a mentor from a Big 4 practice to work with in relation to your business project in this course. Tax avoidance and evasion are the dark side to taxation and participation in them can lead to large fines and incarceration so we will spend some time looking at the laws surrounding the anti- avoidance legislation and examine some high profile cases that have seen the ATO and taxpayers in battle. Business structuring and ensuring taxpayers are abiding by the rules is a large part of all tax professionals work whether in a commerce role or a law role ... also remember that a career within the government is also available

title: Foundations of International Relations
description: This unit serves as a foundational introduction to the academic study of International Relations (IR) and is designed to serve School common curriculum objectives for global studies more broadly. Students will leave the unit with a more sophisticated understanding of the history and function of the modern international system and will be prepared for subsequent specialist units in the IR major. Topics include an introduction to the main theoretical and methodological approaches, the use of coercion and cooperation in interstate relations, foreign policy-making and diplomacy, forms of international order, global governance, and international law.

title: Teaching Health Education in Primary Schools
description: This unit introduces students to primary health education in the contemporary Australian primary school curriculum, where emphasis is on developing children’s health literacies within safe and lifelong learning frameworks so they are able to flourish as healthy and active citizens. With attention to diversity and social justice, children’s rights to develop health literacies within their personal, physical and socio-cultural contexts are explored, and relevant teaching approaches identified. Given the emphasis on evidence-based curriculum design, students will investigate the research that underpins the contemporary Health Education curriculum rationale and focus.The unit reviews ongoing, developmentally appropriate and explicit teaching about health, where children participate in developmentally appropriate learning activities to develop the knowledge, skills, dispositions and understandings so they can be empowered to make healthy choices for the wellbeing of themselves and others. Given the importance of health literacy skills in the primary years, effective pedagogies for teaching health content are addressed. Opportunities to integrate health education with physical education and other curriculum areas will also be explored in this unit. The unit will also address the need for inclusivity in Health Education and develop in students, practical ways of approaching inclusivity in planning and implementation of the curriculum, with focus on a strength-based approach.

title: Business Process Management
description: This unit introduces the principles of business process management required for a digital age. A new generation of techniques for the identification, modelling, discovery and analysis techniques are systematically developed for process aware information systems. Implementation issues with executable models suitable for a context aware environment and the requirements for monitoring and governance are also covered as risks of modelling.

title: International Experience 5
description: n/a

title: Textual Futures
description: This unit explores different textual representations of the future in terms of the questions they raise about the world today. From science fiction and dystopian classics, through futurology and trends forecasting, to climate change narratives and extinction studies, students will engage with a variety of texts and discourses engaging in the question of the future. The unit will develop skills in analysing the relationships between language, genre and contexts, and explore how textual choices position audiences for particular purposes, shaping attitudes, values and perspectives on contemporary social, cultural and political trends.

title: Global Health Perspectives
description: This unit examines global health issues, including biological, social and environmental impacts. It looks at health inequities from a global perspective, as well as global initiatives to improve access to healthcare. It will also explore current global public health perspectives in Indigenous health, including health promotion initiatives to improve global health.

title: Dynamic Earth
description: This unit is an introduction to Geology, the science studying processes of Earth and planetary bodies and will illustrate various degree of interaction between the atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere and those of the geosphere. From workshops, lectures, assignments and hands on experiences, you will learn the language of the Earth sciences, will be shown how Earth scientists utilize scientific principles to gain knowledge of the Earth and be introduced to current theories of the origin, composition and structure of Planet Earth, and the nature of internal and external planetary processes. In laboratory and field classes, you will develop practical skills in data interpretation, geological communication and critical thinking a through group activities around geological data, mineral and rocks.

title: Legal Research and Writing
description: This unit introduces students to specifically legal research goals, methodologies and databases which are used to find, update and critically analyse the primary and secondary sources of law used in a problem solving context. Students will practice law specific forms of effective written communication including client files, memoranda of advice, solicitor's letters and written instructions. Students are also introduced to legal referencing standards.

title: Human Genetic Disease
description: In this unit students will understand the molecular basis for Human genetic diseases and traits. This will include an understanding of both Mendelian and non Mendelian genetic diseases, complex diseases, diseases caused by epigenetic changes, risk and environmental factors affecting human disease progression and the methods of interpreting variants as a key member of a multidisciplinary team.

title: A Global History of the Cold War
description: This unit deals with the study of the Cold War from a global perspective, spanning the end of the Second World War in 1945 to the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991. It examines the ideological, political, social, economic and cultural dimensions of the Cold War across the world. By studying this unit, students develop the ability to critically analyse how historians and historical actors have interpreted and responded to the Cold War and its effects over time. By exploring the Cold War as a global phenomenon, playing out in Asia, Latin America, the Pacific, Africa as well as Europe and Australia, students will gain insights into recent developments in historical writing and research on this topic. Finally, the unit discusses the Cold War’s legacies on global politics today.

title: Advanced Strength of Materials
description: The first part of this unit will introduce the concept of metal fatigue using industry examples and explain underlying reasons for the phenomenon. Following this, metal fatigue will be analysed for the following situations: (i) ideal specimens, (ii) non-ideal specimens without a stress raiser, (iii) non-ideal specimens with a stress raiser, (iv) complex loading spectra, (v) superposition of mean and alternating stresses, (vi) superposition of multiple loading types and (vii) linear elastic fracture mechanics, crack growth, stress intensity and fracture toughness. The second part of the unit will investigate energy methods for the deflection of components, Euler buckling of columns and thick cylinder theory and its applications. Rotating rings, discs and shafts will also be considered.

title: Medicine 4 Rural
description: This unit is based on six themes - professional, leader, advocate, clinician, educator, and scholar. Teaching in all these themes is provided within the rural clinical attachments and related teaching in Year 4 of the B-MBBS course. This consists of student attachments to rural medical practitioners and includes exposure to, and practice in, a variety of clinical disciplines including, but not restricted to, surgery, psychiatry, internal medicine, general practice, ophthalmology, paediatrics and child health, and women's and infants' health. Students undertake clinical care of patients under the supervision of experienced clinicians in a real rural clinical environment, including ward rounds, operating theatre, outpatient clinics, emergency department attachments, community practices, and other clinical encounters. Students engage in small group learning sessions to discuss evidence-based practice in related clinical disciplines in rural health contexts. Students are expected to apply the knowledge, skills, and professional attitudes gained in a rural context. Specifically, they will develop skills in diagnosis and management of common clinical problems; skills related to patient interaction, physical examinations and performing procedures in various clinical disciplines will be developed.Communication and clinical skills learned in previous years are extended further and applied within the rural clinical setting. Skills related to patient interaction, physical examinations and performing procedures in various clinical disciplines will be developed.

title: Korean Advanced 6
description: This is an advanced level unit in Korean, designed to extend students’ ability to demonstrate advanced-level written and oral composition skills through interactive and task-based approaches established in KORE3000. This unit is primarily taught in the Korean language to maximise students’ opportunities to practise advanced level communication skills. This unit utilises authentic Korean texts ranging from news articles to popular culture texts, and introduces students to basic translation strategies for working with previously unseen texts. Students will achieve mid- to upper advanced level conversation and writing skills through engaging in interactive class discussions and practising in real-life communicative situations such as workplace interactions and job interviews. It will also include the development of research and debating skills in Korean.On successful completion of Korean 5 and 6, students will reach a level of competency equivalent to the National Institute of Korean Language’s Standard Curriculum for Korean Language upper 3/lower Level 4 on the TOPIK (Test of Proficiency in Korean) scale of proficiency.

title: Psychological Science Correlational Methods
description: Correlational designs in psychological research, with a focus on the development and analysis of questionnaires and the psychometric properties of psychological measures.

title: Computer Simulation
description: This unit introduces the foundation of simulation techniques and their applications in a chosen area. The unit introduces the theoretical foundation of simulation with a focus on its scope and limitation. Several tools and techniques for designing and implementing simulation procedures on various computing platforms will also be introduced. Students will then have the opportunity to choose an area of focus where they can apply the principles of simulation on solving discipline specific problems.

title: Principles and Practice of Paediatrics
description: In this unit, students will develop the skills to enhance the occupational performance and participation of children and adolescents with developmental delay and disability using occupation-based and family-centred practice. Students will utilise their clinical reasoning skills to implement assessments and develop intervention plans within the frameworks of the International Classification of Functioning (ICF) and the Person Environment Occupation (PEO) model. This unit teaches units skills in professional documentation and report writing, communication skills, assessment and intervention.

title: Advanced Topics in Physics and Astronomy 2
description: This unit is designed as an adjunct to the Honours Research Dissertation. Students will further develop their research, technical, professional and communication skills, and specialised knowledge through the exploration of advanced concepts in the field of Physics and Astronomy.

title: Forensic Trace Evidence
description: This unit provides students with an opportunity to develop their knowledge of the practice of forensic science with particular reference to trace evidence analysis. The forensic process, will be examined in detail through a study of the principles and applications of trace evidence analysis including sampling of evidential material and interpretation of trace evidence. Issues concerning quality management and implications for the practice of forensic science in an international context will also be addressed.

title: Occupational Therapy Fieldwork 2
description: Students undertake practicum experience that meets the requirements of the World Federation of Occupational Therapists. Practicum experiences integrates occupational therapy theoretical frameworks, development of essential clinical and ethical reasoning, demonstration of essential skills in planning, assessment, intervention, communication, documentation and management functions.

title: Proficient Japanese: Language Variation
description: This unit introduces students to an advanced level of Japanese, which is equivalent to N2 of the Japanese Language Proficiency Test. Students learn to discuss a wide range of topics as well as substantially increase their knowledge of vocabulary and kanji. The use of online resources provides students with enriched opportunities to use Japanese.

title: Medical Radiation Instrumentation 3
description: Physical factors of digital imaging systems that affect quality of medical images will be discussed. Various techniques to improve the digital medical image quality such as image post-processing will be explored, with opportunities for practical experience in computer laboratories. Technological features and issues of health information systems (Hospital Information System [HIS], Radiology Information System [RIS] and Picture Archiving and Communication Systems [PACS] including their components, workflow, communication standards - Health Level 7 [HL7] and Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine [DICOM], and image / data security) in relation to digital radiographic practice will be discussed. Solutions to address the issues of these systems including their current and future development will be analysed.

title: Health and Safety Management
description: This unit extensively covers the systems approach in the management of occupational health and safety. It aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the significance of effective health and safety management in fostering sustainable employment and driving economic growth in modern workplaces. Additionally, it explores the influence of government and public policy in shaping health and safety practices.

title: Advanced Refrigeration System Design
description: In this unit, students will build on the fundamental system theory covered in the pre-requisite unit, covering methods of improving system efficiency and practical aspects of refrigeration plant design. Students will learn about all aspects of theoretical refrigeration system design, including system types, load calculations, component selection, piping systems and refrigerants, with a view to minimising energy consumption and environmental footprint. In addition, practical system considerations outlining operating and maintenance requirements not directly affecting theoretical performance, will be integrated into the overall system design and analysis.

title: Indigenous Australian Community Development Strategies and Practices
description: Analysis of local and national socio-political contexts to identify appropriate Indigenous community development strategies. Apply the Indigenous Terms of Reference and Community Development Principles frameworks to determine "the goodness of fit" of the evaluation research project. Students will demonstrate the use of culturally appropriate methods to engage Indigenous community members in evaluation processes, and apply research principles through observational and participatory fieldwork practices. Engagement with development groups will enable peer review of ways of working.

title: Ethical Decision-Making and Leadership
description: This unit provides students with an understanding of good national leadership as something that is both ethical and competent. It will draw on the fields of normative and applied ethics, philosophy, professional ethics, management theory, and classical thinking about the nature of well exercised authority. A particular emphasis is placed on political and military leadership and the modern moral dilemmas faced by statespersons. It examines issues such as the roots of ethical leadership, authenticity and virtue, notions of the common good, the importance of public values and the private morality of leaders.

title: Mechanical Design for Materials Handling
description: This unit is focused on concepts and practices of designing mechanical components and systems for handling materials. It covers principles of materials handling and materials characterisation and testing, followed by designing chutes, conveyors, feeders and dischargers, and integrating various equipment into a system. Emphasis is also placed on dust control, wall loads, quaking and stockpile design. Handling of bulk solids and relevant equipment design is presented based on problems provided by industry.

title: Start Design Thinking
description: This unit allows students to develop fundamental knowledge of design thinking processes and approaches to solving problems. Through an exploration of a range of introductory research methods relevant to the disciplines of Design, students will approach design problems in an organised and creative way. Design thinking and doing research methods focus on understanding human needs through observation, interviews and a number of other essential design research methods leading to the analysis (and in some cases re-definition) of a design problem. Applied to practical design problems, learners work both individually and in teams.

title: Health Care Systems in Australia
description: This unit is designed to provide you with a thorough understanding of health care systems through the application of systems theory. This theory views the health care system as a transformation process of inputs to outputs situated within an environment. Major areas addressed in the unit include financing, service provision, government role and responsibility as well as primary health care and vulnerable groups in the system. These areas are considered within the Australian health care system, and in comparison with other systems. The unit aims to be reflective and thought provoking, and focuses on promoting lifelong learning in the areas of health care provision, policy and management.

title: Changemakers Innovation Lab
description: Changemakers Innovation Lab gives you the opportunity to develop 21st century innovation skills, integrate Indigenous Knowledge Systems* and apply your own disciplinary background to develop practical solutions for the world's most complex environmental, social and governance (ESG) sustainability challenges. Whatever your area of study, you will learn the necessary changemaker skills for effectively advocating, collaborating, and co-creating regenerative strategies and solutions with regional, rural, and remote communities and industries. *Please note that the teaching team is made up of Indigenous and non-Indigenous staff. All content has been developed in consultation with Indigenous leaders and knowledge holders.

title: Primary Physical Education: Curriculum & Assessment
description: This unit introduces students to physical education curriculum and assessment practices in the contemporary Australian primary school curriculum, where emphasis is on developing children’s physical literacies within safe and lifelong learning frameworks so they are able to flourish as healthy and active citizens. With attention to diversity and social justice, children’s rights to develop physical literacies within their personal, physical and socio-cultural contexts are explored, and relevant teaching and assessment approaches identified. Given the emphasis on evidence-based curriculum design and assessment practices, students will investigate the research that underpins the contemporary curriculum rationale and focus.The unit reviews ongoing, developmentally appropriate curriculum and assessment practices relating to health and movement, where children participate safely to develop the knowledge, skills, dispositions and understandings to make healthy and active choices for the wellbeing of themselves and others. In this regard, the importance of physical skills development in the primary years is addressed through in-depth study of theories and practices that inform developmentally appropriate PE curriculum design and sound assessment practices. The unit will also address the need for inclusivity in Physical Education curriculum and assessment as well as develop in students, practical ways of approaching inclusivity in planning and implementation of the curriculum, including management and safety issues.

title: Curriculum and Instruction Lower Secondary: Mathematics
description: This unit is designed to prepare pre-service teachers in Lower Secondary Mathematics. The focus of the unit is on curriculum planning, teaching strategies, evaluation, resources, the demonstration of positive impact on student learning and research relating to Lower Secondary Mathematics. Teaching and learning practices to support and challenge a diverse student cohort are explored.

title: Mental Health 1
description: This unit is designed to introduce students to knowledge, skills and attitudes related to mental health and wellbeing in the context of primary health care. The social determinants of mental health, resilience and wellbeing and mental health promotion and early intervention will be explored and discussed. Using an evidence-based approach, the unit will focus on developing an understanding of the prevalence of mental health issues in the community, the connection between physical and psychosocial wellbeing, the impact of co-occurring substance use and eating disorders and the importance of cultural considerations. The specific mental health needs of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, people from culturally and linguistically diverse (CALD) backgrounds, and LGBTI (lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex) populations will be explored.

title: Special Topics in Law (International)
description: This unit will focus on a specialised area of law, which will vary from year to year. The specific content that will be covered will depend upon the subject of the special topic(s) and the academic undertaking the teaching of the unit. The unit content will involve an international and/or comparative component, which will also be embedded in one or more of the unit’s assessment tasks. Students will be required to undertake intensive reading and research on the specialised topic(s) to develop an in-depth knowledge of the unit content. Students will also develop an appreciation for international and/or comparative perspectives (as they relate to the subject of the special topic(s)), together with critical thinking and (both written and oral) communication skills.

title: Survey Computations
description: Basic and fundamental mathematics for Surveying. Significant figures, precision and accuracy. Plane triangle solutions. Radiation, intersection and resection on the plane. Traverse computations and the Bowditch adjustment. Areas of rectilinear figures. Basic survey computations using plane coordinates - forward and reverse geodetic problems on the plane. Missing elements. Road intersections. Simple subdivision calculations. Curves - simple, compound and reverse.

title: Medicine 2
description: This unit aims to provide knowledge of the structure, function and development of systems of a normal human body at all levels of organisation, from molecular and cellular to organ systems and the total individual, and the changes that occur as a result of disease, injury and abnormal development. The systems covered in this unit will include cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, reproductive and endocrine systems. The major focus is on the foundations of biomedical science. Students will locate, critically appraise, interpret and apply biomedical information in clinical contexts. Students will also learn how to communicate with patients, some basic clinical procedures, and how to conduct physical examinations in clinical practice.The unit also includes patterns of behaviour through the human life cycle and draws on aspects of the physical and social environment, and behaviour at individual and group levels affecting the incidence of, and response to disease in the community. This unit also develops knowledge and understanding of concepts that underpin socially responsible health professional practice and public health, and will include developing deeper understandings about ethics, law, and professionalism, and concepts of cultural safety for Indigenous people, in relation to medicine.

title: Psychology of Learning
description: The major areas of learning such as classical and operant conditioning, and complex learning. Motivation for behaviour. Animal and human models of learning and motivation, and the application of these to areas such as therapy, intervention, education and parenting.

title: Creative Literacies
description: This unit is one of a set of three undergraduate option units to prepare Initial Teacher Educators (ITE) to specialise in teaching literacy and English. This unit emphasises the power of creativity to support adventurous literacies and the ways in which a teacher can use big ideas to inspire and engage children. ITE will explore, reflect critically and develop resources about new directions in literacies and envisage what is possible in today’s classroom and how to inspire and enhance teaching of creative literacies.

title: Clothing in Context -The Business of Fashion
description: Driven by aesthetics and visual communication, fashion design practice within the context of fashion business emphasises the importance of creative production, marketing, and new modes of fashion presentation.

title: Secondary Professional Teaching Practice 2
description: This unit is the second in a sequence of four professional teaching practice focused units. This unit will develop your ability to critically analyse key education theories, concepts, and skills to develop your professional teaching praxis. Within this unit, there are three modules. The first module will further examine evidence based learning and teaching models, philosophies, processes and government policies for inclusive learning design and assessment. The second module explores strength-based strategies to support students' wellbeing within a safe learning environment. The third module will continue to address professional conduct behaviours, and effective interpersonal and communication strategies focusing on communicating with students as well as colleagues and parents/caregivers. This unit is designed to provide an ongoing theoretical and practical foundation of essential skills you will need to demonstrate on your second school-based professional experience placement.

title: Practice of Evaluation in Indigenous Community Program Context
description: This unit focuses on connecting theory to evaluation practice. Students will be able to explore how evaluation is linked to the Indigenous program context and research utilising ethical research values, principles and practices. They will also learn about different evaluation research methods, planning, conducting data collection, analysis and managing evaluations. Students will have opportunities to learn about and assess quality evaluation reporting.

title: Introduction to Applied Statistics
description: This unit covers fundamental (bio)statistical methods and their application to real data using the R statistical software. Topics include study design, summarising and presenting data, basic statistical hypothesis tests and commonly used statistical models (linear, logistic and survival). The emphasis is on developing an understanding of the use and interpretation of basic methods as applied to health and biomedical research, rather than formal theory.

title: Advanced Japanese: Language Variation
description: This unit strengthens students’ ability to engage in authentic communication in formal settings such as interviews for job hunting. Students gain real life experience in writing job applications. Tutorials include comprehensive practice in using honorifics. Reading materials are extracted from newspaper reports and magazine articles which are at levels N2 and N3 of the Japanese Language Proficiency Test.

title: Planning Graphics and Design
description: A practical introduction to graphic presentation and design.  Learning design principles for preparing public space designs and town centre plans.

title: Copywriting for Design and Advertising
description: An introduction to the principles of Copywriting as well as Copywriting processes and methods. Through a series of practical exercises, students will gain a working knowledge of Copywriting structure, style and format in a variety of persuasive writing contexts.

title: Integrated Management of Pain Disorders
description: This unit involves understanding pain experiences across the lifespan, across all practice specialties, and inter-professional healthcare settings. Contemporary, evidence-informed knowledge about the multidimensional and individual variability of factors that contribute to each person’s pain experience will be developed. Clinical vignettes of acute and persistent pain will be used to strengthen knowledge transfer, to help make sense of pain. Clinical assessment will be developed in a pain disorders context, further developing empathetic person-centred communication and use of validated screening tools contextualised to contemporary biopsychosocial frameworks. Care planning will focus on skills to interpret the unique biological, psychological, social, and cultural factors that can influence each individual’s pain experience and translation of this understanding into supported self-management. Shared decision-making will form a fundamental principle to guide holistic, ethical, culturally-appropriate high-value care.

title: Clinical Education for Practice
description: The Clinical Education unit explores models of learning and teaching in relation to clinical supervision, peer teaching, patient education and interprofessional learning in a variety of health settings. Evidence-based learning and teaching is applied alongside evidence-based clinical practice and knowledge to optimise health outcomes

title: Epidemiology - From Principles to Practice
description: Evolution of epidemiology. Dynamic interaction between agent, host, and environment. Concepts of health and disease. The natural history of disease. Estimating health and disease in populations. Demography. Concepts of risk factors and causes. Validity and reliability of data. Epidemiological study designs, their strengths and limitations, inference and causation, bias and confounding, issues of reliability and validity, properties of rates and ratios, age standardisation procedures and application of epidemiological knowledge, principles and techniques to investigate public health issues.

title: Survival Models & Analysis
description: This unit will cover survival models, lifetime distributions, statistical models of transfer between multiple states, binomial and Poisson models of mortality, maximum likelihood estimation of transition intensities, age-specific transition intensities, statistical tests, standard life tables, and graduation of crude estimates.

title: Cyber Crime and Security Enhanced Programming
description: This unit examines common threats to computer systems ranging from organised attacks to viruses and malware. It provides students with the knowledge required to identify, analyse and respond to these threats and vulnerabilities affecting enterprise networks. The unit also develops detailed knowledge of computer forensics including investigative approaches and tools used in both Linux/Windows environments. Students explore techniques used in large-scale and coordinated network attacks and evaluate methods for mitigating and responding to such attacks. The unit further examines the foundations of viruses and malware including typical security weaknesses exploited by malicious software and web-based attacks. In the final component of the unit, students study in detail the tools available on Windows and Unix-based systems for detecting and trace hacking and intrusion activities.

title: Introduction to Human Systems and Pathophysiology
description: This unit introduces students to human systems, their inter-relationships, and their role in maintaining homeostasis and health. The impact of on an individual’s health, function and life quality of injury, dysfunction, stress, or ageing in a system is explored, with reference to an individual’s experience, social determinants and environment (national and international) within a biopsychosocial framework. Key physiological and pathophysiological processes which underpin common diseases and disorders managed by physiotherapists across the lifespan will be explored.

title: Paramedicine Honours Preparation
description: Fundamental competencies to enable students to develop an appreciation of the ethics and principles of research and research design; critically appraise and interpret scientific literature; as well as develop skills in planning and writing a research proposal.

title: Employment and Environment Law
description: This unit will explore the framework, functions and practices of occupational health and safety (OHS), environmental, industrial relations (IR) and employment law, and how these impact on occupational   health and safety practices in the workplace. The unit will review the effects each discipline has on achieving organisational goals and objectives in relation to occupational health and safety.

title: Business Information Systems Capstone Project
description: This unit assists students in making the transition to professional practice as an information systems professional. Students will demonstrate the application of information systems methods, tools, and techniques to a relevant industry-based project of significant scope. Students will work collaboratively to understand and document stakeholder requirements, implement and test a technical solution to address a real-world business problem, and manage project risks and ethical considerations. Depending on the project brief, students may demonstrate skills in systems analysis, programming, database design and management, accessibility, and addressing human factors. The project will also involve verifying and validating the solution through acceptance testing, as well as developing strategies for ongoing support and change management. Professional conduct, including teamwork, communication, technical competence, and project management skills, is assessed throughout the project.

title: Physics Project 1
description: This unit is designed to increase students' understanding and skills in physics research. The specific scientific project objectives are determined by the student and supervisor. PHYS3003 emphasizes literature searches and reviews of other work with reference to students' preliminary research, experimental planning and acquisition of experimental, analytical and computational requirements to perform the research.

title: Reading Gender
description: This unit examines key concepts, approaches and debates in the study of gender and sexuality, with a focus on analysing the representation of gender and sexuality in a range of literary and cultural texts. Recent theoretical developments are explored in the context of pioneering work in second- and third-wave feminism, psychoanalysis and queer theory. The unit’s focus on developing critical reading skills and strategies will give students the tools to interpret, evaluate and challenge the reproduction of different gender and sexuality value systems in a range of literary and cultural texts.

title: Business Analytics Techniques
description: This unit focuses on the use of organisational data to support business decision making. Students will develop skills in planning and implementing business analytics environments, including data gathering and exploration, creation of analytics-ready datasets, and visualisation and presentation of analyses using industry standard software and methods.

title: Photography Project
description: In this unit, students will identify theoretical concepts and develop critical skills that are used to frame and inform imaginative photographic work. Students will implement and experiment with research strategies that contribute to innovative images in response to both set and self-generated projects. Weekly content, discussions and class assignments will significantly challenge students to extend their levels of thinking and advance creative practice.

title: Basin Dynamics
description: Sedimentary basins record the deformation of the lithosphere.  Their structural and stratigraphic architecture reflects the sedimentary response to their tectonic setting, the geodynamic processes responsible for their formation, their structural evolution and changes in climate and sea level.  However, as sedimentary basins are a result of subsidence and sediment accumulation, most of their record occurs in the sub-surface.  In this unit, we learn to interpret the main sources of subsurface information (core data, well log data, seismic data) and we will apply that to understanding the formation of sedimentary basins in rifts, passive margins, compressional, strike-slip and intra-cratonic settings.  Sedimentary basins also contain important resources, so we will consider how our understanding of basin evolution can help us evaluate potential energy reserves (hydrocarbons, natural hydrogen) and storage (underground hydrogen storage, gas storage, carbon capture and storage).

title: Women's Reproductive Health
description: This unit centres on women’s reproductive health issues and is focused on the impacts of social determinants of health on women’s well-being and health outcomes. Students explore the impact of infertility and sub-fertility and the options of care available. Women preparing for a pregnancy and midwifery management of early pregnancy are considered. Common pathologies, such as endometriosis, PCOS and cancers are investigated. The final postnatal 6 week examination of mother and baby midwife is appraised. Midwifery practice is consolidated with student continuation of CCE women and clinical placement so that all course and ANMAC requirements are met.

title: Graphic Design Studio
description: This is a digital studio based unit in which students undertake a series of practical projects relevant to graphic design. Students are expected to complete design briefs within the designated class time, with a focus on creating technically sound and relevant design solutions. Projects are designed to reflect real-world practices, with the aim of preparing students for industry conditions.

title: Allied Health Research Design
description: In this unit students develop an understanding of human inquiry through naturalistic and experimental designs pertaining to allied health evidence-based practice. The unit explores the relationship of theory, research and practice. Issues of methodology in design, including sampling, analysis and ethics. Knowledge of measurement principles, including psychometric properties and interpretation of outcome measures, is applied to critically analyse research literature and to guide allied health practice.

title: Curriculum and Instruction Senior Secondary: Mathematics
description: This unit is designed to prepare pre-service teachers to teach the Senior Secondary Mathematics curriculum. The focus of the unit is on curriculum planning, teaching strategies, assessment, reporting, the demonstration of positive impact on student learning and research relating to Senior Secondary Mathematics. The unit examines moderation, the provision of feedback and responding to individual student needs.

title: Advertising Design 1
description: Advertising Design 1 is an introductory unit that prepares students for study within creative advertising, by developing conceptual techniques essential to the advertising industry. Students will research and explore a number of different creative thinking and ideation strategies, then apply these to solve advertising briefs across a broad range of media. Students will examine and conduct critical analyses of existing advertising campaigns through looking at branding, campaigning, images, art direction and copywriting, and how the different elements contribute to the communication of the idea of the advertisement of campaign as a whole. Throughout the unit students will begin to develop an understanding of production, art direction, copy writing, and industry practice.

title: Public Relations in Industry
description: This unit explores the various subspecialties of public relations practice: For example, topics may cover government relations, agencies, internal relations, sports, travel, investor relations, health communication and science communication and other newly emerging trends, themes and areas of practice. The unit is a meld of theory and practically applicable information offered through case studies and hands-on workshop activities. Using a strategic issues management approach, learners can choose among issue interest areas to analyse and draw upon.

title: Vibration
description: Matrix modelling of vibration systems with multiple degrees of freedom, including transient and forced response. Vibration modelling including Normal Mode, symmetrical eigenvalue formulations, transfer function and State Space Techniques. Introduction of Finite Element Modelling of beam type structures. Vibration isolation. Dynamic Vibration Absorbers, Experimental techniques for vibration measurement and vibration analysis. Introduction to vibration analysis, discrete Fourier transforms and the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). Application to machine condition monitoring including balancing.

title: Introduction to Cultural Studies
description: This unit explores general ideas and critical concepts that form the foundations of cultural studies. The unit develops ideas about culture, texts, and modes of power and production. The unit aims to expand student understandings of the complex and interwoven operation of culture through examining a variety of texts through historical and social disciplinary lenses.

title: Laws and Legislation in Indigenous Australian Community Development
description: This unit examines laws and legislation that govern community organisations for both internal and external operations. Students will be introduced to areas of law that significantly impact upon community development and management, and will apply this knowledge in a discrete community context.

title: Occupational Therapy Fieldwork 1
description: Practicum experience that meets the requirements of the World Federation of Occupational Therapists. Integration of occupational therapy theoretical frameworks. Development of essential clinical and ethical reasoning. Practical demonstration of essential skills in planning, assessment, intervention, communication, documentation and management functions.

title: Reading Screens
description: An advanced level unit that applies media theory to analyse the practical, technical and aesthetic aspects of screen storytelling.

title: International Finance
description: In this unit, students extend their understanding of financial management, operations and decisions to an international setting. Students will assess emerging technologies to generate forward-looking novel ideas and solutions in international finance. The content of this unit includes the foundations of international financial management; the foreign exchange market; exchange rate determination; currency derivatives; foreign exchange exposure and management; world financial markets and institutions; and the financial management of the multinational firm.

title: Health Promotion Principles and Values
description: Health promotion action not only strengthens individual skills and capabilities but also influences social, environmental, political and economic conditions to improve health at a population level. This unit is an introduction to the principles and values of health promotion as a theoretical foundation for contemporary practice, policy and research. Critical concepts in health promotion are explored including: historical contexts and developments; key frameworks and theory underpinning health promotion; health promotion case studies; evidence-informed health promotion practice; ethics and the role of the health promotion practitioner in public health.

title: Business and Law International Experience 1
description: International mobility experience for undergraduate students.

title: Applied Metallurgical Chemistry
description: This unit will cover three important Metallurgical Engineering concepts - kinetics, interfaces, and electrolyte. Kinetics determines the rate of reactions such as leaching, roasting and precipitation used in Process and Resource Engineering. This unit introduces homogeneous kinetics, activation energy, collision and transition state theories. Interfaces are important in the study of flotation, ore wetting, solvent extraction, etc. Specifically, surface tension, gas-liquid and liquid-liquid interfaces, adsorption of gaseous and soluble species on solids, solid-liquid interfaces and three phase systems will be covered. Electrolytes are important as they influence the efficiency of electrowinning, leaching, liquid-liquid separation, and many other processes. The importance of electrolytes will be examined focusing on ionic interactions and activities including the concepts of conductance of electrolytes and transference numbers

title: Reputation and Crisis Management
description: This unit develops students’ understanding of reputation and the role public relations plays in protecting, maintaining and restoring reputation for brands and organisations. Students will learn about the role of managing reputation and gain a strong understanding of brand management and stakeholder relationship building. Students will gain hands on knowledge in managing an issue and experience a crisis simulation.

title: Introductory Systems Analysis and Design
description: This unit introduces the concepts and practices of systems analysis and design, with a focus on developing global, responsible, innovative and technology-driven information systems. The unit covers the fundamentals of systems development life cycles, business problem analysis, system requirements elicitation and specification, and user interface design. The unit will also explore professional and business ethics in a global context and the role they play in the development of information systems.

title: Applied Bioscience for Health Complexity 1
description: This unit investigates pathophysiology, clinical presentation diagnosis and clinical decision making for individuals with complex conditions, including: psychosis, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, major depression, anxiety disorders, eating disorders, substance addiction and withdrawal, head injuries, seizures and psychopharmacology.

title: Neuroscience
description: Nervous system development, overview, plasticity, blood supply, meninges, CSF, receptors, somatosensation, visual, auditory vestibular perception, cortical, cerebellar and brainstem control of movement. Hypothalamus structure and role with autonomic nervous system function, control and interaction with cerebral function. The role of the limbic system in emotion, learning and memory. Behaviour, sleep & dreaming, hunger & thirst.

title: Introduction to Midwifery Clinical Practice
description: This unit will introduce students to the clinical area and professional practice to facilitate the development of skills in the management of midwifery practice of well women and babies in a variety of midwifery settings. The student explores reflective practice, interaction and communication with the woman and family. This unit includes experience in woman-centred care as part of midwifery continuity of care with individual women through pregnancy, labour and birth and the postnatal period. The Midwife Standards for Practice (2018) inform the scope and purpose of this introductory unit.

title: Clinical Radiation Therapy Practice 4
description: This unit provides authentic radiation therapy professional practice experience in the clinical setting, at the level appropriate for the advanced beginning reflective professional. Students will have the opportunity to advance their capacity for culturally safe practice.

title: International Study Abroad
description: A formal learning contract will be negotiated between the student and their nominated supervisor prior to the commencement of the internship.  This will include the specific tasks and timeframe required to meet the unit criteria.

title: Introduction to Property Markets
description: This industry focused unit will introduce students to the basics of property and the techniques and technologies used to understand these complex markets. Students will collect and analyse property information to evaluate local markets and understand trends and drivers within those markets. Fundamental concepts around property rights, contracts, real estate investment and market structures will deliver a strong base for students looking to understand the diverse property industry.

title: Foundations of Physics
description: This is a first year level non calculus unit for students who have not previously studied Physics. Students who have passed Physics ATAR and Mathematics Methods ATAR or equivalent should instead take PHYS1005 Physics 1. Foundations of Physics provides an introduction to some of the fundamental principles of classical mechanics, kinematics and dynamics, circular motion, gravitation, mechanical energy, thermal properties of matter, gas laws, simple harmonic motion, wave motion and sound, electrical charges, static and current electricity, DC Circuits, electromagnetism, electrical safety, optics, microscope, human vision, atomic and nuclear radiation physics. Students will examine the fundamentals of experimental methods, including accuracy and precision, interpretation of physical measurements, graphical representation of data and uncertainties of measurement.

title: Mathematics Pedagogies and Integrated Curriculum
description: This unit focuses on the development of a range of effective pedagogies with particular emphasis on consideration of integrated curriculum principles. Students will continue to develop a deep understanding of the Number and Algebra strand of the Australian Curriculum: Mathematics. Topics include effective teaching and assessment of primary mathematics and planning mathematics teaching and learning. Curriculum content focuses on understanding operations, computational choices and number patterns. As well, there is a focus on strategies for mathematics working in a differentiated learning environment, including the use of tasks that suit a diversity of learners, with a particular focus on Indigenous learners.

title: Grant Writing for Community Organisations and individual projects
description: INCD3015 is in the study package Indigenous Community Management and Development Major (BAppSc).

title: Ecotoxicology and Environmental Monitoring
description: The most common aquatic and terrestrial contaminants are studied: classification of contaminants, effects of contaminants on biota, physiological effects at the organism level and effects at the population levels and community levels. Laboratory toxicology and endpoints measured: effective concentration (EC50), no observed effect concentration (NOEC) LC50 etc. Field toxicology, biomarkers, bioindicators and urban toxicology. The knowledge is integrated by presenting case studies where theory is applied to real-life scenarios. The practical portion of the unit is composed of a mixture of tutorials and laboratories. Students design environmental monitoring plans and learn basic laboratory techniques: standard curves, protein determination, and biomarker analysis.

title: Introduction to Financial Instruments and Markets
description: An overview of global financial markets and the major instruments traded within those markets. The focus is on equity and debt markets. The importance of ethics within financial markets will also be discussed.

title: Humanities Honours Project 2
description: This unit extends skills acquired during HUMN4004 Humanities Project 1. Students will acquire new knowledge through independent research and guided supervision in order to develop a research project through to submission for examination.

title: Supply Chain Decision Analytics
description: This unit examines operational efficiency and effectiveness within operational and supply chain management processes. The unit will develop knowledge and skills to understand techniques to optimise the supply chain configuration. The unit introduces fundamental understanding of the data-driven paradigm to support supply chain management analytics and decisions. The analyses will demonstrate how data is used to improve and drive operations strategies in organisations. The unit uses decision support tools to enhance the modelling and solution process in authentic real-world scenarios.

title: Geographies of Migration
description: This unit is concerned with the mobility of human life and the contemporary and historical processes of migration. Drawing on findings from human geography, demography and political geography, the unit will encompass: the history of migration, spatial patterns of migration in Australia, settler colonial migration, international migration, the globalisation of labour markets, the complex ethical, economic and security concerns emanating from migration, skilled migration, population ageing, and rural to urban (and urban to rural) migration.

title: Information Security
description: The Information Security unit provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental principles and practices of information security. The unit covers a wide range of topics, including security threats, vulnerabilities, attack methods, and the technologies, tools, standards, and strategies used to defend against them. Upon completing this unit, students will have a solid foundation in the principles and practices of information security and be prepared to pursue further study or certification in the field.

title: Qualitative Methods for Research
description: An overview of qualitative research within the social sciences. This includes an overview of the ontological and epistemological underpinnings of research. Commonly used qualitative research methodologies including case studies, grounded theory, action research, narrative studies amongst others will be reviewed. Qualitative data collection methods including common and emerging methods will be examined, along with options for analysis and CAQDAS. The essential aspects of rigour, relevance, research design, ethics and impact will all be reviewed.

title: Human Geography
description: This unit provides an introduction to human geography at the local-global scale focussing on the key concepts of place; space and globalisation. Topics include: population; migration; mapping; rural/urban change; and the relationships between people, resource use and the environment.

title: Applied Fluid Mechanics
