description: Fluid Dynamics plays a significant role in the fundamental understanding, and in the design and analysis of various external and internal flow systems. This unit will build on the foundations of fluid dynamics that students have learned in the previous year, and apply those concepts to various applications in the discipline of mechanical engineering. The unit will provide basic mathematical aspects of modelling fluid flows and provide the knowledge required to analyse fluid flow behaviour in external and internal flow geometries. An introduction to computational fluid dynamics, and its current practise in research and industrial scenarios is also covered.

title: Illustration and Visual Development
description: This unit explores the benefits of the role of the computer in modern image making techniques. It serves to break down the traditional barriers between illustration and photography by synthesising the common ground in both fields of image creation and enhancement.

title: Global Governance
description: This unit explores existing institutional arrangements for global governance and the management of international norms. The goal of global governance is to provide global public goods, particularly peace, security and justice, as well as mediation systems for conflict. This unit explores the ways that diverse actors are brought together to coordinate collective action. In particular, it examines the institutions that coordinate the behaviour of transnational actors, facilitate cooperation, resolve disputes, and alleviate collective action problems. The United Nations is the leading institution for global governance, but we will also consider the key roles of non-state actors. Furthermore, this unit looks at the contours of International Law and outlines the ways in which global norms are created, monitored, and enforced.

title: Applied Midwifery Bioscience
description: This unit introduces the applied pathophysiology and care of women and babies when complications emerge across the continuum of midwifery care. Students will explore a range of midwifery emergencies, variations from normal and contemporary issues in maternity, along with the associated pharmacology.

title: Survey Law Ethics Practice
description: Development of English, Australian and Western Australian land tenure, law and title systems. Statutes and regulations, case and common law principles governing land boundaries and surveys in Australia, focussing on Western Australia. Foundation and development of professional ethics and responsibilities for Licensed Surveyors. Cadastral surveying operations and processes relating to land development and administration in Western Australia.

title: International Perspectives for Planning
description: Develops an understanding of planning theories, critically examines past and present trends in planning theories and investigates the links between theory and practice exploring the scope for new planning theories.

title: Professional Engineering Management and Practice
description: This unit introduces the fundamentals of Project Management. Key topics include opportunity and scope development with a focus on sustainability as well as the management of projects in a high-risk environment. A key focus is on project management, including the Project Execution Plan, scope development, scheduling, estimating, systems engineering and resource allocation. This unit also introduces project reporting including variation management, contract management, schedule review and cost control. Contract and OH&S Law is covered. There is also a focus on Engineering, Construction, and Commissioning Management.

title: Drilling Engineering and Fluids Laboratory
description: This unit aims at providing students with a general overview of the fundamental aspects of drilling engineering including rotary drilling rig systems, drillstring design, introduction to drilling fluid and cementing, hydraulics calculations including flow in pipes and annuli and drilling bits. The lab sessions are designed to familiarise students with the basics measurement of drilling fluid and cement properties such as rheology and density.

title: Curriculum and Instruction Lower Secondary: Science
description: This unit is designed to prepare pre-service Lower Secondary Science teachers. The focus of the unit is on curriculum planning, teaching strategies, evaluation, resources, the demonstration of positive impact on student learning and research relating to Lower Secondary Science. Teaching and learning practices to support and challenge a diverse student cohort are explored.

title: Motor Control
description: In this unit students will develop knowledge of the anatomy and physiology of the neural, muscle and sensory systems. Students will investigate higher brain functions within the context of exercise and sports science. Students will explore the changes in sensorimotor function that occur through the human lifespan.

title: STEM Professional Practice
description: This unit is for students in Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) disciplines to undertake professional practice and apply discipline specific knowledge and employability skills in the workplace.The placement may be with industry, community, a research group or a government agency; paid or unpaid; work experience, projects or research; and may be advertised by Curtin or arranged by the student themselves.The work placement will be full or part-time for a minimum 100 hours but may be longer if requested by the host organisation. Students can undertake the work placement prior to semester, in the semester tuition free weeks, or during semester breaks but it must be completed by the end of the following study period. In addition to the hands-on development of industry-specific skills and connecting with mentors in their chosen profession, students will engage in a series of career development activities designed to increase job-readiness.

title: Pharmacology and Prescribing for Midwives
description: This unit focuses on the advanced principles of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, with reference within professional practice. Students explore the safety and quality use of medicines and the accountability, legislation, regulations and policies relevant to the prescribing of medicines.

title: Information Governance and Emerging Technologies
description: This unit discusses laws that govern and regulate information flows, such as Intellectual Property (IP) law, in the context of emerging technologies. You will consider select case studies to explore the impact of such laws on society, and be challenged to explore and formulate proposals on how the law should adapt in a dynamic technological environment. By focusing on specific cutting-edge topics, you will understand the competing interests arising in these contexts and be equipped to develop persuasive arguments for advancement of the law. Topic coverage in the unit will vary from year-to-year, as will the specific technologies that interact with the law. Possible topics, for example, include IP and artificial intelligence, trademark and digital assets (e.g. non-fungible tokens) and copyright and digital communications.

title: Engineering Foundations: Principles, Design and Communication
description: This unit covers the engineering design and tendering process, used by engineers from all disciplines to determine a solution to a problem. It helps the engineer define the problem, imagine innovative conceptual designs, write and respond to a tender document, prototype possible design solutions, refine several designs to a single final design, and determine specifications of the final design. In order to simulate a real-world experience, students are required to determine the role of the stakeholders in the project, and create an implementation plan for the final design. Students will be working in teams throughout the semester to gain the communication skills which are highly desired by industry. They will be required to reflect on their: work to help them improve in their teamwork skills, personal growth in learning the engineering process, as well as engineering responsibilities and duties. To complete the picture, since engineers need to submit proposals and pitch their ideas to stakeholders within communities and their team members, students will be able to give presentations to their peers, project managers, and possible stakeholders to hone in on their presentation skills. On completion of this unit, students should be able to participate in multidisciplinary conversations about the engineering design and tendering process. This unit is designed for those students who have passed Western Australian Certificate of Education (WACE) Mathematics Methods or equivalent.

title: Applied Cartography
description: This unit introduces students to the techniques used in the construction of thematic and purpose maps. It will focus upon the symbolisation used in these maps as well as the psychology of employing colour in their representation. Students will apply classification methods for the presentation of maps and the construction of thematic map communication and visualisation.

title: Power System Analysis
description: This unit covers power system’s modelling using single line diagram and per-unit system. The calculations of overhead transmission line parameters (Resistance, capacitance, and inductance) are demonstrated and used to model transmission lines of various lengths (short, medium, and long) using equivalent electrical circuits. These models are used to calculate the ABCD parameters, efficiency, and voltage regulation of transmission lines. Various power flow calculation methods (Gauss-Seidel, Newton Raphson, fast decoupled and DC) for power systems during steady state operation are explained. The last topic covered in this unit includes fault current calculations during symmetrical and unsymmetrical (line-ground, line-line, 2 lines-ground) faults, rating of circuit breakers and power system stability.

title: Foundations of Environment, Health and Disability
description: This unit explores the social construction of health, illness and disability and applies person-centred approaches to people with disabilities as occupational beings. Students engage in studying the impact of personal and societal values on outcomes for people with disabilities, the impact of service systems on people and contemporary service approaches for people with disabilities.

title: Honours Research Seminar
description: This unit facilitates peer learning toward a deeper understanding of the conceptual and contextual base to your Honours dissertation/creative project and is designed to incorporate your particular research interests. The unit content is determined by student’s research interest.

title: Database Systems
description: This unit explores the design, use, and maintenance of relational databases as a facet of software development. Students develop entity-relationship (ER) models using established theory on database normalisation and relational algebra, map these models to the structures of a relational database, and construct SQL queries to update and answer complex questions about the data. The unit addresses advanced aspects of database programming, including triggers, transactions and concurrency control, and the integration of databases into software applications.

title: Event Risk Management
description: This unit examines risk in the context of events. This unit will build knowledge and develop competence and skills in the techniques that support the identification, analysis and control and application of business risks with particular emphasis on responding to change, facilitating improvement and creating value. Practical frameworks for the application of risk and hazard assessment will be integrated into the major project.

title: Movement for the Actor
description: A theoretical and practical exploration of movement for actors aiming to expand their understanding and skills relating to their physical presence and expressive movement range. These skills are designed to provide a conceptual framework, a terminology and a set of practical tools to develop the actor's ability to articulate and embody movement choices for more effective meaning making in performance.

title: Engineering: Connecting Past, Present and Future
description: In this unit students will study successful and unsuccessful engineering projects throughout history to make connections between the projects and non-technical aspects of engineering, namely: ethical behaviour, health and safety, historical context, social environment, risk management and environmental impact. Students will use critical thinking to engage in conversations about projects in different disciplines. Students will submit their work using written, oral and multimedia formats.

title: News Writing and Reporting
description: An introduction to news writing and reporting for publication, whereby students develop news gathering, writing and research skills and an awareness of different styles and genres within print and online journalism. Students learn how to generate ideas, undertake research, conduct interviews, take news photographs and write in news style to strict deadlines. The highly practical nature of the unit provides students the opportunity to experience work integrated learning as reporters for Curtin Journalism’s online publication, Western Independent.

title: Foundations of International Taxation
description: Studying this unit will immerse you in the dynamic world of international tax which is full of rewarding career opportunities for tax professionals. Within the unit we will cover off on looking at anti-avoidance mechanisms that are employed by governments to combat international tax avoidance methods used by multinational companies and how the majority of tax authorities worldwide joined together with the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) to create agreements to cease this type of avoidance behaviour. Double tax agreements play an important role in the international tax arena to who has the taxing rights of taxpayers who reside in corresponding countries, you will get to dive into some of these and see how Australian works co-operatively with other countries. Another aspect of a career in international tax is the ability to advise clients who operate international businesses therefore we will consider the structuring and use of international tax planning as we work our way through the course. Playing a major part of international tax is for advisors to act in the most ethical and socially responsible manner and we look at the consequences of not sticking to these fundamental principles. A career in taxation can lead to you working anywhere in the world if you have experience in international tax.

title: Curriculum and Instruction Senior Secondary: Science
description: This unit is designed to prepare pre-service teachers to teach the Senior Secondary Science curriculum. The focus of the unit is on curriculum planning, teaching strategies, assessment, reporting, the demonstration of positive impact on student learning and research relating to Senior Secondary Science. The unit examines moderation, the provision of feedback and responding to individual student needs.

title: Foundations in Pharmacology
description: This unit is delivered in 5 modules designed to introduce students to the discipline of pharmacology and the pharmaceutical industry and provides understanding about pathogenic microorganisms, the diseases they cause and responses of the human immune system. Through the modules the drug discovery process is explored, highlighting the key role the pharmaceutical industry plays in this process including prominent global ethical issues. Key immunological mechanisms that stop microbial invasion and removal are presented within the context of microbial pathogenesis and survival strategies. Finally, diseases of local and global importance are discussed along with the pathogens that cause them.

title: Disability and Multimodal Communication
description: This unit focuses on developing students’ understanding of social, cultural and international perspectives of disability. Students will apply this to working with individuals with disability, for example; Autism spectrum Disorders and Cerebral Palsy. Throughout the unit, students will integrate the use of multimodal communication theories and technologies.

title: Foundations of Health Promotion Planning and Evaluation
description: An introduction and overview of health promotion planning and evaluation principles and practice. The role of planning and evaluation in health promotion. Planning for evaluation. Mapping theory to planning and evaluation. An introduction to qualitative and quantitative evaluation instrument design and data collection. Formative evaluation to inform health promotion planning. Assessing the implementation of health promotion projects via process evaluation. Application of theoretical and empirical evidence to develop a health promotion plan.

title: 3D Modelling and Digital Fabrication
description: The designer's use and application of computer modelling are extended in this unit for the purposes of digital production and manufacture. Parametric Solid modelling software CAD is further used and applied to create form, interface, and instructions for digital fabrication. The required application of technical communication to Australian and international standards is established. Low-fidelity physical modelling techniques studied include object printing, laser engraving and profile shaping. The design potential of different digital fabrication methods is studied by examining iconic designs, human sensory experience, research and creative experimentation.

title: Speech Pathology Fieldwork 4
description: In this unit, students will undertake speech pathology clinical practice to develop and demonstrate competency according to Speech Pathology Australia Competency-Based Occupational Standards (CBOS). This unit will facilitate the development of skills in the management of paediatric or adult clients across a range of practice areas. Students will be expected to demonstrate competency relative to their stage of their fieldwork progression: They will demonstrate approaching entry level competency at the end of their penultimate placement and at entry level competency at the end of their final placement.

title: Science Fundamentals for Health and Safety
description: The unit aims to introduce students to key scientific concepts, including force, energy, mass, waves, mechanics and optics, and their application to contemporary workplace technology. It introduces the fundamental aspects of experimental design, measurement, and analysis that form the basis of evidence-based practice in health and safety. The unit will provide opportunities for students to develop problem solving and critical thinking capabilities and skills in communicating health and safety information.

title: Advanced Topics in Mathematical Sciences B
description: Australian Mathematical Sciences Institute (AMSI) is the collaborative enterprise of Australia’s mathematical sciences, of which Curtin is a member. AMSI Advanced Collaborative Environment (ACE) Network offers a wide selection of honours level mathematical Sciences subjects in online mode. Within this unit, you will enrol in one of the ACE subjects available for your period of study. A detailed subject guide and pre-enrolment quizzes are available for each subject under ACE network tab of AMSI. The subject may be selected to complement your existing strengths and knowledge. You will be completing this unit alongside other fellow students from Australian and New Zealand universities.

title: Fine Art Studio Methods
description: This unit is designed to engage you in the ideas of contemporary art through practical application of technical skills and conceptual development. In this unit you will be encouraged to align conceptual development with the acquisition of traditional and contemporary skills across a range of visual art methods. You will undertake several set art projects utilising traditional and contemporary skills and concepts from a wide range of fine art media.

title: Investigations in Infectious Microbiology
description: This unit studies microbiological cell structures and functions, and works on identifying and highlighting the virulent aspects of bacteria to understand how these factors can influence the pathogenesis of infectious disease. The dynamic interrelationship between a human host’s defense mechanisms and how the immune system deals with pathogens, and how the pathogens deal with the host’s immune system is examined. The developing pathogenesis of an infectious disease is examined and understood by exploring clinically relevant case studies using bacteria and viruses in a laboratory setting. The clinical diagnostic cycle for describing, classifying and diagnosing microbial pathogens includes the collection of relevant human clinical specimens, laboratory processing of collected specimens, cultivation and taxonomic identification of pathogens and possible treatment avenues (antibiotic susceptibility testing). This unit also covers the important topic of antibiotic therapy as well as an introduction to epidemiology covering disease distribution, causality, monitoring disease of outbreaks and the control of infectious diseases within the framework of health.

title: Environmental Chemistry and Microbiology
description: This unit is concerned with the behaviour of contaminants in the air, water, soils and sediments. It is an interdisciplinary field at the crossroads of important scientific subjects centred around advanced analytical chemistry. It requires knowledge of the fundamental principles of many subject areas, including organic chemistry, biochemistry, toxicology, ecology, microbial activity, and diversity. Students will be taught to evaluate the pathways of pollutants in water, air, and soil and interact with the microorganism to remediate the contaminated environment. The impact of human activity on the health and safety of aquatic systems will also be discussed.

title: Allied Health Honours Proposal
description: The focus of this unit is to introduce students to planning and designing research. Students will apply skills in critical analysis, review of literature, research methodology and developing and writing research proposals.

title: Health and Safety Technology
description: The health and safety technology unit provides students with theoretical background and practical approaches to the control of a range of safety hazards. Emphasis is given to the use of effective planning, design and engineering technology in accordance with the hierarchy of hazard control principle.

title: International Study Abroad 1
description: n/a

title: Strategic Rewards and Performance Management
description: This unit examines concepts and theories related to the management of total rewards systems within organisations. It explores the four main elements of a total rewards system: financial, developmental, social and intrinsic rewards. The unit analyses the main components of remuneration: base pay, employee benefits and performance related pay. It examines the processes and challenges of designing a strategic-aligned reward management system. Students will be able to analyse and understand contemporary reward practices and apply them within a range of organisational, industry and cultural contexts.

title: Contingencies 2
description: This unit covers the pricing and valuation (reserving) of financial contracts involving multi-decrements and multiple lives. Practical knowledge is presented alongside mathematical techniques relevant to actuarial practice in life and health insurance and superannuation (pensions).  The principles of cashflow modelling are discussed including such topics as choice of model, deterministic and stochastic models and use of scenario and sensitivity testing. Practical, hands-on modelling experience is developed through the use of Excel spreadsheets (students are assumed to have basic Excel skills prior to commencement of this unit).

title: Electrical Systems
description: Electricity is the greatest energy source of our time. Engineers from all disciplines need to have a basic understanding of the fundamental principles of this valuable energy source, as well as the main tools and techniques used to specify and analyse electrical circuits. This unit covers the fundamentals of Direct Current (DC) and Alternating Current (AC) circuit analysis. The use of electricity in electro-mechanical and electronic systems is covered, with emphasis in instrumentation and control. To complete the picture, computer embedded systems are introduced as a tool for monitoring and controlling engineering processes, whether they be a bridge, a refinery, or a robot. On completion of this unit, students should be able to participate in a multidisciplinary conversation about electrical systems.

title: Principles of Psychological Assessment
description: This unit focuses on the theory and practice of psychological testing and assessment relevant to professional practice as a psychologist in a range of professional settings.

title: Secondary Professional Experience 2
description: This is the second in the suite of professional experience units that includes a practical component (a 15 day placement in a school). The unit will extend your application of relevant philosophies and theories related to teaching to deepen and extend the implementation of effective planning for diverse groups of learners. The unit will continue to address professional responsibilities, effective communication and reflective practices to support learning in school based context. The professional experience practical assessment is a 15 day work place learning opportunity intended to enable practical application of the knowledge and skills gained, along with providing students with insights into the complexity of the teacher’s role. All required clearances to work with children must be valid, and all other preparation requirements met prior to commencement of Professional Experience placement.

title: Indigenous Australian Land and Environments
description: Investigates the physical and spiritual relationship between Indigenous Australians and the land and water, including traditional and contemporary use of land and water, the law of Native Title and associated cultural, economic, social and political issues.

title: Fundamentals of Mineral Processing
description: An introduction to the main technologies and techniques currently used for mineral processing in the mining industry. Students will gain a conceptual understanding of mineral processing by applying various terms and principles to extractive metallurgical processes, and will learn about the key role that mineral processing plays in the mining value chain and how mining practices can impact on processing outcomes. They will be introduced to three overarching processes: the comminution and liberation of minerals; the separation of minerals; and, the extraction of metals, including emerging approaches, technologies and digital applications in these areas. The unit will enable students to specify appropriate methods for processing a variety of ore types, as well as the relevant underlying phenomena involved. Sustainability issues will be examined, ranging from energy consumption to environment considerations, and safety risks associated with mining processing operations, as well as factors impacting efficiency and cost of the processing system. Students will also have the opportunity to develop their academic and professional communication skills through exposure to, and application of, terms and principles relevant to extractive metallurgical processes.

title: Environmental Impact Assessment
description: Historical background to Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA). Practical understanding of the project, and strategic EIA (including sustainability assessment) procedures in Western Australia and across Australia. Federal and State legislation controlling EIA in Australia. Structure and functions of the WA Environmental Protection Authority. Review of EIA documents. Practical preparation of an EIA document.

title: Penetration Testing and Defence
description: The unit will help students learn to discover how vulnerabilities in systems exist and how these could be managed. It would further focus on the reconnaissance and basic exploitation of different network and web applications.

title: 3D Digital Sculpting
description: Designing a 3D digital sculpted outcome, the unit covers selected digital sculpting methods of production, technologies and approaches which are applied to a creative project. In addition to digital sculpting, students will study human anatomy to enhance their creative outcome. Students analyse trends, related techniques and similar creative work to inform their creative project. Concepts studied and applied include the use of relevant 3D modelling and digital sculpting tools to achieve a high-fidelity 3D sculpted creative project.

title: Marketing Intelligence
description: Marketing Intelligence teaches students the scientific and practical methods of marketing research to ascertain practical and actionable insights. It develops the analytical skills students need to analyse and interpret a diversity of qualitative and quantitative information sources in professional marketing practice. Having ascertained key data-driven insights, students communicate visually and verbally to inform practical strategic marketing decisions.

title: Australia's Global Politics
description: This unit introduces students to Australia’s global positioning in the international political system and develops critical analysis of the influences, interests, processes and policies that shape Australia’s international relations. Students will examine the factors that frame Australia’s national identity and national interests, including its strategic geography, natural resources, economic profile, socio-cultural values, and political system, and then explore how foreign policy is made and implemented through Australia’s political, bureaucratic and diplomatic machinery. The unit will explore Australia’s key bilateral and regional relationships, such as with the USA, China, India, and ASEAN, as well as its engagement with the wider systems of global governance, including the United Nations. The unit will examine Australia’s policies and positions in international negotiations on major issues such as climate change, geopolitical tensions, conflict resolution, inequality, international trade, and Indigenous rights.

title: Environmental Monitoring and Analysis
description: This unit introduces sampling techniques and analytical methods to monitor and analyse environmental contamination in air, water, and soils. Emphasis is placed on environmental investigation techniques, instrument selection, and quality control, including documentation, calibration, and sample management. Students will be taught to evaluate the data using statistical analysis such as hypothesis testing of measured parameters, analysis of, design of factorial experiments, and multiple linear regression. The students will also be introduced to the latest data analytics methods, such as machine learning analytics.

title: Health and Wellbeing in Social and Cultural Contexts
description: An introduction to sociological and anthropological perspectives on health, wellbeing illness and disability in society; understanding the contribution of the biomedical and social models of health for transdisciplinary practice for nurses, midwives and allied health: professionals. Incorporating contemporary, historical, social and cultural perspectives in local and global contexts to identify social determinants of health. Understanding traditional healing and other healing practices within a diverse community to cultural safe, secure and competent care, which is necessary to build individual and community empowerment. Recognising the impact of gender, sexuality, disability, migration, being a refugee, internally displaced person or member of any marginalised population on health. Evaluating humanitarian health care delivery and disaster relief within a human rights and 	social justice framework to support community development in national and international settings.

title: Issues in Financial Planning Practice
description: This course builds on students’ financial studies to date to focus on areas of importance to Financial Planning practice in more depth. Students will learn to apply Chapter 7 of the Corporations Act and other legal matters not covered elsewhere to their practice. Ethical dimensions of Financial Planning are considered, including FASEA’s code of conduct and financial planning issues relevant to the experience of Indigenous Australians. Students will apply develop an understanding of risk and how this can be mitigated with insurance in the context of Financial Planning.

title: Marketing Across Borders
description: Marketing Across Borders scopes the macro and micro environments of multi-national, international and transnational corporations in order to understand sustainable and ethnic issues and resourcefully propose marketing solutions. Students enhance their skills in working independently and collaboratively to analyse and interpret sourced data, develop original proposals as well as implement and evaluate deliverables that impact global trade.

title: Specialised Property Valuation
description: This unit introduces students to the valuation of different asset classes such as licensed premises, petrol stations and plant and machinery. It also examines valuation methodologies used for statutory requirements including compensation and business valuations.

title: Fundamentals of Geology
description: This unit provides a comprehensive overview of the basic principles and practice of geology. You will learn the language of geology and the geological processes that form minerals, rocks, geological structures and mineral deposits. In the laboratory, you will develop practical skills in the description and identification of common rocks and minerals, including ore minerals, and in the interpretation of geological data.

title: 3D Game and Level Design
description: This unit introduces students to the design and development of 3D game levels. The unit focuses on applying fundamental game design principles to implement playable levels. Through a series of technical and conceptual activities, students will have the opportunity to utilise level design tools to express their game concepts and realise their play experiences.

title: Coordinate and Mapping Systems
description: This unit provides an introduction to geodesy, the study of the shape (and gravity field) of the Earth. It covers coordinate systems, both on a plane and on the surface of a sphere or ellipsoid in two dimensions, and three dimensional coordinates referenced to the centre of the Earth. You will also study the methods to transform between the various types of coordinate systems. The unit also covers the definitions of horizontal and vertical datums, and introduces the geoid, a surface approximating mean sea level that is used to define heights. You will learn about map projections, with focus upon the Map Grid of Australia (MGA), the projection used in Australia, and Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM), a similar projection but used globally.

title: Mining and Sustainability
description: This unit provides students with a comprehensive and practical understanding of the range of impacts that mining may have on society and the environment. Broadly, the unit covers the concept of mining and sustainability; responses of government, industry and private firms to the sustainability agenda; environmental management in mining (including water, waste, acid and metalliferous drainage, and mine closure planning); social and cultural issues in mining, and best practice for environmental and social impacts of mining. Students will acquire an understanding of state-of-the-art techniques in environmental management of mine sites as well as being able to identify the major issues and management strategies associated with social/community engagement and impacts, particularly in relation to Indigenous communities in Australia and internationally. Students’ communication and collaborative skills will also be developed in this unit. Students will also be required to participate in fieldwork activities and industry based problem solving.

title: Principles of Geomechanics
description: This unit introduces principles of geomechanics and basic geotechnical engineering. Students will learn about the physical properties, composition and classification of soils. Students will also develop an understanding of the fundamental concepts of soil compaction, stresses in soils and seepage in soil masses.

title: Urban Geographies
description: This unit explores the key concepts and approaches for understanding cities. The unit draws on consideration of the processes of globalisation, gentrification and urban contestations shaping the social geographies of cities.

title: Geology for Resource Engineers
description: An introduction to planet Earth and its geological resources. Students will examine key rock types (igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic) and how their constituent minerals and structures define a range of rock properties. They will also infer 3-dimensional patterns of rock units and structures from maps, cross-sections and stereographic projections; and, identify key ore and fossil fuel deposit types and learn how their size, shape and location are controlled by the spatial arrangement of rock types and structures.

title: Dynamic and Stochastic Modelling and Optimisation
description: This unit focuses on dynamic and stochastic systems and provides a solid foundation in a range of tools applicable to the complex problems arising in industrial modelling and optimisation. The following areas are covered: Dynamic programming: Basic concepts, applications,models and algorithms are investigated with optimal solutions developed and implemented for relevant applications. Queuing models: Basic concepts are covered. Several types of queuing models and their advantages and disadvantages are studied and optimal solutions are derived for each. Simulation: Simulation is a very powerful tool that provides the industrial modeller with the ability to study complex systems in considerable detail. Simulation modelling comprise of three major components: input generation that allows the system to be viewed "in action"; a bookkeeping phase that keeps track of transactions occurring in the system and keeps counters on ongoing processes in order to calculate appropriate performance measures and output analysis that establish the effectiveness of the system's performance. The unit provides the necessary skills to analyse, develop and implement simulation models. Techniques and methodologies used for the effective optimisation of simulations are also studied.

title: Australian Employment Relations
description: In this unit, you will learn about the key aspects of employment relations in Australia, such as the main actors, institutions, processes and policies that shape the world of work. You will also explore the legislation that regulates employment relations and how it applies to different groups and contexts, such as justice and indigenous rights. You will develop your analytical skills by comparing and contrasting various workplace situations and their implications for economic growth, social justice and environmental sustainability. This unit will equip you with the knowledge and skills to engage with employment relations in an informed and responsible manner.

title: Industrial Automation and Robotics
description: Introduction to Industrial Automation and Robotics covers the use of robotics and related fields including automation, sensing, artificial intelligence, data transmission, management and mining, and human system interaction. Students will gain an understanding of the terminology used to describe the various capabilities, when and why they are important and how to analyse requirements and compare implementations.

title: Water and Environmental Engineering
description: This unit covers topics within the field of environmental engineering - particularly those in the sub-disciplines of water, soil and air. The principles of water and wastewater quality and treatment, as well as wastewater recycling are presented, covering both conventional and advanced water and wastewater treatment processes. Concepts in soild waste (including hazardous waste) will be discussed. Air quality, pollution control, water quality and environmental impact will be discussed and applied.

title: Graphic Design 3
description: Students produce solutions to a variety of practical design briefs through rigorous application of the design process, inclusive of research, development, refinement and reflective practice. Students are expected to validate their outcomes through AV presentations, designed to simulate client pitches. Interpretation and analysis of one’s own work, and that of others, is encouraged throughout this unit.

title: Physics 1
description: This unit assumes that students have passed Physics ATAR and Mathematics Methods ATAR or equivalent. Students who have not passed both these subjects or equivalent should enrol in PHYS1006 Foundations of Physics. It provides students with a detailed knowledge of some of the core concepts of physics including linear mechanics (Newtons Law), work and energy conservation equations (energy and momentum), rotational mechanics (conservation of angular momentum), gravitation, fluid mechanics, waves and oscillations (superposition, interference and standing waves, sound waves, doppler effect) and an introduction to thermodynamics. The unit is underpinned by physical data analysis and graphical techniques, and a sound understading of uncertainties in measurement

title: Advanced Business Technologies
description: The Advanced Business Technologies unit is designed to equip students with the skills necessary to develop and manage computer networks that support global, responsible, and innovative business practices. This includes an exploration of Network Operating Systems (NOS) and their role in facilitating communication and resource sharing across a network. Students will learn about network administration, configuration, and security measures that ensure the responsible use and protection of sensitive data. The unit will also cover the installation and troubleshooting of LANs and WANs, with a focus on designing networks that support global collaboration and innovative business strategies. Understanding network design, students will develop the ability to create flexible, scalable network solutions that meet the changing demands of the global business landscape.

title: Strategic Career Design
description: This unit develops students’ awareness of the impact of global labour markets, changing social trends, and technological innovation on career opportunities and the future of work. Through the application of career theory and design thinking frameworks, students will examine and develop the critical employability skills required to create and sustain meaningful work across a broad range of industry sectors and cultural contexts. The unit demonstrates strategies for effective individual and organisational career management, incorporating theory and concepts on career choice, career change, organisational and entrepreneurial careers, and careers in the ‘gig’ economy. Global and industry trends will be explored with a specific focus on the implications for individual and organisational career management strategies and personal and professional branding in a digitised global economy.

title: Geodata Management
description: In this unit, students will learn how to solve geospatial and surveying problems and study theory of geographic information systems and technology. Skills and best practice learned in this unit will be supported by the theoretical fundamentals of geoinformation science, geodata organisation and management (including standard geodata structures, design and implementation of geodata management systems), and with necessary essentials of primary and secondary techniques used to acquire geodata (including Remote Sensing and Earth Observation, geodata search and discovery, geodata digitization and geodata format conversion). The emphasis in this unit is on learning about fundamental geodata types and their representation, organization and management. Students will understand the process and requirements for basic geospatial analysis with geographic information systems. Upon completion of this unit, students will be able to use geographic information systems to solve common geospatial and surveying problems.

title: Art Visual Research 4
description: You will develop a self-directed visual art practice project by negotiated proposal to progress skills in the techniques and processes of the various specialisations within contemporary art practice, through drawing and other media.

title: Abnormal Psychology
description: This unit provides an introduction to the history and classification of psychopathology and information about the diagnostic criteria and features of a range of psychological disorders in adults and children. An overview of evidence-based treatments for selected psychological disorders is also provided.

title: Foundations of Biomedical Science
description: This unit is an introduction to the theory and application of disciplines in the biomedical sciences: microbiology, immunology, histopathology, haematology, biochemistry and molecular genetics. Themes include the basic theory of the cellular and molecular components that form the foundations of biomedical science, the investigation of disease and infectious agents, occupational health considerations, the use of specialized equipment and testing of biological samples in a professional manner. The role and function of medical and research laboratories will also be explored.

title: Planning History and Theory
description: Develops an understanding of planning theories, critically examines past and present trends in planning theories and investigates the links between theory and practice. Explores the scope for new planning theories.

title: Advanced Occupational Therapy Professional Practice
description: This unit incorporates the integration, evaluation and critique of core occupational therapy practice skills and theories. These include clinical reasoning; professional behaviours and leadership; occupational therapy models; occupational therapy process; ethics and values-based practice; application of person and client centred practice; inter-professional practice; reflective practice; evidence-based practice; practice in cultural diversity and cultural competency; and the promotion of the occupational therapy profession.

title: Extended Cyber Security Concepts
description: An introduction to information security and management and cover the basic ISO27000 standard - how to build a security program and develop the appropriate security controls (administrative, logical and physical control); how to develop a set of policy to ensure effective risk management and resource usage verification. Industry standard for information security - ISO27000. Procedures used to secure data and resources at all levels in an information and communication technology organisation. Risk assessment and management.

title: Principles and Practice of Clinical Biochemistry
description: This unit covers the biochemical investigation of abnormalities in electrolyte, carbohydrate, cholesterol, calcium and haem; biochemical markers of cardiac, pancreatic and liver function and/or damage. In the specific context of analytical techniques, lectures and practicals cover quality control and the physicochemical principles underlying clinical biochemistry tests/techniques such as chromatography, enzymology, electrophoresis, fluorimetry, nephelometry and turbidimetry, and ligand binding assays (for example, immuno and receptor assays).

title: Principles of Epidemiology and Biostatistics
description: This unit provides an introduction to the core skills in epidemiology and statistical concepts, their use and relevance in health research. Topics covered include: quantitative and qualitative research methods, study design, characteristics of a good research question, definition and selection of study population and participants, reliability and validity of data, statistical methods and the use of statistical software. The emphasis is on practical enabling students to conduct independent public health research.

title: Machine Design
description: This unit deals with the theory, procedures, data, and analysis techniques to design machine elements commonly used in mechanical systems. Students learn the modern concepts of product safely, liability, and substantiality. The unit covers the analysis and design of machine elements, such as gears, shafts, bearings, mechanical springs, and columns. Through the study of machine elements, students will develop their capacity to understand and apply advanced engineering concepts to integrate the individual elements into a system. Students will also learn the concept of statistical analysis to assess the reliability of components.

title: Introduction to Medical Radiation Science
description: The origins and scope of the medical radiation science professions, nationally and internationally, and the role of the practitioner including ethical, professional, legislative and regulatory requirements. Foundation knowledge and skills in the clinical environment including some basic procedures, which include patient care and communication based on a wide range of patient presentations. Introduction to medical image production and radiation therapy procedures including the technology used, quality of outcomes and safe and effective use of radiation. Use of effective communication in all professional contexts.

title: Africa's International Relations
description: This unit explores and critically analyses the international relations of Africa, drawing on historical developments to examine the continent’s contemporary dynamics. We first examine key concepts and contexts—including the slave trade, colonialism, the Cold War, pan-Africanism, the state and the global political economy—that have shaped and help us to understand contemporary African actors and their regional and international relations. We then interrogate key relationships between African states, the African Union, and major external actors including the US, EU, China and the UN, examining key themes including regional integration, geopolitics, natural resources, security and equality. The final part of the unit examines the negotiating positions, diplomatic strategies, agency and impacts of African actors on the contemporary global governance agenda, including in sustainable development, climate and trade negotiations.

title: Sustainable Business Innovation Project
description: This project-based unit offers an experiential work integrated learning opportunity, where students work on an industry connected business innovation project related to sustainable development and social impact. Students will enhance their critical employability skills using creative and responsible decision making while working collaboratively with a team and industry professionals. The unit explores the intersection of business, innovation, and sustainability to address a real-world problem in a hands-on learning experience. The aim is to create solutions that benefit the environment, society, and the economy, working collectively with a team. This experience will foster communication, collaboration and project management skills. These capabilities are vital for graduates entering a workforce where a sustainability and social impact mindset, together with ethical considerations and practices are essential for business, governments, and society.

title: Geotechnical Engineering Practice
description: This unit covers some aspects of applied geotechnical engineering. The first part is stability of slopes and embankments. The second part is determination of lateral earth pressure. The third part is design of earth retaining structures, including flexible and ridged retaining walls, mechanically stabilised walls and braced excavations. The fourth part covers ground improvement techniques.

title: Introduction to History of Art and Design
description: This unit provides students with an introduction to some of the key ideas and events in the history of art and design. It is intended as a basic introduction to the history of ideas and the effects such ideas have had on the recent evolution of art and design. While this unit has a Euro-centric bias, ideas from other cultural histories are introduced. Students are taught the visual literacy and analysis needed to be able to understand historical and contemporary art and design.

title: Rock Art, Archaeology and Antiquity
description: This unit studies Indigenous perspectives of Rock Art and Archaeological sites in terms of cultural heritage and histories. It also reviews global perspectives through the UNDRIP and UNESCO initiatives. There are opportunities for students to review global examples of rock art in comparative contexts. Students will explore contemporary research in this field descriptive of the Indigenous voice to create a living narrative of cultural practice from time immemorial until the present. The unit explains the importance of understanding the continuity of Indigenous ontologies and the very fabric of the interrelatedness of Indigenous ownership, inclusive Indigenous spiritual feeling for Country. The unit describes evidence of long-time occupation, heritage, cultural practices and philosophies.

title: Calculus for Engineers
description: This unit builds on students' knowledge of functions and calculus, further extending to a range of techniques used in solving problems arising in engineering and related fields. Students will extend their differentiation skills to implicit and logarithmic differentiation, and will apply differentiation techniques to optimisation problems and the approximation of functions. This unit will cover a range of integration techniques, and students will apply these to find volume, length and surface area. Students will also be introduced to the concept of complex numbers, together with their applications and use in solutions to polynomial equations. This unit will also introduce students to first and second order differential equations. This unit is designed for those students who have passed WACE Mathematics Methods or equivalent.

title: Continuity of Midwifery Care
description: This unit will allow students further experience in the clinical area to facilitate the development of professional practice and skills in the midwifery management of women and babies in a variety of midwifery settings. The student explores reflective practice, interaction and communication with the woman and family. This unit includes experience in woman-centred care as part of midwifery continuity of care with individual women through pregnancy, labour and birth and the postnatal period.

title: Fundamentals of Mechanical Design
description: This unit introduces several fundamental mechanical engineering topics. Students will be taught how to calculate the Centroid and Second Moments of Area for composite areas, and how to determine stresses in straight beams by using Shear Force and Bending Moments Diagrams. Load Analysis will be covered, including free-body diagrams, beam loading and impact. Failure Theories for static condition in ductile materials will be introduced, including Mohr’s theory. These topics will then be applied to machine elements, such as threads and power screws. Furthermore, students will study the different types of machine joints such as bolts (non-permanent), rivets and welding (permanent). To conclude motion control clutches and brakes will be investigated.

title: Physical Education Pedagogy
description: This unit introduces students specifically to physical education pedagogy in the contemporary Australian primary school curriculum, where emphasis is on developing children’s physical literacies within safe and lifelong learning frameworks so they are able to flourish as healthy and active citizens. With attention to diversity and social justice, children’s rights to develop physical literacies within their personal, physical and socio-cultural contexts are explored, and relevant teaching approaches identified. Given the emphasis on evidence-based pedagogical approaches, students will investigate the research that underpins the contemporary PE pedagogy.The unit reviews ongoing, developmentally appropriate and explicit teaching strategies about health and movement, where children participate safely and enthusiastically to develop the knowledge, skills, dispositions and understandings to make healthy and active choices for the wellbeing of themselves and others. In this regard, the importance of physical skills in the primary years, including teaching and assessment of fundamental motor skills (FMS) and appropriate interventions, is addressed. The unit will also address the need for inclusivity in Physical Education pedagogy and develop in students, practical ways of approaching inclusivity in planning and implementation of lessons, including management and safety issues.

title: Electrical Machines Drives and Control
description: This unit introduces electrical drive technology, covering the motor types, power electronic converters, sensors and controllers. Drives based on DC motors, induction motors, synchronous motors, and switched reluctance motors are discussed in detail. It explores their operation under both steady-state and transient conditions. The control of the drives in the four-quadrant torque-speed plane to deliver various performances such as regenerative braking and closed-loop speed control are discussed.

title: Curriculum and Culture in Secondary Schools
description: This unit examines a number of social, political, cultural and economic relations of Australian society and their impact on education policy, classroom practices and student learning. The unit provides students with concepts and perspectives to think about schooling and society with. Students examine the characteristics of education systems and learning settings that promote inclusivity, celebrate diversity and reduce the effects of disadvantage, inequality and social exclusion. The unit aligns with the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers associated with student diversity, including consideration of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children in secondary schools.

title: Theories and Methods for Honours Research
description: This unit offers Humanities students experience in the use of significant research methods and critical understandings of the relationships between researchers, their topics and their fields of inquiry. In focussing on methods of collection of evidence, of analysis and interpretation, and representation, it enables students to develop methodological frameworks appropriate to their individual fields, whether the outcomes are through creative practice and exegesis or dissertation only.

title: Property Economics and Policy
description: Economic theory can help explain a variety of property market outcomes and offer solutions to complex problems. This unit introduces students to key economic theories such as supply and demand and discusses how theory helps explain the operation of various property markets both in Australia and internationally. Students will examine the planning system in Western Australia and relevant state and federal policies related to housing to understand how they shape the operation of property markets and the actors operating within it.

title: Integrated Cardiopulmonary Science
description: This unit develops communication, assessment, and treatment skills when managing more challenging cardiopulmonary problems in patients with additional comorbidities, complex care needs, or who are severely ill. Subjective and objective information gathering, analysis and prioritisation of key problems and safety concerns, and goal-setting with more complex patients are developed. Using the ICF framework, an interprofessional team approach, and person-centered communication, decision-making using evidence-informed management strategies is developed. Management strategies include the use of exercise prescription, application of technological devices, rehabilitation principles, and ongoing self-management. Challenging discharge issues are considered.

title: Go Practice - Internship
description: This unit provides students with fieldwork opportunities through internships or industry and community engagement opportunities in simulated work-based environments. Independent student learning will be supported by academics and industry advisors, and students in courses without professional work experience are encouraged to apply.

title: Database
description: This unit provides a comprehensive understanding of relational database modelling and design, with a focus on creating innovative and responsible solutions. Students will learn how to transform a conceptual entity relationship model into a rational model, ensuring data integrity and normalization. By incorporating cutting-edge technology, the course covers the design and definition of database structures such as tables, fields, indexes, sets, and views. The use of structured query language (SQL) as a database interface language will also be emphasized, to allow for seamless interaction with global databases.

title: Studio Production
description: Creative development of practical multi-camera and single-camera skills and an understanding of studio based production in a practical, production-oriented environment. Students work collaboratively in authentic industry roles to produce a television project.

title: International Study Abroad - Asia Study Tour
description: An educational study tour and seminar through Curtin Campus and Community Life that visits several culturally diverse Asian countries.  Many transnational organisations from America, Australia and the region see a growing need for a mobile workforce with improved cross-cultural communication and people management skills, and a better understanding of the economic and political realities of the region.  This tour will sensitise participants to the need to develop these skills and become a more valuable and more adaptable human resource in an increasingly interdependent world.  The following themes in the context of the tour will be studied in depth: sustainability, political economy, and leadership. Countries that have previously been included in these tours are: Indonesia, India, Myanmar (Burma), Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Laos, Vietnam, China (including Hong Kong), Japan, South Korea and the Philippines.  The study tour runs twice each year (for a minimum  of three  weeks) prior to the beginning of first semester, and immediately following the examination period in second semester.

title: The Digital Economy
description: The Internet has fundamentally reshaped the global economy, and with it our experiences as workers and consumers. In this unit, you will come to understand the dynamics of the digital economy, including the importance of platforms, networks, attention, and growth. You will also explore alternative economic models facilitated by the Internet, such as the gift economy. This unit will provide you with a nuanced perspective on how the economy has changed over recent decades, why it matters, and what might happen next.

title: Nutrition Communication
description: This unit will ask the emerging nutritionist to explore effective nutrition communication methods within the current media and societal landscape. Student nutritionists will consolidate their discipline knowledge and sociocultural awareness to develop and deliver tailored communication for a range of audiences and channels. Skills relating to the translation of nutrition science and evidence evaluation will be further developed. This unit will also explore themes relating to the communication of nutrition science within a framework of professional identity, leadership and scope of practice.

title: Digital Culture and Everyday Life
description: For many people, everyday life now involves constant interaction with the Internet via digitally networked platforms and devices. As cyberspace and real space come together, it can be easy to miss the impacts of the Internet on us and on our society and culture. Students will explore how their own experiences and ‘everyday Internet’ may be different from others, and the implications of this for studying digital culture. Through specific topics such as entertainment, politics, sex, and relationships students will analyse digital culture conceptually, towards better understanding how technology and society are intertwined.

title: Creative Documentary and Actualities
description: The unit examines the history, practices and narrative forms of non‑fiction media texts with a specific focus on documentary film. Major historical and current trends in the creative treatment of actuality in documentary and factual production are identified and critiqued; the impact of digital technologies in the development of hybridism and nonlinear forms blurring traditional distinctions between fiction/non‑fiction texts are also studied in connection with current critical discourse and new models of distribution. Students will research, develop and produce creative documentary screen projects, as well as examining and practising a number of documentary specific techniques and approaches.

title: Resources, Processes and Materials Engineering
description: This unit introduces the whole-of-life cycle of resources and the underlying flow of materials, established and emerging, from their origins on to extraction, processing, selecting, applying and disposal. The unit approaches engineering decision making regarding resources as an ethical and technical systems-thinking process. A key ability that students should gain on completing this unit is to select potential materials for a given application, accounting for the suitability of their properties as well as their impact on society and the environment. Material and energy balances are introduced to quantify the resources consumed in the chemical, metallurgical, physical and biological processes associated with transforming resources and energy into end products. The origin and extraction, physical and chemical processing, sustainable use and disposal of resources are illustrated with case studies of different resources encountered across engineering disciplines, for example: metals and alloys, polymers, glasses, ceramics and composites. Foundational experiments spanning chemical processes, material properties and metallurgy support the syllabus. Assessments provide opportunities to demonstrate academic integrity and communication skills.

title: Supply Chain Logistics
description: Management decision-making involves coordinating material, information flow across the supply chain and current leading-edge thinking on logistics. Effective, efficient and insightful examination of supply chain as a whole by meeting end-customer demand helps understand the relative importance of logistics performance objectives. Key concepts that will be examined includes the circular economy, globalisation, end-to-end supply chains, logistics networks and sustainability. Analytical and simulation tools and techniques will also be applied to inform decisions that may improve the value and cross-functional involvement of a company.

title: Crude Oil Processing
description: Introduction to crude oil processing, Two phase seperators, Three phase seperators, Emulsion Treatment and Dehydration, Desalting of Crude Oil, Stablization and sweetening, Storage tanks, Produced Water Treatment, Choosing a Line Size and Wall Thickness, Organizing the project, Flow Assurance, Flow in wells & pipes.

title: Assessment in Secondary Schools
description: Educational assessment and evaluation. The importance of reliable and valid assessment practices in secondary schools.

title: Mental Health Law and Ethics
description: Students will need to be able to differentiate between Westminster Law and the Mental Health Law from a mental health context, and identify consumer's key rights and responsibilities, examine ethical practice and apply professional ways of working, and identify the importance of diversity within an Aboriginal context and when working with multidisciplinary teams. The unit also examines and explores the ethical principles of autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, justice, fairness and truthfulness, in the context of the practitioner's role and the care they will deliver.

title: Behavioural Science for Indigenous Mental Health Practitioners
description: An introduction to the primary features of the brain, circulatory, respiratory, and nervous systems and their relationship to mental health wellness. The nine areas of Behavioural Science are explored from a cultural, social, behavioural and Indigenous perspective.

title: Crisis Intervention, Self-Harm and Suicide Prevention
description: Application of understanding of recovery-focused suicide prevention and recovery-reframing whilst focusing on different aspects of care and recognising and responding to consumers who may be experiencing suicidal thoughts and demonstrating self-harm.

title: Indigenous Australian Community Practice
description: The role of Indigenous practitioners in the promotion of Indigenous self-determination and empowerment. Consolidation of Indigenous Community Management Development and Indigenous Community Health practitioner skills. Use of Indigenous Terms of Reference and Ways of Working to achieve best practice. Peer review and Professional Development Group.

title: Working in Indigenous Australian Contexts
description: Explores culturally appropriate ways of engaging with Indigenous individuals, groups, communities and organisations, including working with Indigenous Australian people in traditional and contemporary contexts, socio-economic issues, experiences of institutional systems, ways of promoting self-determination, empowerment and reconciliation.

title: Applied Anatomical Practice
description: This unit provides an opportunity for students to focus on selected aspects of human anatomy and to develop skills in prosection. In addition, students will be challenged to consider the role of human anatomy in scientific inquiry, and its importance in a real world context.

title: Health and Wellbeing in Older People
description: Global and national context of ageing and associated implications for health; changes associated with ageing; 	perspectives of ageing, including ageism and stigma; cultural diversity in ageing; communication and health challenges for the older person; interprofessional care; holistic nursing assessment and best practice interventions relevant to well being (physical, mental and psychosocial); also including reference to cognitive status; care 	continuum, including community, institutional and transition car; philosophy of nursing care, including palliative, person and family centred approaches; ethical and legal concerns related to the older person.

title: Microbes and Disease
description: In this unit students will develop advanced knowledge of the microorganisms involved in infectious diseases, with a focus on molecular evolution and how it contributes to the emergence and re- emergence of bacterial and viral pathogens with increased antimicrobial resistance and virulence. Modern sequence-based analyses of microbial pathogenesis which offers new insights and solutions for the surveillance, prevention and control of infectious diseases will also be studied. The unit focuses on infection control and prevention strategies for bacterial and viral infections transmitted through multiple routes. Students will have the opportunity to gain additional practical knowledge and microbiology laboratory experience.

title: Education Project
description: This unit provides an opportunity for students to study a topic of educational significance that is not covered in the existing available education units, or to examine a specific topic from the course at greater depth. Projects could also be based on an experience that the student is undertaking such as volunteering abroad or in the community. A negotiated program of study is established either for an individual student or a group of students. Students will review relevant literature and resources related to the topic to produce a negotiated outcome such as a written report or presentation. This final product will include students’ reflection on their learning and implications for educational practice.

title: Clinical Practice in Speech Pathology Honours 1
description: Students in this unit will undertake Speech Pathology Clinical Practice to develop competency according to Speech Pathology Australia Competency-Based Occupational Standards (CBOS). This unit will facilitate the development of skills in the management of paediatric or adult clients across a range of practice areas.

title: Clinical Practice in Speech Pathology Honours 2
description: Students in this unit will undertake Speech Pathology Clinical Practice to develop competency according to Speech Pathology Australia Competency-Based Occupational Standards (CBOS). This unit will facilitate the development of skills in the management of paediatric or adult clients across a range of practice areas.

title: Professional Practice in Secondary Education 3
description: Evaluation of models of classroom management. Behaviour management theories. Development of a classroom management plan. Legal responsibilities of the teacher. Students will complete an extended school placement.

title: Computer Project 2
description: Supervised investigation of a problem in the computing field or in the application of computers. Development and implementation of a solution and presentation of a written report. The principles of project management applied to the conduct of the project with attention to scheduling and documentation.

title: Design Technology
description: This unit introduces students to the use of design technologies to solve design tasks. The unit examines the relationship between technology, design and application. Technology relevant to students’ major area of design study is introduced allowing them to creatively explore the process and the resulting impact on aesthetics, and function.

title: Honours Research in Speech Pathology 1
description: Students will begin advanced research methodology in human communication disorders and science. Students will undertake a comprehensive review of pertinent literature and submit a research proposal. Approval from the HREC is required for all research projects in this unit.

title: Professional Practice in Secondary Education 2
description: The social dynamics of learning environments. The impact of teaching styles on the classroom learning environment. Promoting a classroom climate conducive to social and cognitive development of students.

title: Foundations of Food Microbiology
description: This unit examines the source, types, growth and effects of microbes in food and their impact on food quality and safety; food spoilage and preservation; sterilisation, disinfection and sanitation relevant to food production; microbial intoxications and infectious diseases transmitted in food and water; effluent and wastewater treatment from food production facilities; use of predictive microbiology to determine safe storage and distribution of food.

title: Nursing Honours Proposal Preparation
description: Submission of a research proposal in a nursing clinical problem. Students, in consultation with supervisor and committee, crticially review the literature and develop, the methodology for the study. Proposal preparation for submission for school review.

title: Special Topics in Architecture Construction and Planning
description: Special topics relating to the built environment, building on previous studies in areas of student interest.

title: Asian Religion and Philosophy
description: An exploration of Asia's major religions and philosophies, such as Hinduism, Buddhism, Sikhism, Taoism, Islam, Christianity, Confucianism, Shinto and Shamanism, in association with social institutions. The aim of the unit is to relate social, political,cultural and environmental practices to religious views on life, after life, reincarnation, divinity, health, human nature and self, and shows how they are reflected in everyday life and social institutions. The analytical and comparative approach aims to increase 'literacy' in Asian societies and cultures.

title: Technologies to Engage Learners
description: Ways in which information and communication technologies impact upon learning and teaching. The knowledge and skills to use a range of software and hardware technologies effectively in educational contexts. Approaches to the utilisation, development and evaluation of digital educational resources.

title: Curriculum and Instruction in Upper Secondary Languages
description: Introduction to local and national perspectives on upper secondary curriculum. Critical analysis and evaluation of language documents. Curriculum planning processes. Micro-teaching - planning, teaching and evaluating lessons. Teaching for diversity of learners' needs.

title: Honours Research in Speech Pathology 2
description: Advanced research methodology in human communication disorders and science. The conduct of supervised original research project and written and oral communication of research.

title: Go Global - Internship 1
description: This unit provides students with internship opportunities in becoming job-ready graduates. Students in courses without professional work experience are strongly encouraged to enrol in this unit.

title: Go Global - Internship 3
description: This unit provides students with internship opportunities in becoming job-ready graduates. Students in courses without professional work experience are strongly encouraged to enrol in this unit.

title: Honours Research Project Skills
description: Searching quality evidence, using software and reference management systems; systematic literature searching, reviewing the literature relating to an area of interest within clinical practice; principles of scientific writing; classifying evidence, concept mapping, structured planning, ethical standards and research project planning

title: Rock Art, Archaeology and Antiquity
description: This unit encourages a study of Aboriginal perspectives of Rock Art and Archaeological sites.
