Students will explore contemporary research in this field descriptive of the Aboriginal voice which creates a living narrative of Aboriginal cultural practices from time immemorial until the present. The unit explains the importance of understanding the continuity of Aboriginal ontologies and the very fabric of the interrelatedness of Indigenous ownership, with Indigenous spiritual feeling for Country. The unit describes evidence of long time occupation, heritage and cultural practices.

title: Physiology in Extreme Conditions
description: This unit examines how human physiology adapts and responds to extreme environmental conditions. It looks at the effects of heat, cold, high altitude, high pressure, and gravity on physiology. Physiological responses such as acclimatisation and adaptation as well as human variability are studied. Factors affecting the ability to perform work under extreme conditions and tolerance limits for humans are examined.

title: Multiphase Flow in Porous Media
description: This unit will provide students with a comprehensive overview of the physics of multiphase flow in porous media and their relevance and applications in various real-life situations. The unit begins with a detailed discussion of Darcy’s Law and applications, wettability, interfacial phenomenon, capillary pressure, gravity effects, relative permeabilities and residual saturations. The implications of these basic but important concepts for fluid distribution in porous media for a range of scenarios -such as oil and gas extraction and CO2 geo-sequestration, will also be discussed. The unit will then present a more detailed discussion of the dynamics of fluid flow in porous media by introducing and solving Radial Diffusivity Equation (RDE) under a series of realistic conditions relevant to the extraction/injection of fluids. Subsequently, the unit will discuss the concept of fractional flow and Buckley-Leverett Theory and elaborate on how the end results may be analytically extended and upscaled to more realistic multidimensional/heterogeneous systems. Finally, an overview of the uncertainties to consider while attempting to forecast the performance of a fluid-fluid displacement in porous media over the intermediate to long term will be presented.

title: Facilitating Indigenous Community Education
description: Facilitate participatory inquiry, learning and education in Indigenous settings using culturally appropriate methods and processes. Provide background information about local issues to engage community members in the learning and development process. Develop, integrate and apply conceptual frameworks and skills related to learning about local issues in a community setting.

title: Educating Adolescents: Diversity and Inclusion
description: The focus of this unit is on building on previous knowledge to further understand the characteristics of adolescent development that impact teaching and learning in a classroom setting. This examination will lead to the development of pedagogical strategies designed to maximise the outcomes of a diverse range of adolescent learners. On completion of this unit students will have developed a portfolio of practical strategies and professional resources upon which to draw when they are educating adolescents.

title: Unconventional Threats and Conflict
description: This unit introduces students to a relatively new paradigm of current and emerging risks and threats to national security, ranging from organised crime, globalised terrorism and insurgency, to political warfare and how it destabilises international political and security environments. Students will gain an in-depth understanding of the current and future spectrum of conflict, unconventional ways of using force as part of multi-domain warfighting (hybrid warfare), and its application across the so-called “grey zones”; the factor of deception in contemporary strategic, foreign and defence policies conduct, and its role in current and future operations.

title: Engineering Sustainable Development
description: Sustainable development is about forms of progress that combine economic development, social advancement, environmental protection and is widely recognised by the public, private and civic sectors as one of the key challenges for the 21st century. Deals with the contribution of engineering to the development and implementation of sustainable solutions. Introduction to the sustainable development agenda. Practical methods and tools for development and implementation of sustainable solutions which complement generic 'good engineering and management practice'. Introduction to sustainable technology development.

title: Mechatronics Modelling Project
description: Topics of modelling, experimentation and simulation using problem based learning to solve problems in the context of a mechatronic system. The tasks which students complete in this unit provide opportunities to solve “open”, rather than “closed” problems.  The “open” problem of this unit is to develop a model that predicts the time for a simple mechatronic vehicle to ascend an incline.  The syllabus requires the student to actively participate and seek out “better” answers. Solving open mechatronic engineering problems and using system principles: hierarchies and abstractions.  Problem analysis, design and creation of models and experiments. Reoccuring Modelling concepts: elements and governing equations. Engineering Communications.  Experiment theory and design to determine stall torque and torque-speed characteristics of a DC motor including applications of Newton’s Laws to dynamic systems. Applications of electromagnetics and efficiency concepts.  Use of computer tools Excel and Simulink for modelling and analysis.  System response: concepts of transient and steady state behaviour.  Results anaylsis.

title: Strategic Analysis Project
description: This project-based unit offers an opportunity to explore in detail some of the challenges previously considered within the Strategic Studies Major. Students will gain experience in creating major intelligence products as part of their education and professional training. This supervised project may be undertaken individually or as part of a research team.

title: Geotechnical Design and Construction
description: This unit covers the design, construction and modelling of deep foundations and earth retaining structures, including single and group pile foundations, flexible and ridged retaining walls, mechanically stabilised walls, braced excavations and ground improvement.

title: Advanced Computer Communications
description: Computer network applications rapidly develop with the massive proliferation use of the internet in the world. The unit describes the overview of the Internet Protocol (IP), Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), User Diagram Protocol (UDP) and Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP). The students will learn the conceptual and programming of network applications in TCP/UDP/SCTP/IP environments using sockets. The students will have hands-on experience in writing client-server network program using TCP and UDP sockets, input/output multiplexing, socket options, name and address conversions, process/thread, and client-server design alternatives. The unit also covers some Peer-to-Peer (P2P) applications as well as their distributed protocols.

title: Physiotherapy Leadership
description: This unit will provide emerging practitioners with an understanding of the key management and leadership competencies employed in the delivery of physiotherapy services contextualised within the Australian Health Care system.

title: Physiotherapy Honours Research
description: This unit develops skills to undertake quantitative and/or qualitative research.

title: Physiotherapy Honours Dissertation
description: This unit further develops skills to undertake quantitative and/or qualitative research.

title: Interprofessional Practice
description: This unit covers the integration of clinical knowledge in inter-professional teams, using case-based workshop scenarios. The topics will include areas critical to care provision such as palliative care, chronic disease, neurological conditions, altered mental health. In addition, reflective practice is facilitated during concurrent clinical placement experiences, encouraging self-exploration of student experiences beyond surface level descriptive narratives.

title: Evidence Based Practice in Physiotherapy
description: This unit covers the skills in applying evidence-based practice to clinical issues including ethical considerations. Accessing and searching electronic databases.

title: Mineral Processing
description: The aim of this unit is to familiarise students with mineral processing in order to converse with industry as chemical engineers.  Students will be introduced to the formation and occurrence of economically important minerals, making the distinction between separation efficiency and economic efficiency.  Representative solid sampling and particle size distribution will be investigated.  Students will learn about various ore dressing operations such as comminution, sizing and sorting, jigging, tabling, flotation, and magnetic and electrostatic separations.  Typical problem-solving related to solids balancing and size separation in grinding circuits will be presented.  A group project involving evaluation of various separation processes for beneficiation of minerals, such as electrolysis, electrowinning, leaching, solvent extraction, precipitation and by reaction, will be undertaken.  The application of gas-sold reaction models in pyro-metallurgical extraction (roasting) will be examined.  Typical examples from the local mineral processing industry will be presented throughout the unit.

title: Sports Media Production
description: This is a practical unit in which students will build on the skills acquired in their Screen Production course. Students will work collaboratively with a community sports organisation to produce a quality media product. The unit will focus on the development of professional standard production skills and advanced project planning skills. The opportunity for feedback is regularly provided when students meet with mentors to discuss production standards, students’ professional practice and to share workplace experiences with their peers. Students develop team-work capabilities, communication skills and production skills to enhance their confidence and employability.

title: Visual Narrative Studio
description: In this unit students will work collaboratively on cross-disciplinary projects to construct engaging visual narratives. Students will work with illustrators, creative writers, filmmakers, animation and game designers to develop visual narrative content and apply skills in animation design, game design, screen writing and visual development. Storytelling techniques and strategies will be explored considering emerging cultures, cyber-cultures, global cultures and Indigenous cultures in order to promote and preserve local and international cultures across various platforms.

title: Advanced Animation
description: This unit provides students with an opportunity to further develop their skills and conceptual approach in the areas of animation, 3D and motion graphics. It encourages students to explore established conventions, visual styles, animation techniques, audio design, narrative structures, and screen language in their own work.

title: Introduction to 3D Modelling and Rendering
description: This unit introduces students to the foundations of 3D modelling, texturing and rendering in a digital environment. It enables students to work on a defined multi-phase project that encompasses the conceptual and technical elements that are fundamental to 3D design.

title: Exercise and Sports Science Honours Preparation
description: Fundamental competencies to enable students to develop an appreciation of the ethics and principles of research and research design; critically appraise and interpret scientific literature; as well as develop skills in planning and writing a research proposal.

title: Web Design 1
description: This unit introduces students to the concepts, skills and toolsets required to understand and apply user-focus design for the web. Students will create a basic website that employs current web design standards. By synthesising web usability theory with a project-centred approach, students will develop and iterate on their designs to produce a website that effectively addresses a design brief.

title: Digital FX Production
description: An introduction to the skills and concepts required to implement effective editing and other post-production techniques including: digital visual effects, colour grading, audio mixing and sound design, and advanced editing techniques. These are essential components of many contemporary media productions, both for small screen and web-media productions, as well as documentary and dramatic video works. This unit concentrates on enhancing the production value of screen productions, addressing post-production and digital effects at the planning and scripting phase. The unit covers planning and post-production skills involved in generating emotional and aesthetic effect, audio recording and manipulation to generate immersion, as well as introduces essential compositing skills such as advanced “blue-screen” chroma key work, motion tracking, object replacement, as well as the integration of graphics and stock footage to simulate advanced practical effects such as fire, smoke and explosions.

title: Law for Engineers
description: Introduction to the law and Engineering standards. The Australian legal system. Contract law. Tenders. Law of negligence. Intellectual property law copyright, patents and designs. Occupational, safety and health. Employment or Environmental law.

title: Creative Writing
description: An introductory creative writing unit leading to completed examples of the student's own prose, poetry and writing for performance.

title: Agribusiness Capstone 2
description: This is a capstone unit, drawing on all units studied in the course. Students will gain an understanding of the role of engagement and communication in sustainable agricultural and agribusiness development across the triple bottom line. Students will use the theory, techniques and skills necessary for facilitating change in rural communities, people and businesses.

title: Community Media Production
description: This unit enables students to tell visual stories that either effect social change, or deliver an original visual idea. Students will work collaboratively with not for profit community organisations on an approved project to create media content in an authentic, professional environment.

title: Publishing Studio
description: This unit provides students with the opportunity to apply their existing knowledge and skills in order to publish real books, by real authors, for real readers. Depending on the books accepted for publication, where these books are in the publishing process, and the skills and interests of individual students, the unit will vary from semester to semester, as well as from student to student. Nonetheless, every student will be involved in at least two of the following publishing processes: acquisitions, editorial, design, print production, digital production, marketing, and sales. Students will also learn about project management, collaborative problem-solving, financial planning, brand development, social media marketing, and more, as these are all required to operate a real publishing house. The skills developed and practised in this unit are transferrable to a wide variety of industries and workplaces. The Work-Integrated Learning (WIL) approach used in this unit represents a blend of curricular and workplace learning – of theory and practice – which is used to achieve outcomes that meet the needs and expectations of both a diverse student body and the diverse industries that employ students majoring in Professional Writing and Publishing.

title: Introduction to Creative and Professional Writing
description: This unit explores representation in writing and how the dynamic relationship between Self and Other plays a central role in the writing process. The representation of the self and of others is central to a broad range of written genres and forms. Students of writing will find that the unit introduces them to a variety of genres and forms essential to the portfolio of a professional writer, and will discover how creative writing techniques can enrich their professional work.

title: Business Engagement
description: The aim of this unit is to examine contemporary issues in business within a managerial framework. You will apply business skills and knowledge to industry based problems. For each contemporary business issue, you will examine industry and academic literature to identify and analyse the problem(s), and apply critical and creative thinking to develop recommendations.

title: Writing Short Fiction
description: An intermediate unit in the theory and practice of writing short prose fiction. Emphasis on critical workshop discussion leading to completed examples of the students own work. The curriculum further encourages an appreciation of language through textual consideration and the practice of creative writing, including drafting and editing.

title: Writing Long Fiction
description: An advanced unit which examines the techniques and problems involved in writing long fiction - specifically the long story, the novella and the novel. Students look at the work of a variety of fiction writers from the point of view of the writer who wants to learn how the authors of particular works succeeded. Students devise and carry out their own writing projects in long fiction.

title: Advanced Studio Production
description: Further development of skills and understanding of multi-camera and studio based production in a practical, production-orientated environment. Students will engage in weekly skills development sessions in which they will undertake a range of production roles, including director, director's assistant, floor manager, lighting, camera, technical director and staging. Both single and multi-camera production skills will be put into a practical context by students in the production of a series of programs for broadcast. Opportunities for cultural and interdisciplinary engagement will be encouraged.

title: Editing
description: This unit provides a practical introduction to editing. Students learn about the editor’s role and profession, the publishing process, and editorial project management; and they learn and practice the skills needed for professional proofreading and copyediting, including language skills, on the page and the screen. Student learning is graduated through a series of successively higher-level editing tasks, which students practice thoroughly in workshops, and are assessed in before moving to a higher level.

title: Devising Fundamentals
description: This unit introduces both practical and theoretical approaches to understanding and creating contemporary theatre specifically focussing on devising. Students will incorporate practical processes and theoretical material to gain a critical understanding of devising techniques and processes and will apply them to the rehearsal and presentation of an original devised work. Attending performances at the Hayman Theatre will be central to the experience of this unit. Students will apply the processes and skills of contemporary theatre practitioners to the rehearsal and presentation of an original devised work. They will extend their performance practice through active participation in the Hayman Theatre Company performance season and will attend a variety of performance pieces. They will develop a critical mind enabling them to offer sophisticated critique and analysis of their own and a range of different theatre-making processes.

title: Game Design Introduction
description: This unit invites students to consider the design, structure, functionality and application of games and gaming. The unit presents various ways to consider game elements including as virtual environments, toys, narrative engines, sets of algorithmic rules, simulations. There is a primary focus on digitally mediated games, especially those that leverage three dimensional modelling and rendering. Students will undertake critical analysis of existing games, as well as explore the potential for game creation through the design and conceptualisation of their own games.

title: The International Baccalaureate in Action
description: This unit builds on the work covered in the previous International Baccalaureate units. It addresses the values of the teacher award schemes and the Domains of Knowledge relating to the International Baccalaureate Primary and Middle Years Programme. The focus is on student examining their own professional practice based on the Domains of Knowledge. The evaluation of the relevant International Baccalaureate programme is also addressed.

title: International Baccalaureate Primary Years Programme
description: This unit builds on the work covered in the Introduction to the International Baccalaureate Programme unit. It provides an overview to the key theories and principles relating to the International Baccalaureate Primary Years Programme. There is a focus on transdisciplinary themes and planning and assessing programmes of inquiry.

title: Digital Portfolio Development
description: In this unit, students will develop a professional portfolio as the culmination of their undergraduate study. This portfolio will collate students' best project work into a professionally presented portfolio and online presence in preparation for a final exhibition presentation to industry. The portfolio will highlight an ability to implement a range of fully resolved and deliverable folio pieces, as well as function as a public showcase of work. By consolidating and synthesising the knowledge, skills and awareness garnered from previous semesters, students will present a portfolio using cross-disciplinary approaches that exhibit their potential in the discipline field.

title: Secondary Professional Experience 1: Planning
description: This is the first in the suite of professional experience units and includes both a theory and a practical component (a placement in a school). The unit explores philosophies and theories related to teaching and then introduces the nature and role of effective planning for a diverse groups of learners. Specific attention is given to lesson planning that includes selecting objectives and appropriate teaching, learning, assessment strategies and resources. The unit also addresses professional responsibilities, effective communication and reflective practices to support learning. The professional experience practical assessment is a 2 week full-time block placement intended to enable practical application of the knowledge and skills gained, along with providing students with insights into the complexity of the teacher’s role. All required clearances to work with children must be obtained and valid, and all other professional experience requirements met. Both theory and practical components must be passed in order to pass the unit.

title: Writing for Children
description: An advanced, special topic in writing for children leading to the production of marketable concepts for works of children's literature.

title: Energy Engineering Design Project
description: Energy engineering design project is a multi-disciplinary unit, which involves thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, energy systems, energy storage, energy conservation, management and environment with consideration for social and sustainable aspects. Both low emission energy and renewable energy resources such as solar, wind, and geothermal energy and related topics will be covered. This design project will highlight the integration of an energy system including energy production, transmission, transportation, storage and utilization. The main objective of energy engineering design project is to equip students with design experience in a customer oriented setting where required to specify and integrate the energy system, satisfying the customer’s demand and specification. The final solutions of the design project involves the selections of an integrated energy system from real-world vendors, such as a real wind turbine, solar farm, pipelines and storage facilities. Therefore, students would have experience in solving a real world design-type problems in an industrial setting rather than solving standard textbook style problems.

title: Writing Poetry
description: An intermediate unit on the theory and practice of writing poetry. An appreciation of language through textual consideration and the practice of creative writing, including drafting and editing.

title: Introduction to Screenwriting
description: The unit examines screenwriting techniques and practices in how to develop and create a narrative screenplay for drama production.

title: Reading Screens
description: An intermediate level unit that explores the history and theory of screen arts with an emphasis on semiotic analysis.

title: Drama Narratives
description: Students will study a variety of drama film styles and narrative screen forms in order to understand and critique a range of creative and filmic approaches to drama production. These investigations will inform the development and production of their own drama screen projects. Students will engage with a variety of technical, operational and aesthetic conventions and practices used in the concept development and production of screen drama.

title: Voice for the Actor
description: This unit develops awareness of vocal strengths, weaknesses and habits and explores a range of exercises to help develop the performer’s voice. Students will also apply vocal technique to spoken language, verse and dialogue.

title: Agribusiness Capstone 1
description: This is a capstone unit, drawing on all units studied in the course with the development of a professional quality business plan as a tangible outcome. The planning will encompass management processes for analysing agribusiness systems, including assessment of risk and evaluation of options. The unit requires students to link with agribusiness enabling development of the business plan.

title: Mental Health Research Project
description: Evaluate research design, practice and outcomes. Facilitation of Critical Reference Group (CRG) and other stakeholders to develop and implement evaluation research recommendations. Application of Indigenous Terms of Reference to overcome structural impacts on community practice. Produce findings and recommendations for future action and policy development. Examine issues central to the representation of Indigenous people in research. Consider implications for own evaluation role as an Indigenous Community practitioner.

title: Studio Production
description: Creative development of practical multi-camera and single-camera skills and an understanding of studio based production in a practical, production-oriented environment. Students work collaboratively in authentic industry roles to produce a television project.

title: Narrative Nonfiction
description: This unit introduces you to narrative nonfiction, including its role and significance in telling true stories and reflecting contemporary issues. You will explore, analyse, and experiment with a range of written narrative nonfiction forms including feature articles and flash nonfiction. The aim of the unit is to provide you with a critical understanding of the influence of narrative nonfiction in contemporary life, to provide practice in writing in a variety of forms, and to enhance awareness of changing genres, styles, and issues.

title: Web Design 2
description: This unit introduces students to more advanced concepts, skills and toolsets required to design and construct intermediate websites which feature enhanced interactivity and engagement, while maintaining a high level of user-friendliness. It builds on the foundations set in the preceding unit, Web Design 1, and extends that knowledge with workflows into modern front-end development methodologies.

title: Applied Paramedic Bioscience 4
description: This is the final bioscience unit in the paramedicine curriculum, designed to bring together students’ understanding of clinical theory and management principles. Like previous units, this unit takes an integrated, systems-based approach to learning, where pathophysiology, diagnostic strategies, and pharmacology are taught concurrently through their application to real-world case studies. Students will begin by consolidating their biomedical knowledge with patient-centred and culturally safe care to address obstetric conditions commonly managed by paramedics. Building on this foundation, they will apply their cumulative knowledge to complex and/or less frequently encountered clinical cases. Emphasis is placed on discussing the aetiology, pathophysiology, and clinical manifestations of conditions commonly managed by paramedics, selecting and interpreting diagnostic strategies, and understanding pharmacotherapeutics and the quality use of medicines. Students will apply the critical thinking skills developed throughout their studies to critically appraise primary evidence and clinical standards, focusing on how these align with or challenge current paramedic practice to develop evidence-based, person-centred, and culturally safe management strategies.

title: Writing Genre Fiction
description: An intermediate unit in theory and practice of writing short prose fiction. The particular genres studied depend on availability of staff. Emphasis on critical workshop discussion leading to completed examples of the student's own work

title: Advanced Narrative Nonfiction
description: Narrative non-fiction is a hybrid of literature and non-fiction. It includes narrative non-fiction, memoir, personal essay and literary journalism, and combines the diligence of the journalist, the analysis of the essayist, and the story telling techniques of the novelist. The genre encompasses a broad range of topics in which the narrative events and experiences are used to explore more complex themes and issues, and in which ethical and cross-cultural issues are addressed. In this unit, you will read and analyse works of narrative non-fiction and write an original work of your own.

title: Creative Documentary and Actualities
description: The unit examines the history, practices and narrative forms of non‑fiction media texts with a specific focus on documentary film. Major historical and current trends in the creative treatment of actuality in documentary and factual production are identified and critiqued; the impact of digital technologies in the development of hybridism and nonlinear forms blurring traditional distinctions between fiction/non‑fiction texts are also studied in connection with current critical discourse and new models of distribution. Students will research, develop and produce creative documentary screen projects, as well as examining and practising a number of documentary specific techniques and approaches.

title: Animation Design Introduction
description: The unit introduces students to the principles of spatial and temporal design by focusing on animation fundamentals. Students develop conceptual understanding through the completion of two of the most fundamental and classic animation exercises - making a ball bounce, and creating a walk cycle using sophisticated animation software tools. A third project introduces students to the narrative potential of animation.

title: Publishing
description: This unit provides advanced practical editing instruction, and allows students to build on existing knowledge and skills. They learn and practice the skills of editing to a real-world publishing project in which project management skills, high-level editing skills, and professional writing skills are utilised. The capacity to work independently and collaboratively to take a written text from submission to publication is developed. Students also learn to analyse and reflect on issues relevant to contemporary publishing industries.

title: Secondary Professional Experience 3: Using Data to Inform Teaching and Learning
description: This is the third in the suite of professional experience units and includes both a theory and a practical component (a placement in a school). This unit focuses on principles, processes and impacts of classroom, school level and system data collection, analysis and interpretation. Data relevant to Indigenous educational outcomes will be interrogated, emphasising an evidentiary approach to program and policy development in classrooms, schools and beyond. The professional experience practical assessment is a three week full-time block placement intended to enable practical application of the knowledge and skills gained. All required clearances to work with children must be obtained and valid, and all other professional experience requirements met. Both theory and practical components must be passed in order to pass the unit.

title: Agribusiness Risk Management
description: Students will learn strategies for managing production, price, financial, legal, human and technological risk. Students will apply industry standard frameworks and methodologies to assess and control risk in agribusiness. Students will develop an understanding of commodity trading and hedging. Government and institutional policies and their implications for risk management are introduced.

title: Experimental Screens
description: Introduction to the history, theory and practice of experimental and avant garde screen arts.

title: Introduction to Screen Practice
description: Introduction to national and global cinematic and broadcast industries. Students study historical and contemporary business models and screen audiences while simultaneously developing their professional practice, technical and teamwork skills as creators of screen works. This unit combines critical studies and creative practice through action/reflection and production/analysis tasks.

title: Experimental Writing
description: An intermediate unit in the theory and practice of creative writing with a particular emphasis on contemporary avant-garde poetics and other experimental forms.

title: Commerce Consultancy/Internship Advanced
description: In this unit you will demonstrate mastery of the theory and practice of your discipline by applying knowledge and skills to a real-world experience whilst developing career readiness. You will undertake an internship or take on the role as a consultant to an organisation and analyse a business problem or issue, create solutions, and provide recommendations. You will experience how key innovations and emerging trends in business practice play an important role in enabling business change and reviving organisations.

title: Electrical Plant
description: Three-phase circuits. Reactive power and power factor correction. Transformers. Single and three-phase induction motors. Electric motors: starting, speed control, and motor selection. Condition monitoring in process plants.

title: Mechanical Engineering Research Project 2A
description: Detailed experimental or development study of process or device, or design study including laboratory and or manufacturing work. (Normally undertaken individually with provisions made for group projects. Students choose projects relating to local industry).

title: Introduction to Screen Creativity
description: Introduction to classical and contemporary screen genres and methods of screen appreciation, including fiction and non-fiction modes of film making. This unit combines critical studies and creative practice through action/reflection and production/analysis tasks.

title: Design of Mechanical Components
description: This unit gives a brief introduction to many aspects of mechanical design. Topics include load analysis, equilibrium and free body diagrams, deflection and stiffness, energy absorption, three dimensional stress and combined stresses, and Mohr’s circle representation. Stress concentration factors and residual stresses are also considered, along with column buckling, impact loading, failure theories and introduction to fatigue failure. Finally, students will be introduced to the concept of safety factors, and a brief analysis of threaded fasteners and power screws, and design of welded joints subjected to static loading.

title: Introduction to Agribusiness Management
description: Students will be introduced to management theory and the management cycle as it applied to agricultural production and agribusiness. Students will gain knowledge on budgeting and accounting techniques for agricultural production and financial management and apply these to relevant case studies. The unit will include an introduction to agricultural production economics.

title: Major Project Pre-production
description: This unit builds on previously acquired skills in production and screen studies, deepening application, evaluative and creative practices to select and develop a major screen project ready for production in semester two. Students will demonstrate that they are ready for the major drama, documentary or broadcast project in line with funding applications in industry, developing script, pre-production planning and budget, individual crew portfolio support and a finished pilot scene.

title: Fundamentals of Air Pollution Control
description: Introduction to air pollution; Chemistry of air pollution; Effects of air pollution; Air pollutants from industrial processes; Transport of air pollutants; Indoor air pollution; Air pollution measurements and analytical techniques; Air pollution laws and regulations and the emission standards; Air pollutant concentration models; Air pollution control; Future of air pollution.

title: Agribusiness and Farm Management
description: This unit covers the processes of planning, implementation, management and control of agriculture and associated agribusiness industries. Students will undertake analysis, implementation and monitoring of existing strategies and tactics for enterprises and associated activities in agribusiness. Students will apply these principles to benchmark agribusiness data.

title: UX Design 2
description: In this unit students explore advanced user experience (UX) methodologies, such as design sprints and industry-aligned research and testing methods. Building on foundational skills, they develop innovative design solutions that integrate new technologies while maintaining a user-centric approach. This unit empowers students to create impactful and meaningful solutions in the digital landscape.

title: Business and Law International Study Abroad 3
description: International mobility experience for undergraduate students.

title: Professional Engineering Practice
description: This is a unit to develop awareness for student of the Engineering Profession, covering professional behaviour and image. Professional institutions and qualifications are introduced and after graduation activities such as recruitment and career progression are practised. Communications skills are developed, with emphasis on negotiation and presentation techniques. Occupational health and safety is covered and specifically assessed. There is a focus on leadership, technological change and marketing with a view to preparation for future careers. Group presentations are an integral part of the syllabus.

title: Australian Health and Political Systems
description: This unit involves the exploration of the Australian  political system including separation of powers, levels of government and political process. Through the examination of major state and federal health systems and policies the unit analyses the impact of the Australian political system and Indigenous political representation, sovereignty and self-determination for Indigenous Australians.

title: Indigenous Cultural Study Tour 1
description: This unit develops knowledge and understanding of the Indigenous communities and their challenges in comparison to environmental and social challenges faced by Indigenous communities. Enabling the mapping of the contemporary political and economic landscape, especially in terms of how relationships between nations, states, and the local communities within have been formulated and evolved over time on the basis of political exigencies, economic development precedence and cyclical policy-making priorities. Major themes covered in this unit include the origin, culture and languages of Indigenous People, Indigenous entrepreneurship, and self-determination.In this unit students are provided with the opportunity to experience Indigenous cultures and studies in an international context - observe the other First Nation Peoples landscape and be immersed in their culture. Students will reflect on culture and social norms - enhancing their ability to manage and understand concepts in a global environment.

title: Motion Graphics Design Introduction
description: This unit introduces students to the process of designing and creating motion graphics animations. A large percentage of information we see in our everyday lives is conveyed through moving graphics, particularly in television commercials, television program title sequences, movie special effects and music video clips. This unit focuses on the design process of creating motion graphics. It aims to provide a solid understanding of design principles including typography, layouts, storyboarding and aesthetics By applying these process to practical projects, students will learn skills in basic motion graphics and digital production techniques.

title: Photomedia
description: This unit introduces students to the fundamental skills, processes, materials and equipment relevant to the practice of contemporary photomedia studios. It endeavours to expose them to a range of styles and techniques, while promoting a broad use of them in traditional and experimental forums. The role of photomedia as a vital component to contemporary visual communication will be heavily emphasised.

title: Heat Transfer
description: One and two dimensional steady state heat conduction; Numerical methods; Transient heat transfer analysis and Heisler charts; Forced and natural convective heat transfer; Forced convection inside and outside tubes; Radiation heat transfer and selective surfaces, and combined mode heat transfer problems.

title: Acting
description: This unit examines the major influences on contemporary western performance relating to acting for the stage. A consideration of the approaches of key acting theorists and how they can be applied in practice will also be undertaken.

title: Complex Paramedic Professional Practice
description: This unit explores the complexities of high-threat and major incidents, including their societal impacts and the challenges they pose to personal well-being. Beginning with an overview of major incidents and the phases of emergency management, students will critically examine the roles and responsibilities of government, emergency, and non-government organisations in disaster response, focusing on interagency collaboration and the specific duties of paramedics within these organisations. Students will analyse the societal and personal impacts of major incidents, evaluating their professional and ethical responsibilities to mitigate harm while considering how disasters may affect their own well-being. The unit concludes with an exploration of historical and contemporary approaches to paramedic well-being, incorporating evidence-based strategies to build personal resilience and maintain professional capacity in high-pressure contexts.

title: Engaging Narrative
description: Narratives underpin a range of cultural artefacts. This unit explores key elements of narrative construction such as story and narration; time and space; narrating perspective and voice. It also examines the ways in which their elements function in relation to audiences and their social contexts.

title: Early Childhood Professional Experience 2: Quality Frameworks in Early Learning Centres
description: This is the second in the suite of professional experience units and includes both a theory and a practical component (a placement in an Early Learning Centre). This unit will require the practical application of curriculum and early childhood pedagogy appropriate to young children in early learning centres. Planning and implementing high quality learning experiences and supportive environments to maximise learning opportunities for infants, toddlers and young children will be a feature of this unit. The theoretical component includes roles and responsibilities, planning and programming learning environments, health and safety, fostering cognitive, language, emotional and social development, as well as observing and documenting learning. The unit will examine national and state laws and policy and the impact these have on early learning environments, families and children. Students will be provided with an opportunity to develop a leadership style through engaging with the organisational culture and professional learning community while attending a practicum in an accredited Early Learning Centre working with babies, toddlers and young children. The placement will comprise of a 1 day visit for 5 weeks aligned to five theory topics immediately followed by a block of 15 consecutive days. Students will aim to build collaborative partnerships with families and colleagues during the placement. All required clearances to work with children must be obtained and valid, and all other professional experience requirements met. Both theory and practical components must be passed in order to pass the unit.

title: Digital Design 1
description: This unit introduces students to Digital Design production processes. By leveraging case studies and investigative approaches, students will be exposed to the essential phases of informed observation, analysis, conceptualisation, production and concept iteration within the context of Digital Experience & Interaction Design.

title: MarCom Campaign Development
description: This is a campaign unit that guides students through the processes involved in developing and implementing an integrated marketing communication campaign. Specifically, students apply previously taught concepts in their Advertising Major to develop a synergistic communication plan for an industry based client. Students develop an advertising plan and have the opportunity to pitch/sell their ideas to the client and as part of this hands-on process; students justify their communication and media recommendations, Throughout the unit, students are also exposed to industry guest speakers and are provided with career mentoring to further develop their career focus and industry understanding prior to graduation.

title: DigEx Major Project 1
description: In this unit, students will build upon the skills and principles developed throughout the second year of the DigEx Major. In this 3rd year level unit, students will engage with advanced digital product design concepts and have an opportunity to synthesise them through the conceptualisation, design, iteration and development of a comprehensive digital product that addresses real-world design problems. Students will gain experience with evaluative and iterative methodologies using industry standard testing and analytics platforms to shape and inform their design approach.

title: Applied Paramedic Bioscience 3
description: This is the third of four bioscience units in the paramedicine curriculum, designed to deepen students' understanding of clinical theory and management principles. The bioscience units take an integrated, systems-based approach to learning, where pathophysiology, diagnostic strategies, and pharmacology are taught concurrently through their application to real-world case studies. In this unit, students integrate biomedical knowledge with patient-centred and culturally safe care to address common medical and toxicological conditions managed by paramedics. Emphasis is placed on discussing the aetiology, pathophysiology, and clinical manifestations of conditions commonly managed by paramedics, interpreting diagnostic strategies, and understanding pharmacotherapeutics and quality use of medicines. Students will build on their second-year critical thinking skills by critically analysing primary evidence and clinical standards, focusing on how these align with or challenge current paramedic practice to develop evidence-based, person-centred, and culturally safe management strategies.

title: Critical Infrastructure Security
description: This unit provides the information and resources needed for students to identify threads and vulnerabilities to critical infrastructure from the theft and diversion of critical resources, raw materials, and products that can be used for criminal or terrorist activities. The course also identifies actions that participants can take to reduce or prevent theft and diversion.

title: Fieldwork for Occupational Therapy 3
description: Practicum experience that meets the requirements of the World Federation of Occupational Therapists. Integration of occupational therapy theoretical frameworks. Development of essential clinical and ethical reasoning. Practical demonstration of essential skills in planning, assessment, intervention, communication, documentation and management functions.

title: Business Internship
description: Students will undertake an industry experience to gain real world experience where the major activity requires a student to work with an organisation on a business project. Under the supervision of an academic and industry professional, students will apply their learnings to a work context, enhance their professional development and employment potential. Students will spend around 20 working days undertaking their industry experience during, or between study periods. Students will develop a digital portfolio including samples of work undertaken, as well as a critical reflection of professional and personal capabilities. The experience may require students to be co-located at the business location, or at a Curtin University campus.

title: Counselling and Psychotherapy Practice
description: This unit further develops counselling skills in relation to child and adolescent, family and group dynamics. Students will explore the models and theoretical approaches to working with group processes. Attention is given to the social context of counselling dynamics within cultural contexts, and the ethical responsibilities of working within family and community systems. Students are encouraged to identify and appraise their own counselling style, limitations and biases.

title: Interactive Study Tour
description: Adopting a global mindset, students will develop knowledge and understanding of business or law in a complex international setting. The unit provides students with an authentic learning experience designed to develop strategies for dealing with current and emerging global problems. Students will also develop important skills that will enhance cross-cultural awareness, understanding and competency.

title: Mathematics and Probability Theory
description: Sequences and series leading to Taylor’s series; Multidimensional analysis 2-D to n-D functions. Curve, plane and volume parameterisation. Complex functions. Graphing functions;  2-D, 3-D, n-D calculus. Line integrals. Surface integrals. Volume integrals. Iterated integrals; Probability theory. Sample space, events and the definition of probability. Joint and conditional probabilities, Bayes’ theorem, independent events and Bernoulli trials. Discrete and continues random variables, cumulative distribution functions, probability mass functions, probability density functions. Expectations, variances, functions of random variables. Engineering applications and probability theory.

title: Precast Concrete Design and Construction
description: This unit comprises construction and manufacturing practices and design of precast and tilt-up concrete. It more broadly encompasses composite construction, prefabrication, modularisation and fast-track construction. Precast and tilt-up design, construction, building code regulations and safety issues are taught through workshops, lectures and Field Work (site visits) together with independent student research.

title: Spatial Data Modelling and Errors
description: Surveyors and other spatial scientists must always provide an assessment of the reliability of their observations and measurements, typically presented via accuracy, precision and error estimates. This unit provides the student with the tools required for such data analysis. The lectures introduce methods for quantitatively summarising large data sets of distance and angular observations. The distinction between accuracy and precision is then explored, and geostatistical tools are provided for determining the reliability of these parameters in a robust manner that would satisfy a client. The concept of modelling data is explored, once again enabling the summary of large spatial data sets. This leads, finally, to a treatment of the various error types that most commonly occur in surveying and spatial data.

title: Extended Software Metrics
description: The primary goal of this unit is to expose the students to software metrics and give them practical experience developing and using metrics programs for large software systems.

title: Introduction to the International Baccalaureate Programme
description: This unit provides an overview to the key theories and principles relating to the International Baccalaureate Primary Years Programme and International Baccalaureate Middle Years Programme. There is a focus on the fundamental concepts, learner profile and holistic learning. Issues relating to curriculum planning and assessment will be examined.

title: Systems Thinking for Regional Impact
description: With a focus on Western Australia, Systems Thinking for Regional Impact allows you to develop a systems thinking approach, and learn deep mapping techniques, to understand the pivotal role of regions when addressing the world’s most complex environmental, societal, and governance (ESG) sustainability challenges. On completion of the unit, you will be equipped with knowledge and skills to understand complex challenges and how to build partnerships with regional, rural, and remote communities and industries to co-create regenerative strategies and solutions.

title: Listening to Regions: A Place-Based Immersion into Regional WA
description: Listening to Regions provides you with a one-week immersive experience in regional Western Australia where you will tackle real-world challenges and experience work and life in a regional community. Founded on the four pillars of reciprocity, fun, experiential learning and a sense of belonging, you will travel in a group, experiencing a taste of country life through volunteering on community-driven projects, participation in community events, as well as tours of local industry and cultural experiences. The week-long road trip will be complemented by three pre-departure workshops, a separate volunteering activity, and a post-trip debrief workshop. Fostering intercultural understandings, connections, and strength-based partnerships, you will develop your understanding of how to practically contribute to the co-creation of regenerative futures in local, regional, rural and remote communities.

title: Advanced Chinese: Language Variations
description: This unit develops students' communicative competence in the Chinese language over a wide range of real-life situations. The four skills of speaking, listening, reading and writing will be integrated in collaborative learning activities. The emphasis is on language register and language variations when expressing different opinions and dealing with more complex social situations. The cultural significance of language usage will be examined, together with systematic discussion of appropriate manners and social etiquette to enable effective communication with Chinese speakers.

title: Proficient Chinese: Language Variations
description: This unit further develops intercultural communicative competence in the Chinese language through collaborative and self-directed learning activities. Students will acquire linguistic and cultural skills in handling a wide range of topics and social situations. They will be encouraged to express opinions, conduct discussions and present reports in a socially and culturally appropriate manner. Relevant cultural and social issues related to the Chinese speaking communities will be explored and discussed to enable effective communication with Chinese speakers.

title: Business Study Tour
description: In this unit, you’ll embark on a local, national or regional tour that is focused on sustainable solutions, gaining first-hand experience of sustainable practices and responsible innovation. You’ll interact with industry, community and government, developing sustainability insights, and learn about approaches to solve problems responsibly. This unit is the perfect way to expand your knowledge and skills in sustainable development, and the issues facing our planet. You’ll enjoy an immersive experience where you’ll learn about a sustainable future. You’ll be supported through pre-departure seminars, covering the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs), health and safety, assessments, and cultural competency training. During the tour component of the unit, you’ll engage in experiences that include a mix of site visits, cultural activities, discussions with experts, and group discussions. On your return, you’ll attend a final debriefing seminar, sharing your unforgettable experience.

title: Professional Pharmacy Placements
description: This unit integrates the learning outcomes of preceding and concurrent units of this degree in order to prepare a pharmacist for lifelong learning and professional practice. Understanding of the role of the pharmacist as a healthcare provider practising in diverse settings. Professional behaviours, including reflective practice and ethical and cultural competence applied to pharmacy practice. Provision of, and problem solving in, contemporary services offered by pharmacists. Responsibilities and accountability in conforming to legislation. Practical application of essential skills in planning, assessment, intervention, communication, documentation and management functions. Retrieve, analyse and synthesise information. Provision of evidence and information utilising current professional resources. Advanced written and verbal communication with stakeholders in a professional practice setting.

title: Foundations of Medical Practice
description: This unit introduces the doctor/patient relationship in the clinical setting. It develops a structured approach to effective communication and eliciting a patient’s history. It also introduces some aspects of physical examination, particularly observation, inspection and palpation. It applies the basic science underpinning the structure and function of body systems to clinical scenarios. It expands upon and develops further understandings related to aged care and healthy ageing, encountered during the Foundations of Medicine unit.

title: Advanced Molecular Techniques
description: This unit addresses the principles and applications of emerging and best-practice advanced biomolecular techniques.  In a series of case-studies involving both hands-on and theoretical involvement, students will learn the appropriate utilisation of methods for studying cells and molecules. This will include, but not be limited to methods used in: tissue culture and cell based assays; protein expression; and genetic analyses and genetic manipulation.

title: Sustainable Energy Systems and Technologies
description: Introduction to energy sources and supplies. Characteristics of energy systems. Use of macro and micro climatic data to analyse and design energy systems. Critical analysis of potential solutions suggested to overcome energy supply issues. Emerging technologies for securing a sustainable energy future. Recent developments in energy efficient systems and technologies. Energy management and conservation technologies. Energy production, conversion, storage and distribution in the context of Australian economy.

title: Listening to Regions: A Place-Based Immersion into Regional WA
description: Listening to Regions provides you with a one-week immersive experience in regional Western Australia where you will tackle real-world challenges and experience work and life in a regional community. Founded on the four pillars of reciprocity, fun, experiential learning and a sense of belonging, you will travel in a group, experiencing a taste of country life through volunteering on community-driven projects, participation in community events, as well as tours of local industry and cultural experiences. The week-long road trip will be complemented by three pre-departure workshops, a separate volunteering activity, and a post-trip debrief workshop. Fostering intercultural understandings, connections, and strength-based partnerships, you will develop your understanding of how to practically contribute to the co-creation of regenerative futures in local, regional, rural and remote communities.

title: Go Global - Internship 4
description: This unit provides students with internship opportunities in becoming job-ready graduates. Students in courses without professional work experience are strongly encouraged to enrol in this unit.

title: Paramedic Clinical Practice 4
description: Use a systems approach to assess, diagnose, manage, document and evaluate care related to specialised health care needs of patients/families across the life span, including mass casualty and major incident situations. Apply therapeutic communication and meet paramedic competency standards in selected clinical contexts including using alternative pathways. Medication dosage calculations. Integrated care of the unconscious, spinal and multi trauma patient. Management of invasive therapy and monitoring. End of life care. Awareness of physiology of childbearing and ability to manage emergency delivery/obstetric emergencies. Sudden unexpected death in infancy. Peer teaching and mentorship.

title: Paramedic Clinical Practice 3
description: Use a systems approach to assess, diagnose, manage, evaluate care and maintain records related to the patient with acute and chronic conditions across the life span in the pre-hospital setting. Enhanced communication skills. Paramedic professional competency standards. Inter-professional care management including making appropriate referrals to other health care professionals /service providers and alternative care pathways. Medication management preparation/calculations, administration and record keeping. Pain management; emergency procedures, including advanced lifesaving for adults and paediatrics.

title: Nursing Practice for Health Instability 1
description: This unit uses a systems approach to assess, diagnose, plan, manage, document and evaluate patient care across the lifespan, including managing unstable conditions. Students learn to assess and manage care needs of people with confusional states. Students apply therapeutic communication, critical reasoning and meet nursing competency standards in selected clinical contexts. The unit continues the development of knowledge of medication preparation, administration and recording, dosage calculations, legislative control. Content includes applied pharmacology relating to pain, nausea, complementary therapy for pain; wound management including removal of sutures/staples and drains; surgical wound management; ANTT and the use of sterile gloves; continence (bowel and bladder elimination), catheter insertion and care and bladder washouts; emesis management and end of life care. Meeting the needs of people with acute confusion and recognising the deteriorating patient and responding to MET calls (adults) in clinical contexts.

title: International Study Tour
description: This is an international study tour and allows students to compare the Australia taxation system with those of other countries. Over approx. 30 days students will visit a number of countries and visit a number of international taxation organisations including government taxation agencies, as well as various professional organisations and world renown taxation bodies such as the OECD, IBFD. The tour also encompasses students visiting universities in the countries that are visited and meeting other students and lecturers to discuss world taxation issues The aim of the study tour is that students will immerse themselves in learning to understand and appreciate the roles of everyone involved in the International Taxation System. As well the study tour will allow students to research the background of business practices study tour location; eg., cultural, religious, economic, political, historical and geographical.

title: Professional Communication in Exercise Science
description: Apply principles of leadership, professional communication and ethics to the professional practices of exercise and sports science. Includes client centred written and verbal communication for interactions across cultures, health beliefs and health behaviours.

title: Indigenous Australian Health Project Management
description: Development of a health project using Primary Health Care ethics, principles and practice in an Indigenous context. Health problem identification and needs analysis, negotiation and consultation, identification and engagement with stakeholders and potential impacts of the project. Peer review and Professional Development Group processes.

title: Indigenous Australian Organisational Practice and Management Skills
description: Examination of government and non-government health organisations including structure, function and management models. Indigenous management models and organisational governance including Indigenous Ways of Working and Federal and State corporation acts. Developing vision statements and strategic planning concepts at an organisational level.

title: Indigenous Australian Health Project Evaluation
description: Building on a student's research project on a health area the complete project management cycle is demonstrated though the evaluation,monitoring and review of project outcomes, including understanding and applying culturally appropriate ways to maintain health promotion in Indigenous communities. The role of an Indigenous health practitioner is reviewed based on health promotion and project management principles, and Indigenous Terms of Reference.

title: Indigenous Australian Health Project Implementation
description: Principles of project monitoring and reviewing in readiness for project implementation. Review of project logistics, activities and resources. Identification and management of potential risks to project implementation. Peer review and Professional Development Group processes.

title: Art and Creativity
description: Engage and challenge practices of creativity, innovation and aesthetic experience in contemporary life. Students investigate contemporary forms of cultural practice in order to articulate and represent new critical ways of thinking.

title: Workplace Health and Safety Practice
description: Students will apply knowledge and develop practical skills during the placement supervised by nominated health and safety professionals. Students will enhance their professionalism, communication skills and report writing during the practical experience, tutorials and guest presentations.

title: Professional Practice in Urban and Regional Planning 2
description: This unit will prepare students who are about to enter the workforce through developing an understanding of effective policy development in multiple ways. It will also develop professional negotiation and communication techniques used in planning practice.

title: Governance and Policy in Indigenous Australian Contexts
description: Students will be able to identify and demonstrate an understanding of Indigenous governance processes and practices at a national and local levels. They will also develop skills in policy development and decision making to empower and promote capacity building within Indigenous Australian contexts.

title: Control Surveying
description: This unit covers the expectations and requirements of performing control surveying for different applications experienced in industry. Principles covered include specifications of a control network, its design, observational procedures, rigorous calculations and adjustment of the observed data, and appropriate reporting of the final product in line with Australian survey guidelines and practices. The objective is to build upon individual practices and techniques presented in previous units (such as terrestrial surveying, levelling, GNSS, and least squares adjustments), and explore the high level concepts of error propagation and detection, observation weighting, the combined adjustment, and how the different survey measurements and practices interact, compliment and affect each other. Students will be expected to work collaboratively and independently on field work exercises which will reflect contemporary workplace practices and cover the different techniques they will encounter.

title: Clinical Medical Imaging Practice 1
description: This unit provides authentic medical imaging professional practice experience in the clinical setting, at the level appropriate for the beginner reflective professional.

title: Human Physiology for Exercise Science
description: Foundation knowledge of human physiology and the physiological changes that occur through the human lifespan as pertinent to exercise science.

title: Portfolio Management
description: This unit covers essential portfolio theories and the application of security analysis and portfolio performance evaluation techniques. Concepts discussed include asset pricing theory, mean-variance analysis, market efficiency, behavioural finance, liquidity and asset pricing, market microstructure, mutual funds and hedge funds, portfolio optimization, and risk management. This unit also covers Environmental, Societal, and Governance (ESG) investment. Students have opportunities to apply and practice their investment skills by using virtual trading software. In addition, students will be provided with an awareness of ongoing developments in this area of Finance, for instance, high-frequency trading and cryptocurrencies.

title: Introduction to Global Business
description: This unit provides an introduction to global perspectives on conducting business in a global context. It explores the operational environment of international businesses; the core functions of global businesses; as well as global business ethics, responsible management and professionalism in the workplace. The unit will help students to broaden the scope of their thinking from a global perspective when planning and implementing organisational and business strategies and personal work ethics in global markets. The unit is aligned to Curtin’s Graduate Capabilities GRIT mindset – Global, Responsible, Innovative, Technology-oriented. Specifically, IBUS1001 adopts a Global outlook on institutional differences amongst country contexts, encourages curiosity, understanding, and appreciation of differences, as well as openness towards continuous learning and development. Furthermore, the unit encourages Responsibility in aligning with UN SDGs, appreciation of ethics, social responsibility, and sustainability, together with exercising inclusivity and compassion. Innovative mindset adoption involves embracing change as well as critical analysis of issues to challenge outdated inertias and design novel solutions that are flexible and situational. Finally, Technological mindset will provide an outlook on emerging technological trends and their impact on global business.

title: Survey Network Analysis and Design
description: This unit contains advanced topics on least-squares survey network analysis and design. The method of parametric least-squares for one-, two- and three-dimensional survey network adjustments is reviewed. Advanced methods of datum definition are introduced, including inner constraints and pseudo-inverse solutions, as well as the S-transformation between different solutions. The unit covers statistical testing of least-squares results through the goodness-of-fit test, variance factor test, variance component estimation, and Baarda’s and Pope’s tests for outlier detection. It also covers analysis of survey network quality through global and local measures of network precision, redundancy numbers, and reliability theory. In addition, optimisation of network design and the Standard for the Australian Control Network (SP1) are treated.

title: Managing Change
description: This unit examines the theoretical and practical perspectives and frameworks used to identify change. Change type, strategic approaches and tools available to explore and assess organisational change impact are presented, analysed and applied. From the student it requires a problem-solving, creative and innovative outlook coupled with critical thinking skills. A clear demonstration of an understanding of the challenges associated with the phenomena of change in an organisation is the desired outcome.

title: Mental Health Wellbeing
description: Students explore bio-psychosocial lifespan assessment; recovery planning; impact of trauma and legal and ethical issues; application of interpersonal skills. Specific needs of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, people from culturally and linguistically diverse (CALD) backgrounds, LGBTI (lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex) populations.

title: Health Promotion Leadership and Identity
description: Putting theory into practice: Facilitation skills, and public speaking. Professionally working with different personalities, negotiation skills, team work, conflict management. Case studies in health promotion practice. Networking skills. Ethics in health promotion. It is recommended that this unit be taken in the final year of a student's degree, preferably in the last semester of study.

title: Sustainability and Renewable Energy
description: This unit provides an introduction to sustainability challenges in engineering decision making and reviews the importance of the move towards renewable energy systems in the context of reducing our global footprint. The unit focuses on introducing the main global sustainability challenges together with an introduction to renewable energy technologies including Wind energy, Hydro energy, Geothermal energy, Tidal energy, Bio-energy, Solar energy and Wave energy, their application, efficiency and sustainability benefits. The course also reviews the broader technical, economic and environmental challenges faced in incorporating renewable energy into mainstream electricity production systems. The unit frames the use and need for renewable energy systems within a global context and the drivers and barriers faced by government and industry in adopting renewable energy systems.

title: Geotechnical Engineering Analysis
description: This unit covers four important topics in analysis of geotechnical engineering. The first topic is related to site investigation, including principles, planning, field and laboratory studies. The second topic is shear strength of soils and laboratory determination of shear strength parameters and failure criteria. The third and fourth topics cover two aspects related to the geotechnical engineering design of shallow foundations, including bearing capacity (3rd topic) and soil compressibility (4th topic).

title: The Individual in Society
description: This unit introduces students to key sociological concepts relevant to social work practice and social policy, including agency, structure and culture. Students will use these concepts to critically explore contemporary social issues and their ongoing impact on individuals in contemporary society.

title: Genre and Classic Texts
description: This unit explores the complex relation between culture, historical context and modes of representation. Through studying a range of cultural texts, it will consider why and how different narrative forms and generic conventions in fiction and non-fiction narrative emerge, endure and transform across time and space. Students will develop disciplinary knowledge in narrative theory and cultural studies, and refine their critical reading and research skills.

title: Hydrogeology and Engineering Geology
description: This unit introduces key concepts of hydrogeology and the importance of groundwater and the role geology plays in understanding, appraising and managing the valuable and hidden resource. It is thus very relevant to United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 6 on clean water and sanitation. The unit will focus on the hydrologic cycle, recharge-discharge phenomena, groundwater-surface water interactions, aquifer types and their characteristics, groundwater flow, aquifer tests, groundwater classification, groundwater systems, and hydrogeology in mining. A second focus is in Engineering geology and (a) Engineering classification of rocks and soils, elementary rock and soil mechanics and rocks and soil as construction materials, and (b) Engineering geology of dams, reservoirs, tailings dams, and foundations for buildings. This part embeds SDG9 in terms of building resilient infrastructure.

title: Enterprise Technologies
description: In this unit, students will gain a comprehensive understanding of global technology trends and the role of technology in driving responsible and innovative business solutions. Through a hands-on learning approach, students will have the opportunity to evaluate and recommend cutting-edge hardware, software, operating systems, and network devices that align with ethical and sustainable business practices. The OSI and TCP/IP models will serve as the foundation for understanding network protocols and data transmission in a global context. Additionally, students will have the opportunity to develop practical scripting skills to manipulate data files, further enabling them to make data-driven recommendations. Finally, students will implement a Server Operating System, network services and security roles, gaining valuable hands-on experience in responsible technology implementation and management.

title: Fundamental Concepts of Cryptography
description: An introduction to basic concept of cryptography with an emphasis on coding theory, classical cryptosystems and public key cryptography. Principles of information theoretic security. Computational hardness and number theory (Euclid’s algorithm, Euler and Fermat’s theorems). Public and private-key encryption, message authentication and digital signatures.

title: User Interface and Experience Design
description: In this unit, students apply acquired skills and theoretical knowledge in interaction design to develop effective digital interfaces.
