Students explore UI Design principles and UX evaluation methodologies to develop innovative design experiences while maintaining a user-centric approach. This unit empowers students to create impactful and meaningful interface solutions across a range of digital mediums.

title: Cross Institutional Study (within Australia)
description: Please refer to syllabus for the equivalent course

title: Process Mineralogy
description: A review of the basic principles of mineralogy, including crystal systems and physical properties. Introduction to crystal chemistry and the concept of unit cells. Solid solution in minerals. A survey of the composition and structure of the common ore minerals - native metals, oxides and sulphides. Analytical methods for ore minerals, including x-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), electron microbe and SIMS (Secondary Ion Mass Spectroscopy). A review of the mineralogy and textures of the commpn ore deposit types, with special emphasis on how the mineralogy and textures impact on ore processing.

title: The Numerate Educator
description: This unit is the first in a series of mathematics education units for educators. In this unit, the focus is on mathematical content knowledge, pedagogical content knowledge and personal numeracy. Content and proficiencies in all strands of the Australian Curriculum: Mathematics will be developed across Foundation to Year 3, with particular emphasis on teaching Early Number and Algebra. Students will initially attend to their personal numeracy with preliminary preparation for LANTITE and engagement with online exercises and tutorials.

title: Indigenous Australian Political Contexts
description: This unit will examine and explore Indigenous Australian self-determination and international Indigenous political contexts and aspirations.

title: The Professional Educator: Transition to the Profession
description: This unit will provide students with knowledge and skills to support transition into being education professionals and will enable undergraduate students to make important decisions about how to approach professional learning and development in order to meet contextualised student learning needs. Students examine how important information about their class can be obtained to determine group and individual learning needs and reflect on and evaluate their own current expertise and development. The unit examines how to structure personal professional learning that is targeted, collaborative, and aligned to the Australian Professional Standards for Graduate Teachers. Students in this unit will also formulate a general plan for their approach to continued personal learning and growth as they transition into becoming committed, skilled, resilient professionals.

title: Go Global - Internship 2
description: This unit provides students with internship opportunities in becoming job-ready graduates. Students in courses without professional work experience are strongly encouraged to enrol in this unit.

title: Solid and Hazardous Waste Management
description: This unit introduces solid and hazardous waste management; including the sources, composition and properties of solid and hazardous waste. Students will be introduced to the engineering principles, analyses, planning and design problems associated with storage, collection, processing, treatment, disposal and recovery of these wastes. The unit will also include solid and hazardous waste regulation.

title: Operations and Materials Management
description: This unit examines components and activities of operations management within the context of logistics and supply chain management. This unit involves concept application and deployment of analytical techniques specific to improving operations management. These concepts and techniques aim to support enhanced managerial response to market opportunities. It further aims to manage supply chain risks and enhance sustainability and resilience. This is achieved through problem identification, modelling and optimisation to creatively support management decisions and to propose solutions to operations management problems.

title: Physical Geography
description: This unit provides an introduction and exploration of the main principles of physical geography applied to urban, rural and regional environments. A range of topics are examined in relation to both natural and human environmental processes. The unit recognises and appreciates diverse indigenous knowledges of physical landscapes. A strong fieldwork component provides opportunities for problem-based learning in professions that require a broad understanding of physical geography, such as education, rural and urban Landcare, environmental planning and geotourism.

title: Historical Development of Mental Health
description: This unit will explore mental health beliefs, treatments and the changes in understanding from ancient times, through the era of the asylums and onto today’s focus on human rights and patient-focused care. Acts of parliament are examined in relation to these changes, in addition to Indigenous mental health issues pre- and post-colonisation within Australia. Health promotion and social determinates of health principles will be compared against current mental health policies.

title: Globalisation and Employment Relations
description: This unit provides a comparison of the HRM and industrial relations frameworks and processes in a number of countries. There will also be a focus on the historical, social and economic aspects of each country, as well as an examination of the roles of the principle parties and the bargaining processes.

title: Nursing Capstone
description: This unit consolidates prior learning within the course as students transition to the role of registered nurse. It strengthens the conceptual and theoretical knowledge required to provide high quality, comprehensive and safe patient care underpinned by evidence-based practice. The unit prepares students for professional registration and students investigate clinical governance, factors influencing patient safety including communication, partnering with consumers, clinical risk management and the quality improvement process.

title: Mechatronic Engineering Research Project 1
description: Students undertake a significant research project that either develops new knowledge or addresses an engineering problem of interest applying mechatronic tools and technologies. Students are free to choose from a range of projects offered by the faculty members as well as by external partners. In this unit students will: identify a problem, propose and plan a solution that meets the requirements, do a literature review to investigate existing solutions, make design decisions and assumptions to develop their solution, keep a logbook, and submit a written progress report at the end of semester. Projects involve engineering research methodologies, including analytical, numerical or experimental investigation or design, carried out over a period of one year. The students submit their final project work in the form of an undergraduate thesis, at the end of 2 consecutive semesters and at the end of the subsequent unit Mechatronic Engineering Research Project 2.

title: Management of Innovation
description: This unit focuses on the management of innovation. The fundamental ideas underlying this unit are that (1) innovation is the driving force in establishing a firm’s competitive advantage, (2) innovation is managed by leaders and teams with multiple competencies, and (3) a firm’s innovation strategy emerges from its competencies and capabilities. These fundamentals are then applied to new venture creation through first hand interaction with innovative entrepreneurs developing new innovations and technologies from the business community as well as university developed inventions with intent to commercialise their Intellectual Property. This allows the real world of the innovative entrepreneur to reinforce and sometimes challenge accepted theories of innovation and entrepreneurship.

title: Mixed Methods Research in Health Psychology
description: Mixed methods design and data analysis in psychological research in the context of health psychology. An examination of the philosophical foundations of research into complex human behaviours with a focus on the value of a pragmatic approach, real world outcomes, and improving people's lives at both an individual and national policy level.

title: Interior Architecture Studio – Community
description: Intensive studio unit with a very high level of Work Integrated Learning. The studio introduces and explores the processes of project management and interdependent teamwork to enable students to work effectively and collaboratively with each other as well as with an external group. Students will have the opportunity to research, debate and encounter a range of cultural situations, focusing on international perspectives, and work collaboratively and creatively on a spatial design problem, the process of which offers a deeper understanding of the complexities of community and culture. This in turn raises students’ awareness of their own communities. Through these processes students develop communication, problem solving skills and the independence essential to enter the senior years of the course.

title: Creative Arts Practice
description: This unit encourages multidisciplinary approaches to Creative Arts through individual and group creative activities. Students will align conceptual development with the acquisition of traditional and contemporary skills across a range of creative arts methods and strategies. This unit encourages innovative ways of thinking, practicing and reflecting.

title: Communication, Culture and Indigenous Perspectives in Business
description: This unit develops students' understanding of cultural, academic and professional integrity in a business context. Students will reflect on their own cultural background, and consider how this impacts on communication with diverse cultures including Indigenous Peoples. By applying knowledge about global and Indigenous cultures, and ways of working that are respectful, students will develop capability to communicate responsibly and in ways that are aligned with varied audiences. Responsible business practices will be explored, with students examining Indigenous perspectives in global business and how these perspectives should inform business communication and decision making. Students will be equipped with fundamental communication and academic integrity skill development appropriate for all business disciplines, in academic and professional settings.

title: Pharmacy Practice 3
description: This unit develops students’ skills in effective patient and inter-professional communication and in clinical, ethical and legal reasoning as part of decision-making in professional pharmacy practice.   Students learn about professional pharmaceutical services including prescription dispensing, packaging dose administrative aids, bioequivalent and generic medicines, and pharmacy practice incentive programs including professional software systems used for recording and delivering services.    Students also learn about safe medication practices and risk management via pharmaceutical calculations, root cause analysis, adverse drug reaction reporting, consumer protection, product liability, off-label prescribing and laws related to the therapeutic goods and the dispensing of drugs of addiction.

title: Public Health Honours Dissertation
description: A continuation of attributes learnt from Public Health Honours Preparation, students will develop competencies in the research process and interpretation of data from their research project. Students will develop skills in: oral presentations communicating the results and significance of their research; preparing a research article and dissertation; as well as responding to examiners’ comments.

title: Transmission and Interface Design
description: The computer bus as a transmission line. Loading effects. Transients. The role of a computer interface, Interfacing methods; some common analogue and digital interface circuits. Isolation and protection. Timing issues. Bandwidth issues, Cabling issues; coaxial and twisted pairs. Connectors. Fabrication techniques. Electromagnetic Compatibility.

title: Creating Content and Marketing Briefs
description: In this unit you will develop the essential skills needed for success in the marketing profession, specifically focusing on content creation and marketing briefs. Through a combination of theory and practical exercises, you will learn the purpose, importance, and creation of effective marketing briefs, as well as how to organise, manage, and prepare high-quality content for various purposes. By the end of this unit, you will have gained knowledge of marketing in agencies and companies, and developed skills in content creation, content strategy, content promotion, and content analysis. These skills will be highly beneficial for your transition into the marketing profession, making you a more employable and well-rounded graduate.

title: Health Partnerships, Politics and Power
description: Students will analyse processes for promoting health using a settings based approach. Students will explore the social and political contexts that influence health and the need for comprehensive responses in public health interventions. The unit has a major focus on the State as a setting, and the legislative process. Students will also critically assess corporate influences on health, conduct stakeholder analyses and examine the role of health promotion in influencing public policy. This unit involves both a theoretical and practical understanding of contemporary political issues and their impact on health.

title: Linear Algebra 2
description: Linear Algebra introduces students to linear techniques and their transformation properties. These techniques are often used in engineering, physics, science, computing and economics. The unit comprises four parts. In the first part, the students are introduced to the concept of vector spaces, subspaces, linear dependence, independence, span, basis, dimension and coordination of vectors. In the second part, students learn about linear transformation, inner products, inner product spaces, orthogonal and orthonormal bases. In the third part, students practice techniques dealing with matrix decomposition and generalized inverse. In the last part, students learn about linear systems of differential equations.

title: Technologies: Design Solutions
description: This unit is one of three units in the Technologies Options group. Completing all three will provide a specialisation in Technologies. This unit provides an overview of the fundamental elements of the Design and Technologies curriculum. By applying knowledge and practical skills and processes when using technologies and other resources to create innovative solutions, independently and collaboratively, students will develop knowledge, understanding and skills to respond creatively to current and future needs. The unit will engage students in critical and creative thinking, including understanding interrelationships in systems when solving complex problems.

title: Social Media, Communities and Networks
description: Digital and social media offer many opportunities for people to create and share media content and information, engage in social interaction, and build communities and networks. Social media platforms now play a major role in bringing people together - whether to connect with others with shared experiences or interests, maintain social relationships, advance political causes, or for commercial and self-branding purposes. In this unit, you will investigate the opportunities and possibilities, as well as harms and social problems, that arise in relation to social media communities and networks. You will develop knowledge and skills to become more thoughtful and effective in navigating such. This knowledge is key for digital content creation, policy development work, and online community and network building.

title: Hospitality Management
description: This unit is designed to equip students with the strategic management, practical and personal skills necessary to work successfully in a highly competitive global environment within the hospitality industry. In order for students to successfully complete this unit, it is recommended that students have prior basic understanding of the hospitality industry. This unit provides a student-centred and academically rigorous program, which seeks to develop students’ competencies and encourage their intellectual skills in examining the planning, organising, leadership and control functions associated with the management of hospitality organisations. The aim of this unit is to create an awareness of the management issues as they relate to areas of lodging, food service, travel, tourism and recreation. In addition, students will develop an understanding of the major influences affecting the international hospitality business environment which will facilitate the assessment of strategic issues resulting from globalisation.

title: Typography
description: Through a series of practical design projects and exercises, this unit addresses the fundamental principles of form and function in typographic design.

title: Philosophy and Practice
description: Philosophy and Practice offers an introduction to key philosophies, issues, practices, theories and concepts related to design practice, in particular design of the interior. Students will explore questions of identity, the person-community-environment relationship, aesthetics and experience, symbols and meaning, and occupation and habitation that is inclusive of indigenous perspectives. Principles of design practice, and theoretical frameworks relating to design methodologies are also considered. Students will develop an understanding of the concepts of community, cultural diversity, social sustainability, social equity within local and global contexts. Students will investigate design as a process, as communication and representation, and importantly as ways of questioning and thinking.

title: Geographies of Food Security
description: This unit will provide an insight into the global food situation and the challenge to increase food production given the contexts of population growth and increased competition over access to resources. A range of topics will be examined through case studies from Australia, its region and worldwide. The unit recognises and appreciates diverse Indigenous knowledges, perspectives, cultures and histories of food and food security. A strong fieldwork component provides opportunities for problem-based learning in professions that require a developing understanding of food security, such as education, government agencies, NGOs and tourism.

title: Business and Law International Experience 2
description: International mobility experience for undergraduate students.

title: Workplace Writing
description: This unit introduces you to writing tasks that are common to a variety of workplaces. You practise the types of writing that help you get a job, including cover letters and resumes, as well as the types of writing that help you succeed in virtually any industry, such as emails and website copywriting. This unit helps you begin to understand how your writing skills can be applied to a career that matches your interests and values.

title: Human Structure and Function
description: This unit serves as an introduction to the human body and key organ systems. It begins with anatomical terminology and the relationships between body cells, tissues and organs. Key cell processes such as respiration, protein synthesis, and cell division will be covered. Students will then explore the basic function and control of the circulatory, respiratory, digestive and excretory systems, and how these systems contribute to the changing needs of the human body. The unit includes exploration of the lymphatic and immune systems and how they provide defence against microorganisms. Students will investigate the maintenance of homeostasis and the governance of body systems by the nervous and endocrine systems.

title: Foreign Policy
description: This unit explores foreign policy-making and the development of professional skills in the field of foreign affairs. It examines the full range of individual, organisational, bureaucratic, societal, and/or state factors. The unit is designed to employ a wide range of approaches, including historical, normative, rational, behavioural, liberal, institutional, psychological and constructivist. Case studies and simulations are used to answer why and how decision-makers choose a particular policy. It also examines the central role played by intelligence institutions in the making of foreign policy.

title: Human Resources Development
description: This unit examines the theory, principles and practices associated with adult learning in the workplace. It focuses on adult learning theory, learning needs analyses; evaluating learning and development activities and their impacts, and designing and delivering training and development workshops. There is also an emphasis on the challenges presented by the changing nature of work and careers in the contemporary job marketplace. Technological developments in the arena of Human Resources Development are also explored.

title: Site Planning
description: A practical introduction to the design process for site planning, the principles of open space design, community facilities planning and the design of a neighbourhood centre.

title: Exercise and Sports Nutrition
description: This unit examines the effect of diet on health, exercise and sports performance in applied settings spanning apparently healthy populations through elite sport. Areas of specific relevance to diet in health, exercise and sports will include, but not be limited to, nutrition for optimal exercise performance and recovery; the control and modification of body composition; optimal fluid balance; and the function of vitamins and minerals. Evidence based best practice derived from current scientific literature is emphasised.

title: Organisational Behaviour
description: Organisational Behaviour is a unit that explores the human aspects of organisations and how they affect individual and group performance, motivation, leadership, decision-making, and organisational change. You will learn the key concepts and theories of organisational behaviour and how to apply them to real-life contexts. You will also develop skills in interpreting, solving, and evaluating organisational problems and situations using various frameworks, models, methods, and tools. This unit will help you enhance your employability capability by improving your critical thinking, communication, teamwork, and ethical awareness.

title: Responsible Management in Asia
description: This unit considers management practices and issues in the Asia-Pacific region especially multinational corporations and local businesses operating in the Asia-Pacific. Students will gain knowledge of business operations in Asia and how to do business responsibly and sustainably. Students will explore the grand challenges societies face with a focus on the Asia-Pacific region and learn how to approach and solve these grand challenges responsibly and sustainably. Students will learn corporate social responsibility, business and human rights, institutional theory, and institutional voids through student-centred activities, learning and teaching.

title: Start-Up Business Planning
description: The unit examines Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) from a practical perspective and provides students with a hands on approach to the art of small business planning. This includes creating a business plan in teams that considers the main functional areas necessary for the establishment and continuous operation of a small business.

title: Corporate Finance
description: This unit focuses on aspects of corporate finance theories and the tools and techniques to facilitate excellent corporate financial decision making. It aims to expose students to, and familiarise them with, corporate sector financial management by examining the main issues faced by financial managers of public companies, both in Australia and around the world. In addition, students will explore innovations in financial technology and environmental, social and governance (ESG) issues; and gain insights how corporate financial decision making can contribute to meeting the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Students are expected to perform hands-on analysis and build Excel spreadsheet models to assist with analysis. The unit also aims to help students develop oral and written communication skills through individual and/or group assignments, presentations and interviews. Topics covered are: advanced capital budgeting under uncertainty (developing what was introduced in FNCE2000 Introduction to Finance Principles); market imperfections and signalling; agency theory; capital markets and sources of funds; capital structure; dividend policy; and the market for corporate control and corporate governance.

title: Technologies: Digital Solutions
description: This unit is one of three units in the Technologies Options group. Completing all three will provide a specialisation in Technologies. It is designed to provide students with a framework for developing and implementing digital solutions to contemporary issues in education. It has a pedagogical grounding that looks specifically at learning rather than the technological tools and platforms themselves. It is designed to give students the critical literacies required to assess the merit of such tools, use them to design and build robust solutions to everyday problems and evaluate their suitability for the chosen task. Students will be able to take the lessons learned in this unit and apply them across a range of learning landscapes.

title: Fine Art Studio Extension
description: This unit is designed to further develop your capacity for research-based enquiry into skills, techniques, methods and processes of fine art. You will develop and extend your practical engagement with the studio research process. You will apply advanced technical and conceptual skills to develop a series of artworks.

title: Workplace Human Factors
description: This unit examines the physical, physiological, cognitive and social characteristics of humans which influence their interactions with work, equipment and the physical and organisational environment of the workplace.

title: Engineering Industry Research Project 1
description: In this unit students will develop skills to conduct independent research through an authentic, industry related engineering project. Students will integrate and apply knowledge and skills acquired in preceding units to plan a safe, cost effective solution to engineering / industry related problems.

title: Capstone Computing Project 2
description: Students continue the projects that were designed and planned in Capstone Computing Project 1. Each student will be assigned a staff member as a supervisor and a client (or client group). Supervisors assist in the details of the project relating to the unit and advise students on best practice. Students develop the project implementation for the client(s) and thus meet with them regularly for progress updates and to obtain feedback. All development is carried out using industry best-practice, including the use of an agile methodology and the use of tools such as an online repository. Projects are usually carried out in small groups of three to four students, although this can vary with the project. Teams may include students from other discipline areas where a project requires this.

title: English: Researching the Field
description: This unit begins by identifying key issues in English and engages a critical analysis of theories, pedagogies and philosophies associated with the teaching of language, literacy and literature. Individual students will select a key issue and conduct an investigation of relevant theories, pedagogies and philosophy. Individual investigations will be followed by collaborative discussion of findings with peers investigating the same issue, followed by critical analysis of thinking around the issue, culminating in the presentation of conclusions and recommendations for future practice/further research. This unit prepares students to be active participants in identifying effective programs and practice in the teaching of primary English in their future school/work context.

title: Supply Chain Management
description: This unit provides an introduction to the concept of supply chain management, its challenges and current trends. It explains typical operations, procurement, risk management, services and relationship building activities within the context of supply chains. The unit examines the impacts of globalisation and technology to support global supply chain challenges. Ethical, responsible and sustainable practices and strategies are developed. Consideration is given to the importance of relationship management in the design of a healthy, efficient supply chain.

title: Mechanical Engineering Research Project 1
description: Students undertake a significant research project that either develops new knowledge or addresses an engineering problem of interest. Students are free to choose from a range of projects offered by the faculty members as well as by external partners. In this unit students will: identify a problem, propose and plan a solution that meets the requirements, do a literature review to investigate existing solutions, make design decisions and assumptions to develop their solution, keep a logbook, and submit a written progress report at the end of semester. Projects involve engineering research methodologies, including analytical, numerical or experimental investigation or design, carried out over a period of one year. The students submit their final project work in the form of an undergraduate thesis at the end of the subsequent unit Mechanical Engineering Research Project 2.

title: Mechanical Engineering Research Project 2
description: Students undertake a significant research project that either develops new knowledge or addresses a mechanical engineering problem of interest. Students are free to choose from a range of projects offered by the faculty members as well as by external partners. The theory units that they learn in the classroom provide them with existing knowledge in the field whereas the undergraduate project provides them with an opportunity to demonstrate their inventiveness, degree of effort and self-management skills. In this unit students will: carry out and complete the research project planned and commenced in Mechanical Engineering Research Project 1. Projects involve the application of engineering research methodologies, including analytical, numerical or experimental investigation or design, which is carried out over a period of one year. The students submit their project work in the form of an undergraduate thesis at the end of 2 consecutive semesters, and deliver their research findings in an oral form to their peers and staff in a project research seminar.

title: International Human Resources Management
description: This unit explores the impact of the global environment on the management of human resources; examines processes of expatriation and repatriation in multinational organisations and the impact of cultural and country differences on human resource policies and practices. The unit develops students’ theoretical and conceptual understandings of core Human Resources Management problems relating to relocation of employees and specifically facilitating and managing expatriation. Students analyse workplace problems through real-life case study examples and generate innovate and effective solutions.

title: Structural Analysis of Determinate Structures
description: This unit introduces classical methods of analysis to enable students to assess, quantify and communicate an understanding of statically determinate structures’ behaviours. The syllabus includes types of structures and loads, analysis of statically determinate structures (including beams, frames and trusses), elastic beam theory, deflections using geometrical and energy methods, and influence lines for statically determinate structures.

title: International Study Abroad 2
description: n/a

title: Curriculum and Instruction Lower Secondary: The Arts
description: This unit is designed to prepare pre-service teachers to teach The Arts curriculum in Lower Secondary school. The unit will focus on curriculum planning, teaching strategies, evaluation, resources, the demonstration of positive impact on student learning and research relating to The Arts in Lower Secondary Teaching and learning practices to support and challenge a diverse student cohort are explored.

title: Reviewing Indigenous Australian Community Projects
description: Indigenous Project Management principles applied to project closure and review. Use Community Development and Indigenous Ways of Working principles to ethically close a project. Review project benefits and initiate strategies to ensure realisation of project benefits.

title: Project Management
description: Project Management is a unit that introduces you to the principles and practices of managing projects in various contexts and domains. You will learn the main framework, knowledge areas and processes of Project Management, and how to apply them to real-world scenarios. You will also develop the skills and techniques to use a contemporary Project Management tool to plan, execute and monitor a project from start to finish. Additionally, you will be able to evaluate the effectiveness and efficiency of Project Management practices and outcomes, and reflect on your own performance and learning. This unit will equip you with the knowledge and skills to become a competent and confident project manager in your future career.

title: Physics Honours Dissertation
description: Students will be required to conduct an independent research project under the guidance of a supervisor, resulting in the preparation, submission, presentation and defence of a dissertation. Students will develop research, technical and professional and communication skills, research autonomy and specialised knowledge through a process of inquiry involving the formulation of research questions and hypotheses; selection of appropriate methodology and experimental design; ethical consideration of the research process; critical review of scientific literature; effective scientific writing; development of a project proposal, and the preparation of a dissertation.

title: Chemistry Honours Dissertation
description: Students will be required to conduct an independent research project in the chemical sciences under the guidance of a supervisor, resulting in the preparation, submission, presentation and defence of a dissertation. Students will develop research, technical and professional and communication skills, research autonomy and specialised knowledge through a process of inquiry involving the formulation of research questions and hypotheses; selection of appropriate methodology and experimental design; ethical consideration of the research process; critical review of scientific literature; effective scientific writing; development of a project proposal, and the preparation of a dissertation.

title: Actuarial Control Cycle 1
description: Develop a holistic rev to problem-solving, the ‘actuarial control cycle’, extending knowledge of technical actuarial skills acquired in prior learning to a variety of commercial situations. Understand the context and need for continuing and reassessment of past solutions. Develop communication skills and understand the importance of professionalism in the application of actuarial principles.

title: Introduction to Health Sciences
description: An overview of the structure and function of human anatomy and physiology with an emphasis on musculo-skeletal, cardiovascular, respiratory, nervous, digestive, endocrine, immune, lymphatic and urinary systems. Human cell biology and homeostasis will also be investigated. Introductory of epidemiology will be discussed.

title: Science Foundations
description: This unit introduces students to the landscape of introductory Chemistry and Physics. The focus is in developing concepts of laws, theories, atomic structure and relationship between periodic table and bonding including balancing equations and mole concept. Students will formulate the concepts of graphs and vectors by looking at the importance of measurements in Physics.

title: Introduction to Financial Literacy and Mathematic Fundamentals
description: Introduction to basic mathematical skills, including: the Number System; decimals, fractions, metric measurement, estimation and calculators, problem solving, percentage and ratio, financial literacy, and financial planning and management.

title: Introduction to Finance Principles
description: This unit explores the financial decision-making processes within businesses, along with the tools and techniques employed to support these decisions. It introduces foundational financial mathematics; covers the concepts and theories of debt and equity with a focus on the valuation of bond and stock; and applies basic risk management techniques.

title: Sedimentology and Stratigraphy
description: Introduction to sedimentology; physical properties of sediments, weathering, erosion and the sediment cycle. Sediment classification. Sedimentary processes and structures. Diagenesis and petrology; post-depositional change and sediment investigation at the microscopic scale. Principles, nomenclature and procedures in stratigraphy; lithostratigraphy, biostratigraphy and sequence stratigraphy. Stratigraphic correlation in the sub-surface. Sedimentary depositional systems and models; environments, facies and basin fill. Sedimentary geochemistry and climate.

title: Indigenous Australian Studies
description: An overview of Aboriginal history pre and post colonisation, including: governance, contemporary health issues, Aboriginal education, Australian and Aboriginal Lore, Aboriginal art, the impact of reconciliation on Aboriginal and non-Indigenous Australians and Aboriginal self-determination.

title: Biomedical Science Honours
description: Students will undertake a yearlong individual research project closely supervised by an academic researcher. The unit involves preparation and presentation of a scientific research proposal to an academic audience, as well as development of hands-on scientific skills in an authentic research environment. Students will apply knowledge, conduct a scientific research project, demonstrate academic and research integrity, and accurately disseminate research findings. Scheduled classes will assist in the development of generic research skills and statistical methods. This unit encourages independence, trains students in research, and enhances employment prospects. It is excellent experience for students wishing to pursue a career in research or project management.

title: Participatory Planning
description: Examines the role of community and stakeholder participation in the planning process and governance of urban and regional places. Critical evaluation of participatory practices and theories.

title: Fundamental Chemistry for Biosciences
description: This unit is a practical and theoretical exploration of the fundamental principles of chemistry as they apply to the biosciences, and with a focus on human systems. We will describe principles to develop your understanding of molecular-scale biological structure and apply conventions to communicate chemical structures and reactions that underpin life. We will relate chemical reactions to energy transfer as electrons and protons used to fuel biological systems. Lastly, we will categorise biomolecules on the basis of patterns in their chemical structures. Together these will provide a foundation for your future studies in biochemistry, molecular genetics, pharmaceutical science and cell biology.

title: Actuarial Control Cycle 2
description: Develop a holistic approach to problem-solving, the “actuarial control cycle”, extending knowledge of technical actuarial skills acquired in prior learning to a variety of commercial situations. Develop critical thinking and judgement skills and understand the importance of professionalism in the application of actuarial principles.

title: Foundations of Communication
description: Students develop their knowledge and skills in effective spoken, written and graphic communication in a tertiary context. Communication strategies appropriate for purpose and audience are applied in practical and interactive learning tasks involving interpersonal communication, presentation, negotiation and language skills.

title: Introduction to Commerce
description: This unit will provide an introduction to the fundamentals of economics, marketing, law, and accounting principles. The unit will focus on the basic concepts and techniques in accounting that apply to business; law with a business context; as well as giving attention to the basic principles relating to economics. It will explore the decisions made by individuals and groups, and the impact this had on wealth, income and everyday living. Students will be shown how to apply basic economic, marketing, legal and accounting concepts to practical situations therefore shedding light on key commercial operations.

title: Indigenous Australian Honours Dissertation Preparation
description: A semester of intensive supervised research in an Indigenous Australian context. Students are expected to demonstrate appropriate research knowledge, skills and understandings in planning and implementing an effective and culturally appropriate small-scale research project. Research should maximise opportunities for local Aboriginal participation and control, and benefit those who are the focus of the research activities.

title: Psychology Honours Dissertation Preparation
description: This unit involves the preparation of a research proposal under the guidance of your supervisor.

title: Indigenous Australian Honours Dissertation
description: A semester of intensive supervised research and dissertation writing in an Indigenous Australian context. Students are expected to demonstrate appropriate research knowledge, skills and understandings in planning and implementing an effective and culturally appropriate small-scale research project, and to present this research in a written dissertation.  Research should maximise opportunities for local Aboriginal participation and control, and benefit those who are the focus of the research activities.

title: Fundamentals of Academic Writing
description: The complex processes, strategies, attitudes and language that characterize academic learning, research and writing are identified, discussed, practiced and applied in relation to set tasks to build a foundation for academic success.

title: Communications, Ethics and Research
description: Students will develop spoken and written communication skills appropriate for tertiary studies. Effective intercultural communication strategies will be covered, along with the role of ethics in research and the importance of ethical decision-making.

title: Preparatory English
description: This unit provides English language preparation for students from non-English speaking backgrounds for undergraduate study at Curtin University. It is designed to give students additional language skills and strategies in listening, speaking, reading and writing in order to better prepare them for participation in an undergraduate course. The unit enables students to develop skills to participate effectively in general English language tasks which include a focus on grammar and vocabulary, self-editing, note-taking and speaking tasks which cover pronunciation. A pass in this unit will not guarantee the student reaches the proficiency standard required for Curtin university entry. The student will still have to provide the qualifications that satisfy Curtin’s minimum English admission criteria.

title: Introduction to Humanities
description: This unit explores the interrelationships of people within society. Students will explore themes related to society, culture, environment and technology and their reciprocal impacts. The unit seeks to develop students understanding of self as part of diverse and complex systems viewed through a critical lens.

title: Humanities Foundations
description: Development of skills required for mainstream university study in Humanities. Students will gain an understanding of the role of Humanities in society, the nature of the various disciplines, and will develop communication skills appropriate to each discipline area.

title: Communication Skills
description: Communication Skills is designed to develop students' analytical and critical thinking and communication skills in English for undergraduate study in the discipline of Science, Engineering, and Health Sciences. This unit aims to develop students’ skill in listening, speaking, reading, viewing and writing as well as enhancing students’ ability to read and interpret discipline-specific text for a range of purposes, audiences and contexts and to develop student production of discipline-specific text for a range of purposes, audiences and contexts. The unit will also explore an understanding of ways in which meaning is conveyed and the use of language for communication in multiple contexts. Students’ engagement in critical analysis and evaluation will also form an integral part of the learning experience. The unit will use the broad themes of Health, Safety, Environment and Culture to develop students’ reading, listening and viewing skills in order to analyse and evaluate the purpose, stylistic qualities and conventions of text for the disciplines of Science, Engineering and Health Sciences. Students will develop strategies for speaking and writing their own analytical responses to topics relevant to Health, Safety, Environment and Culture. The unit is designed to foster an appreciation of the value of English for lifelong learning in the discipline areas of Science, Engineering and Health.

title: Numeracy Essentials
description: This unit aims to develop a core set of numeracy skills that will aid students in further study - particularly in Health Sciences, Humanities, and Business. Students will be introduced to a variety of mathematical concepts from basic numerical to statistical to financial, and to their real-life applications in Health Sciences, Humanities, and Business.

title: Preparation for Paramedic Clinical Practice
description: This unit builds on the non-clinical skills introduced in semester one. It will introduce the foundational clinical skills required for paramedic practice within a basic life support scope of practice. Students will build on their systematic patient assessment skills to identify and respond effectively to immediate health concerns. The unit will introduce the principles of safe medication administration through oral, topical, inhaled, intranasal and intramuscular routes. Students will also learn to manage unwell patients within a basic life support scope of practice. This includes core clinical skills such as essential airway management and resuscitation. Non-technical skills such as reflective practice, communication, teamwork, and problem-solving will be expanded in clinical and non-clinical settings. All clinical practice will be framed within relevant paramedic ethical, legal, professional and person-centred frameworks that will underpin student practice.

title: International Economic Law
description: Governed principally by treaties on trade, investment and international monetary system, International Economic Law regulates the international business and economic relations among nations and between foreign businesses and states. It is an area of intense international disputes between or among states and between foreign investors and states. Thus, International Economic Law is an area of practical relevance both in terms of the substantive protections it affords to states and foreign businesses and the mechanisms for the resolution of trade and investment disputes. Broadly structured in three parts, the unit first explores the historical and normative foundations of international trade law, culminating in an examination of the World Trade Organisation (WTO). It then shifts to international investment law, assessing its architecture, dispute resolution mechanisms, and current reform efforts. The final part addresses the global financial architecture, with a focus on institutions such as the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank, sovereign debt governance, and emerging issues like crypto assets and digital currencies.

title: Hydrographic Surveying
description: Elements of hydrography and oceanography. Tidal theory and application to marine surveying and navigation. Creation and interpretation of hydrographic charts. Precise marine positioning, navigation and track control using satellite- and shore-based navigation systems. Real time kinetic (RTK) GPS. Maritime boundaries. Choice and establishment of sea level datums for depth sounding. Depth determination: sonar surveys, including multibeam and sidescan, three-dimensional seismic surveying, depth reductions. Planning and specifications for marine survey. Case studies, including fieldwork. Aspects of well-head and oil-rig positioning, remotely operated underwater vehicles (ROVs) and underwater pipeline surveying.

title: Actuarial Asset Liability Management
description: Describe and critically evaluate the types of investments; their attributes in varying circumstances; valuation methods including assumptions and limitations; and the critical application of models from economics and finance to investment management. Construct, critically evaluate and apply asset models of a stochastic nature that are appropriate to the management of liabilities. The outcome of such an exercise is usually an investment strategy for managing the liabilities.

title: Actuarial Risk Management
description: Develop a deeper approach to managing the risks of an organisation, utilising principles from Actuarial Control Cycle 1 (ACTL4000). Actuarial consideration of product design and liabilities are explored in greater detail. Practical, hands-on modelling experience is developed through the use of R and EXCEL (students are assumed to have functional R and EXCEL skills prior to commencement of this unit).

title: Industrial Automated Systems
description: Instrumentation and Control is vital to the operation of modern automation systems. In this unit, you will learn about Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems, and how to program them. These devices accept signals from sensors which monitor the performance of an automation system, and produce signals which adjust its operation. You will learn about the principles of operation of sensors and their accuracy specifications, the design of appropriate instrumentation amplifiers, and the characteristics of data acquisition devices. You will also learn about control algorithms such as the PID, and how to set their parameters to keep the automation system functioning efficiently. Finally, you will learn how to design for Reliability, Availability and Maintainability (RAM), and for the appropriate Safety Integrity Level (SIL).

title: English: Extending Reading and Writing
description: The focus of this unit is on pre-service teachers developing an in-depth understanding of how to extend children’s reading and writing. Teaching  will be situated in the context of understanding different perspectives and theories about how children extend their literacy. This unit will prepare pre-service teachers with knowledge of the symbiotic relationship between reading, writing and creating.

title: Data Visualisation
description: Data visualisation is an essential aspect of data science that deals with the graphical representation of data with the purpose of discovering hidden patterns, understanding data and conveying findings through visually engaging and informative figures. In this unit you will be trained to effectively use modern data visualisation tools for both exploring and explaining data while working on real world problems

title: Exercise and Sport Psychology
description: In this unit, students will learn about key theories and principles regarding the individual, social, and environmental factors that influence people’s uptake of and engagement with sport, exercise, and health. The knowledge and experience gained through this unit will provide students with the necessary conceptual and practical foundations upon which to appreciate the significance of the person in context for human behaviour in sport, exercise, and health contexts.

title: Professional Communication in Exercise Science
description: Apply principles of professional communication and ethics to the professional practices of exercise and sports science. Includes client centred written and verbal communication for interactions across cultures, health beliefs and health behaviours.

title: International Study Tour
description: The study of the effect of local cultural, social, political and economic influences on countries outside of Australia. Students will undertake research during a study tour and carry out fieldwork to develop reflective, critical and evaluative thinking of an aspect of the built environment in an international context.

title: Agribusiness Systems
description: To be able to work at any level of the Agribusiness sector requires an in-depth understanding that it is made up of a number of different parts working together as a system. Agribusiness Systems is designed to develop a detailed knowledge of the components that make up the agribusiness sector and how they interact. Students will gain an understanding of how the input, production, processing and consumer sectors influence each other and how the success of enterprises in each is reliant on the success of all others along the value chain. Product, information, payment and cost flows through the system will be discussed. Students will have the opportunity in this unit to enhance their understanding of parts of the Agribusiness System through external certification.

title: Metallurgical Process and Plant Design
description: This unit covers the basic principles and practice of metallurgical process and plant design. Working in groups, students will be provided with a project brief consisting of essential mineralogical and metallurgical data for a particular ore body and a design brief specifying the various design tasks that they need to carry out. These include process selection, software-assisted process development and optimisation, equipment selection and sizing, plant layout, process control scheme, cost estimation and assessment of the economic feasibility of the project. Occupational health and safety, environmental impact, sustainability and social impact issues need to be considered at every step of the design process.

title: Planning Honours Dissertation
description: Design, implement and present an individual research program on an urban and regional planning issue.

title: Humanities Honours Dissertation 1
description: This unit extends skills acquired during a relevant Bachelor of Arts Degree. Students will acquire new knowledge and develop a research approach through the development of a project. Through independent research and guided supervision students will produce work for review and examination at the end of semester.

title: Humanities Honours Dissertation 2
description: This unit extends skills acquired during HUMN4000 Humanities Honours Dissertation 1. Students will acquire new knowledge through independent research and guided supervision in order to develop a dissertation through to submission for examination.

title: Actuarial Science Honours Dissertation 1
description: The proposing and planning of a research project related to an advanced actuarial related issue undertaken by the student, including preparation of a literature review, documentation of the research proposal and timeline.

title: Mechatronic Engineering Research Project 2A
description: Students undertake a significant Mechatronic research project that either develops new knowledge or addresses an engineering problem of interest, applying mechatronic tools and technologies. Students are free to choose from a range of projects offered by the faculty members as well as by external partners. In this unit students will: carry out and complete the research project planned and commenced in Mechatronic Engineering Research Project 1. Project involves the application of engineering research methodologies, including analytical, numerical or experimental investigation or design, carried out over a period of one year. The students submit their project work in the form of an undergraduate thesis at the end of 2 consecutive semesters, and deliver their research findings in an oral form to their peers and staff in a project research seminar.

title: Work Based Project
description: This unit provides students with an opportunity to work as part of a multi-disciplinary team and engage with an external organisation (e.g industry partner, community, voluntary organisation,…) on a project / problem specific to the organisation’s needs. It aims to provide students with an opportunity to apply independent problem solving in real world scenarios, supported by both an academic and a work based supervisor. Importance is placed on the project design process in a multi-disciplinary, collaborative environment and students are responsible for developing strategies to meet the challenges of working in this type of environment.

title: Psychology Honours Dissertation
description: Conducting research and writing a research dissertation.

title: Honours Dissertation in Business
description: A supervised in-depth research study in a specific business related discipline.

title: Geoscience Honours Dissertation
description: Students will be required to conduct an independent research project in an area of geological, geophysical or spatial sciences under the guidance of a supervisor, resulting in the preparation, submission, presentation and defence of a dissertation; students will develop research, technical and professional and communication skills, research autonomy and specialised knowledge through a process of inquiry involving the formulation of research questions and hypotheses; selection of appropriate methodology and experimental design; ethical consideration of the research process; critical review of scientific literature; effective scientific writing; development of a project proposal, and the preparation of a dissertation.

title: Actuarial Science Honours Dissertation 2
description: The completion of a research project related to an advanced actuarial related issue undertaken by the student, writing the research report and presenting the findings at a seminar.

title: Creative Arts Project
description: This unit encourages students to explore the context of their developing practice, progressing a body of work that builds on the creative arts profession. Emphasis in this unit is given to bringing a creative work to a final showcase. Students will draw from major discipline knowledge and skills to develop a way of documenting and reflecting the progress of a Creative Arts project that culminates in a public showcase -exhibition/screening/performance. Students will work collaboratively using entrepreneurial strategies to plan, promote and present a final showcase to an audience.

title: Strategic Marketing
description: Advanced unit aimed at developing strategic decision-making skills with particular reference to marketing. This unit presents the philosophy of integrating market planning into the strategic planning process to cope with an ever-changing and challenging business environment characterised by unparalleled technological developments and intensifying competition. Strategic market planning enables managers to undertake a process of market analysis and identification that will determine what business direction it wants to achieve, and how to proceed in a systematic way to turn specific opportunities into profitable businesses.

title: Professional Experience 4: The Internship
description: This final unit in the suite of professional experience units is referred to as the Internship. It is for one full school term conducted in a full-time continuous block at the specified time. All required clearances for working with children must be valid and other units within the degree must be completed and passed in order to undertake the Internship. This unit provides students with the opportunity to exercise the professional skills, knowledge and attitudes in a school setting that demonstrate their classroom readiness. During this sustained professional experience, students will be required to demonstrate that they meet the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers at the Graduate Career stage. This is done through a practical and a theoretical assessment. Both the practical and theoretical assessments must be undertaken together and passed in order to pass the unit. The professional experience practical assessment requires successful completion of the Internship. The theoretical assessment is a teaching performance assessment.

title: Advanced Clinical Immunology
description: This unit explores diagnostic clinical immunology and recent advances in immunology. Students will examine key immune processes and the role of the immune system in disease, including in transplantation, immunotherapy and vaccine development. Selected immunoassays will be used to demonstrate clinical analysis of immune function in medical laboratories, with emphasis on recognising how immune dysregulation presents in laboratory data and clinical cases.

title: Workplace Rehabilitation
description: The unit introduces occupational/vocational rehabilitation theories including the Model of Human Occupation, the occupational therapy process for individuals with a range of illness, injury or disability; hazard identification and injury prevention, industry management and case management within relevant legislative frameworks. The unit develops students’ fundamental knowledge and skills in the application of risk management processes, including skills for professional documentation and report writing, effective communication and development of industrial partnerships

title: Planetary Science
description: This unit provides an introduction to planetary science, focusing on the geology of planets and exploration of the solar system. Topics that will be covered include: history of solar system exploration, space missions and mission design, introduction to cosmochemistry, sample return, analysis, meteorites, impact cratering, origin of life, exoplanets, and planetary/space resources. This unit involves a combination of weekly lectures and laboratory exercises.

title: Indigenous Cultures and Health Behaviours
description: In this unit students will examine culture and diversity within local, national and global Indigenous populations; impacts of specific policies and historical events on Indigenous Australians and the effects of these policies on health, illness and disability, and health care access. Applying theories of health behaviour students will analyse health outcomes of Indigenous Australians and explore underlying social, environmental, psychological and biological determinants. Within a primary health care model, students will explore how health professionals can work inter-professionally and in partnership with Indigenous individuals, families, communities and organisations.

title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
description: This unit provides an introduction to contemporary nuclear and particle physics for non-specialists. The unit starts with a historical introduction and some qualitative formalities. Then we consider the size and shape of nuclei, the masses of nuclei, nuclear instability, alpha decay, nuclear collisions and reactions including fission and fusion, and nuclear models. The second half of the unit is devoted to particles and their interactions. We consider the strong interaction of hadrons and the quark model, the electromagnetic interaction, the weak interaction including beta decay, give a summary of the standard model and discuss what is beyond the standard model. The unit concludes by considering nuclear and particle astrophysics.

title: Special Topics in Urban & Regional Planning
description: Exposure to a specialist area of Urban and Regional Planning or extension of knowledge in selected areas of Urban and Regional Planning. Course will be offered as either short courses and through regular contact throughout the Semester. Students will benefit from the expertise of eminent visiting scholars and/or URP staff who will present in the area of their particular research interest.

title: Applied Paramedic Bioscience 1
description: This unit is the first of four bioscience units in the paramedicine curriculum, designed to deepen students' understanding of clinical theory and management principles. The bioscience units take an integrated, systems-based approach to learning, where pathophysiology, diagnostic strategies, and pharmacology are concurrently taught across the lifespan through application to real-world case studies. In this unit, students will begin with a foundations module that explores core topics such as the basics of pharmacology, haemodynamic stability, shock, inflammation, sepsis, and pain management. Following this, students will integrate biomedical knowledge with patient-centred and culturally safe care to address musculoskeletal, integumentary, and neurological conditions commonly managed by paramedics. Emphasis is placed on discussing the aetiology, pathophysiology, and clinical manifestations of conditions commonly managed by paramedics, interpreting diagnostic strategies, and understanding pharmacotherapeutics and quality use of medicines. Students will also develop skills in evaluating and applying primary evidence and clinical standards to inform management strategies that are evidence-based, person-centred, and culturally safe.

title: Hydrometallurgy
description: Chemical, thermodynamic and kinetic aspects of leaching, separation, extraction and recovery of metals. Oxidative and non-oxidative leaching of minerals, purification and recovery of metals by precipitation, ion exchange and solvent extraction and the recovery of metals by reduction and electrowinning. The design of solvent extraction, ion exchange and leaching circuits.
